title: Prediction of Mode I fracture toughness of porous rocks using rheological dynamics
abstract: Purpose The aim of this paper was to define the Mode I fracture toughness of porous dry rocks based on the rheological-dynamic theory (RDT). The topic is potentially relevant in the context of constitutive modeling and damage mechanics. Design/methodology/approach The fracture toughness is defined within the fracture process zone (FZZ) as a function of the void volume fraction (VVF), which represents existing pores and newly formed voids due to loading. The problem is formulated on a standard cylindrical specimen with a ring-shaped crack under unconfined compressive strength (UCS). Due to the differently defined cohesions in the RDT and Mohr-Coulomb (MC) material, a lateral principal stress appears in the cylinder. The conventional Griffith criterion is improved by introducing this lateral principal stress. Findings The improved Griffith criterion is consistent with the RDT at zero porosity when the rock is treated as elastic. However, differences occur within the inelastic FPZ. The fracture toughness within the FPZ is a function of: VVF, UCS, damage variables, porosity thresholds, creep coefficients, dynamic Poisson's ratio, elastic modulus ratios, cylinder diameter and geometric factor. Originality/value This study uses Zhang's empirical equation to confirm the accuracy of the results obtained by RDT. Evidence for the obtained Mode I fracture toughness is related to the FPZ. …

title: OpenGRF: prediction of ground reaction forces and moments during activities of daily living using OpenSim
abstract: Abstract OpenGRF is a new OpenSim-based tool that estimates ground reaction forces and moments (GRF&Ms) and centre of pressure (CoP) directly from joint kinematics, addressing an existing limitation of current OpenSim workflows. The approach combines calibrated foot–ground contact probes with an optimization framework derived from static optimization, and computes CoP by accounting for both kinematic and dynamic contributions. Its performance was validated against force-plate measurements. Validation involved 126 marker-based trials from seven healthy adults, each performing six trials of level walking, stair ascent and stair descent. Results showed the highest accuracy for vertical GRF, with normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) ≤ 1.5% and Pearson's correlation coefficient (ρ) ≥ 0.94, particularly during level walking. Anterior–posterior GRF was also satisfactorily predicted (nRMSE 4.4%–6.1%, ρ = 0.81–0.91). By contrast, medial–lateral GRF was less reliable, especially in stair tasks, with errors up to 11.2% and correlations as low as 0.48. Free moments were the hardest variable to estimate (nRMSE up to 28%), whereas ankle moments showed excellent agreement with force-plate data (nRMSE ≈ 1.7%, ρ ≈ 0.98). Median CoP error was 21–23 mm, with the largest discrepancies during double support. Overall, OpenGRF enables physics-consistent estimation of GRF-related variables, parti…
venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface

title: A Critical Analysis of Sociology Teachers' Pedagogical Practices Through Performance Test Documents of the 2025 In-Service Teacher Professional Education Program
abstract: This study aims to (1) describe the completeness and alignment of lesson planning in the teaching modules of Sociology teachers who took the 2025 In-Service Teacher UKIN with the indications of learning practice they contain, viewed through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and (2) critically analyze teacher performance in the UKIN through the critical pedagogy perspectives of Paulo Freire and Henry Giroux and Stephen Ball's theory of performativity. The study used a qualitative approach, applying Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis to a purposive sample of 190 Sociology teaching-module documents from UKIN participants at one teacher-education institution (LPTK). The results show that the administrative-format completeness of the teaching modules is generally good, while the substantive depth of teachers' pedagogical competence remains variable. Lesson planning tends to target low-to-moderate cognitive levels, with lower-order thinking categories dominating most modules; assessment items misalign with Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS)-oriented learning objectives in most documents; and PowerPoint remains the dominant, often the only, technology used across most modules. Viewed through the critical lenses of Freire's banking education, Giroux's transformative intellectuals, and Ball's performativity theory, these findings suggest that the UKIN…

title: An exploratory Kano survey of community sports service demands among participating older adults in six selected Wuhan communities
abstract: Background Community sports facilities and related services may shape opportunities for physical activity, but an overall satisfaction score can obscure asymmetric responses to service provision and non-provision. This study described service demands among older adults participating in community sports in six selected Wuhan communities. Methods An exploratory cross-sectional survey with non-probability recruitment yielded 1,065 valid questionnaires, of which 825 current community-sports participants were included in the Kano analysis. Twenty-eight services across six domains were classified by the largest A/O/M/I frequency. Better (SI), Worse (DSI), and their descriptive asymmetry contrast were recalculated from item counts. Sample-specific mean coefficients defined the quadrant reference lines. A deterministic response-recoding analysis examined the sensitivity of dominant categories. Results Eight services were must-be, eight one-dimensional, seven attractive, and five indifferent. Maintenance had the largest |DSI| (0.788), and professional guidance the largest SI (0.700). The contrast SI − |DSI| was negative for maintenance (−0.326) and safety (−0.279), but positive for free facilities (0.290) and age-friendly modification (0.260). For intercommunity exchange, reallocating four of 807 nonreverse responses from the leading category to the second category removed its unique do…

title: The Effect of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on The Decision Not to Return Furniture in E-Commerce Purchases Through Customer Trust
abstract: The growth of e-commerce has made furniture purchasing more convenient for customers; however, it has also introduced risks associated with discrepancies in product information, shipping damage, unclear delivery status, and product returns. This study aims to examine the effects of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on the Decision Not to Return Furniture, both directly and indirectly through Customer Trust as a mediating variable. The study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire comprising 46 indicators administered to 301 customers who had purchased furniture through e-commerce platforms within the preceding 12 months. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software. The results indicate that Last-Mile Service Quality and Shipment Trackability have significant effects on Customer Trust, whereas Product Information Quality does not. Product Information Quality, Shipment Trackability, and Customer Trust significantly influence the Decision Not to Return Furniture, while Last-Mile Service Quality has no significant direct effect. Furthermore, Customer Trust mediates the relationships between Last-Mile Service Quality and the Decision Not …

title: Spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of urban carbon sequestration service flows in China
abstract: Global climate governance increasingly relies on understanding the spatial mismatch between carbon emissions and ecosystem carbon sequestration capacity. As a critical regulating ecosystem service, carbon sequestration service flows exert substantial interregional spillover effects through spatial ecological interactions. However, existing research has largely focused on static supply–demand evaluations at regional scales, while the spatial flow processes and driving mechanisms of carbon sequestration service flows across cities remain insufficiently explored. This study quantified the supply, demand, and flows of carbon sequestration service flows across 333 prefecture-level administrative units in China from 2010 to 2024 using breakpoint–field strength models and spatial flow analysis. Furthermore, the XGBoost-SHAP model was adopted to detect the nonlinear driving mechanisms behind carbon sequestration service flows. The results showed that China’s carbon sequestration service flows presented a potential west-to-east linkage pattern, indicating a pronounced spatial mismatch between carbon sequestration supply areas and carbon emission demand areas. High-supply regions were predominantly distributed in western and northern China, whereas demand regions were concentrated in eastern coastal urban agglomerations. The total volume of carbon sequestration service flows first rose a…

title: Typologies Of Political Patronage: Expert Evidence From Mongolia's Civil Service
abstract: Political patronage remains a persistent feature of civil service systems worldwide, even where formal recruitment rules are nominally meritocratic. This article examines the typological forms political patronage takes within Mongolia's civil service, addressing a gap in the comparative literature between highly institutionalized European party-government systems, where influential typologies of patronage were originally developed, and post-socialist, semi-presidential contexts, where such typologies remain largely untested. Despite two decades of civil service reform explicitly modeled on career-based meritocratic systems, official Civil Service Council statistics document a rise in unlawful personnel rotation from 5.2 percent of civil servants in 2007 to over 22 percent in 2019, indicating a persistent divergence between formal rule and administrative practice. Drawing on a two-stage expert survey and interview design involving 55 experts from academia, the civil service, and political practice, this study tests the applicability of the influential typology developed by Kopecký, Mair, and Spirova (2012)—distinguishing party-apparatus-based, technocratic, agency-based, and party-membership-based patronage—to the Mongolian case. Findings indicate that all four typological categories are unanimously or near-unanimously recognized by experts as operative, evidencing pronounced ty…
venue: Theory and Practice in Social Studies

title: Before regulation: structural lock-out of mass timber in Pakistan's built environment
abstract: Purpose Existing studies explain mass timber nonadoption through regulatory; insurance and liability mechanisms derived from Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) markets. This article asks what happens when those gatekeeping institutions are weak or absent, yet low-carbon materials still fail to enter the market. It develops and empirically applies a mechanism-based diagnostic framework distinguishing formal regulatory lock-in from informal structural lock-out, using Pakistan as a critical case. Design/methodology/approach Phase One consolidated a process model of lock-in through a critical interpretive synthesis (CIS) of 22 OECD mass timber studies drawn from a 95-study scoping corpus (literature searched January 2015 to January 2026). Phase Two tested and extended it through a qualitative Pakistan case study. Data comprised 32 semi-structured expert interviews with architects, structural engineers, developers and building regulators in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad (September 2025 to February 2026), triangulated with policy documents, tariff schedules, trade statistics, procurement records and marketing materials. Inter-coder reliability: Krippendorf’s a = 0.81. Findings The three OECD mechanisms (risk categorization inertia, epistemic closure and liability lock-in) are absent or latent in Pakistan. Yet no market presence was identified; official reco…

title: Developing Students’ Self-Regulation through Active Participation in the Sang Pendakwah Community (KSP) at SMPN 48 Surabaya
abstract: This study examines how students’ active participation in the Sang Pendakwah Community (KSP) contributes to the development of self-regulation in a public school. This research employed a qualitative approach with a case study design at SMPN 48 Surabaya. Data were collected through non-participant observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation. Ten informants were purposively selected, consisting of one community advisor, two student administrators, and seven KSP members or participants from Grades VIII and IX. Data credibility was strengthened through technique triangulation, while analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that students’ participation in KSP provides opportunities to practice five aspects of self-regulation: discipline, responsibility, independence, self-control, and self-confidence. This process occurs through preparation and planning, fulfillment of responsibilities and peer interaction, and evaluation with feedback. These processes correspond to Zimmerman’s three phases of self-regulation: forethought, performance, and self-reflection. The novelty of this study lies in examining a student-led religious community as a space for developing self-regulation beyond formal classroom learning. Therefore, providing meaningful responsibilities and opportunities for active participat…

title: Regulation of endogenous dsRNA: strategies for self-tolerance
abstract: Abstract Cells must continuously distinguish cellular-derived RNA from pathogenic RNA to mount effective antiviral responses while avoiding harmful autoinflammation. Cytoplasmic RNA-sensing receptors, including RIG-I-like receptors, PKR, OAS-RNase L and ZBP1, detect RNA primarily through molecular features such as structure (double- versus single-stranded), modification state and subcellular localization rather than sequence. While these are characteristics of viral nucleic acids, mammalian genomes generate abundant self-derived double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), including from transposable elements, antisense transcription and RNA processing intermediates, which exist in the cytoplasm. This review describes our current understanding of how cells achieve self-tolerance through the active regulation of endogenous RNA. These mechanisms comprise epigenetic silencing of repetitive elements, RNA modifications (such as A-to-I editing and m6A), precise splicing, regulated nuclear export and decay, circRNA buffering, protein shielding and dedicated RNA degradation pathways. Insights from rare inherited monogenic interferonopathies and murine models illustrate how perturbations in these pathways lead to inappropriate activation of cytoplasmic RNA sensors and inflammatory disease when cellular dsRNA is mistakenly recognized as non-self. We highlight how dysregulated dsRNA homeostasis contribut…

title: The two-component system CrdRS mediates sub-inhibitory antibiotic-induced biofilm formation in Helicobacter pylori via bidirectional regulation of transporters PlpA and GlnP
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofilm formation by Helicobacter pylori is a major driver of antibiotic tolerance and treatment failure, yet the signaling pathways that trigger biofilm development under sub-inhibitory antibiotic pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we show that sub-MIC levels of metronidazole, amoxicillin, and ciprofloxacin potently induce dense H. pylori biofilms. Through transcriptomic and genetic analyses, we identify the two-component system CrdRS as a central signaling hub that orchestrates this response via the bidirectional regulation of two ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. Phosphorylated CrdR binds to AC-rich promoter motifs to directly activate plpA , which encodes a substrate-binding protein that drives exopolysaccharide secretion and matrix assembly. Concomitantly, CrdR represses glnP , which encodes an inner-membrane permease, thereby relieving transcriptional inhibition of the L-asparaginase gene ansB . This derepression triggers aberrant reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which promotes oxidative stress-dependent biofilm maturation. Through phenotypic analysis of c rdRS deletion mutants, phosphorylation-defective point mutants (CrdR D53A and CrdS H173A ), and exogenous hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) induction, we demonstrate that CrdRS is required for mediating antibiotic-induced stress responses in a manner genetically separable from ROS sensing. Collec…

title: Frequency of Diabetes Mellitus andHypertension among Physicians Working inSelected Medical Colleges inChattogram, Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) and Hypertension (HTN) are important occupational-health concerns among physicians, whose work may involve prolonged sitting, irregular schedules, psychological stress, and limited opportunity for preventive care. This study assessed the frequency of DM and HTN and their associated factors among physicians working in selected medical colleges in Bangladesh. Materials and methods: A multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted from June to December 2025 among 284 physicians from seven selected medical colleges. Sociodemographic, professional, clinical, treatment, family-history and behavioural data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, with blood pressure, random capillary blood glucose, height, and weight recorded. Separate multivariable logistic regression models identified factors associated with DM and HTN, adjusted odds ratios (AORs) 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p values were reported. Results: Among 284 physicians (Mean age 40.18 ± 10.64 years; 54.9% male), 64 (22.5%) had DM and 65 (22.9%) had HTN. Sedentary physical activity was reported by 60.9%, overweight or obesity was present in 58.8% and current or former smoking in 17.6%. For DM, increasing age (AOR per 5 years 1.58, 95% CI 1.34–1.85), smoking (AOR 5.59, 95% CI 2.46–12.70) sedentary activity (AOR 2.69, 95% CI 1.24–5.86) and reported stress (AOR 2.88, …

title: Legal Regulation of Intellectual Property in the Field of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study aimed to identify differences between contemporary approaches to protecting intellectual outputs created or used with artificial intelligence and to establish criteria connecting rights, obligations, and liability to human contributions at successive stages of the technological process. Conducted in August 2026, the study examined a purposive, non-random sample of 45 legislative, judicial, administrative, and official analytical documents from the World Intellectual Property Organization, the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Ukraine. The documentary cutoff was 27 August 2026. Documents were examined against 13 criteria encompassing input authorization, text and data mining, rights reservations, training transparency, authorship, creative control, output protection, special protection regimes, inventorship, human inventive contribution, liability, trade secrets, and remedies. European Union materials constituted 28.9% of the sample, followed by United States materials at 24.4%, United Kingdom materials at 20.0%, Ukrainian materials at 15.6%, and international institutional materials at 11.1%. The European Union instruments connect distinct mining exceptions with rights reservations and general-purpose model transparency; the United States materials emphasize fair use and case-specific analysis. United Kingdom legislation retains a computer-ge…

title: Beyond single regulation: how does green agriculture comprehensive pilot achieve fertilizer reduction? Evidence from China
abstract: Introduction Compared with single regulation, the Green Agriculture Comprehensive Pilot (GACP) is a comprehensive pilot policy promoted by China to advance agricultural green transformation. However, few questions remain unclear whether and how this policy reduce the fertilizer use. Methods Using panel data of 106 cities from 8 Chinese central and eastern provinces over 20002022, this study adopts difference-in-differences (DID) and causal mediation analysis (CMA) to evaluate GACP’s effect on fertilizer application density, identifying its underlying mechanisms and heterogeneities, and discuss its implications for food security. Results The results show that the GACP effectively reduces fertilizer use, decreasing the average annual fertilizer per unit of sown area in pilot cities by 9.9% (44.046 kg/ hm2). The reduction effect initially strengthens but then gradually weakens over time, but remains effective throughout the observation period, these results remaining robust after a series of tests. Mechanism analysis indicates that the GACP reduces fertilizer use by establishing a green agricultural support system and promoting four internal institutional incentive mechanisms: technological progress, scale operation, professional division, and industrial convergence, with respective contributions of 11.15%, 5.46%, 12.66%, and 8.12%. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the reduction …

title: Hemodialysis patients exhibit T-cell activation accompanied by an enhanced frequency of IFN-γ+CD4+/CD8+ T cells
abstract: T-cell immune dysregulation is common in end-stage renal disease (ESRD), but whether hemodialysis (HD) differentially affects T-cell immune activity remains unclear. We evaluated the peripheral T-cell immune characteristics of 96 patients with ESRD and 86 healthy controls to explore the effects of HD on T-cell immune function. T-cell subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry for phenotype, number, and function (represented by interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] secretion capacity). Compared with healthy controls, patients with ESRD showed significant reductions in the absolute number of CD8 + T-naïve (TN)/T effector memory (TEM)/T effector memory regulatory (TEMRA), CD4 + T-cell memory (TCM), CD4 + CD38 + , CD8 + /CD4 + HLA-DR + , and CD8 + /CD4 + CD28 + cells, especially in the proportion and quantity of CD4 + TN cells. Compared with nHD patients, HD patients showed significantly different peripheral T-cell immune characteristics. Phenotypically, the changes in CD4 + T-cell subsets were more significant than those observed for CD8 + T cells, with activated T cells (CD4 + CD38 + , CD4 + HLA-DR + , and CD8 + CD38 + T cells) increased and functional T cells (CD4 + CD28 + T cells) decreased in proportion and quantity. Functionally, the frequency of IFN-γ + CD4 + /CD8 + T cells was significantly higher in HD patients than in nHD patients, indicating the enhanced functional activation of T cells…

title: Integral sliding-mode current regulation for sequence-impedance shaping and oscillation suppression in virtual synchronous generators
abstract: Cascade-controlled virtual synchronous generators (VSGs), widely adopted in grid-forming battery energy storage systems (BESS), may experience low-frequency instability when connected to stiff grids characterized by relatively high short-circuit ratios (SCRs) and small equivalent grid impedances. A frequency-coupled sequence-impedance model was developed to investigate the instability mechanism. The conventional proportional-integral (PI) current regulator was replaced with an integral sliding-mode controller incorporating an integral sliding surface and a boundary-layer reaching law, while retaining the outer power and voltage control loops. Small-signal impedance analysis, MATLAB/Simulink simulations, and RT-LAB real-time simulation tests were conducted under different SCR conditions. The baseline model identified a capacitive region in the positive-sequence impedance that resulted in insufficient phase margins at converter-grid impedance crossovers. The proposed controller narrowed the capacitive region and yielded positive phase margins in the analyzed cases. Simulations and real-time tests confirmed the suppression of sustained grid-current oscillations. Compared with a fixed virtual-inductance benchmark, the proposed method shortened recovery time and reduced grid-current total harmonic distortion from 3.38% to 0.54% at SCR = 30 (Lg = 1.5 mH). The results indicate that th…

title: LAND CARRYING CAPACITY, WATER SAFETY, AND COMMUNITY HEALTH UNDER POPULATION PRESSURE: A MULTIDISCIPLINARY ASSESSMENT OF HILLSIDE SETTLEMENT IN NEGERI BATU MERAH, AMBON, INDONESIA
abstract: Background Small island cities grow on scarce, steep, and hazard-prone land. Negeri Batu Merah, a customary village in Ambon City, is classified as a heavy slum area with 66,424 people on 911 ha. Its dense settlement relies on septic tanks and shallow wells, linking land limits to water safety, and maternal and child health. This study assesses Batu Merah’s land-carrying capacity, measures how existing settlements are distributed across it, and interprets the results for engineering, water safety, community health, access, and spatial governance. Methods Nine land capability units were analyzed following Minister of Public Works Regulation No. 20/PRT/M/2007 and converted into potential, limitation, and constraint zones. Settlement from the 2018 national land cover map is overlaid on these zones and each unit. Published water quality and health studies on Ambon were compiled, and the results were interpreted from eight disciplines, including chemistry, global health, and midwifery. Results The village had moderately high (56.14%), moderate (42.87%), and low land capability (0.99%). Settlement covers 600.61 ha at about 110 persons per settled hectare. The potential zone was 96.5% built-up, and the constraint zone was almost entirely. All 97.67 ha of settlement in the limitation zone stands on land with low foundation stability, moderate slope stability, and a moderately high haza…

title: Recovery physiology: a testable systems framework for preserving the capacity to function
abstract: Living systems must restore function after perturbation while operating under finite energetic, structural, regulatory, and environmental constraints. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes Recovery Physiology as a testable framework for studying that problem. Recovery is defined narrowly as the time-dependent response following a prospectively specified perturbation that measurably displaces one or more prespecified functional variables from a relevant reference state. Recovery Capacity (RC) is defined separately as a hypothetical latent, context-dependent property that may influence the magnitude, rate, completeness, coordination, and cost of that response; favorable outcomes are not evidence of high RC by definition. Three candidate domains—bioenergetic capacity, biological information integrity, and systems coordination—are proposed as a parsimonious but revisable architecture. The framework makes three separable claims: recovery phenotypes may contain reliable challenge-specific latent structure and possibly a higher-order cross-challenge factor; the proposed domain architecture may explain recovery beyond simpler alternatives; and dynamic trajectories may add prognostic information beyond baseline state and established constructs. Each claim is paired with competing models and falsification criteria. A standardized exercise protocol illustrates how reliability, const…

title: Processing capacity under complexity: an organizational information processing perspective on humanitarian supply chain performance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the role of processing capacity in shaping humanitarian supply chain performance under crisis conditions. Specifically, it examines how information processing capacity influences response performance and equity performance, and how environmental complexity and structural integration moderate these relationships. It also examines whether environmental complexity moderates the information processing capacity-equity performance relationship more strongly than the information processing capacity-response performance relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) and a contingency perspective, the research model is proposed and empirically evaluated using survey data collected from 600 professionals with relevant experience working in the humanitarian supply chain across India. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Findings The PLS-SEM results show that processing capacity has a significant positive effect on both response performance and equity performance. The environmental complexity amplifies the impact of processing capacity on both outcomes, but results confirm that it has stronger moderating effect for equity performance compared to response performance. Similarly, structural integration also significantly streng…

title: Temperature-accelerated multiscale degradation in manganese-based blended-cathode pouch cells: evolution and origins of capacity loss
abstract: Abstract Understanding how dominant capacity-loss factors evolve under deeper cathode delithiation is critical for improving the capacity utilization and durability of lithium-ion batteries employing Mn-based blended cathodes. Here, 6.2 Ah graphite pouch cells with an NCM/LMFP/LRMO blended cathode were cycled between 3.0 and 4.3 V at 1 C at 25 and 45 ℃ and investigated using electrochemical diagnostics, ultrasonic inspection, and multiscale post-mortem characterization. The 25 ℃ cell retained 87.9% of its initial capacity after 1,200 cycles, whereas the 45 ℃ cell retained only 75.0% after 457 cycles. Electrochemical analysis indicates that capacity fading at 25 ℃ initially exhibits features consistent with reduced electrochemically accessible reaction capacity and LAM-related degradation, followed by increasingly evident LLI-related electrode slippage and ultimately a late-stage regime involving coupled LAM-related degradation, LLI, and impedance growth. At 45 ℃, this evolution is markedly compressed, with these degradation factors becoming strongly coupled within the first several hundred cycles. Multiscale characterization further links the accelerated degradation at elevated temperature to intensified interfacial parasitic reactions, cyclable-lithium and electrolyte consumption, gas generation, anode-material detachment, separator pore blockage, transport deterioration, and …

title: Bioengineered Andrias davidianus Skin Secretion Sponge: A Sustainable Hemostatic Material with Enhanced Wound Healing Capacity
abstract: Abstract The skin secretion of Andrias davidianus (SSAD) is a miraculous natural protein-based product with exceptional potential for treating bleeding wounds and has long been used in traditional folk medicine. However, its commercialization and societal benefits have been hindered by challenges in reproducibly manufacturing products with highly consistent properties and bacteria-free conditions. Here, we introduce a straightforward manufacturing method to produce a practically applicable hemostatic sponge derived from SSAD, which significantly enhances wound healing. To further improve antimicrobial properties, the antibacterial peptide ε-polylysine (EPL) was incorporated, resulting in composite sponges (SSAD-EPLs). The fabricated sponges exhibit excellent biocompatibility and are capable of degrading in vivo over a 21-day observation period. Compared to a commercial gelatin sponge (CGS), both SSAD and SSAD-EPL2 (containing 20% EPL) sponges demonstrated superior hemostatic performance, significantly reducing blood loss and clotting time. In a full-thickness skin defect model, SSAD and SSAD-EPL2 sponges showed remarkable efficacy in promoting wound healing and could be easily removed from the wound site without causing secondary injury. Our findings highlight the practical applicability of these sponges, not only due to their outstanding hemostatic and wound-healing properties…

title: Carbon Sequestration Capacity of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati City, Davao Oriental
abstract: The study was conducted to quantify the biomass and carbon storage of the vegetative cover of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati, Davao Oriental. The specific objectives of this study were to determine the total area of the vegetative cover, to determine the vegetative structures, to identify the status of the vegetation, and to provide recommendations in relation to the management of the watershed. Actual surveying of the area as to the hectarage of various vegetative covers of the area was done with the aid of a Global Positioning System (GPS). The determined hectarage was then used in extrapolating the biomass and carbon sequestration capacity of the vegetative cover of the area. The Geographic Information System software was used to come up with a vegetation map of the area. The watershed area in Brgy. Central covers 879.21 ha., comprising agroforestry farms, Tree Plantation, Secondary-growth Forest, Cogon area, and the human settlement of Purok Malipayon and Sitio Banahaw. Their extent is as follows: Agroforestry farms, occupying the largest area, covers 492.36 ha., secondary-growth forest or thickets covers 195.97 ha., tree plantation covers 178.65 ha., and cogon area with 10.02 ha. Human settlement of Purok Malipayon covers 0.69 ha. While that of Sitio Banahaw covers 1.52 ha. The agroforestry farm, having occupied the largest area, has the greatest biomass (25,66…

title: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
abstract: Numerical models are crucial tools for understanding complex chemical systems such as the atmosphere, and their sensitivity across a range of conditions. In atmospheric chemistry models, reaction mechanisms are used to represent chemical transformations and define the underlying system of equations. Building highly explicit mechanisms that capture the full complexity of organic oxidation occurring in the atmosphere remains challenging owing to the large number of intermediates involved, the breadth of reaction pathways, and the limited availability of reliable kinetic and thermodynamic data. The Generator for Explicit Chemistry and Kinetics of Organics in the Atmosphere (GECKO-A) was developed to address these limitations by enabling the systematic construction of near-explicit mechanisms. Here, we present its first open-source release (v1.0), which incorporates updated chemical protocols and structure-activity relationships, together with its companion box model for mechanism integration. GECKO-A's performance is benchmarked through systematic comparisons with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM v3.3.1), based on simulations of the oxidation of five representative hydrocarbons (butane, octane, dodecane, toluene, and α -pinene) under environmental conditions ranging from urban to remote. The two approaches yield similar oxidation pathways for small and structurally simple compou…
