title: Decoupling the Intrinsic Li/Mn Disorder Mechanism in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
abstract: Abstract Li-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are promising high-energy cathodes but suffer from irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation associated with Li2MnO3 domains. Recently, disorder engineering has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the local coordination environment and stabilize the oxygen redox of LLOs. Herein, we confirm the existence of intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within the Li2MnO3 domains, which can be classified into local Li-excess and TM-excess configurations derived from the initial Li-rich framework. Furthermore, DFT calculations suggest complementary local roles for the different disordered configurations: Li-excess domains promote oxygen redox activity, whereas TM-excess domains reinforce TM–O bonding and stabilize the framework against irreversible degradation. Consequently, M-LLO containing the coupled disordered configurations promotes more reversible anionic redox, suppresses irreversible oxygen release and transition-metal migration, and thereby delivers improved electrochemical stability. This work provides new insights into the role of intrinsic disorder regulation in Li-rich layered cathodes.

title: Effect of Launaea taraxacifolia on Pregnancy Outcome, its Safety Profile and Mechanism(s) of Alleviating Labour Pain in Gravid Rats
abstract: Purpose: Launaea taraxacifolia (LT) is traditionally utilised by pregnant women to ease labour. This study evaluated LT’s effects on pregnancy outcomes, its safety profile, and the mechanism by which it alleviates labour pain. Methods: Whole plants of LT were extracted by maceration in distilled water. Pregnant rats were assigned to four groups and treated as follows: control (distilled water, 5 mL/kg/day); 25, 50, and 100 mg/kg/day LT, respectively, from gestational day (GD) 14 to GD 20. On GD 21, pups were delivered via caesarean section, and pregnancy outcome parameters were assessed. Blood samples, amniotic fluid, umbilical cord, placenta, and maternal organs were analysed. The active constituents in LT were identified using High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. Results: No significant differences were observed in pregnancy outcomes, including the weights of dams, pups, and placenta; litter size; crump-rump length; and head circumference. Biochemical analyses indicated a reduction in sodium and chloride ions in the 100 mg/kg LT dose group and an increase in alkaline phosphatase in the 50 and 100 mg/kg LT groups. Estradiol levels decreased across all treated groups; however, prostaglandin E2 concentrations in both the amniotic fluid and umbilical cord samples remained unchanged, while prostaglandin F2α increased significantly in the amniotic fluid of the tr…

title: Unique Regulatory Mechanism of Melatonin-Mediated Defense Against Vanadium Toxicity in Brassica napus L.
abstract: Brassica napus L. (B. napus) is a well-known edible oil crop globally. Its production has been severely damaged by abiotic stresses, including heavy metals. Vanadium (V) is a heavy metal that can cause a reduction in plant biomass, photosynthetic pigments, and alleviate ROS production. Melatonin (MT) is a newly emerged nontoxic, regulatory bio-molecule that regulates plant growth against abiotic stresses, but there is limited knowledge about MT's mitigative role against V-induced phytotoxicity in B. napus. The present study investigates the MT based tolerance in B. napus against V toxicity by contructioing gene regulatory network by Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Transcriptome profiling identified 1767 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) uniquely or commonly regulated in CK, MT, V, and MTV groups. Transcriptome-wide reprogramming at the molecular level showed that MT reduced excessive DEG fluctuations brought on by V stress, bringing expression patterns closer to the control. Cluster analyses (C2, C6) show MT-specific activation of genes involved in phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, jasmonic acid metabolism, and protein folding. WGCNA identified the black and tan modules as strongly correlated with photosynthesis, biomass, and stress traits, pinpointing hub genes NAC072, MYB122, WRKY33, PER72, GSTU19, CYP82G1, ELF5A-2, Cox19-like, RCI2A, GRXC2, MKP1, PNSL2,…

title: The human body as a multi-organ coupled homeostatic organism: the core mechanism of the super minimally invasive surgery paradigm
abstract: Super minimally invasive surgery (SMIS) has been proposed as a treatment paradigm in which minimally invasive care is evaluated not only by access-related trauma but also by treatment-induced biological disturbance and preservation of organ function. We hypothesize that, when disease-control adequacy is comparable, strategies associated with lower multidimensional homeostatic disturbance will be associated with faster functional recovery and better long-term organ- and patient-centered outcomes. We define an SMIS-concordant strategy by three conditions: adequate disease control; lower measurable treatment-induced disturbance than an appropriate comparator; and preservation or faster restoration of organ and systemic function. Homeostatic disturbance is operationalized as a multidomain construct that may include inflammatory/immune, neuroendocrine, metabolic/nutritional, organ-specific, barrier/microbiome/circadian, functional, and patient-reported domains. Because no validated universal score, weighting scheme, or threshold is available, we propose a comparative measurement matrix rather than a new composite index. The framework yields three falsifiable predictions: SMIS-concordant strategies should produce less early biological disturbance, support a faster return toward baseline, and provide prognostic information for long-term recovery beyond conventional perioperative measu…

title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair
abstract: Abstract Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1…

title: Effect of Epoxy Carbon Nanotube Composite Coating on Properties of Steel
abstract: The motivation behind this research is to prepare an epoxy carbon nanotube (EP-CNT) composite coating and apply it for steel protection. Multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) particles were added to epoxy with different loadings as; (0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0) % by the total weight of epoxy matrix. The experimental results of this work detected that 0.75% CNTs have an evident effect for enhancing the protective performance of epoxy composite coatings as follows: the final drying time reduced to 64% from the time for the control sample (without CNTs). On the other hand, both the Dry Film Thickness (DFT) of the applied coatings and adhesion strength values increased by 8% and 36%, respectively. Meanwhile, the hydrophobicity of the epoxy composite coating was enhanced by increasing the contact angle of EP-CNT 0.75% to 47% as compared to the pristine epoxy coating sample. Furthermore, incorporating 0.75% CNTs led to enhanced abrasion and fire resistance by 17% and 11%, respectively. Lastly, the resistance of the applied coatings against chemicals and crude oil was changed from fair to excellent.

title: From PFAD Conversion to Refinery Qualification: Catalyst Lifetime, Hydrogen Efficiency and Carbon Integrity in Renewable-Diesel Co-Processing
abstract: Palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) is an attractive free-fatty-acid-rich intermediate for producing paraffinic fuels, but laboratory conversion does not establish reliable performance in an existing petroleum refinery. This critical qualitative literature review examines peer-reviewed research from 2020 to 2026 on PFAD composition, competing deoxygenation chemistry, catalyst deactivation, hydrogen use, refinery co-processing, product qualification, and lifecycle accounting. The thematic synthesis identifies six interlocking constraints: feedstock variability and adsorption-driven side reactions; the carbon-retention versus hydrogen-demand trade-off; uncertainty in catalyst durability; interactions with fossil-stream hydrotreating; hydrogen and thermal-system integration; and contested allocation of upstream palm-oil emissions. It proposes a Feedstock-Catalyst-Hydrogen-Refinery-Carbon (FCHRC) Readiness Framework and a staged evidence scorecard for testing compatibility before deployment. The central finding is conditional: PFAD-to-hydrocarbon conversion has been demonstrated in several settings, whereas long-term, refinery-specific co-processing reliability and unqualified low-carbon status cannot be inferred from high short-run conversion or yield. Future studies should combine representative PFAD characterization, long-duration fixed-bed testing, mass and hydrogen balances, pet…
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences Technology

title: Bi3+/Ln3+-Codoped Boroaluminate Phosphors with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Multidimensional Luminescence Readout and UV-Shielding
abstract: Abstract Combining lattice regulation of crystal-field-sensitive Bi3+ emission with Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization provides two complementary pathways for tuning the luminescence of single-host phosphors. Herein, Bi3+-activated Sr6Lu1-yYyAl(BO3)6 solid solutions and Bi3+/Ln3+-codoped Sr6LuAl(BO3)6 (SLAB; Ln = Eu, Dy, Sm, and Tb) phosphors were synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction. SLAB:Bi3+ exhibited broadband blue-violet emission centered at 419 nm under 325 nm excitation. Isovalent Y3+ substitution for Lu3+ regulated the local environment of Bi3+ and enhanced the integrated emission intensity by approximately sixfold under 365 nm excitation, with internal and external quantum efficiencies (IQE and EQE) reaching 87.2 and 31.7%, respectively. The lifetime-derived efficiency of Bi3+ → Eu3+ energy transfer reached a maximum of 85.8% and enabled continuous color tuning from blue-violet to orange-red by adjusting the Eu3+ concentration and excitation wavelength. Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization was further demonstrated for Dy3+, Sm3+, and Tb3+, producing purple, purplish-red, and green emissions, respectively. Taking advantage of their strong UV absorption, the phosphors were incorporated into flexible films for a proof-of-concept evaluation of UV shielding. The tunable multicolor emissions were further used to fabricate multicolor security labels and demonstrate binary optic…

title: Fine-resolution carbon dynamics mapping reveals unequal contributions to carbon neutrality within Chinese cities
abstract: Abstract Understanding the inequalities of carbon neutrality within cities is essential for implementing differentiated carbon reduction policies. Here we develop an integrated model to conduct a fine-resolution (250 m, monthly) assessment of net carbon emissions (NCE) for three major urban agglomerations in China. Our results precisely depict the seasonal patterns of NCE and highlight the diverse urban carbon dynamics that contribute to inequalities in carbon neutrality. Nearly half of the 48 cities exhibited NCE exceeding 1000 gC∙m−2∙a−1, while only 5 cities functioned as carbon sinks. Theil index analysis reveals that intra-city inequalities are more pronounced in industrial cities with Theil index over 0.11, while inter-city disparities are primarily driven by economic and industrial imbalances, particularly in the Pearl River Delta, where Theil index has reached 0.18. This emphasizes the dominant role of high-emission cities in shaping regional inequalities. These findings provide actionable insights for urban afforestation and emission mitigation policies aimed at achieving carbon neutrality.

title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
abstract: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. The as-synthesized Co-Mo2S3/carbon foam (CF) achieved an average evaporation rate of 2.13 kg m-2 h-1 during a 1-h experiment under 1,000 W m-2 irradiation using a 3.5% NaCl solution, compared to 1.55 kg m-2 h-1 obtained for CF. A Taguchi orthogonal-array design of experiments (DOE) was used to optimize the effect of input parameters on the evaporation rate of saline water. The experimental design matrix shows a maximum water evaporation rate of 1.77 kg m-2 h-1 under real sunlight. Taguchi analysis presents the optimal operating parameters for the evaporation rate as follows: salinity 30 g L-1 (level 1), saline water pH 5 (level 2), and time 2 h (level 2). The statistical outcomes show that salinity is the main factor affecting the evaporation rate. This study addresses water scarcity and promotes the circular economy by transforming plastic waste into a valuable resource for producing clean water and provides deeper insight into the optimization of the o…

title: Quantitative Evaluation on How Hydrogen-Content Affects the Atomic-Scale Adhesive Wear Behaviors of Hydrogenated Amorphous Carbon
abstract: Abstract Hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H) coatings exhibit excellent tribological properties, including low friction and high wear resistance, making them valuable for numerous engineering applications. However, under real service conditions, these coatings can still experience wear, limiting their long-term reliability. A clearer understanding of the underlying wear mechanisms is essential to improve their durability. The performance of a-C:H coatings is closely linked to their hydrogen content and atomic-scale structure. Following the two-step reaction theory proposed in our previous work [Adv. Sci, 2021, 8, 2002827], this study uses large-scale reactive molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how hydrogen content influences the activation energies (or energy barriers) of the two-step reaction: the interfacial bond formation and the interfacial-bond-induced atom removal. Results show that the activation energy of forming interfacial bonds rises with hydrogen content, because hydrogen passivates surface carbon atoms, reducing their reactivity; while the activation energy required to remove atoms remains largely unaffected by hydrogen content, since the number of bonds broken per removed atom stays nearly constant. These findings help clarify the relationship between the atomic structure of a-C:H coatings and their wear behavior, providing useful insight for designin…

title: Carbon Nanofiber-Integrated CuCo-MOF as a Conductive Bifunctional Electrocatalyst for Overall Water Splitting
abstract: Abstract The CuCo-MOF/CNF electrocatalyst, with a well-defined microstructure and efficient charge transfer was successfully synthesized through a simple solvothermal method. In the CuCo-MOF/CNF composite, the introduction of CNF can effectively improve the conductivity and provide sufficient active sites for the electrochemical reaction. The CuCo-MOF/CNF composite has excellent bifunctional electrocatalytic activity for the HER and OER reactions. The catalyst really stands out with its great performance, requiring overpotentials of 50 mV for HER and 70 mV for OER at a current density of 10 mA cm–2. The CuCo-MOF/CNF electrocatalyst has low Tafel slope values of 98 mV dec–1 for OER and 131 mV dec–1 for HER, along with low charge transfer resistance, exhibiting excellent operational stability for up to 40 h for both OER and HER. Moreover, the catalyst has relatively large double-layer capacitance values of 8.95 mF cm–2 for OER and 3.47 mF cm–2 for HER, implying that the electrochemically active surface areas are quite large (223.8 cm2 for OER and 86.8 cm2 for HER). Overall, these structural and electrochemical advantages contribute to the superior catalytic performance of the electrocatalyst, providing a novel framework for the development of highly efficient and scalable bifunctional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting.

title: From Variable Palm Residues to Certifiable Low-Carbon Concrete: A Critical Review of POFA and Biochar Processing, Microstructure, Durability, and Performance-Based Standardisation
abstract: Palm oil fuel ash (POFA) and palm-biomass biochar have attracted interest as lower-carbon concrete constituents, yet material variability continues to impede confident engineering adoption. This critical qualitative literature review shifts attention from cement-replacement feasibility to the causal relationships among residue origin, processing, cement microstructure, exposure-dependent durability and qualification. Evidence from 2020–2025 journal research is interpreted across mineral-ash treatment, biochar pyrolysis, hydration kinetics, strength and deformation, chloride transport, carbonation, reinforcement corrosion and life-cycle performance. POFA primarily offers potentially reactive siliceous and packing functions; biochar introduces distinct porosity, moisture-management and carbon-retention functions. Neither has universally beneficial effects, and results from non-palm biochars should not be interpreted as direct validation of palm-residue formulations. The review proposes five qualification gates spanning source traceability and environmental safety, processing control, role-specific screening, exposure-based concrete verification and independently monitored pilot deployment. It also outlines an Indonesian tropical/coastal validation roadmap and recommends service-life-equivalent carbon assessment. The principal conclusion is that reproducibility, durability and tra…
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences Technology

title: A Monolithic Carbon Nanotube-Reinforced Cellulose Benzoate Hydrogel for Simultaneous Removal of Microplastics and Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances from Water
abstract: Abstract Simultaneously removing particulate microplastics and dissolved per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), which differ greatly in physical nature, with a single, easily recoverable material remains challenging. Here, we developed a carbon nanotube (CNT)-modified cellulose benzoate (CB) hydrogel as a reusable cellulose-based adsorbent for the removal of polystyrene (PS) microplastics and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), selected as representative microplastic and PFAS contaminants, respectively. Benzoyl functionalization of the cellulose backbone created aromatic, hydrophobic domains that raised the hydrogel’s affinity toward both contaminants, while CNT incorporation opened up the pore structure of the polymer network and improved the mechanical strength. The hydrogel achieved removal efficiencies above 97% for both contaminants, could be readily retrieved from water after treatment, and retained this performance over five adsorption–desorption cycles. Adsorption kinetics showed rapid uptake of both PS and PFOA, and equilibrium isotherms pointed to a high capacity for PS (estimated at ∼700–800 mg/g) and heterogeneous binding for PFOA over the concentration range studied. High removal efficiencies were also maintained in river water and in a cocontaminant system containing both PS microplastics and PFOA. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and X-ray photoelectr…

title: Halogen-Driven Tetrahedral Distortion Enables Tunable White-Light Emission and Scintillation Properties in Hybrid Zinc Halides
abstract: Abstract Organic–inorganic hybrid zinc halides have emerged as promising luminescent materials for solid-state lighting and radiation detection owing to their facile synthesis, tunable crystal structures, and rich photophysical behaviors. Herein, we report two hybrid zinc halides, (C5H14N2)ZnCl4·0.5H2O (Cl4) and (C5H14N2)ZnBr4·H2O (Br4), wherein halogen substitution from Cl– to Br– successfully achieves tunable white-light emission with color coordinates of (0.23, 0.25) for Cl4 and (0.26, 0.29) for Br4, originating from the synergistic contribution of singlet and triplet excited states. Benefiting from the favorable crystal-field environment of the bromide host, Mn2+ ions are further introduced into the Br4 lattice via an N-ion-doping strategy. The incorporated Mn2+ activators endow Br4 with prominent radioluminescence under X-ray excitation, and the optimized Br4:0.6Mn2+ exhibits a light yield of 16900 photons/MeV and a detection limit of 1.28 μGyair/s. Further, a spatial resolution of 7.6 Lp/mm is achieved in X-ray imaging based on the flexible Br4:0.6Mn2+@PDMS films. This work establishes a straightforward anion engineering strategy to simultaneously realize white photoluminescence and efficient X-ray scintillation within a single hybrid zinc halide system, providing a facile route toward multifunctional luminescent materials for white-light illumination and high-performance…

title: Spatial differentiation of transport carbon emissions under the 5Ds framework: implications for sustainable spatial planning in Guangzhou, China
abstract: Sustainable spatial planning is critical for reconciling rapid urbanization with low-carbon transitions, yet the spatial differentiation of transport carbon emissions (TCE) and its moderating factors remain insufficiently integrated into planning frameworks. This study examines how built environment factors influence TCE under the 5Ds framework in Guangzhou, China, using mobile phone signaling data, multi-source spatial data, and the GeoDetector model. We reveal three key findings. First, TCE exhibits a polycentric agglomeration pattern, reflecting finger-like urban expansion. Second, development intensity (FAR) is the strongest explanatory factor (q = 0.309), with the FAR–employment accessibility interaction showing the strongest synergistic effect (q = 0.323), validated as genuine nonlinear enhancement, indicating that density regulation and jobs-housing coordination must be planned jointly. Third, building height and housing price stratifications reveal monotonic gradient effects—FAR’s explanatory power increases from low-rise to high-rise areas and from low-price to high-price zones—demonstrating that uniform policies may exacerbate spatial inequities. Land surface temperature shows an inverted U-shaped moderating effect, highlighting the need for climate-adaptive planning. These findings support a differentiated, context-sensitive planning framework that integrates density…

title: VC/WC Heterogeneous Carbides Synergistically with Nitrogen-Doped Carbon Nanotubes for Enhanced Polysulfide Conversion Kinetics
abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are regarded as a promising candidate for next-generation high-energy-density storage systems due to their high theoretical energy density and the abundant availability of sulfur resources. However, practical applications are severely constrained by the shuttle effect of soluble lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) and the sluggish kinetics of Li2S deposition/decomposition. To address the challenge of simultaneously optimizing adsorption capacity and catalytic activity toward sulfur species conversion, this work proposes an interfacial electronic structure regulation strategy and constructs a composite host comprising VC/WC heterogeneous carbides and nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (W-VC@NCNTs). Through hydrothermal assembly and high-temperature carbonization, VC and WC nanocrystallites were in situ fabricated on the surface of nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes. Benefiting from the moderate downshift of the d-band center induced by electron transfer from V to W at the VC/WC heterointerface, the composite achieves effective chemical anchoring of LiPSs while avoiding product poisoning caused by excessively strong adsorption, thereby realizing an optimal balance between adsorption strength and catalytic activity. Combined with the continuous electron/ion transport pathways provided by the defect-rich nitrogen-doped carbon network, the bidirectional e…

title: Mg 2+ Doped LiFe 0.4 Mn 0.6− x Mg x PO 4 /C (X = 0, 0.01 and 0.03) with a 3D Carbon Network: Structural, Morphological, and Electrochemical Characterization for Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: In this study, LiFe 0.4 Mn 0.6 PO 4 (LFMP) and two Mg 2+ -doped materials, LiFe 0.4 Mn 0.6− x Mg x PO 4 (LFMP-0.01 Mg and LFMP-0.03 Mg), were synthesized via a solvothermal method and characterized structurally, morphologically, and electrochemically. XRD analysis confirmed their orthorhombic olivine structure (Pmnb), with a slight unit cell contraction, attributed to the partial Mg 2+ substitution at the M2 (Fe/Mn) octahedral site. SEM and HRTEM analyses revealed agglomerated nanoparticles with rectangular morphologies and a uniform amorphous carbon coating, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy ( I D / I G = 0.6). BET analysis showed a mesoporous structure with pore sizes of 1.8–1.9 nm. Electrochemical evaluations at 0.1 C revealed discharge capacities of 113 mAh g −1 for undoped LFMP, 143.4 mAh g −1 for LFMP-0.01 Mg and 125.7 mAh g −1 for LFMP-0.03 Mg. Furthermore, an additional discharge plateau at ∼3.6–3.7 V, attributed to the sluggish Mn 3+ reduction kinetics during the MnPO 4 /LiMnPO 4 phase transition, was observed. Its capacity contribution was characterized as a function of Mg 2+ doping level, and this variation is consistent with previous reports in which dopant substitution facilitates the kinetics of this redox process, suggesting an analogous effect for Mg 2+ .

title: Pathogen-specific positron emission tomography for Enterobacterales bone infection
abstract: Aims Gram-negative bone infections involving Enterobacterales group of bacteria pose a growing concern, especially for orthopaedic surgeries and diabetic ulcers. Current imaging methods either identify morphological changes by CT and MRI, or inflammation, using white blood cell scans or 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-glucose ([ 18 F]-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET). While valuable, these are not specific, resulting in delayed diagnoses. PET/CT using 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-sorbitol ([ 18 F]-FDS) is a novel method for detecting living Enterobacterales bacteria in vivo, via a conserved sorbitol-specific bacterial pathway. In this study, we aim to evaluate [ 18 F]-FDS PET/CT for detection and monitoring of Enterobacterales bone infection in a mouse model. Methods We adapted a murine model of Gram-positive implant-associated spine infection to a Gram-negative infection model. We compared microbiological techniques to imaging with [ 18 F]-FDG and [ 18 F]-FDS. We determined the standardized uptake value (SUV) ratios for detection of bacterial infection and response to therapy, in 48 mice with surgical implants infected with either Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus aureus and compared them to controls with surgical implants but no infection. Results Both bacteria induced substantial bone pathology with reduced bone density. [ 18 F]-FDS PET could specifically detect implant-assoc…

title: Society Net Benefit from a Carbon-Based Agroforestry Project: Comparing Private Forest and Social Forestry in Garut Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Carbon-based agroforestry projects are often assessed in terms of carbon sequestration and financial feasibility, with limited attention given to community net benefits after accounting for land opportunity costs. Objective: This study compares the modeled 21-year net benefits of agroforestry production at two adjacent sites comprising private forest and social forestry areas in Garut Regency, Indonesia. Methods: A bottom-up comparative case study estimates non-timber forest product income, deducting production costs, land opportunity costs, and farm tool expenditures, across 133.11 ha of private forest and 133.76 ha of social forestry. Net benefits are discounted at rates of 12% and 7%, with additional sensitivity and switching-value analyses and exploratory, expert-informed risk assessments. Project-related wages are excluded. Results: At a 12% discount rate, estimated net present benefits amount to IDR 43.77 billion (IDR 328.8 million/ha) for private forest and IDR 80.13 billion (IDR 599.1 million/ha) for social forestry. The per-hectare benefit ratio is 1.82, declining to 1.07 when avocado planting density is equalized in the model. The comparative ratio remains broadly stable under common changes in discount rates and yields. Conclusion: Avocado planting density accounts for much of the modeled benefit gap between the two sites. However, institutional explanati…

title: Urban ecological resilience and industrial structure optimization coupling coordination in the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration
abstract: The synergy of industrial transformation and ecological security is an important pair in the regional high-quality development. Previous studies of the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration have mainly examined industrial development, ecological carrying capacity, low-carbon transition, or environmental resilience separately, leaving the coordinated evolution of industrial structure optimization and urban ecological resilience insufficiently understood. This gap is particularly relevant for late-developing coastal urban agglomerations, where rapid industrial restructuring occurs alongside increasing ecological pressures. To address this issue, taking the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration as the study area, an evaluation system for industrial structure optimization and urban ecological resilience was constructed, and the coupling coordination between the two systems was examined from 2012 to 2022. The contribution of this study lies in integrating industrial structure optimization (ISO) and urban ecological resilience (UER) within a unified analytical framework and simultaneously examining their temporal evolution, spatial differentiation, subsystem-lagging characteristics, and interacting driving factors. The findings extend the empirical understanding of industrial–ecological coordination in late-developing coastal urban agglomerations and provide a quantitative basis for differentiated…

title: Synthesis of Quaternary Stereocenters via Asymmetric Cross-Coupling of Arylboronic Acids and Racemic Electrophiles
abstract: Abstract Quaternary stereocenters feature in many natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their synthesis is often difficult. We report an enantioconvergent Suzuki–Miyaura-type cross coupling between arylboronic acids and racemic tertiary electrophiles to give products containing quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic studies suggest that the very high levels of enantiomeric excess observed are due to a Rh-catalyzed dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation.

title: Multiscale design of an organosulfur cathode with superior cycling stability in ether electrolytes under practical conditions via selenium codoping
abstract: Abstract The sulfurized polyacrylonitrile (SPAN) cathode, in which sulfur atoms are covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix, offers a promising strategy for avoiding the dissolution–precipitation mechanism of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) in traditional Li–S batteries. However, the solid–solid conversion mechanism in SPAN cathodes is electrolyte-dependent, and the dissolution behavior of covalently bonded sulfur remains poorly understood. Elucidating this mechanism is important for understanding the sulfur reduction reaction (SRR) pathway in SPAN cathodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the LiPSs still dissolve from the SPAN matrix in ether-based electrolytes, which may promote SRR kinetics. We further show that the sulfur–PAN bonds at the cathode–electrolyte interfaces are vulnerable to being attacked by ether molecules. To address this issue, we introduce a selenization strategy to reinforce the bonding between sulfur species and the PAN matrix. The as-fabricated cathode enables rapid and stable lithium storage, achieving 77% of capacity retention over 200 cycles under practical conditions, including high mass loading of ~7 mg cm−2, low electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of ~2.9 μL mg−1, and a limited negative-to-positive electrode capacity ratio of 1.5. This multiscale design strategy provides a promising approach for fabricating stable organosulfur cathodes for next-ge…

title: Process parameter interactions and volumetric energy density Non-Uniqueness in LPBF-Processed CuCrZr alloy: Effects on defect evolution and densification
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the densification behavior and defect evolution of CuCrZr alloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), with emphasis on the effects of laser power (LP), scanning speed (SS), hatch distance (HD) and powder bed layer thickness (PBLT) on density, microstructure, defects and mechanical performance. The suitability of volumetric energy density (VED) for predicting densification and defect formation is also evaluated. Design/methodology/approach A statistically validated experimental framework based on a modified Taguchi method was used to optimize the LPBF process parameters. Eighty-one CuCrZr specimens were fabricated under different processing conditions. Density measurements, optical and scanning electron microscopy, defect characterization and mechanical testing were performed to establish process-structure-property relationships and evaluate the effects of post-heat treatment. Findings The optimized parameters of LP = 370 W, SS = 610 mm/s, HD = 0.10 mm and PBLT = 30 µm produced relative density above 99.6% with minimal defects. Lack-of-fusion defects, gas porosity and interlayer cracking were strongly influenced by melting pool behavior and process parameter interactions. Microstructural analysis revealed a transition from fine equiaxed grains to elongated columnar grains along the build direction. Direct aging produced the highest …

title: Digital Twins for Biofuel Integration and Optimization in Internal Combustion Engines: A Critical Review and Research Roadmap
abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly proposed as a bridge between high-fidelity engine physics, real-time sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), and closed-loop optimization, yet their role in biofuel-powered internal combustion engines (ICEs) remains fragmented. This critical review evaluates how condition monitoring, AI-based diagnostics, fast-running engine models, and DT implementations can be integrated into a fuel-aware framework for biofuel ICEs. A structured search of original research was conducted across major publisher databases and scholarly discovery services, including ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, Wiley/IET, SAE Mobilus, RSC Publishing and MDPI, with the search updated to 19 August 2026. Review-only papers were excluded from the evidential corpus; the synthesis therefore relies on primary experimental, computational, or validated digital-twin studies. Three contributions distinguish this review. First, a five-layer taxonomy is proposed that separates sensing, state estimation, twin-model fidelity, intelligence, and actuation, allowing DT maturity to be compared independently of terminology. Second, conventional-fuel and biofuel deployments are compared through a fuel-to-fault pathway linking viscosity, volatility, oxygen content, ignition quality, oxidation stability and material compatibility to measurable signatures, degradations and control actions. Third, a…
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)

title: FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT OF A VORTEX TUBE FOR EXHAUST AIR ENERGY RECOVERY IN A PNEUMATIC CYLINDER
abstract: This article discusses an approach to improving the energy efficiency of pneumatic actuators by recovering energy from exhaust air using a vortex tube based on the Rank-Hirsch effect. Based on a review of the literature, the selection of the pipe’s geometric parameters is justified, and a three-dimensional CAD model of the pipe is constructed, adapted to the conditions of supply from the exhaust line of a pneumatic cylinder. The methodology includes numerical simulation of the airflow in ANSYS CFX under steady-state boundary conditions corresponding to the characteristic parameters of the exhaust flow. The results confirm the formation of a cold axial core and a hot peripheral flow zone, with maxima of static entropy and turbulent kinetic energy localized immediately behind the nozzle rim. The obtained data indicate the fundamental possibility of using the cold flow for localized cooling of components in technological systems without the use of additional energy.

title: Energy-band alignment of stacked single-crystalline Si/ α -Ga 2 O 3 p–n heterojunctions
abstract: Abstract A stacked single-crystalline Si/ α -Ga 2 O 3 p–n heterojunction was formed by transferring a 100 nm p-Si nanomembrane onto an α -Ga 2 O 3 epiwafer. The α -Ga 2 O 3 layer exhibited a (110) x-ray diffraction reflection, and the epi-layer at the Si/ α -Ga 2 O 3 interface had a valence-band maximum located 4.29 ± 0.10 eV below the Fermi-level. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling revealed decreases of 0.11 eV in the Si 2p binding energy and 0.35 eV in the Ga 3d binding energy from the bulk-like regions to the interface, consistent with upward band bending on both sides at the junction interface. Applying the Kraut method with the valence-band offset defined as E V (Si) − E V ( α -Ga 2 O 3 ) gave 3.93 eV; the corresponding conduction-band offset was 0.25 eV. The enhanced Si–O and Ga–O components indicate an ultrathin oxide-containing bonding region formed during heterojunction integration. Rather than being treated as a thick parasitic oxide, this region is interpreted as a thin passivating interlayer that does not preclude reliable extraction of the effective band alignment of the as-fabricated junction. Energy band profiles in equilibrium and under forward and reverse bias were calculated using technology-computer-aided design. The fabricated p–n heterojunction diode exhibited rectifying current density–voltage characteristics with an ideality factor of 1.47. …

title: Free Energy Landscape Perturbation for Estimating Mutation-Induced Population Shifts from Reference Molecular Dynamics Ensembles
abstract: Abstract Mutations can alter protein function by redistributing probability among conformational states, even when structural changes are modest. Directly estimating a perturbed conformational free energy landscape with molecular dynamics is expensive because each mutation requires a new converged simulation. Here, we introduce Free Energy Landscape Perturbation (FELP), a state-local reweighting framework that estimates mutation-induced population shifts from a reference ensemble. FELP partitions a reference trajectory into discrete microstates, evaluates restrained reference-to-perturbed energy differences for configurations sampled within each state, and combines spatially regularized state-local Zwanzig factors with the reference state probabilities to estimate the perturbed state distribution. FELP estimates how a perturbation changes the relative probabilities of conformational basins and reports effective-sample and overlap diagnostics that identify when the predicted shift lacks support in the sampled reference ensemble. We describe the FELP estimator, its implementation, and its performance on capped dipeptides, chignolin, T4 lysozyme, and the EGFR kinase domain. FELP is intended for perturbations that reshape populations within a sufficiently sampled reference landscape, providing a practical bridge between local alchemical energy evaluation and ensemble-level mechanis…
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Strategic assessment of hydropower resilience under climate change: an integrated SWOT-PESTEL perspective within the water–energy nexus
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydropower is central to renewable-energy transitions and to the Water–Energy Nexus (WEN), but its resilience is increasingly shaped by hydrological variability, competing water demands, aging infrastructure, and changing governance conditions. This study develops an evidence-weighted framework that integrates SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) with PESTEL (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal) analysis. Twenty-two publicly available institutional reports were examined through 33 structured questions, producing 726 source-question evaluations. Documentary evidence was synthesized into retained SWOT factors and weighted according to source coverage, evidence density, geographic breadth, and recency before being mapped to PESTEL dimensions. Intersectoral water-use conflict and competition, climate change and extreme weather, renewable-energy integration, and adaptive reservoir management emerged as the most strongly supported strategic factors. Technological conditions most strongly reinforced the strengths of hydropower, whereas social, environmental, political, and economic pressures dominated weaknesses and threats. Alternative weighting scenarios produced highly stable rankings (Spearman's rho = 0.976–0.995). The framework provides a transparent and transferable basis for identifying strategic priorities, while it…

title: تقييم الأداء الفيزيائي والاقتصادي للطاقة الشمسية في مزارع الجفرة منطقة ودان دراسة استطلاعية ميدانية
abstract: الخلايا الشمسية أو الكهروضوئية هي أجهزة تعمل على تحويل أشعة الشمس إلى طاقة كهربائية من خلال استغلال التأثير الكهروضوئي، حيث تتكون من مجموعة من الخلايا المرتبطة مع بعضها البعض لتكوين ألواح قادرة على إنتاج الطاقة، وقد شهدت هذه التقنية تطوراً كبيراً خلال العقود الماضية، وتعد من أهم مصادر الطاقة المتجددة في العالم. [13]يهدف هذا البحث إلى دراسة إمكانية استخدام الطاقة الشمسية في تشغيل مضخات المياه في مزارع التمور بمدينة ودان بمنطقة الجفرة، نظراً لما تتمتع به المنطقة من وفرة في الإشعاع الشمسي، إضافة إلى التحديات التي تواجه مصادر الطاقة التقليدية مثل ارتفاع تكاليف الوقود وعدم استقرار التيار الكهربائي. يتناول البحث الجوانب النظرية المتعلقة بعمل الخلايا الشمسية، والعوامل المؤثرة على كفاءتها مثل درجة الحرارة وتراكم الغبار، كما يتطرق إلى تطبيقاتها في المجال الزراعي، خاصة في أنظمة ضخ المياه. ومن الجانب العملي، تم حساب القدرة اللازمة لتشغيل المضخة وتصميم نظام شمسي متكامل يتناسب مع ظروف المنطقة. وقد أظهرت النتائج أن استخدام الطاقة الشمسية في مزارع التمور يعد خياراً فعالاً ومستداماً، حيث يساهم في تقليل التكاليف التشغيلية وتحسين كفاءة الري، إضافة إلى الحد من التأثيرات البيئية الناتجة عن استخدام مصادر الطاقة التقليدية. (استُقبلت يوم/شهر/سنة، روُجعت يوم/شهر/سنة، قُبلت يوم/شهر/سنة )

title: A physics-informed neural network approach for surrogate modeling for PWRs LOOP events
abstract: Accurate and rapid predictions of reactor transients such as Loss of Offsite Power (LOOP) events in Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) is critical for reactor safety assessment. Traditional highly benchmarked codes are computationally expensive, prohibiting their direct use in fast safety assessments. To address these challenges, this study investigates the potential of physics learning based surrogate models. We developed and compared data-driven and physics-informed surrogate models for predicting transient thermal-hydraulics in a triple-loop PWR under the LOOP conditions, focusing on the evolution of primary system pressure, fuel temperature and coolant temperature. Four data-driven Deep Neural Network (DNN) architectures and three Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) variants were trained using data sets covering 36 transient scenarios. Each scenario was varied with initial reactor condition, system configuration and boundary constraints. The results show that the improved Multi-Layer Perceptron (best data driven model) achieved an R 2 of 0.7015 for primary coolant temperature ( T c ), 0.6701 for fuel temperature ( T f ) and 0.8364 for primary system pressure ( P p ) on held-out test scenarios. The Shared-encoder Multi-Head PINN improved R 2 to 0.7449 for T c , 0.6987 for T f and 0.8519 for P p . The PINN also demonstrated improved robustness to sensor measurement uncert…

title: Integrating Space Syntax and User Movement Observation to Identify Potential Human Activity Energy Harvesting Zones in Campus Buildings
abstract: Energy consumption in campus buildings continues to increase with the intensity of building use and user activities, while research on human activity-based energy harvesting remains predominantly focused on energy conversion technologies, with limited attention to the relationship between spatial configuration and the distribution and concentration of user movement. To address this gap, this study integrated Space Syntax analysis and field observation to identify candidate circulation zones for future human activity-based energy harvesting applications.in the HC-A Building of Soegijapranata Catholic University Semarang. The spatial configuration analysis was carried out using DepthmapX through Visibility Graph Analysis (VGA), with Connectivity and Visual Integration analysed independently. Connectivity was used to determine preliminary candidate circulation areas based on the internal spatial configuration, while field observation was used to identify the distribution of actual user movement, particularly at main access points influenced by external movement sources. The Connectivity-based analysis identified 631 m² (67.85%) of the total analysed circulation area as preliminary candidate areas. Afterintegration with field observations, the final candidate area increased to 661 m² (71.08%), representing an additional30 m² or 3.23 percentage points primarily around the main acces…

title: Quantifying the integration impact of Lean and Industry 4.0 on operational efficiency: insights from an experimental case study
abstract: Purpose This study aims to quantify the interaction effects between a Lean tool (Poka-Yoke) and an Industry 4.0 (I-4.0) technology (a machine vision camera) on operational performance, as measured by Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE). Design/methodology/approach A controlled laboratory-based experiment was conducted using a within-subject design with four treatment conditions: Control (paper-based instructions), Lean (Poka-Yoke), I-4.0 (machine vision inspection) and Lean 4.0 (a combination of Lean and digital inspection). Participants completed standardized assembly tasks under each condition. Operational performance was evaluated using OEE, decomposed into performance and quality components. Statistical analyses, including repeated-measures ANOVA and post hoc tests, were applied to examine significant differences among treatments and to assess the individual and combined effects of Lean and I-4.0 interventions. Findings The results demonstrate that the treatment, I-4.0, significantly improves OEE (p < 0.05), indicating an immediate operational benefit. In contrast, the Lean and Lean 4.0 treatments did not yield statistically significant improvements in OEE. These findings suggest that while digital technologies can independently enhance operational performance, the anticipated synergistic benefits of integrating Lean and I-4.0 may not materialize without careful alignm…
venue: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma

title: Integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools into the Design of Learning Activities in Higher Education
abstract: This research paper examines the impact and effectiveness of integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools into the design of learning activities in higher education. Utilizing a mixed-method approach with a sequential explanatory design, the study explored how these technologies transform teaching practices and the overall student experience. The quantitative phase, conducted with a sample of 50 students and 12 professors in Mexico, revealed an outstanding perception of utility (88% acceptance), highlighting significant improvements in instructional design efficiency and the ability to personalize educational content. The qualitative phase, consisting of in-depth interviews with 6 key informants, identified that while GAI optimizes response times and diversifies teaching resources, its implementation faces critical challenges such as data "hallucination," the risk of technological dependence, and the constant need for human pedagogical validation. The findings suggest that GAI functions not merely as a technical assistant but as a catalyst for educational innovation, provided its use is aligned with clear curricular objectives and an ethical framework that preserves critical thinking. The study concludes that faculty training in advanced digital competencies is imperative to transition from an instrumental use of AI toward a purposeful didactic integration.

title: IMPROVEMENT THE GLOBAL ENERGY EFFICIENCY OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS OF TECHNOLOGICAL EQUIPMENT
abstract: This paper investigates multi-scale power losses and global energy-efficiency optimization in process machinery hydraulic systems. Power-loss mechanisms are analyzed at three levels: micro (components), meso (circuits), and macro (system), and a quantitative model accounting for their interactions is developed. A global energy-efficiency model is established, and a collaborative control strategy based on an improved adaptive genetic algorithm (IAGA) is proposed to optimize energy consumption and dynamic performance. Simulation and experimental results confirm that hydraulic pump volumetric losses, control valve throttling losses, and circuit coupling losses account for over 75% of total power losses. The proposed strategy improves system energy efficiency by 12%–18% and reduces dynamic response overshoot by more than 60%. The results provide a theoretical and practical basis for energy-efficient hydraulic system design and control.

title: ESG Disclosure, Profitability, Current Ratio, and Company Value in Indonesian Energy Companies
abstract: Background: The growing importance of sustainable finance has widened the information set used in corporate valuation. This is particularly relevant for Indonesian energy firms, whose market performance is shaped by a combination of environmental exposure, capital intensity, and near-term financial capacity. Objective: This study assesses whether ESG disclosure, profitability, and liquidity are statistically associated with firm value among energy-sector issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2023–2025. Methods: A panel-data design was applied to 90 firm-year observations from 30 energy companies selected purposively from 91 listed firms. The analysis used annual financial statements and sustainability reports. ESG disclosure was scored against the GRI Standards 2021, profitability was measured by Return on Assets (ROA), liquidity by the Current Ratio (CR), and firm value by Price to Book Value (PBV). Panel estimation was performed in EViews 12, with specification testing indicating the use of company fixed effects. Results: In the fixed-effects regression, ESG disclosure was positively associated with PBV (coefficient = 3.379502; p = 0.0158). ROA also showed a positive association (coefficient = 0.019785; p = 0.0049), as did CR (coefficient = 0.265845; p < 0.001). The model was significant overall and produced an adjusted R² of 0.804446. Conclusion: The evidence from t…
venue: Journal of Business, Social and Technology

title: Valorization of Cannabis sativa Residual Biomass from Industrial CBD Extraction as a Renewable Support for Candida antarctica Lipase B Immobilization and Fatty Acid Esterification
abstract: Abstract Residual Cannabis sativa biomass from industrial CBD extraction in ethanol was evaluated as a renewable support for the immobilization of Candida antarctica lipase B (CALB) by physical adsorption, and the resulting biocatalysts were applied to the esterification of long-chain fatty acids with ethanol. Because extractives released by the untreated biomass interfered with protein quantification, three simple pretreatments were compared. Milling alone, with or without buffer washing, gave reproducible immobilization and active, reusable biocatalysts, whereas SDS washing increased protein retention but led to nearly inactive preparations, indicating that protein loading alone does not predict catalytic performance. The milling-only biocatalyst converted two industrial palm fatty acid distillate fractions with conversions comparable to those of Novozym 435, retained more than 80% of its initial conversion after five cycles, and was operated in a continuous-flow packed-bed reactor with conversions of 95% or higher at a residence time of 15 min. These results indicate that this residue is a low-cost, minimally processed support for lipase-catalyzed esterification.
authors: Rodrigo O. M. A. de Souza

title: Optimal bus load grouping method based on source–load-constrained multi-view clustering and TS2Vec-TabM
abstract: Conventional bus classification relies heavily on expert judgment and a single view of load-curve shape, making it difficult to account for source-load attributes and operating mechanisms. This paper proposes an optimal bus load grouping method that combines source-load-constrained multi-view clustering with TS2Vec-TabM. Annual 15-min bus load curves are first normalized by capacity and reconstructed at multiple temporal scales to derive typical-day and seasonal curves, statistics, and customer-composition features. TS2Vec then extracts self-supervised temporal representations from the seasonal curves. These representations are combined with engineered statistics and source-load attributes to form a multi-view feature space. Physical anchors are constructed from renewable-energy penetration, the capacity share of impulsive loads, and the number of impulsive events. Must-link and cannot-link constraints are incorporated into the multi-view distance to cluster buses into conventional, renewable-integrated, and impulsive-load groups. Finally, the parameter-efficient ensemble model TabM performs three-class classification and outputs class probabilities and confidence scores. Experiments on real bus data show that the proposed clustering method achieves an adjusted Rand index of 0.965, normalized mutual information of 0.936, and clustering accuracy of 0.974. In the classification s…

title: Effectiveness of activation energy on Casson nanofluid flow between two exothermic chemically reactive orthogonally moving disks
abstract: Abstract The objective of this study is to address the time-dependent movement of thermally radiative Casson nanofluid between two orthogonally moving disks. The Buongiorno nanofluid model is used to address the critical nanoparticle transport mechanisms, specifically Brownian movement and thermophoretic, which play a major contribution in affecting heat and solutal transfer properties. The modeled equations are transformed into a framework of non-linear ordinary differential equations by employing suitable similarity transformations and then solved using the bvp4c solver. The key outcomes reflected that an increment in the thermophoresis factor improves the fluid temperature but reduces the Nusselt number. A higher Brownian motion boosts both the nanoparticle concentration and Sherwood number. A greater activation energy leads to a temperature drop but an increase in concentration, whereas a higher reaction rate diminishes the concentration. When the thermophoresis parameter values ranged from 0 to 2, the heat transfer rate dropped by 31.87 %. The mass transfer rate reduced by 16.03 % when the activation energy constraint values are between 0 and 3. The numerical results are validated using a Bayesian neural network, which showed good agreement with the bvp4c solutions, with a mean squared error on the order of 10 −9 .

AI-assisted design exploration for post-disaster housing: reassessing Bam reconstruction
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is reassessing Bam reconstruction after earthquake using Artificial Intelligence. Post-disaster permanent housing plays a critical role in ensuring the long-term recovery and well-being of affected communities. However, architectural design processes in disaster responses are often rushed, leading to solutions that may overlook cultural, environmental and functional needs. Design/methodology/approach This study examines the potential role of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving post-disaster housing design by reassessing the reconstruction that followed the 2003 Bam earthquake in Iran. Using a process-oriented perspective, existing post-disaster permanent houses were evaluated against AI-generated architectural alternatives produced through Midjourney. Findings Key indicators and evaluation criteria were identified through a literature review and supported by field surveys conducted in Bam. An evaluation flowchart was then developed to systematically assess design performance in terms of safety, sustainability, cultural compatibility, functionality, accessibility and affordability. Practical implications The findings suggest that generative AI can support architects and planners by rapidly generating diverse design alternatives and expanding the range of solutions considered during the early stages of post-disaster reconstruction. However,…

title: Computational workflow integrating differential growth and robotic WAAM for fabrication-aware architectural design: a furniture-scale demonstrator
abstract: Purpose This study develops a fabrication-aware computational workflow for architectural applications using Wire-and-Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM). It addresses the gap in methods that integrate computational geometry with fabrication constraints, aiming to produce geometries that are both generative and manufacturable. The research formalizes a parameter-driven design-to-fabrication framework bridging computational modeling and robotic metal deposition, providing a transferable methodology that can inform applications beyond prototype-scale fabrication while preserving architectural design intent. Design/methodology/approach A computational workflow using differential growth principles in Grasshopper generates iterative geometries evaluated against fabrication criteria such as deposition stability, curvature continuity and robotic feasibility. Contour segmentation and toolpath simulation are incorporated as active design considerations rather than post-design checks. Designs are iteratively filtered and prepared for WAAM fabrication. The workflow is demonstrated through the production of an aluminum prototype, illustrating the translation of computational models into robotic metal deposition while embedding manufacturing constraints within the design-to-fabrication process. Findings The workflow integrates fabrication constraints within computational geometry generation, p…

title: Reframing L2 Pragmatic Competence in the Generative AI Era: A Co-Design-Oriented Critical Curriculum
abstract: The rapid incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into second-language (L2) education has reopened a foundational question in language pedagogy: what should count as successful communication when English is routinely used among speakers who do not share a native-speaker norm? Much L2 pragmatic instruction continues to treat pragmatics as the acquisition of socially appropriate forms modelled on idealised native-speaker practices. This conceptual review article proposes a co-design-oriented critical pragmatic curriculum that positions GAI (implemented primarily through large language models, or LLMs) not as an infallible tutor but as a contestable intercultural interlocutor. Drawing on English as a Lingua Franca (ELF), World Englishes, translanguaging, critical pragmatics, critical digital literacy, and design-based research (DBR), the paper advances a unified pedagogical architecture comprising three modules: Persona Engineering and Dialectic Diversity, Real-Time Meaning Negotiation, and Deconstructing Algorithmic Bias, each enacted through a four-stage learning episode (persona engineering → GAI interaction → critical negotiation → reflection and transfer) and organised within an iterative co-design cycle. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded model for integrating GAI with intercultural and critical language pedagogy while retaining teacher mediatio…

title: HIV/AIDS patients with low-level viremia in different states have variable risks of subsequent viral suppression failure: a large retrospective study in Chongqing
abstract: Objective To analyze the basic characteristics and influencing factors of low-level viremia (LLV) among treated HIV/AIDS patients in Chongqing and to examine the association between low-level viremia and virological failure. Methods Data from AIDS patients who were diagnosed and treated at the Chongqing Public Health Medical Treatment Center were collected. The incidence rates of LLV and virological failure (VF) were statistically analyzed. Univariate and logistic regression analyses were performed to analyze the risk factors of LLV in HIV-infected individuals, and the correlation between low-level viremia and viral suppression failure was analyzed. Results From 2013 to 2022, a total of 7,685 HIV/AIDS patients were diagnosed and administered standardized antiretroviral therapy, with follow-up, at our center. The numbers (percentages) of patients experiencing virologic suppression (VS), single low-level viremia (sLLV), viral blip (Blip), and persistent low-level viremia (pLLV) were 6,265 (81.5%), 897 (11.8%), 95 (1.2%), and 211 (2.7%), respectively. Direct virological failure (VF) occurred in 217 (2.8%) cases. Univariate analysis revealed that marital status, route of infection, age, WHO stage, baseline CD4 + T lymphocyte count (CD4), baseline HIV viral load, and initial core drug selection were associated with the occurrence of LLV. Logistic regression analysis suggested that o…

title: National goals, local gears: why institutional design and architecture, not mission statements, drive development finance
abstract: Purpose Public development banks (PDBs) have re-emerged as pivotal instruments for industrial policy, green transition and regional rebalancing. Yet the effectiveness of PDBs depends not only on mandates and resources but on the local banking architecture: how credit is originated, priced, monitored and transmitted to place. This is the purpose of this study. Design/methodology/approach This paper compares two centralised PDBs – the Bulgarian Development Bank and the British Business Bank – with Germany’s dense, decentralised savings and cooperative banking pillars (Sparkassen and Volksbanken–Raiffeisenbanken) supported by Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau. This paper shows that Bulgaria and the UK confront a scale-and-proximity constraint: small, national balance sheets delivering primarily via programs and intermediaries versus large, locally embedded networks practicing relationship lending in Germany. Findings “Like-for-like” comparisons to single German local banks underscore the point: individual cooperative or savings banks can match or exceed the balance-sheet size of national PDBs while serving compact regions. The analysis implies that market-shaping outcomes require decentralised, spatially rich banking architecture. Research limitations/implications The study assesses institutional capacity and credit-transmission architecture rather than realised borrower- or regional…

title: Design, Modeling, and Experimental Validation of a Novel Flexible-Joint Robotic Manipulator using Adaptive Sliding Mode Control
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, nonlinear dynamic formulation, simulation, and experimental comparison of a robotic manipulator incorporating a four-spring flexible coupling. The platform is described as a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) arm, and the supplied model distinguishes a motor-side coordinate from three load-side coordinates. Conventional sliding-mode control (SMC) and adaptive sliding-mode control (ASMC) are implemented through a LabVIEW real-time environment and a National Instruments myRIO controller. Reported tests consider no added payload, a 1000 g payload, and an external disturbance at reference angles of 45∘ and 135∘. The supplied simulation and experimental summaries are compared using position-error percentages, settling time, and maximum load torque. Across six matched experimental cases, ASMC reduces the reported position-error indicator by 40.4–50.0%, maximum load torque by 11.8–35.4%, and settling time by 4.6–6.3% relative to SMC. These reductions are calculated from the supplied table values and vary with operating condition and reference angle. The author-reported responses indicate recovery following the applied disturbances and less oscillatory behavior with ASMC. However, the available summaries do not quantify complete chattering suppression, statistical variability, or total actuator energy consumption. The adaptive implementation als…

title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation
abstract: Abstract Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscape analyses and density functional theory (DFT). The membrane simulations preserved the global hSGLT2 fold while revealing distinct ligand-dependent binding behaviours. Myricetin and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside exhibited limited positional deviations; hyperoside achieved persistent accommodation following an initial adjustment, whereas isoliquiritigenin underwent a marked late rearrangement. Ensemble-based energetic analysis prioritized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, while hyperoside and myricetin formed an energetically comparable intermediate group and isoliquiritigenin displayed the least favourable profile. Electronic-structure analysis further characterized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside as the most responsive ligand within the DFT subset. Collectively, these findings indicate that glycone-assist…

STRUCTURAL DESIGN AND LAYOUT OF A COOKING VEHICLE MODIFIED FROM HEAVY-DUTY TRUCK CHASSIS
abstract: To meet the needs of centralized meal preparation for multiple personnel in scenarios such as field emergencies, military garrison training, engineering construction, and large-scale events, this paper introduces the structural design of a cooking vehicle modified from a heavy-duty cargo vehicle chassis. Based on a SITRAK heavy-duty cargo vehicle second-type chassis with a maximum total mass of 16 t, the vehicle was modified through alterations to the body structure, interior decoration, water supply and drainage systems, and power supply system to meet the functional requirements of a mobile kitchen. The interior of the vehicle body is divided into three functional zones: water supply and purification area, cooking and processing area, and storage and preservation area. These areas are sequentially equipped with water pump and water purifier systems, water heaters, clean water tanks, rice steamers, meat mincers and vegetable cutters, workbenches, sinks, freezers, storage cabinets, double-burner stoves, spice boxes and cooking oil, and other equipment. External facilities include side pull-out ladders, rear pull-out ladders, wastewater tank, cable reel, support leg controls, gasoline generator, inverter and battery, support legs, city power input, rear single door, roof side lighting, and side roof access ladder. The vehicle adopts a multi-power supply system prioritizing city …

title: Reply to: multisensory virtual reality reduces postoperative delirium in elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery
First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
abstract: Abstract The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. We trace isotopically tagged greens in lemurs, from ingestion to excretion, through isotopic analysis of higher plant biomarkers recovered in faeces. For frugivorous ruffed lemurs (Varecia rubra), omnivorous ring-tailed lemurs (Lemur catta) and frugo-folivorous sifakas (Propithecus coquereli), respectively, the biomarkers first appeared at 1.2, 4.3 and 23.4 h after ingestion and peaked at 2.9, 5.7 and 48.4 h after ingestion. These measurements generally match published estimates from pre-existing proxies. However, not all animals cleared the isotopic signal by the end of sample collection, yielding minimum gut retention times of 23.9–29.5 h for ruffed lemurs, 25.5–30.3 h for ring-tailed lemurs and 95.7 h for sifakas. We thus extend gut retention times approximately threefold from pre-existing proxies. Our interdisciplinary approach is applicable across diverse plant eaters, can help refine models of nutrient, seed and pathogen dispersal and be used to probe consequences of lifestyle and…

title: Polypropylene microplastics modify copper associated leaf injury and photosynthetic responses in Nymphaea ‘Black Beauty’
abstract: Introduction Microplastics and heavy metals cooccur in freshwater habitats, yet it remains unclear whether microplastics intensify metal toxicity or redirect the dominant mode of plant injury. Methods We exposed the floatingleaved aquatic plant Nymphaea `Black Beauty' for 28 d to control conditions, copper (Cu) alone, polypropylene microplastics (PPMPs) alone, or combined Cu and PPMP stress. Wholeplant phenotype, relative growth rate, leaf chlorosis and necrosis, root scanning electron microscopy, gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, malondialdehyde (MDA), and antioxidant enzymes were integrated to distinguish structural damage from functional inhibition. Results Cu alone produced a necrosisdominated response: relative growth rate decreased by approximately 65%, net photosynthetic rate (Pn) by 54%, effective PSII quantum yield (ΦPSII) by 52%, and electron transport rate (ETR) by 47%, whereas MDA increased by 58% and necrotic area reached 26.4%. PPMPs alone caused moderate growth inhibition and chlorosis, with a numerically higher nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) mean and little lipid peroxidation. Factorial analysis detected Cu × PP interactions for selected endpoints, including growth, necrosis, Pn, NPQ, ETR, and POD; these endpointwise tests were exploratory. Necrotic area declined to 2.1%, but growth and photosynthesis remained strongly inhibited. The density of morpholog…

title: Platform governance and digital property rights in virtual real estate: volatility, user entitlements and regulatory accountability
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how platform governance shapes the content and durability of user entitlements in virtual real estate. It defines virtual real estate narrowly as spatially delimited, platform-mediated parcels in persistent virtual worlds, whether recorded in a proprietary database or linked to a blockchain token. This study asks how access, exclusion, transfer, persistence and redress are distributed among users and platform operators and how uncertainty in those entitlements can contribute to market fragility and regulatory risk. Design/methodology/approach This study combines a targeted interdisciplinary review with comparative legal analysis of disputes and legal developments directly relevant to virtual land and digital property. Bragg v Linden Research and Evans v Linden Research are treated as core virtual-land cases; AA v Persons Unknown, Ruscoe v Cryptopia and the Property (Digital Assets etc) Act 2025 are used as broader digital-property comparators. Platform materials and descriptive post-boom market indicators are used for context. This study does not claim a causal econometric estimate of governance effects on prices. Findings Virtual real estate is governed through layered entitlements rather than a single ownership rule. Technical control, platform contract terms and external legal remedies may diverge, and transfers can occur through platform d…
venue: Journal of Information, Communication and Ethics in Society

title: Taiwan’s Port of Lies
abstract: Abstract Taiwan’s de facto official language in spoken form is Mandarin Chinese, but it is far from the mother tongue of the many who live and work on the island. Port of Lies (2023), an award-winning show adapted from a novel, deconstructs the transparency of Mandarin Chinese as a unifying national tongue by foregrounding Taiwan’s “Chinese” complex and the sociolinguistic hierarchies (Mandarin, Taiwanese, Indigenous languages, migrant worker languages) that have structured its democracy and rule of law since the government of the Republic of China retreated to Taiwan in 1949. This paper treats the show’s fictional adaptation of a historical event — the 1986 murder of a Han employer by his employee of Tsou Indigenous descent — as a discursive means to resist Han-centric narratives on victimhood, empowerment, ethnic, gender, and class relations in contemporary Taiwan. Selected scenes where the dialogue and positions between the characters are culturally charged serve as sites to analyze how identities are negotiated and resist being defined. In particular, the female Indonesian migrant interpreter and the male Amis public defender are the parallel protagonist agents who problematize the larger theme of “justice for whom” in contemporary societies where the need for the dominating culture (the host country) to re-negotiate its relationship with the dominated other (the im/migrant…

title: Perturbation-level predictions of power-law f(Q) gravity from simulation-based inference
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of power-law symmetric teleparallel gravity, [Formula: see text], combining simulation-based parameter inference with perturbation-level predictions and multi-messenger forecasts.
