The sign of the best-fit n depends on the dataset combination, reflecting a residual [Formula: see text]–n degeneracy that only multi-probe analyses can break. From the constrained posterior, we derive four perturbation-level predictions without re…

title: Toxicity Activity of Five Plant Extracts against Tetranychus truncatus (Acari: Tetranychidae) and Its Predatory Mite Amblyseius longispinosus (Acari: Phytoseiidae)
abstract: Tetranychus truncatus Ehara (Acari: Tetranychidae) is one of the major economically important mite pests of numerous plant species. The predatory mite Amblyseius longispinosus (Evans) (Acari: Phytoseiidae) has been successfully used in biological control programs. This study evaluated the contact toxicity activities of ethanol extracts from 5 plants—Cymbopogon nardus (L.) Rendle, Ocimum basilicum L., Ocimum sanctum L., Andrographis paniculata (Burm.f.) Nees, and Stemona tuberosa Lour.—against T. truncatus and A. longispinosus. The ethanol plant extracts revealed different toxicity activity against T. truncatus and A. longispinosus. At concentrations of 7–9% (w/v), Cy. nardus and S. tuberosa extracts showed significant direct contact toxicity against T. truncatus adults, resulting in mortality rates of 64.00–70.67 and 51.33–55.00%, respectively, at 3 d after treatment. Application of 3–9% concentrations of Cy. nardus, 5–9% concentrations of O. basilicum and O. sanctum, and 9% concentrations of A. paniculata to T. truncatus eggs reduced egg viability, with >50% unhatched eggs 4 d following treatment. Concentrations of 5–9% of Cy. nardus and O. sanctum extracts were moderately toxic to A. longispinosus in residual contact toxicity, with mortality ranging from 22.67–34.67 and 22.67–29.33%, respectively, at 3 d after exposure. Based on our findings, extracts of Cy. nardus and T. tub…

title: Perceived autonomy support and exercise persistence intention among university students in app-supported campus running: positive–negative dual-path mechanisms and the boundary roles of individual and peer resources
abstract: Objective In some Chinese universities, campus running is an institutionally organized extracurricular program in which prescribed running tasks are monitored through exercise apps. This study examined the association between perceived autonomy support (PAS) and exercise persistence intention (EPI), testing a positive pathway through basic psychological need satisfaction (BPNS), exercise empowerment (EE), and exercise identity (EI), a negative pathway through perceived threat to freedom (PTF), psychological reactance (PR), and exercise procrastination (EP), and the moderating roles of exercise self-efficacy (ESE) and peer exercise climate (PEC). Methods A questionnaire survey yielded 1,636 valid responses from full-time students at universities operating app-supported campus running programs in Shandong, Hubei, and Liaoning, China. All participants had participated in these programs during the most recent semester. SPSS 31.0 and Amos 31.0 were used for descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, common method bias testing, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples tested direct, sequential indirect, and moderating effects, and PROCESS Model 1 was used for simple slope analyses. Results PAS was significantly and positively associated with university students’ EPI (effect = 0.308, SE = 0.047, 95% CI [0.2163, 0.3986]). BPN…

title: Interfacial Triplet-Energy Funneling Directs Energy-Transfer-Mediated Singlet Oxygen Generation for Deep Toluene Mineralization
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidation is a promising strategy for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement, but incomplete mineralization and carbonaceous intermediate accumulation remain major challenges, especially when conventional charge-transfer pathways generate nonselective radical reactive oxygen species. Selective activation of molecular oxygen toward singlet oxygen (1O2) offers a potential route to controlled oxidation, yet efficient energy-transfer-mediated 1O2 generation in solid-state photocatalysts remains difficult to achieve. Herein, a strongly coupled In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 heterojunction with an electronic structure consistent with an S-scheme configuration is constructed to investigate interfacial excited-state regulation. Spectroscopic measurements indicate modified excited-state relaxation and a reduced effective singlet–triplet energy separation, which may favor singlet-to-triplet conversion. Combined spectroscopic analyses, quenching experiments, and density functional theory calculations support a proposed interfacial triplet-energy-funneling pathway involving ZnGa2O4-related/interfacial triplet-related states and subsequent energy transfer to adsorbed O2 for 1O2 generation. As a result, the optimized In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 photocatalyst achieves 98.3% toluene removal and 92.4% mineralization in a continuous-flow gas-phase reactor, together with excellent cycling stabi…

title: The Impact of Methyl Jasmonate, Chitosan, and Storage Period on the Storability of Local Orange Fruits (Citrus sinensis L. Osbeck)
abstract: This study was carried out on fruit of local Diyala orange (Citrus sinensis L. Osbeck). The fruit were obtained from a private orchard in Buhriz village, Diyala governorate, Iraq, to study the impact of (control, 0.5, 1, and 1.5 mM) methyl jasmonate dipped for 3 min and chitosan (control, 1, 2, and 4% w/v) for 5 min on the fruit quality of orange in terms of (fruit weight loss (%), Total soluble solids (%), titratable acidity (%), ascorbic acid content, Total phenol content, chilling injury (%), decay (%), and catalase enzyme) during 30, 60, and 120 days storage at 5±1°C with 85-90% RH. Results showed that all treatments of (Methyl jasmonate and chitosan) significantly decreased the fruit weight loss (%). Furthermore, fruit treated with (1, and 1.5 mM) methyl jasmonate significantly reduced chilling injury (%), and decay (%), respectively, compared with the control. The titratable acidity (%), ascorbic acid content, total phenols, and enzyme catalase significantly increased in fruit treated with 0.5 mM methyl jasmonate compared to other treatments. On the other hand, the untreated fruits caused a significant increase in total soluble solids of both methyl jasmonate and chitosan compared with all other treatments. Dipping fruit in 2% chitosan effectively reduced chilling injury and decay compared with the control. There was a significant increase in ascorbic acid and total pheno…

title: Responsible entrepreneurship, safety involvement, prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation in a developing economy: a serial model
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how owner-managers’ responsible entrepreneurship influences employee safety participation through the serial mediation of safety involvement and prohibitive safety voice. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 417 owner-managers of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that responsible entrepreneurship positively influences employee safety participation. While safety involvement does not moderate this relationship, it significantly mediates the link between responsible entrepreneurship and both prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation. The serial mediation analysis further indicates that responsible entrepreneurship enhances safety involvement, which fosters prohibitive safety voice and, in turn, increases employee safety participation. Practical implications Owner-managers should involve employees in identifying workplace hazards, discuss safety concerns during routine meetings and provide simple channels for reporting unsafe practices. Policymakers can support SMEs through practical safety guidelines, short training programmes and advisory services that help businesses implement affordable employee-centred safety practices. Originality/value This study develops a process-oriented framework explainin…

title: Association between childhood Taekwondo duration and adult participation intention among South Korean university students: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction Sport participation during childhood and adolescence is associated with physical activity in adulthood, yet how participation in a specific sport relates to adult participation patterns remains unclear. In South Korea, Taekwondo participation is concentrated in childhood and declines across the transition to adulthood. This cross-sectional study examined whether childhood Taekwondo duration was associated with adult participation time and participation intention in Taekwondo, other martial arts, and sports other than Taekwondo and martial arts. Methods Survey data from 173 undergraduate students (74 females, 99 males) at a university in Seoul were analyzed. To obtain sufficient variation in adult Taekwondo participation, current adult Taekwondo participants were intentionally overrepresented through purposive non-probability sampling at a university gymnasium complex hosting Taekwondo classes and clubs. Participation time was analyzed with two-part models (whether and how long participants took part) and participation intention with linear regression, controlling for gender, grade, part-time job status, perceived health, and depressive symptoms. Childhood exposure was also examined as ever vs. never participation and as duration among those with childhood experience. Results Longer childhood Taekwondo duration was significantly associated with stronger adult Taekwo…

title: The coupled influences of precession and spin on the cavitating flow around a cylinder vehicle
A wireless fully automated charging station with IoT-based remote monitoring for unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: Purpose This study aims to build and test a low-cost autonomous wireless charging station for small rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) whose Internet of things telemetry layer lets charging be supervised remotely. Design/methodology/approach A commercial inductive module feeds a step-up converter and a 3S protection board and an ESP32 pushes JavaScript Object Notation telemetry at 5 Hz over its own access point to a Flutter ground control station. The link is characterised analytically, then ten charge cycles, a misalignment sweep and ten stability sessions measured. Findings Transmitter-rail-to-battery efficiency was 70.10 ± 0.55 %, the inductive link accounting for 2.8 W of the 3.08 W lost. Charging current held above 90 % of its centred value to 5 mm and reached zero at 15 mm, the collapse beyond that band being converter drop-out rather than lost coupling. Latency was 199.6 ± 2.85 ms at 0.027 % packet loss. Research limitations/implications One airframe, one pad and one client, indoors. Electromagnetic compatibility, avionics interference, outdoor conditions and communication security were not characterised and the fly-land-recharge loop was not closed. Practical implications Four UAVs and three pads give uninterrupted coverage of the missions modelled and retrofitting costs about 30 g of electronics rather than a coil alone. Originality/value Commercial drone-in-a…

title: Distributed elasticity: a high-reward, moderate-risk strategy for efficient control modulation in insect flight
abstract: Abstract The environments inhabited by flying insects demand a balance between flight efficiency and flight manoeuvrability. In structural oscillators such as the insect indirect flight motor, efficiency (arising from resonance) and manoeuvrability (arising from kinematic modulation) are typically quid pro quo, with modulation incurring penalties to efficiency. Band-type resonance is a phenomenon that offers, in theory, a strategy to lessen these penalties via careful navigation through a band of efficient kinematic states. However, identifying this band is challenging: no methods exist to identify the complete band in realistic motor models, involving elasticity distributed across thorax and wing. Nor are the effects of elasticity distribution on the band known. In this work, we address both open topics. We present a suite of numerical methods for identifying the complete resonance band in general systems. Applying them to models of the insect flight motor with distributed elasticity—thoracic and wing flexion—reveals that distributed elasticity is moderate-risk, but high-reward, morphological feature. Well-tuned distributions expand the resonance band over fourfold, whereas poorly tuned distributions completely extinguish the resonance band. These results indicate that distributing elasticity across the insect flight motor can have an adaptive value, and they motivate broader …
venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface

title: Metacognitive strategy sa pagtuturo ng kuwento sa Filipino 10
abstract: Nilayon ng pag-aaral na ito na masuri ang bisa ng Metacognitive Strategy sa pagpapaunlad ng kasanayan ng mga mag-aaral na nakatuon sa pagsusuri ng antas ng pag-unawa gaya ng Literal na Pagbasa, Inferensyal, Kritikal at Personal na Pag-unawa bago at pagkatapos gamitin ang estratehiya. Ginamit ang one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental na disenyo sa siyamnapu’t siyam (99) na mag-aaral sa Baitang 10 ng General Climaco National High School, Toledo City, Cebu sa taong panuruan 2026–2027. Ginamit ang paunang pagsusulit, panghuling pagsusulit, at talatanungan upang masukat ang saloobin hinggil sa paggamit ng Metacognitive Strategy. Batay sa pagsusuri, gamit ang frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, at paired samples t-test, lumabas na nasa antas na Nagsisimula sa lahat ng pamantayan ng pag-unawa sa pagbasa bago ipatupad ang Metacognitive Strategy. Matapos ang interbensiyon, nakita na umangat ang pagganap sa antas na Umuunlad sa literal, inferensyal, at kritikal at personal na pag-unawa. Ipinakita rin ng paired samples t-test na may makabuluhang pagkakaiba sa pauna at panghuling pagganap sa lahat ng pamantayan (p<.001), positibo naman ang saloobin sa paggamit ng Metacognitive Strategy. Natuklasan na may makabuluhang pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng pauna at panghuling pagganap ng mga mag-aaral sa lahat ng pamantayan ng pag-unawa (p<.001). Nagpakita ang mga mag-aaral ng positi…
venue: International Journal of Research Studies in Education

title: MENGEMBANGKAN STRATEGI INOVASI UNTUK SWA DENTAL CARE DENGAN MENGGUNAKAN PENDEKATAN STRATEGI SAMUDRA BIRU (BLUE OCEAN STRATEGY)
abstract: Increasing competition in the dental healthcare industry requires clinics to develop innovative strategies that create service differentiation and new value for patients. This study aims to develop an innovation strategy for SWA Dental Care using the Blue Ocean Strategy (BOS) approach to enhance buyer value, optimize operational efficiency, and identify new market opportunities. A qualitative case study design was employed. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation involving management, dentists, and patients selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using SWOT analysis, Key Success Factors (KSFs), the Strategy Canvas, the Four Actions Framework (Eliminate–Reduce–Raise–Create), and the Six Paths Framework. The findings identify service quality, patient experience, digital transformation, personalized patient relationships, and operational efficiency as key success factors. Based on these findings, the proposed innovation strategies include developing a family dental care ecosystem, integrating digital services, enhancing patient experience through personalized care and post-treatment services, developing complementary services, and digitalizing operational processes. These strategies are intended to establish service differentiation, create new market opportunities, and strengthen SWA Dental Care’s sustainable competitive…

title: Bottom-up: utilising artificial intelligence to identify what successful leaders do, using an abductive approach
abstract: Purpose Identifying exceptional leaders remains a top priority for organisations. Traditionally, leaders were selected using a battery of assessments measuring key personal attributes believed to make leaders successful. However, there has been a shift away from selecting leaders based on an a priori list of virtues, towards a focus on the actual behaviours linked to high performance. This abductive approach in competency framework development for leaders starts with the behaviours demonstrated in assessments and then constructs the competency framework in a bottom-up approach. Design/methodology/approach In the current study, a total of 15 411 leaders from 283 different companies and 38 countries completed a 3.5-hour online assessment centre simulation exercise. Natural language processing and machine learning were then utilised to identify 38 competencies by screening more than 30 million words. We then mapped this artificial intelligence-derived framework to prominent leadership models. Findings Despite strong congruence between frameworks, the abductive approach revealed three critical findings: 1) Not all competencies are equally distributed across the leader population; 2) Competencies are distributed across job levels, with some commonly observed in junior leadership roles and others primarily amongst senior leaders; and 3) the artefacts collected by the machine-learning…

title: G-quadruplex-binding ligand RHPS4 reduces Plasmodium falciparum mitochondrial DNA level providing a novel antimalarial strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum remains a major health threat, killing over 600,000 people annually. The spread of resistance to all major antimalarials, including artemisinins, highlights the urgent need for new drugs with distinct mechanisms of action. Here, we show that the G-quadruplex ligand RHPS4, an acridine derivative, displays strong antiplasmodial activity against both drug-sensitive and drug-resistant P. falciparum strains and clinical isolates. RHPS4 primarily targets the trophozoite stage and induces major mitochondrial alterations, including reduction of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and transcriptional dysfunctions. Bioinformatic analyses identified at least eight putative G4-forming sequences within the parasite’s mtDNA. Biophysical studies confirmed G4 folding of at least one sequence and its interaction with RHPS4. These findings indicate that RHPS4 impacts P. falciparum mitochondrial DNA replication and transcription, leading to parasite death, and establish G4 ligands as novel antimalarial agents.

title: Guest editorial: Retail property post Covid – structural change and investment opportunities
Self-livestream or platform traffic support? The role of online channel disadvantage in dual-channel retail
abstract: Purpose Digital platforms increasingly control both consumer attention and transaction access, forcing brands to choose between developing self-operated content capabilities and purchasing platform traffic. This study examines how intrinsic online channel disadvantage affects the relative value of self-livestream and platform traffic support in dual-channel retail, thereby identifying when platform dependence creates value. Design/methodology/approach We develop a Cournot game involving a brand, a digital platform and an offline retailer. Self-livestream enhances consumer cognition across channels through endogenous effort, whereas platform traffic support expands online market potential in exchange for revenue sharing. Consumer heterogeneity and cross-channel cognition spillovers are incorporated. Robustness analyses further consider incomplete cognition spillovers, alternative channel-substitution intensities and positive baseline platform commissions. Findings A greater online disadvantage shifts sales toward offline retailing under both strategies, but through different mechanisms. Under self-livestream, the brand reduces its effort as online cognition becomes harder to monetize. Under platform traffic support, the traffic package becomes less convertible into profitable sales. When the fixed cost of self-livestream is moderate, the optimal strategy follows a non-monotonic …

title: Empathy-driven remote pedagogy in accounting education − a bilingual model for student engagement and digital resilience
abstract: Purpose This paper presents the empathy-based bilingual digital pedagogy (EBBDP) model, a practice-informed framework developed through the author’s experience in remote teaching of accounting and taxation during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It aims to show how pedagogical empathy can be translated into bilingual and digitally supported teaching practices intended to strengthen engagement, accessibility and emotional safety in virtual learning environments, particularly within technical education. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a reflective-practice methodology grounded in lived teaching experience within Portuguese vocational and professional training. It draws on pedagogical documentation, autoethnographic reflection and iterative adaptation of instructional strategies. The model integrates empathy, bilingual inclusivity and digital co-creation as central pedagogical pillars, illustrated through concrete examples using tools such as Google Workspace, Canva, Padlet and ChatGPT to support collaborative learning and formative assessment. Findings The reflective analysis identifies structured emotional check-ins, bilingual scaffolding, digital co-creation and multimodal assessment as practices through which pedagogical empathy may support accessibility, belonging and sustained participation. These practice-based interpretations are presented as conceptual propo…

title: Decoding the war for talent: a hybrid systematic review and research synthesis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of talent management (TM) research over the past two decades. The study seeks to offer insights into how effective TM fosters development, retention, and alignment of talent, contributing to continuous learning organizations (LO) for sustainable competitive advantage. Design/methodology/approach A hybrid systematic review approach is adopted by analyzing a sample of 996 studies extracted from the Scopus database. The research uses multiple analytical techniques for a robust synthesis of the literature review. Findings This review systematically synthesizes extant research through publication trend analysis, yielding insights into influential works and intellectual collaboration analysis. Content analysis of the literature underlines the thematic focus and conceptual orientation of the studies. It further identifies psychological contract and social exchange theories as the dominant theoretical foundations. The review also organizes TM research into thematic clusters covering its conceptualization, challenges and opportunities, as well as its relevance for LOs. Practical implications The findings underline the practical relevance of emerging aspects such as generational workforce, organizational learning, competency building, and employer branding for TM amid global demographic shifts. Originality/value…

title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches
abstract: Abstract Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔGML < −11 kcal mol−1. Molecular docking identified six top candidates with favorable binding affinities ranging from −5.856 to −9.667 kcal mol⁻¹, which subsequently underwent 200 ns MD simulations. Structural analyses confirmed the stability of all ALK–ligand complexes, while interaction studies revealed extensive hydrophobic contacts and conserved hydrogen bonds involving key ALK residues. US calculations estimated binding free energies from −8.354 to −13.272 kcal mol−1, with compound 54 exhibiting the strongest affinity (ΔGUS = −13.272 kcal mol−1). Several alkaloids, including acrifoline, heptazoline, and atalaphyllidine, also demonstrated promisingbinding properties and reported anticancer activities. Toxicity prediction indicated acceptable safety profiles, highlighting Glycosmis-derived phytochemicals as promising …

title: EFFECT OF FATTY ACID CONCENTRATION IN THE WORKING FLUID OF MACHINE HYDRAULIC DRIVES ON BOUNDARY LUBRICATING FILM FORMATION
abstract: An analysis of research regarding the effect of fatty acid additives on enhancing the anti-wear properties of working fluids was conducted. The characteristics and molecular state of the additive within the oil were identified as factors influencing the formation of a boundary lubricating film on friction surfaces. A method for intensifying additive adsorption by subjecting the working fluid to an electric field was proposed. A methodology was developed to experimentally investigate how the concentration of surfactant molecules – specifically the fatty acids under study – affects the formation of a lubricating layer on the friction surfaces of machinery hydraulic drives. Experimental studies were carried out to examine the effect of stearic and oleic acid concentrations on changes in boundary lubricating film thickness when the working fluid undergoes electrostatic treatment. A non-linear relationship between lubricating film thickness and additive concentration was established, and the optimal concentrations of stearic and oleic acids – yielding the maximum boundary lubricating film thickness – were determined.

title: Leakage-resistant graph learning for risk propagation and risk-constrained control in construction supply networks
abstract: Introduction Construction supply network decisions require both predecision warning from information available before operations unfold and topology-aware diagnosis after the disruption context becomes visible. We introduce an auditable framework that separates these regimes through a strict start-of-week information contract and connects risk scores to safety-gated resource allocation. Methods We combined public SUCCESS construction-logistics records with a frozen queue-flow mechanism producing paired counterfactual outcomes on a heterogeneous network with 302 nodes and 1,277 edges. Models were trained on pilots A and B, selected on pilot C, and evaluated on pilot D. The strict contract excluded all week-t outcomes, service levels, and shock-source indicators. Complementary evaluations comprised context-aware diagnosis, a construction consolidation center (CCC) outage panel, leave-one-project-out evaluation, and an independent SupplyGraph boundary test. Six resource policies were compared through validation-only selection and a held-out Pareto audit. Results Under the strict contract, the graph convolutional network achieved the highest held-out area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.2397 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8161 for 4,252 node-weeks with 60 positives. In the context-aware regime, relational GraphSAGE achieved an …

title: Instructional Time Adequacy and Its Implications for Teaching Delivery and Students’ Learning Performance in Araling Panlipunan
abstract: This study examined the relationships among instructional time adequacy, teaching effectiveness, and students’ learning performance in Junior High School Araling Panlipunan within selected schools in the Schools Division of Talisay City, Cebu. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, the study involved 120 Araling Panlipunan teachers selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through a researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, independent-samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson product–moment correlation. Findings revealed that instructional time adequacy, teaching effectiveness, and teacher-assessed students’ learning performance were generally manifested to a Great Extent. No statistically significant differences in instructional time adequacy were identified according to age, sex, educational attainment, and years of teaching experience. Significant positive relationships were established between instructional time adequacy and teaching effectiveness (r = .510–.631), instructional time adequacy and students’ learning performance (r = .522–.600), and teaching effectiveness and students’ learning performance (r = .600–.659), all p < .001. These findings highlighted the importance of purposeful instructional time utilization and responsive teaching practices. Consequen…

title: Unsupervised selection and characterisation of little red dots in JWST surveys with manifold learning
abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources discovered at high redshifts by JWST, and their physical nature and selection function remain a topic of debate. Here, we investigate whether an unsupervised machine-learning approach applied to multi-band photometry has the capacity to identify LRD-like objects, along with other populations, without relying on predefined colour-cuts. Using UMAP, a manifold-learning (dimensionality-reduction) method, we placed ∼242,000 isolated, well-measured sources from the ASTRODEEP-JWST catalogue on a 2D map, where objects with similar broadband colours, morphology, and photometric redshift lie close together. We then used spectroscopically confirmed LRDs to identify where LRD-like objects lie within this map. We compared the resulting areas with published colour cuts and validated our data-driven selection against archival NIRSpec spectra from the DJA. We find that the spectroscopically selected LRDs are concentrated in two well-defined regions with no colour-cut imposed, tracing populations that differ mainly in redshift; a difference that is imprinted on their broadband colours. The main region reaches a purity of ≃0.78 at ≃0.82 completeness on the spectroscopically classified subset. This result is competitive with (or cleaner than) literature colour-cuts, and yields ∼100 additional candidates. We also tested the method as a general tool f…

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning for Multilingual Edge Translation
abstract: Multilingual edge translation must transfer knowledge across uneven language resources while controlling uncertainty and communication. Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning (MT-BayesFL) combines a shared six-layer Transformer encoder, target-specific decoders, lightweight adapters, and matrix-normal posteriors. The refined formulation separates Gaussian pooling from separable covariance approximation, preserves positive-definite sampling factors, and applies error feedback before sparse transmission. An adaptive projected-moment variant adds bounded reliability weights, between-client disagreement, and participation-dependent shrinkage. Reference-system results span eight English-to-target directions and five reported seeds. Low-resource macro BLEU is 26.0 versus 22.6 for FedMTL, with a 3.43-BLEU gain calculated from pairwise means. English–Swahili reaches 28.3 BLEU and expected calibration error 0.082. BLEU retention is 92.1% at 30% dropout; normalized retention over 0–40% dropout is 94.54%. Communication is 1.8[Formula: see text]MB per round, 70.5% below the dense-upload ablation, and personalization improves by 4.5 BLEU on average. The parameter-efficient comparator remains stronger on English–Chinese. Numerical checks verify covariance and residual invariants; translation gains from the refinement remain unmeasured. These results support uncertainty-aware sharing for imbal…

title: When Learning Becomes a Game: The Impact of Ladders War in Game-Based Learning on Students' Mathematical Critical Thinking Skills
abstract: Mathematical critical thinking remains a persistent challenge in elementary education globally, as TIMSS 2023 findings show that only a small proportion of fourth-grade students worldwide reached the High and Advanced benchmarks in mathematics, while empirical evidence on the effectiveness of game-based approaches at the primary level remains limited. This study examined how the Game-Based Learning (GBL) model, assisted by Ladders War media, influenced fourth-grade students' mathematical critical-thinking skills in number patterns, a topic fundamental to algebraic reasoning that remains persistently difficult for young learners. Employing a quasi-experimental Nonequivalent Control Group Design, 50 students (aged 9–10; 25 males, 25 females) from two intact classes in Bekasi, Indonesia, participated. The study was conducted over four 90-minute sessions: the pretest was administered at the beginning of the first session, followed by the first treatment, two additional treatment sessions, and a posttest in the fourth session. Critical thinking was assessed using a five-item expert-validated essay test (reliability = 0.74) measuring analysis, inference, evaluation, and explanation. ANCOVA with pretest scores as the covariate yielded a large effect size (η²p = 0.217) and a significant between-group difference (F = 13.013, p < .001), with an adjusted mean difference of 13.132 points (…

title: The Use Of Artificial Intelligence (AI) As An Interactive Learning Tool For Students With Intellectual Disabilities In Special Education Schools
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities to develop adaptive and interactive learning media for students with intellectual disabilities, whose learning needs often require concrete explanations, repetition, and individualized support. This study examines the potential, applications, and implementation challenges of AI-assisted learning media in special education. A qualitative literature review was conducted using a PRISMA-guided identification and screening process. Of 72 publications collected, 11 articles published between 2020 and 2026 were selected for critical analysis and synthesis. The reviewed studies addressed AI-based applications, multimodal instructional media, adaptive learning, and assistive technologies. Findings suggest that these technologies can support students' attention, engagement, motivation, conceptual understanding, memory, and independence by providing visual representations, structured practice, and immediate feedback. However, evidence varies considerably across study designs, learner characteristics, and technologies. Several studies relied on teachers' perceptions or small samples rather than direct classroom measurements, limiting conclusions about effectiveness. Implementation challenges include inadequate devices and internet connectivity, insufficient teacher training, accessibility barriers, and concerns about privacy and data ethics…

title: Quantum machine learning for quantitative finance
abstract: Abstract Machine learning (ML) and quantum ML (QML) have gained significant importance, as they offer powerful tools for tackling complex computational problems across various domains. An overview of QML’s uses in quantitative finance is presented here. The connection between quantum computing and ML in financial applications, spanning a range of use cases including portfolio optimization, market prediction and trading, pricing and risk management is examined. The different applications from the literature review are categorized based on specific use cases, ML approaches, optimization methods, and the types of quantum hardware utilized. To facilitate this examination, we employ a morphological box, which allows us to analyze different combinations of these elements across financial use cases.

title: Bridging the Gap: Student Perceptions of Instructor Engagement in Pandemic-Era Online Learning
abstract: This study examines student perceptions of instructor engagement in online learning environments during the initial onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular attention to differences between students with prior online learning experience and those transitioning from traditional face-to-face instruction. Grounded in Moore’s transactional distance theory, the research explores how sudden shifts in instructional modality influenced students’ perceptions of instructor engagement and identifies strategies that may reduce perceived distance in online learning contexts. Survey data were collected during the summer of 2020 from students enrolled at a regional comprehensive university in the mid-South following the emergency transition to remote instruction. A comparative analysis was conducted across course modalities, focusing on seven survey items related to academic engagement, changes in instructor interaction, and student preferences for engagement. Findings indicate that students with prior experience in online courses perceived less disruption in instructor engagement following the transition, while students who had been enrolled primarily in face-to-face courses reported more noticeable declines. These differences suggest that familiarity with online learning environments may buffer students against perceived losses in engagement during periods of instructional disruption…

title: The Team Academy learning environment: supporting the developing recognition of learners' agency
abstract: Purpose This paper explores how the Team Academy learning environment supports the developing recognition of learners' agency through developmental space, developmental relationships and authentic responsibility. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative interpretive case study of Team Academy Debrecen. The analysis draws on contemporaneous reflective documents written during the author's Team Mastery development and retrospective written reflections from former Team Academy graduates and team coaches. Findings Participants described changes in self-understanding, recognition of personal strengths and confidence in their capacity to act, often as a gradual process rather than a single transformative moment. The findings suggest that acting under uncertainty within a supportive developmental environment may contribute to greater certainty in how learners understand themselves and their capacity to act. Research limitations/implications As a single interpretive case study, the research does not seek statistical generalisation. Future research could investigate how recognised agency contributes to intentional and responsible participation beyond the learning environment. Practical implications The findings suggest that higher education can complement disciplinary knowledge with developmental learning environments that prepare learners to engage with uncertainty. S…

title: Regular physical activity is associated with slightly lower subsequent depressive symptoms in Chinese adults aged 18–64 years: a longitudinal double machine learning and causal forest study
abstract: Introduction Physical activity is widely associated with better mental health, but observational estimates can be distorted by pre-existing health and socioeconomic differences, and it remains unclear whether potential benefits can be reliably individualized. We examined the association between regular physical activity and subsequent depressive symptoms among Chinese adults and evaluated whether treatment-effect heterogeneity was interpretable and predictively useful. Methods We used three waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS; 2018, 2020, and 2022). Depressive symptoms, prior physical activity, and demographic, health, and socioeconomic characteristics measured in 2018 were treated as pre-exposure covariates. Regular physical activity was defined as participation at least once per week in 2020, and the 2022 Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) score was the outcome. The main analytic sample included 10,159 adults aged 18–64 years. Average effects were estimated using DoubleML-IRM with random-forest learners, household-clustered 5-fold cross-fitting, and 10 repeated sample splits. Causal forests were used to examine conditional treatment-effect heterogeneity and cross-fitted benefit ranking. Sensitivity analyses included alternative exposure definitions, common-support restriction, complete cases, and inverse-probability-of-observation weighting fo…

title: ADVERSITY QUOTIENT DAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH MATEMATIS DALAM PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING BERBANTUAN LIVE WORKSHEET: KAJIAN LITERATUR SISTEMATIS
abstract: The low mathematical problem-solving ability of Indonesian lower secondary students calls for inquiry that considers not only instructional models but also students' persistence when facing difficult tasks. This article synthesises research on the relationships among Adversity Quotient (AQ), mathematical problem solving, Problem-Based Learning (PBL), and Live Worksheet-based digital worksheets. A qualitative systematic literature review was conducted on 18 publications from 2018 to 2026 selected through inclusion criteria and examined using six-phase thematic analysis. Four themes emerged. First, AQ types (climber, camper, quitter) consistently correspond to how far students progress through Polya's stages. Second, AQ contributes meaningfully but is not the sole determinant, so the design of the learning environment remains decisive. Third, PBL acts as a structured space of difficulty and generally benefits junior high school students' problem solving, although effect sizes vary. Fourth, digital worksheets provide scaffolding and immediate feedback that may support medium- and low-AQ students, yet current evidence relies mostly on short-term designs that do not disaggregate results by AQ. Future studies are recommended to treat AQ as a moderating variable in PBL implemented with digital worksheets at the junior high school level. ABSTRAK Rendahnya kemampuan pemecahan masalah ma…
venue: EDUCATOR : Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan

title: Enhancing Numeracy Skills through Animated Video-Based Learning Media Among Early Grade Elementary School Students: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Developed numeracy skills are essential for students to understand mathematical ideas and apply them to everyday problems. This study investigated whether animated video-based learning media improved the numeracy skills of third-grade elementary school students. A quasi-experimental pre-test-post-test control group design was conducted with 48 students at SD Negeri 1 Tanjung Seneng, Bandar Lampung, Indonesia, comprising 24 students in the experimental class (IIIA) and 24 students in the control class (IIIB). Data were collected using a 20-item numeracy test; all items were valid (r = 0.461–0.698 > r-table = 0.413) and the instrument demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.892). The experimental group increased from a mean pre-test score of 58.13 (SD = 3.35) to 87.88 (SD = 3.30), whereas the control group increased from 57.29 (SD = 3.01) to 71.58 (SD = 2.98). Within-group paired-samples t-tests were significant for the experimental group, t(23) = 197.70, p < .001, and the control group, t(23) = 112.19, p < .001. The experimental group had a mean N-gain of 0.715 (high), and the control group had 0.336 (medium). ANCOVA indicated a significant effect of learning group on post-test numeracy scores after controlling for pre-test scores, F(1,45) = 6113.92, p < .001, partial η² = .993, with adjusted means of 87.47 and 71.98 for the experimental and control groups, …

title: Pelatihan Menulis Cerita Anak Bagi Siswa Kelas V MI PUI Santi Asromo Kabupaten Majalengka
abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan keterampilan menulis kreatif siswa kelas V MI PUI Santi Asromo Majalengka melalui pelatihan menulis cerita anak berbasis proyek buku kumpulan cerita anak. Permasalahan utama mitra meliputi rendahnya minat dan kepercayaan diri siswa dalam menulis, terbatasnya kesempatan siswa mengembangkan ide kreatif, serta praktik pembelajaran menulis yang masih didominasi tugas konvensional tanpa publikasi karya yang bermakna. Program ini menerapkan pendekatan Project-Based Learning melalui kegiatan pelatihan dan pendampingan intensif yang mencakup eksplorasi cerita, penyusunan story map, penulisan draf, umpan balik teman sebaya, revisi, hingga menghasilkan kumpulan cerita anak. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi tahap persiapan, sosialisasi, workshop interaktif, praktik menulis, pendampingan, dan evaluasi produk karya siswa. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa siswa sangat antusias dan terlibat aktif selama pelatihan berlangsung. Sebagian besar peserta mampu menghasilkan cerita anak dengan struktur naratif yang jelas, alur yang runtut, serta ide cerita yang lebih kontekstual berdasarkan pengalaman sehari-hari dan lingkungan sekitar. Luaran kegiatan ini berupa kumpulan cerita anak karya siswa MI PUI Santi Asromo, modul pelatihan, serta LKPD yang dapat direplikasi di sekolah dasar. Kegiatan ini berkontribusi terhadap penguatan budaya liter…

title: Detection of sacroiliitis in spondyloarthritis patients via deep learning from computed tomography scans
Free-Vibration Performance–Robustness Trade-Offs in Hybrid Composite Laminates under Manufacturing Uncertainty: A Probabilistic Decision Framework
abstract: Manufacturing variability introduces uncertainty in the vibration response of laminated composites, which can affect decision-making on laminate selection based on nominal parameters. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware methodology for free vibration evaluation and selection between Kevlar/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, and Kevlar-Glass hybrid plates. The first five natural frequencies were determined by propagating uncertainties in the material properties and manufacturing processes using a Mindlin-Reissner FSDT finite-element model in combination with Monte Carlo simulation. Published benchmark frequencies were matched with a maximum absolute relative error of 0.38%. Convergence of mesh and sampling was verified independently. The coefficients of variation for frequency ranged from about 2.8% to 3.3%. The local and global sensitivity analyzes showed that the ply thickness and the longitudinal elastic modulus were the main sources of uncertainty, followed closely by density. The Kevlar laminate had the maximum natural frequencies and Rank-1 probability (61.61%) and continues to be the leader under all nine decision assumptions. The KGGKs with Kevlar outer plies showed a favorable balance between cross-modal performance robustness and stable near-top ranking, while the glass laminate had the least variability in four of five modes, but at lower frequencies. These results indicate tha…
venue: Scientific Journal of Engineering, and Technology

title: Social uncertainty and school disengagement: a theoretical framework of early school leaving in precarious family contexts
abstract: Romania has had the highest rate of early leaving from education and training in the European Union for several years, with the burden concentrated in rural areas and among Roma young people. Existing explanations attribute early school leaving to poverty, family disadvantage, institutional exclusion or individual disengagement, but they say little about why families with similar resources make different educational choices when their futures are unpredictable. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes that social uncertainty, defined as the reduced predictability of a household's material circumstances and of the returns to schooling, is analytically distinct from the level of deprivation and from neighbouring concepts such as precarity, vulnerability, risk and exclusion. Using a staged procedure for building conceptual frameworks, we derive a model in which uncertainty affects school engagement through four mechanisms: the contraction of temporal horizons, family stress, the reallocation of children's time to care and work, and the responsiveness of schools. We specify five moderators, including family resilience resources and student agency, set out eight testable propositions with their boundary conditions, and identify the evidence that would contradict them. We distinguish absenteeism, including its voluntary and involuntary forms, from disengagement, dropout and early …

title: An Intelligent Decision-Making Methodology Based on a New Fermatean Fuzzy Similarity Measure: A Case Study of Building Site Preference
abstract: Intelligent-driven decision-making through soft computing tools like Fermatean fuzzy sets has proven to be effective even in the presence of imprecision. The Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure is one of the avenues through which intelligent-based decision-making is made. Various methods of Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure have been fashioned; however, many of them are deficient in terms of formulation, precision, and compliance with the similarity conditions. These deficiencies can result in faulty decision-making with a concomitant effect during implementation. To this end, this paper presents a new approach of Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure, which outperformed the extant measures by comparison. Equally, the new approach evidently satisfies the similarity’s conditions. To test the application potential of the new similarity approach, it is used to discuss the complexity of locating a prefer location for an estate building based on TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution). In addition, a comparative analysis of the new approach in conjunction with the extant ones based on TOPSIS is presented, and the new approach unmistakably shows precision and reliability over the extant approaches. The flexibility of the new approach of intelligent-based decision-making qualifies its application in other complex decision-making scenarios.
venue: International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems

title: Heterogeneous impact of digital technology adoption on ambidextrous innovation: the moderating role of environmental uncertainty and industry competition
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how digital technology adoption differentially affects the two dimensions of ambidextrous innovation. From the perspective of resource crowding-out and empowering effects, the authors analyze the impacts of digital technology adoption on exploratory and exploitative innovation, as well as the moderating effects of environmental uncertainty and industry competition. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a fixed-effects model with a sample of China’s Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed companies from 2008 to 2024. Findings There is a U-shaped relationship between digital technology adoption and exploratory innovation, while a positive linear relationship exists between digital technology adoption and exploitative innovation. The U-shaped relationship is flatter for firms under high environmental uncertainty and steeper for those facing fierce industry competition. Environmental uncertainty and industry competition weaken the positive relationship between digital technology adoption and exploitative innovation. Originality/value This study deepens the theoretical understanding of how digital technology adoption differently influences exploratory and exploitative innovation, thereby addressing ongoing debates in the literature.

title: Perpendicular transport in isotropic magnetic turbulence. The role of stochastic drifts
abstract: In the context of cosmic ray propagation in a turbulent magnetic field, transport perpendicular to the mean field plays an important role in a variety of situations of physical interest. Numerical simulations of test particles in isotropic turbulence with a guide field show that, for r_L<L_c, the parallel and perpendicular diffusion coefficients scale differently with energy, so that the corresponding ratio D_⊥/D_∥ increases with energy. Several attempts have been made to address this phenomenon, but no consensus theoretical understanding has yet been reached. We used test-particle numerical simulations of particle transport in synthetic turbulence over a broad energy range to establish a general trend of the perpendicular diffusion coefficient. We also provide a theoretical description of our findings based on an extension of the nonlinear guiding-center theory that includes stochastic drifts. The numerical simulations of isotropic turbulence are based on a wavelet method that allows us to reproduce turbulence over ∼ 6-7 orders of magnitude in wavenumber. This wide wavenumber range is reflected in a correspondingly wide energy range for test particles. The theoretical part presents a novel description of perpendicular transport based on autocorrelation functions of turbulent magnetic fields. It describes how particles diffuse perpendicular to the field lines through a combinat…

title: Multi-objective optimization of resource allocation and patrol routing for a maritime patrol and rescue system considering spatial risk distribution
abstract: Timely and effective search and rescue (SAR) services are crucial for ensuring maritime safety. Proactive patrol operations provide an effective means of improving the response capability and resource utilization efficiency of maritime patrol and rescue systems. However, existing maritime rescue systems mainly rely on fixed rescue bases and cannot fully account for spatial variations in maritime risk during resource allocation. To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-objective optimization approach for a maritime patrol and rescue system considering spatial risk distribution. Historical maritime accident data and AIS data are integrated, and a convolutional neural network–multilayer perceptron (CNN–MLP) model is developed to estimate the risk index of each service subarea. Based on this, a multi-objective optimization model is formulated for maritime patrol and rescue operations, integrating patrol-point location, SAR ship task allocation, and patrol routing into a unified framework. Considering the large continuous search space for patrol-point locations, the varying number of decision variables, and the complex combinatorial optimization characteristics, a hybrid optimization algorithm combining fuzzy C-means clustering and simulated annealing-based variable neighborhood search (FCM-SA-VNS) is proposed. Numerical experiments are conducted in the South China Sea, an…

title: Stochastic Mortality Modelling for Small and Data-Scarce Populations: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Stochastic mortality models developed for large national populations face challenges when applied to small populations with volatile death counts, short data series, and potentially biased parameter estimates. This systematic review synthesizes modelling strategies for small and data-scarce populations from an actuarial perspective, examining uncertainty quantification, model evaluation, and remaining research gaps. Following PRISMA 2020, records were identified through Semantic Scholar and citation snowballing. Of 40 unique records screened, 18 studies published between 2011 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria; included journal articles appeared in Scopus-indexed journals. Data were extracted using a structured form and synthesized thematically. Five categories emerged: reference-population and two-population models, credibility and Bayesian methods, analyses of small-population bias, subnational and small-area methods, and hybrids incorporating machine learning. Most approaches stabilized projections by borrowing information from larger, related populations. However, the reviewed machine-learning studies seldom reported forecast intervals, and none of the included studies used Southeast Asian data. The evidence supports selecting an appropriate reference population and reporting distinct sources of uncertainty separately when modelling mortality in small populations. By con…

title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio-integrated index and 28-day mortality in sepsis: a dual-cohort study
abstract: Background Stress hyperglycemia is common in sepsis, but admission glucose is influenced by antecedent glycemia. The stress hyperglycemia ratio-integrated index (SHRI) combines hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)-normalized glycemia with serum potassium. We examined the association between early SHRI and 28-day mortality in adults with sepsis. Methods This retrospective dual-cohort study included 4,495 adults with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database and 320 patients from an independent hospital validation cohort. SHRI was calculated using HbA1c measured from 90 days before to 24 hours after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and glucose and potassium measured within 6 hours before or after ICU admission; the same exposure definition was applied in both cohorts. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, previously diagnosed diabetes, and day-1 Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, and restricted cubic splines characterized dose–response associations. Results Within 28 days, 903 patients (20.1%) died in MIMIC-IV and 64 (20.0%) died in the validation cohort. In MIMIC-IV, the adjusted hazard ratio per 0.1 increase in SHRI was 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04–1.11). The corresponding hazard ratio in the validation cohort was 2.00 (95% CI…

title: DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN AND INTEGRATED EVALUATION-CONSTRUCTION: PARADIGM RECONSTRUCTION AND PRACTICAL EXPLORATION OF "INTERCULTURAL COMMUNICATION" COURSES IN HIGHER EDUCATION
abstract: Addressing critical bottlenecks in traditional intercultural communication instruction—specifically, fabricated communicative contexts, the decoupling of teaching and assessment, and superficial technology integration—this study introduces a synergistic mechanism of "data-intelligence driving" and "evaluation–construction integration" to construct a data-driven precision teaching framework for college foreign language courses. Adopting a backward design approach, the study reconstructs a four-dimensional curricular objective matrix comprising language proficiency, digital-intelligence literacy, intercultural communicative competence, and comprehensive qualities. By deconstructing typical tasks in international professions, it develops a multimodal digital case repository and a three-phase, five-step virtual-real hybrid training chain ("Orient–Instruct–Practice–Explore–Evaluate"). Furthermore, a tripartite attainment assessment model integrating process evaluation, summative evaluation, and value-added evaluation is established. Drawing upon multiple rounds of pedagogical implementation at Zhejiang Yuexiu University, this paper summarizes the implementation pathways, core mechanisms, and preliminary observations of the proposed paradigm, while reflecting on its inherent constraints. This research aims to provide a transferable operational framework for the digital-intelligence t…

title: An integrated gut phage catalogue of nonhuman primates reveals functional adaptation to host ecology and evolutionary link to humans
abstract: Abstract Nonhuman primates (NHPs), the closest evolutionary relatives of humans, are pivotal models for biomedical and ecological research. Gut phage are recognized as critical modulators of gut microbial communities; however, comprehensive insight into gut phage of NHPs is lacking. We used gut metagenomes spanning 25 NHP species and constructed an integrated gut phage catalogue (IGPC) comprising 11 389 nonredundant phage genomes. Our results revealed that the composition and function of NHP gut phage were significantly influenced by host clade, dietary niche and lifestyle. Host clade exerted a stronger influence than dietary niche on gut phage diversity. The lifestyle of NHPs influenced gut phage diversity and altered auxiliary metabolic gene profiles for different NHP species. Comparatively, 78.5% of IGPC phages were detected in human guts, with higher prevalence in nonindustrialized human guts. crAss-like phage—the most prevalent human-associated phage—were abundant in NHP guts, while exhibiting distinct evolutionary differences from crAss-like phage of humans. These findings comprehensively characterize the gut phageome of NHPs, revealing NHP host-driven and environment-driven functional adaptations, and provide an evolutionary understanding of the gut phageome between NHPs and humans.
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: Social prescribing link worker voices through the lens of proportionate universalism
abstract: Purpose Drawing on testimony from frontline Social Prescribing Link workers (SPLWs) in England, this article analyses their perspectives and argues for increased resources at the community level, awareness of social determinants and stronger link worker identity. Design/methodology/approach This ethically approved small-scale qualitative study undertook interviews with eight SPLWs, employed in two different locations across the North of England, that encompassed both urban and rural locations. Findings The study produced rich testimony from their direct experience of SPLWs, which were mapped, against the regional determinants of health, incorporating Proportionate Universalism principles. Respondents felt that more could be done to support the development of a stronger identity for link workers. Importantly, the issue of resources, particularly in areas of deprivation where available services may be more limited, emerged as a strong theme. Originality/value The analysis suggests that resourcing is crucial for the success or otherwise of SPLWs input. The adoption of Proportionate Universalism (Marmot) in social prescribing and beyond could improve the resource allocation link workers have to support people in communities and raise awareness of working on the wider determinants of health and wellbeing, thus contributing to the sustainability of Social Prescribing and the SPLWs ro…

title: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human–domestic animal–wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
abstract: Abstract Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife–domestic animal–human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that susta…

title: A multi-class anomaly signal classification method for fixed-point deformation combining PSO–VMD multiscale adaptive sample entropy and ALO–SOM model
abstract: To address the challenge of identifying five predefined categories of disturbance-related abnormal signals (lightning interference, artificial blasting, power-supply failure, collapse-related events, and meteorological anomalies) in fixed-point deformation monitoring, this paper proposes an identification framework integrating parameter-optimized variational mode decomposition (VMD), multiscale entropy analysis, and an intelligent classification model. Firstly, particle swarm optimization is adopted to adaptively determine the mode number and penalty factor for VMD to realize adaptive signal decomposition. Then, an adaptive sample entropy algorithm with self-adjustable similarity thresholds is applied to extract multiscale complexity-oriented features from each decomposed modal component. Finally, the ant lion optimizer optimizes the competitive-layer topology and training hyperparameters of a self-organizing map network to build the target classifier. Comparative experiments against 18 widely-used classification models (including AdaBoost ensemble learners, generalized regression neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and gated recurrent units) are carried out on the real-world observation dataset from the Yixian seismic station. The experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive classification performance for the five anomaly categories.…

title: A multi-database bibliometric study of cancer-related depression: hotspots and emerging trends
abstract: Background Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects cancer patients and survivors, exerting a persistent negative impact on their lives. This study aims to investigate the current status and potential trends of depression in cancer research from 2015 to June 2026. Methods The publications related to cancer-related depression were retrieved from the core database of Web of Science and Scopus, analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer software, and a corresponding visual network diagram was generated for display. Results Annual output increased overall from 1,359 publications in 2015 to 3,275 in 2025, with fluctuations between years; the 1,588 publications for 2026 represent an incomplete year. The United States is the country with the largest number of publications and is at the center of international cooperation. Harvard Medical School in the United States has been the leading institution in terms of both the volume of published papers and the significance of its research contributions. Christine Miaskowski emerged as the author with the greatest output, while Jennifer S. Temel’s work achieved the highest average citation count. Among the journals, Supportive Care in Cancer published the most articles, whereas Psycho-Oncology garnered the greatest number of citations. Frequently occurring keywords in the research included “depression”, “quality of life”, and “anxiet…

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk
abstract: Objective Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells. Methods Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R. Results BAFF-R on CD20 − (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797–0.926, P = 7.17 × 10 −5 ) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843–0.961, P = 1.57 × 10 −3 ) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs. Conclusion This multi-omics genetic-toxico…

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis deciphers the molecular mechanisms underlying the characteristic volatile flavor of Meishan pork
abstract: Abstract Background The Meishan pig is a celebrated indigenous Chinese swine breed renowned for its distinctive flavor profile. However, the specific signature flavor compounds and the molecular mechanisms underlying their formation remain largely uncharacterized. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the volatile flavor compounds across five pig breeds and decipher the molecular basis of the characteristic flavor of Meishan pork. Results Comparative analysis combining electronic nose, headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), and relative odor activity value calculations revealed that Meishan pork contained significantly higher levels of four key aroma compounds: hexanal, nonanal, 2-pentylfuran, and (E,E)-2,4-nonadienal. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses identified oleic acid and α-linolenic acid as critical precursors and highlighted the high expression of the arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase gene ( ALOX5 ) in Meishan pigs. Heating experiments confirmed that these fatty acids yield characteristic flavor compounds upon thermal oxidation. Furthermore, functional studies demonstrated that ALOX5 catalyzes the conversion of these precursors into flavor aldehydes. Conclusions The distinctive flavor of Meishan pork is associated with a dual mechanism: thermal oxidation of abundant precursors during cook…
venue: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology

title: Management Challenge in a Known case of Chronic Kidney Disease on Immuno-Suppressive Agents Now Presenting with Acute Viral Hepatitis
abstract: Background: Tubulo-Interstitial Nephritis (TIN) is a nonsuppurative inflammatory disease of the kidney interstitium and if chronic, almost always progresses to Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). Hemodialysis is frequently performed as renal replacement therapy. However, to treat the underlying cause of CKD, like in autoimmune cases immunosuppressive agents are needed in addition. Patients undergoing hemodialysis are at higher risk of developing blood borne infections such as HBV and HCV. Due to impaired immunity in CKD, TIN patients on immunosuppressive therapy becoming HBV infected, warrants a clear treatment limitation like withholding of immunosuppressants as the viral replication soars high, increasing the chances of developing chronicity and viral mutants. Anti-viral drugs are very helpful for HBV infection control in these patients. The purpose of this case report is to draw the clinicians' attention towards early diagnosis and management of HBV infection among such groups of CKD patients, as it can cause higher morbidity and mortality, if not appropriately addressed. Case Presentation: We report here a female of 37 years age suffering from CKD due to TIN, priorly on Maintenance Hemodialysis (MHD) for 3 months followed by immune-suppressive agents for next 3 months with evident clinical improvement. She suddenly developed silent deep jaundice and health deterioration with hepa…
venue: Chattagram Maa-O-Shishu Hospital Medical College Journal

title: The Role of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) Curriculum Management in Improving the Quality of Islamic Educational Institutions
abstract: Curriculum management in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) plays a strategic role in aligning academic achievement with students’ religious and moral development. This study examined its contribution to the quality of Islamic educational institutions through four management functions: planning, organization, implementation, and evaluation. A qualitative literature review was conducted, with relevant sources examined and analyzed descriptively to identify relationships between curriculum management functions and educational quality indicators. The synthesis indicated that planning aligned with students’ needs and institutional vision establishes clear instructional direction. Effective organization facilitates resource utilization and collaboration among educators, while innovative and contextualized instruction supports student engagement and the understanding and application of Islamic values. Systematic evaluation informs instructional improvement and continuous quality development. Together, these findings emphasize that curriculum management requires coordinated implementation across all four functions. The study contributes a synthesis of their complementary roles and provides a basis for strengthening instructional quality, cultivating students’ moral character, and developing adaptive Islamic educational institutions committed to continuous improvement.

title: Designing employee wellness programs in hotels: a prioritized resource framework
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how employee wellness programs (EWPs) function in high-demand service environments, addressing the limitation that prior research assumes wellness resources automatically improve employee well-being. Design/methodology/approach A four-stage mixed-methods design was adopted, including literature review, expert content validation, Fuzzy Delphi analysis with 28 experts and a survey of 507 hotel employees analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings A six-dimensional EWP framework comprising 26 validated indicators was confirmed. The results show that EWP dimensions are not functionally equivalent but operate within a structured system. Organizational resources, particularly healthcare support and health management policies, play a foundational role, while other dimensions contribute to recovery and longer-term development. The findings suggest that the effectiveness of wellness initiatives depends on employees’ capacity to use available resources. Research limitations/implications By integrating conservation of resources theory with the well-being-as-capability perspective, this study reframes EWPs as a capability-enabling system that emphasizes resource usability rather than mere provision. Practically, hotels should prioritize foundational organizational resources before expanding other wellness initiatives, using…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: The Effect of Instagram Social Media Marketing and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of H'zhazu MSME Products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang
abstract: Social media marketing and product quality are important considerations in consumer purchasing decisions, particularly for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating in competitive markets. However, further empirical investigation is needed to understand how these factors are associated with purchasing decisions in the context of traditional-snack MSMEs. This study examines the individual and joint associations of Instagram social media marketing and product quality with purchase decisions among consumers of H'Zhazu MSME products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang. A quantitative cross-sectional design with an associative approach was employed. The study population comprised 348 consumers, from which 78 respondents were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 29. The results revealed that Instagram social media marketing had a positive and statistically significant association with purchase decisions (B = 0.512; β = 0.437; t = 4.103; p < 0.001). Product quality also demonstrated a positive and statistically significant association (B = 0.541; β = 0.465; t = 4.371; p < 0.001). Furthermore, the regression model was statistically significant (F = 110.734; p < 0.001), with an R² of 0.747, indicating that the two predictors jointly accounted for 74.7% of t…
venue: International Journal of Management Science and Application

title: Beyond completeness
Regulatory fragmentation in bank–insurance conglomerates: a qualitative index for cross-regime supervision
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how differences across accounting, banking, insurance and group supervision affect the interpretation of capital strength and risk capacity in bank–insurance conglomerates. Regulatory fragmentation is treated as an interpretive and supervisory problem rather than proof of financial weakness. A structured method is developed through which observable differences can be identified from public evidence and compared across financial groups. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative documentary method is applied to laws, technical standards, supervisory guidance, consultation papers, enforcement reviews and corporate reports. A Regulatory Fragmentation Risk Index (RFRI) is developed across four pillars: measurement, capital aggregation, disclosure and supervisory coordination. Each pillar is classified through structured criteria and a common evidence hierarchy. The index is applied to 30 financial conglomerates across six regulatory environments and the results are examined through descriptive comparison and external plausibility assessment. Findings The greatest divergence is found where accounting and prudential valuations are compared, sector capital rules are combined at group level and related disclosures cannot be reconciled directly. Higher scores are also found where supervisory responsibility is divided across jurisdictions. L…

title: Financial Constraints and Perceived Bakery Operation Competency Among Public Senior High School Students
abstract: This study examined the financial constraints and perceived Bakery Operation competency of Grade 11 students at Tuy Senior High School during School Year 2026–2027. Using a descriptive-correlational quantitative design and total enumeration, the study involved 57 students. A researcher-made questionnaire assessed access to ingredients and baking materials, availability of baking tools and equipment, transportation and related school expenses, family financial support, and perceived competency in baking skills, equipment handling and operation, food safety and sanitation, and product preparation and presentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson product–moment correlation. Financial constraints were generally manageable, although access to tools and equipment represented the most evident resource challenge and family support was strong. Students rated their competency highly in all four domains. Selected differences according to sex were significant, whereas differences by age, family income, and monthly allowance were generally nonsignificant. None of the financial-constraint dimensions showed a statistically significant relationship with perceived Bakery Operation competency. The proposed BAKE-SUPPORT Program addresses resource access and practical skills reinforcement. The findings concern self-reported c…
