title: Reported expulsion and displacement of the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system in women with adenomyosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Forecasting geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties for ESG stock markets in developed and developing countries
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the influence of trade policy uncertainty (TPU) and geopolitical uncertainty (GPU) on ESG stock performance and further examines their interconnectedness across developing and developed markets. Design/methodology/approach This study used GARCH-MIDAS and DCC-GARCH techniques for data analysis. The study collected monthly and daily TPU and GPU data from https://www.matteoiacoviello.com/. The daily data of ESG Leader indexes were obtained from MSCI and span from 2014 to 2024. Findings The findings show that ESG stocks serve as a safe-haven asset, making them an attractive option during times of GPU. ESG stocks tend to increase significantly during periods of high GPU, reinforcing that ESG stocks remain resilient. This highlights their potential as a reliable choice for investors navigating turbulent market conditions. It gives high returns during periods of uncertainty. ESG stocks are a strategic option for those seeking growth and stability in their portfolio. The Results found a positive impact of TPU on UESGL, CESGL and JESGL, while a negative influence on CHESGL and IESGL, reflecting the sensitivity of these markets to regulatory rigidity and trade disruptions. The DCC-GARCH results indicate that UESGL, CESGL and JESGL act as net receivers of shocks while CHESGL and IESGL serve as net transmitters. The result of net directional connectedness re…
venue: Journal of Economic and Administrative Sciences

title: Explainable hour-ahead traffic-volume forecasting with condition-stratified evaluation: an interstate I-94 case study
abstract: Introduction Hour-ahead traffic-volume forecasting can support traveler information, staffing, and advance corridor management. However, reliable evaluation requires attention to data quality, temporal variation, and forecasting uncertainty. This study evaluates an auditable, condition-stratified forecasting framework using traffic observations from westbound Interstate I-94 in Minnesota. Methods The Metro Interstate Traffic Volume dataset was audited for duplicate records, repeated timestamps, physically implausible rainfall observations, and missing hourly intervals. After preprocessing, 40,574 usable hourly timestamps yielded 28,855 valid gap-aware forecasting sequences with 24-hour input windows. The evaluated models included persistence, a 24-hour seasonal-naive baseline, LightGBM, XGBoost with and without weather variables, DLinear, GRU, a compact iTransformer-style model, and the Temporal-Mean Residual Network (TMRNet). Trainable models were evaluated using five prespecified random seeds. Performance was assessed through forecasting accuracy, paired statistical comparisons, direct forecasting horizons, rainfall-stratified errors, empirical prediction intervals, grouped permutation importance, TreeSHAP, and Integrated Gradients. Results XGBoost without weather achieved the lowest mean test MAE of 141.67 ± 0.31 vehicles/hour, followed by LightGBM (142.63 ± 0.41) and all-fe…

title: Spatial and vertical price transmission in potato markets in India
abstract: Purpose This paper has examined the dynamics of price transmission and co-movement across geographically dispersed markets and in the wholesale–retail supply chains for a perishable crop (potato) in eight major Indian cities, evaluating the interconnection among the wholesale and retail prices and market arrivals of the crop. Design/methodology/approach It has applied various unit-root tests, a standard vector autoregressive model, the Granger causality test and a correlation method to monthly potato prices and market arrivals data from January 2010 to December 2022. Findings It has offered evidence for spatial and vertical integration of potato markets. The wholesale prices were transmitted across the cities involved in potato trading. The prices were transmitted between wholesale and retail markets in most cases. While market arrivals have influenced the prices and marketing margins, these factors in turn have some effects on market arrivals in some cities. There exists evidence of significant co-movement of prices in the spatial and vertical markets. Research limitations/implications In the markets with significant cross-market price transmission, the effects and incentives of any policy are likely to be transmitted to all the markets without requiring much intervention. The policies to reduce price variability and enhance market integration should focus on facilitating trad…
venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Electric Vehicle Price Prediction Using Real-World Online Listings: An Explainable Machine Learning Approach
abstract: The recent gains in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) have triggered the emergence of secondary markets concerning EVs, where the determination of prices accurately and transparently is an extreme challenge. In the current study, we propose an explainable machine learning model to predict the advertised price (in Jordanian dinars) of used EVs, using actual online advertisements obtained in the Jordanian market. An EV-oriented and custom-made dataset of 2,165 listings was used that specifically includes battery capacity and driving range along with the typical vehicle features. The coefficient of determination (R²), mean absolute error, and root mean squared error were used to assess the performance of three tree-based regressors: CatBoost Regressor, Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressor, and Random Forest Regressor trained with a leakage-safe pipeline and evaluated using grouped, repeated cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to the fitted models to quantify the global contribution of each feature to price predictions and to assess the stability of these contributions across validation folds, providing a transparent account of the price-determination mechanism. The empirical data indicate that battery capacity and driving range are the most dominant EV price determinants that continue to overshadow conventional predictors of price, including brand, mi…
venue: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and international positioning of carbon emission factors of electricity in China
abstract: In the context of China’s dual carbon goals, the electricity sector is both the primary source of carbon emissions and a key driver of socioeconomic development. A systematic assessment of the evolution of electricity carbon emission factors is critical for tracking electricity system decarbonization and formulating effective emission-reduction policies. This study develops an integrated analytical framework for examining the spatiotemporal heterogeneity and international positioning of electricity carbon emission factors of China. Based on official national- and provincial-level data, the framework combines the statistical analysis modules including spatiotemporal characteristics analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, policy-stage comparison, and international benchmarking to characterize the ECEF patterns. Results show that China’s electricity sector has achieved substantial low-carbon transition progress. Based on the available benchmark-year observations, China’s national average ECEF decreased by 13.03% between 2015 and 2023, while interprovincial disparities widened and maintained a “high in the north, low in the south” spatial pattern. The spatial correlation structure has continuously evolved, with weakened global positive spatial autocorrelation, contracted High-High and Low-Low clusters, and strengthened High-Low heterogeneity, indicating diminished geographic pr…

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic …

title: A Review of the Accuracy and Computational Cost of AI Regression Models for Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting
abstract: Short-term wind power forecasting models must meet both accuracy requirements and computational limits. Published comparisons use different datasets, forecast horizons, and timing boundaries. In this focused narrative review, twelve publications on artificial intelligence (AI) regression models and their evaluation are examined. Support vector regression, random forests, XGBoost, and long short-term memory networks are the main model families discussed. Prediction errors and computational costs are compared within studies, and changes in input information are examined. Under the reported experimental conditions, lower prediction errors do not always require higher computational costs. Runtime rankings can also differ between training and inference. Meteorological inputs and data enrichment affect accuracy and the performance gaps between models. However, cost reporting remains incomplete. The evidence cannot establish whether these accuracy gains require longer computation times or more resources. A conditional screening procedure is therefore suggested. The forecasting task and input availability should be checked first. Parameter search, training, and inference costs should then be compared separately. Results should also be tested across several time windows. These recommendations can support model screening under operational constraints. Their applicability still requires v…

title: Vehicle trajectory prediction with temporal–channel attention and GRU
From structure prediction to ligand–target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research
A Statistically Robust Machine Learning Framework for Thyroid Dysfunction Prediction Using Classical Classifiers
abstract: Abstract—Thyroid dysfunction is a common endocrine problem whose symptoms may overlap with many non-thyroid conditions, making timely screening important. This paper presents a conference-style classical machine-learning framework for predicting thyroid dysfunction from structured clinical and laboratory variables. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Gaussian Naive Bayes are compared under a leakage-aware preprocessing and validation protocol. The framework emphasizes rigorous statistical evaluation through stratified nested cross-validation, bootstrap confidence intervals, receiver-operating-characteristic analysis, probability calibration, DeLong comparison of AUCs, and McNemar testing of paired classification errors. Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Specificity, and F1-score are reported with their mathematical definitions. In the illustrative project experiment, Random Forest provides the strongest overall discrimination and balanced error profile, while Logistic Regression remains a transparent baseline and calibrated SVM is competitive. Feature analysis identifies thyroid-stimulating hormone and free-thyroxine-related variables as the dominant predictors. A lightweight web prototype demonstrates patient/laboratory input and real-time prediction output for hypothyroid-pattern and euthyroid cases. The framework is …
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Reply to the comment by Kuzukıran Kocataş on “Can full-stay lactate burden predict ICU mortality? The importance of a defined prediction time”
Development and internal validation of a serum ferritin-based prediction model for coronary artery aneurysms in Kawasaki disease
abstract: Abstract Background: Kawasaki disease is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, and coronary artery aneurysms represent its most important cardiovascular complication. Identifying children at risk for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset is clinically important. Serum ferritin may reflect systemic inflammation in Kawasaki disease, but its incremental predictive value remains uncertain. This study developed a ferritin-based model for predicting coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks. Methods: Patients with Kawasaki disease were retrospectively identified at a single centre and randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts in a 6:4 ratio. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and reclassification metrics. Results: Among 378 patients, 98 (25.9%) had coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset. The ferritin-based model included male sex, platelet count, serum ferritin, albumin ≤ 31.5 g/L, and baseline maximum coronary artery Z score ≥ 2.5. Adding serum ferritin increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.853 to 0.899 in the training cohort and from 0.842 to 0.868 in the internal validation cohor…

title: Adverse Drug Reaction Detection with Drug Prediction Using BERT–LSTM–SVM
abstract: Social media can be a useful resource for assessing patient-reported drug experiences. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important public health issue, but finding social media posts in which adverse reactions are described is a difficult task, since not all posts are related to ADR. The proposed work in this research is a hybrid model of BERT-LSTM-SVM for detection of ADRs and drug classification. The input is preprocessed as follows: the text is cleaned, tokenized, normalized, and noise is removed. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) is used to produce contextual representations of the text, and a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) is used to model sequential dependencies to aid binary classification of ADR and non-ADR text. Then, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier is used to classify the associated medicine based on the extracted textual features. In our validation of the method, the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and precision were 0.99 with a recall. The proposed framework combines contextual language representations, sequential modeling, and supervised classification approaches to facilitate the automatic detection of ADRs and medicine identification.

title: Physics-Constrained Machine Learning Based Long-Term Performance Prediction Method for Asphalt Pavements
abstract: Long-range pavement forecasting should incorporate nonlinear dependencies between traffic, structure, climate, and material aging processes without creating unrealistic degradation paths. In this work, a physics-constrained machine-learning architecture is proposed, utilizing the Federal Highway Administration Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) data set. Multivariate time series consisting of annual records of International Roughness Index (IRI), rutting depth, cracking severity, traffic loads, structure characteristics, material properties, and climate factors are used for training of the two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. The loss function consists of prediction error and soft constraints on deterioration continuity, untreated section monotonicity, cumulative traffic damage, climate aging, and physically realistic condition boundaries. The forecasting performance is examined at 5, 10, 15, and 20-year horizons for random forest, XGBoost, and unphysical LSTM methods. For 20-year forecasts, IRI, rut depth, and cracking RMSE errors were 0.284±0.031 m/km, 2.18±0.26 mm, and 5.73±0.61 percentage points, respectively. Deterioration direction violations were reduced to 2.7±0.8% and the deviation of the timing of the serviceability threshold violation was 1.34±0.29 years. The results indicate that embedding engineering deterioration knowledge improves both long-…

title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Early Seizure Prediction in Pediatric Epilepsy Using Hybrid Deep Neural Networks and Multi-Resolution EEG Analysis
abstract: Early seizure prediction in Pediatric epilepsy remains a significant clinical challenge due to complex neurophysiological dynamics, high inter-patient variability, and the non-stationary nature of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Although deep learning models have demonstrated promising performance in seizure detection, their translation into clinical practice is limited by insufficient interpretability and inadequate modelling of multi-scale temporal patterns preceding seizure onset. Addressing these limitations, this study proposes a clinically interpretable hybrid deep neural network framework for early seizure prediction using multi-resolution EEG analysis in paediatric patients. Multi-channel scalp EEG recordings obtained from the CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database were pre-processed using adaptive bandpass filtering and artifact suppression techniques to enhance signal quality. A discrete wavelet transform–based multiresolution decomposition strategy was employed to capture time–frequency characteristics across delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands, enabling robust representation of preictal dynamics. The extracted feature maps were integrated into a hybrid CNN–BiLSTM architecture designed to simultaneously learn spatial correlations across EEG channels and long-range temporal dependencies. To enhance clinical transparency, gradient-based attribution mapping and SHAP-driv…

Blockchain-Federated Learning using advanced Bayesian LSTM-FAN for Real Option Valuation prediction
abstract: Real Option Valuation (ROV) forecasting is an estimate of the value of flexible investment opportunities in the presence of uncertainty treating them as financial options. Unlike conventional valuation techniques, ROV considers the acknowledgment of strategic choices that can be decided by managers, like waiting, growing, or shelving a project depending on evolving market conditions. Forecasting methodologies tend to employ simulations and complex models, such as Deep Learning (DL), to predict uncertain variables affecting option value. This strategy delivers a more realistic and flexible evaluation, enabling organizations to make more informed decisions in the context of uncertainty. This work aims to design a hybrid DL model for ROV prediction. The key objective is to design a blockchain-Federated Learning (FL) model integrated with DL for ROV prediction. FL constructs a global model by aggregating locally trained models on the blockchain so that the collaboratively trained global model can give improved and more accurate predictions. The local model learns with the proposed Bayesian Long Short-Term Network-Fourier Analysis Networks (BayesianLSTM-FAN), a fusion of Bayesian Long Short-Term Network (BayesianLSTM) and Fourier Analysis Networks (FAN). The data is preprocessed first by data cleaning and scaling (StandardScaler) and then by statistical feature extraction (Rolling w…

Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction
abstract: Abstract Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. Here we benchmark three ML-based structure prediction models, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold3 (AF3), against a curated data set of viral antigen-nanobody complexes deposited after the AF3 training cutoff. AF3 outperformed the other models: success (interface DockQ > 0.23) rose from 33% with a single seed to 50% and 65% with 10 and 100 seeds-per-target, respectively, compared with 18% for Boltz-2 and 30% for Chai-1. Using an expanded data set, we evaluated confidence metrics and found that a strict ipTM cutoff of 0.8, or a combination of ipTM ≥ 0.6 with a CDR3 loop pLDDT ≥ 60, reliably excluded incorrect predictions while retaining most successful ones. We further establish best practices for two AF3-specific capabilities, the choice of antigen multimeric state and the inclusion of N-glycosylation, both of which can be decisive for epitope success depending on the target. Finally, we apply these guidelines to two design problems: ranking a library of VEEV-neutralizing nanobodies and mapping the epitope of the broadly neutralizing nanobo…

Simulated Feature Fusion for Parkinson’s Disease Prediction Using Non-aligned Public Handwriting and Voice Datasets
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects over 10 million people worldwide, with prevalence increasing due to aging populations. Early symptoms such as tremor, micrographia, bradykinesia, and voice changes often remain undetected until substantial neuronal loss has occurred, leading to irreversible damage and increased treatment costs. This paper presents a comparative study of five machine learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (RBF Kernel), K-Nearest Neighbors, and XGBoost—for Parkinson’s disease prediction using handwriting and voice-based features. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC, 5-fold cross-validation, ROC curve analysis, feature importance analysis, and SHAP-based explainability.XGBoost achieved the highest test-set F1-score (0.7407) and AUC (0.8329), while SVM achieved the highest average cross-validation F1-score. Decision-level fusion further improved recall (0.88) while maintaining competitive overall performance. K-Nearest Neighbors produced the lowest overall performance, while XGBoost achieved the best balance between classification accuracy, F1-score, and AUC.

Cultural Perceptions and Country Brands in the Global Art Market
abstract: This study bridges a gap in the literature concerning brand image, country of origin, and consumer perceptions of luxury products, specifically exploring the relatively unknown roles of geographic distance and sales transaction location. Utilizing the luxury art market, data encompassing 1726 transactions over thirty years was collected. The study examined the relationship between sale price and cultural indulgence, as well as the relationship between sale price and the distance between the sale location and the artist's home nation. The methodology employed three separate multiple linear regressions: a base model incorporating artist nationality, gender, and art history textbook representation; the base model plus cultural indulgence; and the base model plus geographical distance. Results indicated that auction houses located in more culturally indulgent areas command a premium, as do those located farther from the artist's home nation. The data is limited to two-dimensional artworks post-1750, included in prominent art history texts, and only includes auction sale price information. It is suggested that future researchers explore different art transactions or other industries like collectible luxury sports cars. The Influence Mechanism of Housing Affordability Stratification on Community Public Service Accessibility
abstract: The issue of housing affordability has become an important factor that defines not only where people can live but also where they can actually access the services of the city. This research explores the impact of housing affordability stratification on public service accessibility in New York City and transmission of such effects through public service resource density and transit connectivity. The data obtained from the 2023 American Community Survey about socioeconomics of census tracts of New York City is merged with housing data from NYC PLUTO, public service facilities' data from NYC Open Data and pedestrian network data from OpenStreetMap. Housing cost burden of households is divided into three strata using the Jenks natural breaks classification. Healthcare, education, parks, libraries and public transit accessibility is calculated using an advanced version of the network-based two-step floating catchment area method and is weighted using entropy weights. Further analysis includes spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatial durbin modeling and mediation analysis. As a result of simulation of the proposed research design, tracts with high cost burden have a lower value of accessibility index (Mean = 0.486, SD = 0.137) compared to low burden tracts (Mean = 0.672, SD = 0.118). title: Does Green Brand Equity Buffer or Burn? Understanding Boundary Conditions in Justice Evaluations of Sharing Economy Service Failure
abstract: Abstract The authors investigate green brand equity as a representation of firm phenotype in terms of its impact on the relationship between perceived justice of service recovery and customer citizenship and behavioral loyalty behavior. The firm phenotype of GBE can perform different roles as a moral signal, a normative expectation or a value laden identity cue. The purpose of this study is to identify the role/s performed in the fair recovery of sharing economy service failure. Drawing on the tradeoff between expectation-disconfirmation versus judgment assimilation-categorization, this study seeks to understand the buffering/incendiary influence of green brand equity in the context of service recovery in a sustainable services context. The findings of the conceptual model are empirically verified through surveys distributed to 804 digitally engaged sharing economy consumers using Partial-Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The results reveal that while consumers demonstrate desirable citizenship towards the firm when it is perceived to be a high green brand equity firm that delivers fair service recovery, it does not extend the same leeway in terms of service re-patronage. The conclusion of the study is that sustainability signaling, though morally rewarded in the long-term through citizenship connoting judgment assimilation may not necessarily transform into a short-t…

title: Reconsidering green logistics adoption: the role of perceived behavioral control and ESG information in shippers' selection of logistics service providers
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how perceived behavioral control and environmental, social and governance (ESG) information shape shippers' adoption of green logistics service providers. Specifically, the study aims to (1) investigate the presence of an intention–behavior gap in green logistics adoption and (2) assess whether ESG information enhances perceived behavioral control, thereby facilitating actual adoption behavior within an extended theory of planned behavior (TPB) framework. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a quantitative survey-based research design. Data were collected from shippers involved in logistics service provider selection and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The research framework integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with persuasion theory, incorporating ESG information as an external antecedent influencing perceived behavioral control, behavioral intention and actual adoption behavior. Findings The results show that environmental attitudes significantly influence behavioral intention, while subjective norms do not. Behavioral intention does not directly translate into actual green logistics adoption, indicating a clear intention–behavior gap. Perceived behavioral control has a strong and direct effect on actual adoption behavior. ESG information significantly enhances perceived behavioral control, indirectly s…

Service use following violence: insights from the linked administrative data in South Wales
abstract: Abstract Background To better support victim-survivors of violence and inform violence prevention initiatives, it is important to understand potential barriers and facilitators for using services such as healthcare and police. Administrative data are often limited to the users of a particular service, while linked data provides an opportunity to examine factors associated with the use of multiple services or one over the other. The present research used linked emergency department (ED) and police data from South Wales to understand the individual and contextual factors associated with the use of healthcare and police support. Methods Analyses of the sociodemographic characteristics of victims and characteristics of violent incidents were conducted for the incidents that appeared in the police data only, ED data only, and both services. Adjusted logistic regressions were used to examine factors associated with contacting both services and police first. Results Victims of violent incidents that happened at the victim’s home rather than on the street were more likely to approach the police in addition to the ED. Those who experienced violence from a current or former partner were also more likely to approach the police first than those who experienced violence from a stranger. title: The contingent effects of AI transparency in service recovery: a moderated mediation model of perceived warmth and competence
abstract: Purpose This research investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) transparency shapes consumer responses in service recovery. By revealing the reasoning process behind AI decisions, transparency functions as an anthropomorphic cue that humanizes the system's communication. Drawing on social cognitive theory, the research develops and tests a generalizable mechanism framework linking AI transparency, consumer cognition and recovery satisfaction, while identifying boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach Three scenario-based experiments were conducted. Study 1 (N = 98) tested the direct effect of AI transparency on recovery satisfaction. Study 2 (N = 230) examined the parallel mediating roles of perceived warmth and competence. Study 3 (N = 284) tested the moderating role of service failure severity and the corresponding conditional indirect effects. Findings AI transparency significantly improves recovery satisfaction, indirectly through perceived warmth and competence. Service failure severity moderated the effects of transparency on both mediators. The indirect effects through warmth and competence were significant under low service failure severity but not under high severity, identifying severity as a boundary condition for the effectiveness of AI transparency in service recovery. Originality/value This research conceptualizes AI transparency as a form of anthropom…

abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, the effect of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, the effect of company image on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, and the simultaneous effect of service quality, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and company image on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants at the Makassar Branch of the BPJS Employment. This study used a quantitative approach, with the research object being the Makassar Branch of the BPJS Employment. The sample consisted of 100 workplace accident insurance participants. Data analysis techniques included instrument testing, classical assumption testing, multivariate regression analysis, and hypothesis testing. This study found that service quality had a positive and significant effect on the satisfaction of work accident insurance participants. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) had a positive and significant effect on the satisfaction of work accident insurance participants. How are Perfectionistic Strivings and Perfectionistic Concerns Differentially Associated with Emotion Regulation
abstract: Perfectionism includes perfectionistic strivings and perfectionistic concerns, and both dimensions lead to different emotion regulation. This review looks at how the two dimensions link with emotion regulation and why these differences happen. Past studies show that perfectionistic strivings usually connect with better emotion regulation strategies, like cognitive reappraisal and accepting bad feelings. But perfectionistic concerns link with negative emotions, rumination, expressive suppression and emotion-regulation problems. These differences can be explained by their motivation types. Perfectionistic strivings connect more to approach-oriented and autonomous motivation, while perfectionistic concerns connect to avoidance-oriented and controlled motivation. However, researchers still disagree on whether perfectionistic strivings can buffer perfectionistic concerns when both are very high. So, the link between perfectionism and emotion regulation is not just about single dimensions, but also depends on how they work together.

title: TECHNOLOGY, REGULATION, AND THE DIVERGENT TRAJECTORIES OF RETAIL AND CROSS-BORDER CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY
abstract: Background. Central bank digital currency (CBDC) sits where fast-moving cryptographic and ledger technology meets fast-moving regulation, yet the two are usually studied separately, and retail and cross-border uses are usually treated as one object. Between 2024 and 2026 major jurisdictions made sharply different regulatory choices. Research Purpose. This review examines how advanced cryptographic solutions and hybrid blockchain architectures interact with evolving regulatory frameworks to shape economic outcomes and user adoption, and how that interaction differs between retail and cross-border implementations. Research Method. We conduct a critical review. A Scopus search on 8 October 2026 (1,418 records, 1,045 retained) maps the field, and a purposive selection of peer-reviewed studies and official publications is synthesised around four research questions. Findings. Technology and regulation terms co-occur at about the level expected by chance, and evidence on cryptographic feasibility and on adoption comes largely from separate literatures. Hybrid, two-tier architectures dominate, and the tension between privacy and anti-money laundering is increasingly handled through cryptographic design. Retail adoption is weak in every live system reviewed, while wholesale cross-border arrangements show the clearest technological value but are limited by governance. Regulatory choices …

Emotion regulation, academic resilience, and perceived stress in health professions students: a cross-sectional analysis of indirect associations
abstract: Background Health professions students face substantial academic and clinical demands that may increase perceived stress. Previous studies have examined emotion regulation and academic resilience separately, but little is known about whether academic resilience is related to the association between emotion regulation and perceived stress. Academic resilience was examined because students who regulate their emotions more effectively may be better able to cope with academic difficulties, and greater resilience may in turn be associated with lower perceived stress. This study examined the associations of emotion regulation with academic resilience and perceived stress, as well as their indirect associations with perceived stress through academic resilience. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 180 health professions students recruited from a medical university in Taiwan using convenience sampling. Participants completed measures of emotion regulation, academic resilience, and perceived stress. Cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression were analyzed separately. Pearson correlation analyses and PROCESS Model 4 were used to examine the proposed associations and statistical indirect associations. title: Association between self-reported resistance-exercise frequency and abdominal adiposity among Chinese adults: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Resistance exercise is included in adult physical activity recommendations, but the weekly frequency associated with abdominal adiposity in free-living adults remains unknown. We examined the association between self-reported weekly resistance-exercise frequency and abdominal adiposity; an exploratory secondary analysis compared ≥3 days/week with 2 days/week. Methods This single-center cross-sectional study analyzed 913 Chinese adults selected from the 3,411 adults consecutively screened at the Health Examination Center of Taizhou People’s Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University between November 2025 and July 2026. Self-reported resistance exercise was grouped as 0, 1, 2, or ≥3 days/week. Body roundness index (BRI) was the primary outcome, with waist circumference, body mass index (BMI), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) as the secondary outcomes. Multivariable linear regression analyses with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors were adjusted for age, sex, aerobic moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), sedentary time, smoking history, and alcohol consumption. The primary analysis used complete cases; multiple imputation was used to evaluate robustness in the 2,958 participants remaining after clinical exclusions, alongside additional sensitivity analyses. abstract: Introduction The present study explores how technoference in parent -child interactions is linked to emotional and behavioral problems in preschool aged children and examines whether emotion regulation and self-regulation function as serial mediators in this relationship. Methods To evaluate the proposed associations, mediation analysis was carried out using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). A crosssectional research design was employed in the present study. The study sample consisted of 518 children attending independent preschools located in the central districts of Denizli, Türkiye, along with their parents. Among the children, 304 were girls (58.7%) and 214 were boys (41.3%). Of the children, 216 (41.7%) were 5 years old, and 302 (58.3%) were 6 years old. Data were collected using the Technoference Scale in Parent Child Relationships, Emotion Regulation Scale, Psychological Well-Being Scale for 5 and 6 Year Old Children (PWBSC), and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). The technoference Scale in Parent -Child Relationships was completed by parents, whereas the other measures were completed by teachers. title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
abstract: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. Coaching is justified by its capacity to build independent, self-regulating professionals, but it is typically structured in a way that locates diagnosis, goal setting, strategic planning, and accountability in the coach rather than the client. The result can be improvement that does not outlive the engagement. This paper introduces Self-Directed Coaching (SDC) as a theory-based framework that repositions the client as the principal agent of their own developmental regulation. Grounded in self-determination theory, intentional change theory, regulatory focus theory, self-directed and self-regulated learning, cybernetic control theory, and attachment theory, SDC reframes coaching as a scaffolded process whose intended end-state is reduced dependence on formal coaching support. The framework’s central mechanism is self-regulatory internalization, the progressive transfer of coaching functions from an external agent to the client’s own regulatory repertoire. Exit without Migration: Cloud Switching and Operational Continuity in EU Law
abstract: Abstract EU law can make cloud exit legally enforceable while leaving migration operationally uncertain. This article asks why a customer with a binding right to leave a cloud provider may still lack a workable way to continue the service elsewhere. Reading the EU Data Act alongside the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), it shows how switching and operational continuity depend on conditions governed by different obligations and actors. The Data Act addresses provider-side switching obstacles but bounds the departing provider’s responsibility where reconstruction also depends on the customer, the destination environment and differentiated service functionality. In finance, DORA requires financial entities to prepare for continuity of critical or important functions. These limits on provider responsibility can be proportionate, even as migration remains operationally uncertain. The article argues that DORA’s existing requirements for feasible, tested and continuity-preserving exit plans should substantiate a credible path for reconstituting and continuing the regulated function after exit. More broadly, it shows how individually defensible regulatory duties can leave a shared operational outcome insufficiently substantiated when responsibility is distributed across instruments.

More Than a Coin Flip: Forced-Choice Performance Above the Binomial Mean and Word-Frequency Bias on the Word Memory Test Under Sham Random Responding
abstract: Abstract Below-chance performance on forced-choice performance validity tests (PVTs) is typically interpreted against a binomial model that assumes a .50 probability under uninformed responding. We tested whether this assumption holds for the Word Memory Test (WMT) and whether item-level lexical properties account for departures from the binomial expectation using a sham extrasensory perception (ESP) paradigm to elicit uninformed (i.e., “random”) responding. Fifty-five undergraduates completed the WMT Immediate Recognition (IR) trial without prior exposure to the study list. Total scores and item-level responses were tested against exact binomial expectations. Pair-level lexical contrasts (target minus foil) for log word frequency, age of acquisition, concreteness, and orthographic distance were derived from the English Lexicon Project and examined as predictors of item selection in ordinary least squares (OLS) and generalized estimating equation (GEE) models. Mean IR performance was 24.15 of 40 (60.4% correct), exceeding the binomial mean, t(54) = 8.40, p < .001, d = 1.13. Eighteen IR items deviated from .50 after false-discovery-rate correction, predominantly toward the keyed-correct word. title: Dupilumab-associated eosinophilia in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: frequency, temporal dynamics, predictors, and clinical consequences—a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Dupilumab may cause a treatment-emergent rise in circulating eosinophils, but the frequency, temporal pattern, predictors, and clinical consequences of hypereosinophilia (HE) in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) remain incompletely defined. Methods We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase.com studies reporting post-treatment circulating eosinophil outcomes in dupilumab-treated CRSwNP. Potentially overlapping reports were linked at the cohort and outcome level. The primary outcome was post-treatment HE ≥1,500 cells/µL, synthesized using a binomial-normal random-effects generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with a logit link. Results The combined searches identified 368 records; after deduplication, 255 records were screened, 72 reports underwent full-text assessment, and 50 eligible reports mapped to 42 study/cohort clusters. Six independent cohorts contributed 172 HE events among 1,047 patients, yielding a pooled HE proportion of 7.9% [95% confidence interval (CI), 2.8%–20.1%; τ = 1.19]. Following outcome-specific risk-of-bias reassessment, a sensitivity analysis excluding the two high-risk cohorts retained four studies (166 events among 865 patients) and yielded 12.1% (95% CI, 3.9%–32.0%; τ = 1.06). title: Functional contribution of the gut microbiota to digestive capacity during ontogeny in greater amberjack (Seriola dumerili) larvae
abstract: Introduction The intestinal microbiota is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to host digestive physiology; however, its potential contribution to digestive capacity during fish larval development remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the coordinated development of host digestive physiology and gut microbial function throughout larval ontogeny in greater amberjack ( Seriola dumerili ) larvae sampled at 10, 19, 32, 40 and 60 days post-hatching (dph), covering the main dietary transitions from live prey feeding through co-feeding with formulated diets to post-weaning. Methods Intestinal digestive enzyme activities were quantified in parallel with the enzymatic potential of the associated bacterial community, allowing, for the first time in marine fish larvae, the estimation of the potential contribution of the microbiota to digestive capacity. These analyses were integrated with 16S rRNA gene sequencing, FAPROTAX functional prediction, indicator taxa analyses and zymography to characterize the taxonomic and functional maturation of the intestinal microbiota. Results Host digestive capacity underwent marked ontogenetic changes associated with major dietary transitions. abstract: Abstract Background The World Health Organization Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) pathway has yielded inconsistent effects on locomotor capacity, partly because transitions from assessment to intervention are fragmented in community settings. We merged ICOPE steps 1 and 2 for the locomotion domain into a single encounter (4-m walk test [4MWT] and five-times sit-to-stand test [FTSST]), followed by a four-movement progressive resistance-training program and week-8 reassessment, delivered through a blended eHealth and community model embedded in Taiwan’s Long-Term Care 2.0 tier-C network. Methods In this retrospective, quasi-experimental study, 858 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 60 years were assessed at baseline; after seven exclusions, 851 were analyzed (811 intervention; 40 self-selected, assessment-only comparators, 15 with baseline impairment). Participants were stratified by baseline locomotor status (impaired: 4MWT speed < 1.0 m/s and/or FTSST > 10.8 s). Building capacity in institutional voids: carbon competency development among quantity surveyors in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment
abstract: Purpose This study assesses the training needs and competency strategies that quantity surveyors (QSs) perceive as important for enhancing embodied carbon estimation (ECE) in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment. It addresses gap in understanding how global sustainability norms may be taken up by a profession traditionally focused on cost management, in a setting where institutional pressures remain limited. Design/methodology/approach This organization-based study collected data from 132 quantity surveying firms (QSFs) in Lagos, Nigeria, using a structured questionnaire covering 21 training needs and competency strategies. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to rank the perceived importance of these items and to identify the underlying competency clusters. Findings The factor analysis identified two clusters of perceived training needs and competency strategies: (1) technical and operational capacity building comprising skills for lifecycle assessment and the use of carbon digital tools; and (2) knowledge infrastructure and strategic integration, comprising systemic support such as carbon databases and online resources and industry guidelines. All 21 competency strategies were rated as highly important, suggesting that respondents did not strongly differentiate among them and regarded all of them as priorities for impro…
venue: Journal of Knowledge, Risk, and Sustainable Management

title: Capacity and Electrochromism Decoupling Strategy for Real-Time State-of-Charge Monitoring of High-Areal-Capacity Electrochromic Batteries
abstract: Abstract State-of-charge (SOC) is a central parameter in battery management systems for electric vehicles, directly affecting driving range, power delivery, safety, and battery lifetime. However, real-time and high-precision SOC monitoring remains a challenge for practical batteries. Here, we report a capacity and electrochromism decoupling strategy for real-time SOC monitoring of high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. The bilayer cathode combines a pure electrochromic coloration layer with an underlying conductive, high-loading capacity layer, thereby spatially separating optical readout from high-capacity storage. The device delivers an areal capacity of 3.4 mAh cm–2 with 97.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The monotonic SOC–Hue relationship with 1% SOC intervals was established by converting in situ reflectance spectra into Hue values. The modulation of reflectance-peak wavelength shift retains 81.2% after 1000 coloration cycles. This architecture provides a route toward batteries with built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.

title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
abstract: Abstract Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. Here we quantify this divergence using an integrated city-scale framework that combines spatial landfill siting, engineering-based net-present-value modeling, and satellite-derived metropolitan gross domestic product. Applying this framework across six developing megacities with over 100 million residents, we find that all cities possess surplus land meeting screening-level suitability criteria. Required cost-recovery tipping fees range from 54–130 US dollars per tonne, with 5 th –95 th -percentile intervals of ±25%–30% under joint parameter uncertainty. Under full household cost recovery, these fees imply annual disposal costs equivalent to 1.2%–2.0% of the minimum wage, whereas associated revenue requirements represent only 0.26%–1.04% of metropolitan gross domestic product. Across cities, household affordability is uncorrelated with metropolitan economic capacity. Landfill depth is the dominant engineering control on affordability, particularly in high-rainfall systems, but cost allocation exerts greater leverage than any design parameter. Thus, techn…

title: Security Indexing Coding under the Eavesdropper Model: A Review of Capacity Boundaries and Secure Indexing Methods
abstract: With 5G and Internet technology developing quickly, broadcast and multicast communications are widely applied in many scenarios such as the Internet of Vehicles, edge distributed networks and group transmission for the Internet. Wireless broadcast channels are open, but transmitted signals are easy to intercept and pose a risk of data leakage. This study focuses on a survey of secure index encoding. This work defines the secure index encoding model, adversary model, strong security and weak security. Based on the above, it discusses how to use and where to use linear coding and random linear coding. Through analysis, this paper find that secure index encoding also have some troubles, like inaccurate minimum rank, difficulty in solving optimal coding solution and hard to achievement. This paper reviews the theoretical framework of secure index encoding based on existing research, which can provide a reference for more in-depth research in the future.

title: It’s all in my head: informal visitor knowledge and capacity constraints on Vermont agritourism farms
abstract: Agritourism, opening farms to visitors, can contribute to food systems sustainability goals, including economic prosperity and livelihoods, social engagement, environmental quality, and human health. Agritourism is particularly important in states like Vermont where direct-to-consumer sales and community engagement are part of the rural fabric. While much scholarship has focused on farmer motivation and economic outcomes, less research has examined how operators come to know their visitors and what limits their use of marketing information. We report on year one of a multi-year project on how Vermont agritourism operators understand their visitors, what visitors’ information they currently collect or want, and what capacity constraints affect their ability to use it. We conducted semi-structured interviews with operators of 10 farms (December 2025-January 2026) and analyzed them thematically. Findings indicate that all 10 operators relied on informal, memory-based visitor knowledge, and nine had no formal system for collecting or analyzing visitor data. All 10 named word of mouth as a visitor discovery channel; nine used social media, at widely varying levels of activity. Operators most wanted to know what activities visitors are interested in and how visitors find the farm, and all farmers wanted to use visitor data for planning. Several farmers cited time constraints, a lack …

title: VALUE IDENTITY AND PSYCHOLOGICAL RESILIENCE: COLLABORATIVE MECHANISM BETWEEN NATIONAL SECURITY EDUCATION AND MENTAL HEALTH EDUCATION IN THE CONTEXT OF PRECISION IDEOLOGICAL AND POLITICAL EDUCATION
abstract: The integration of mental health education and national security education has become an important issue in higher education, particularly in promoting students’ psychological development, value identification, and civic responsibility. Based on the concept of precision-oriented ideological and political education, this study explores a collaborative education model that integrates curriculum content, teaching methods, learning environments, and evaluation systems. It proposes a “national security–people’s security–psychological resilience” framework, arguing that security awareness should be transformed from knowledge acquisition into emotional identification, psychological resilience, and responsible action. By connecting psychological mechanisms with value-oriented education, this study provides a new perspective for developing students’ security literacy, psychological resilience, and responsible citizenship, while offering practical implications for innovation in higher education.

title: Plastisphere Formation on Microplastics: A Key Mechanism for Potential Toxic Element Accumulation in Wetlands
Analysis of the Coercivity Mechanism of High-Performance Nd-Fe-B Magnets Prepared by Synergistic Diffusion
abstract: Abstract The grain boundary diffusion process is an important approach for preparing high-performance Nd-Fe-B magnets. In this study, Nd-Fe-B diffusion magnets with both high remanence and high coercivity were prepared via a two-step synergistic diffusion process. The process combined Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion with subsequent DyH3 diffusion. Compared with DyH3 diffusion alone, this two-step synergistic diffusion strategy increased the coercivity increment from 3.30 to 3.84 kOe while maintaining a remanence of 15.03 kG. Microstructural and elemental analyses showed that Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion modified the grain-boundary phase and promoted Dy diffusion to greater depths. The modified grain boundaries facilitated the formation of continuous (Dy, RE)2Fe14B shells around the main-phase grains. These shells increased the local magnetocrystalline anisotropy and strengthened the grain edges against reverse-domain nucleation. Micromagnetic simulations indicated that a complete core-shell structure increased the demagnetization nucleation field at grain edges, thereby suppressing magnetic domain reversal. This study establishes a direct relationship between grain-boundary modification, shell continuity, and coercivity enhancement in Nd-Fe-B magnets.

title: Failure mechanism of rotational landslide on red bed triggered by heavy rainfall–a case study from the Wushanping landslide, Chongqing Province, China
Solvent Effects on the Photophysical Mechanism of a 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone Derivative with TICT Characteristics
abstract: Abstract 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone derivatives serve as solid-state laser materials and promising high-sensitivity fluorescent probes with TICT and ESIPT dual photophysical pathways, yet their solvent-dependent mechanisms remain ambiguous. Herein, synthesized 2’-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzochalcone (HMBC) was systematically explored via spectroscopic characterization and theoretical calculations in three aprotic solvents of varied polarity. Increasing solvent polarity induces a gradual red shift in the absorption peaks, and dual fluorescence emission is observed with a significantly large Stokes shift for the long-wavelength band. DFT and TD-DFT results reveal that the initial hydroxyl proton configuration plays a critical role in directing the excited-state relaxation of HMBC. In combination with the extremely low fluorescence quantum yields measured in dilute solution, the excited-state behavior of HMBC was shown to be predominantly governed by TICT rather than ESIPT. Moreover, a clear correlation among solvent polarity, excited-state molecular torsion, charge-transfer character, and luminescence behavior was established. This work offers guidance for the rational design of advanced fluorescent probes toward environmental and biomedical detection based on 2’-hydroxylchalcone template.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A

title: Exploring the formation mechanism of new energy vehicle technology innovation network: a stimulus–response model analysis
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry based on the stimulus-response model and to analyze the dynamic interaction process among innovation subjects, platform and government under the market mechanism, platform participation and government regulation. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts static regression analysis to study the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry. Multiagent simulation model is used to explore the dynamic evolution mechanism of innovation network formation. Findings The research findings indicate that the innovation behavior of technology receivers is significantly influenced by their own technology cross-border search and technology internalization capability, and technology ecological niche of technology senders, information stimulation intensity, the level of platform participation and government regulation. The simulation results show that in the interaction among innovation subjects under the market mechanism, a greater number of enterprises choose technology-restructuring innovation. However, in the interaction between innovation subjects and the environment, a higher number of technology-distributed innovation subjects is observed. Originality/value This paper reveals the “black box” of technological innovation…

title: Research on the Mechanism of Offline Retail Visual Marketing Influence on Consumer Purchase Decisions
abstract: With the the rapid growth of online shopping, offline physical stores face declining customer traffic and intensified competition. Compared with online consumption, which is largely based on information presented through digital interfaces, offline stores use visual elements such as display windows, lighting, product displays, and digital displays to influence consumers' perceptions of the store environment, product value, and brand image, affecting purchase decisions. Based on SOR (Stimulus-Body-Response) theory and referencing foreign research on retail and consumer behavior from 2023 to 2026, this paper analyzes the pathways of visual marketing's influence on consumer decision-making from three perspectives: visual perception, emotional experience, and consumer behavior. It further explores the moderating roles of individual consumer characteristics, shopping contexts, and product attributes in shaping the effects of visual marketing. The study finds that a coordinated and orderly visual environment can boost consumers' perceived value of stores and products, enhance positive emotions, extend dwell time, and promote purchase intention formation. Issues such as visual information overload and chaotic spatial layout increase consumers' psychological burden, hence reducing shopping experience and purchase tendencies. Based on the research results, this paper proposes optimizati…

title: Biostimulant potential of Limnospira platensis biomass fermented with lactic acid bacteria in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris): strain characterization, biochemical shifts, and growth promotion
abstract: The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in conventional agriculture poses significant risks to soil health, environmental quality, and food security. Plant biostimulants derived from microorganisms, microalgae and cyanobacteria offer a sustainable alternative. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and cyanobacteria such as Limnospira platensis are recognized for their plant growth-promoting characteristics. However, the combined effects of LAB-fermented L. platensis biomass on common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) remain underexplored. This investigation assessed the phytostimulant potential of L. platensis extracts, live LAB, and LAB-fermented L. platensis extract on growth parameters, yield, soil microbiota, and chlorophyll content of P. vulgaris under field conditions. Five treatments were evaluated: T 1 (water, negative control), T 2 (commercial biostimulant containing humic/fulvic acids, amino acids, N-P-K, and micronutrients), T 3 (0.5% L. platensis biomass extract), T 4 (live LAB culture, 1.4 × 10 8 cells mL -1 ), and T 5 (0.5% extract of L. platensis biomass fermented with LAB). Foliar applications were applied weekly from week 2 to week 9. Phenological parameters, chlorophyll concentration (SPAD-calibrated), root nodulation, soil CFU, and final yield (kg ha -1 ) were measured. Results indicated that T 5 consistently yielded the highest values across all parameters…

title: Exogenous benzyl cyanide activates the somatic embryogenesis program in Arabidopsis
abstract: Abstract Phenylacetic acid (PAA) is a naturally occurring auxin whose biosynthesis and function during plant regeneration remain poorly understood. PAA may be synthesized from phenylalanine via the CYP79A2-dependent phenylacetaldoxime pathway, in which benzyl cyanide/phenylacetonitrile (BnCN/PAN) is a potential intermediate and substrate for NITRILASE (NIT) enzymes. Here, we investigated whether exogenous BnCN/PAN promotes somatic embryogenesis (SE) through NIT-dependent PAA biosynthesis. Low concentrations of BnCN/PAN stimulated somatic embryo formation in Arabidopsis thaliana , whereas exogenous PAA also promoted embryogenic induction. Transcriptome profiling revealed that BnCN/PAN upregulated genes associated with SE, including key embryogenic regulators and EMBRYO DEFECTIVE genes. RNA-seq data further indicated enhanced auxin signaling, which was independently confirmed using the pDR5::GUS reporter line. Inhibition of NIT activity by heatin reduced the embryogenic competence of BnCN/PAN-treated explants, supporting the involvement of NIT enzymes in this response. Collectively, our findings provide the first evidence that exogenous BnCN/PAN can promote embryogenic transition, and suggest that NIT-dependent metabolism may contribute to this response.

title: The assessment power of Gaokao English: washback, regulatory mediation, and educational inequality in the context of China's Double Reduction Policy
abstract: This conceptual analysis examines the assessment power of Gaokao English in contemporary China, focusing on how high-stakes foreign-language assessment influences teaching, learning, family investment, supplementary education, and educational inequality. Drawing on selected policy documents and published research on assessment washback, test impact, assessment as language policy, and linguistic capital, it develops a conceptual model of assessment power and regulatory mediation. Assessment power captures the capacity of a consequential assessment to organise expectations, preparation, and resource allocation, while regulatory mediation describes how policies governing the conditions of preparation reshape actors’ responses to assessment incentives. The analysis argues that Gaokao English exerts influence beyond the test event through anticipatory washback and broader test impact. The Double Reduction Policy illustrates how regulation can reshape the conditions and channels of preparation without removing the underlying incentives generated by high-stakes assessment. Students, schools, and families differ in the resources and opportunities available to them, and regulatory change may therefore shape differentiated forms of adaptation and reconfigure how educational advantage is pursued. By integrating the established distinction between washback and broader test impact and theor…

title: Euclid preparation. CXV. Galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum modelling
abstract: Higher-order correlation functions of the large-scale galaxy distribution offer access to information beyond that contained in standard two-point statistics, such as the power spectrum. In this work we assess the potential of the Euclid mission to provide such functions using synthetic catalogues of H,α galaxies based on the 54Ģpc Flagship 1 simulation, which is designed to reproduce the Euclid spectroscopic sample. We comprehensively validate the one-loop galaxy power spectrum and tree-level bispectrum predictions from perturbation theory in both real and redshift space. Assuming scale cuts consistent with our previous power spectrum study on the same catalogues, this modelling yielded unbiased cosmological constraints for the bispectrum up to ̊m max = 0.15̨Mpc in real space and 0.08 , (0.1)̨Mpc at the lowest (highest) redshift, corresponding to z=0.9 (z=1.8), for the monopole and quadrupole in redshift space using statistical uncertainties corresponding to the full simulation volume. With these scale cuts, adding bispectrum information to the power spectrum improves constraints on the amplitude of scalar perturbations and the matter density by up to 30%, increasing the overall figure of merit for key cosmological parameters by a factor of about 2.5. A simple rescaling of the statistical uncertainties to a Euclid -like volume indicates similar conclusions, highlighting the add…

title: Phenotyping replication strongly influences genomic predictive ability in sweet sorghum (Sorghum bicolor [L.] Moench)
abstract: Article summary Genomic selection can accelerate breeding when the phenotypic and genomic information used to train prediction models is sufficiently reliable and relevant to the prediction target. Using a sweet sorghum breeding population evaluated in three Haitian field environments, we quantified the effects of phenotyping replication, training population (TP) size, TP–validation population (VP) genomic relatedness, and prediction model on genomic predictive ability for grain yield, plant height, stem weight, and total soluble solids. Increasing phenotyping replication consistently improved predictive ability across traits and environments and increased the precision of phenotypic estimates, with particularly large effects observed for grain yield. Larger TPs generally improved predictive ability; however, when TP sizes of 150 and 200 individuals were compared, the effect of increasing phenotyping replication was consistently greater than that of increasing TP size. Greater TP–VP genomic relatedness was also generally associated with higher predictive ability, whereas differences among prediction models were comparatively small and inconsistent across traits and environments. These results provide empirical evidence that genomic prediction performance in sweet sorghum depends not only on prediction model choice but also on the design and quality of the TP. In particular, for…

title: Development of a UAV for vision-based fault detection in power transmission systems using deep learning
abstract: Purpose Reliable operation of power transmission systems depend on timely detection of insulator faults, yet conventional manual inspection is costly, hazardous and inconsistent. This study presents an unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)-based vision inspection approach integrating platform development, autonomous flight validation and a controlled multi-generation You Only Look Once (YOLO) benchmark for binary insulator fault detection. Design/methodology/approach A lightweight quadrotor UAV was developed and validated through six autonomous missions along a 132 kV transmission corridor near Prayagraj, India. A dataset of 3,951 annotated insulator images combining 3,173 UAV-collected images and 778 from a publicly available source, comprising 2,847 normal and 1,104 defective instances, was assembled with an 80:10:10 split and flight-level data leakage prevention. Five YOLO variants (YOLOv8s–YOLOv12s) were trained under matched conditions from Common Objects in Context (COCO)-pretrained weights. A FLUKE TiS75+ thermal camera was used separately as complementary qualitative evidence. Findings YOLOv8s achieved the best test-set performance: precision 0.895, recall 0.810, mAP@0.50 of 0.879 and mAP@0.50–0.95 of 0.482 at 142 FPS, outperforming all four newer YOLO generations. Thermal imaging at defective locations revealed hotspot temperatures of 83.5°C–197.6°C against backgrounds below…

title: Sexual assault medical and forensic examiners in regional and rural New South Wales, Australia: a qualitative study of experiences impacting workforce participation
Advanced Practice Nursing Students’ Experiences of the Virtual Learning Cafe Method
abstract: Background: The Learning Café method based on educational constructivism may increasingly be used as Online Learner Collaboration facilitated by the teacher. Purpose: This qualitative study draws together Advanced Practice Nursing students’ experiences of the Virtual Learning Café method. The findings can be useful when evaluating the suitability of the method for students undertaking Master-level health or social studies, especially from the perspective of developing evidence-based clinical practice and interprofessional collaboration. Materials and Methods: 28 nursing students earning a Master’s Degree in Advanced Practice Nursing were requested to write an essay reflecting on a Virtual Learning Café experience. The data was analyzed using inductive content analysis. Results: The study participants agreed that the Virtual Learning Café could be effectively used for both learning and development, or as a collaborative learning structure and as a model transferable to the development of health service practice. According to the participants, the method may be effective in development efforts for individual professionals, in interprofessional teams, in and between organizations, and between citizens and health service professionals. The participants appreciated the dialogic and participatory nature of the method and emphasized collective construction of knowledge. Conclusion: Th…
