Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
abstract: Objective: To evaluate 2-year weight loss after bariatric surgery among adults with intolerable adverse effects or inadequate weight loss with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Summary Background Data: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are effective obesity medications, but intolerance and inadequate weight loss are common, creating uncertainty about next-step therapy. Methods: This retrospective cohort included adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) at Cleveland Clinic hospitals from 2018 to 2024. Electronic health record and dispensing data classified preoperative semaglutide or tirzepatide exposure and response. The primary outcome was estimated 2-year total body weight loss (TBWL), stratified by procedure and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) status. Results: Among 4929 patients, 4661 had no prior exposure (comparator group), 61 discontinued semaglutide or tirzepatide because of intolerable adverse effects, and 207 had inadequate weight-loss response. Before surgery, estimated 2-year medication-associated weight change was a 1.4% gain in the intolerance group and 1.5% TBWL in the inadequate-response group. After surgery, 2-year TBWL in the intolerance group was 27.9% and 22.7% after RYGB and 20.1% and 21.6% after SG among patients without and with T2DM, respectively. Corresponding estimates in the inadequate-response group were 35.8%, 27.4%…

title: Religious Guidance Strategy through Majelis Taklim for Employees of the Koja Container Terminal, Jakarta
abstract: Workplace religious education must operate within organizational constraints that differ from community-based learning, particularly in continuous operations with rotating shifts. This study examined how Majelis Taklim functions as nonformal Islamic education for employees at Koja Container Terminal, Jakarta, and how its strategies, value internalization, participant experiences, and organizational conditions are interpreted. A constructivist qualitative case-study design was used. Six substantive semi-structured interviews were analyzed purposively: one manager, one Islamic spiritual-development organizer, two active participants, and two less-active participants. Data were coded in two cycles, compared across informant positions, and interpreted through social construction, knowing-feeling-acting, and workplace-spirituality lenses. The findings show an adaptive strategy characterized by needs mapping, contextual religious content, flexible scheduling, blended access, repeated materials, humanistic facilitators, and social activities. Internalization appeared through increased religious understanding, affective calmness, and reported everyday practice, but the pathway was not uniform. Less-active participants still valued the program while reporting barriers related to time, fatigue, location, transportation, digital limitations, and work priorities. Organizational support was…

title: An advanced control strategy for matrix converters in unbalanced grid voltage conditions
abstract: Purpose A novel control technique for the matrix converter (MC) under unbalanced grid voltage conditions is proposed in this paper. Compared to conventional direct AC–AC power conversion systems that require an intermediate DC link, matrix converters provide direct AC–AC conversion between sources with different phases and frequencies, and are compact and efficient. But maintaining balanced output voltage and current remains a significant challenge under grid voltage imbalance. This paper aims to propose a novel control technique for the matrix converter (MC) under unbalanced grid voltage (UGV) conditions. Design/methodology/approach To address this challenge, the proposed control algorithm uses a voltage imbalance compensation technique, a reference-frame transformation and space-vector modulation to achieve stable, balanced MC operation. Moreover, a new Matrix Converter Control-Deep Reinforcement framework is designed, comprising fundamental control features and processing steps for maximum adaptability and robustness under dynamic grid conditions. Findings The suggested method successfully maintains output voltage and current balance, even with a significant voltage imbalance in the grid, as demonstrated by extensive MATLAB simulations. Waveform regulation, output voltage control and speed response analysis are used to further validate the system’s performance. Originality/v…

title: Managing critical raw materials supply chains: aligning capabilities and strategic levers for effective strategy formation under uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms should design supply chain strategies to secure Critical Raw Materials (CRM), which are scarce, geographically concentrated, and exposed to geopolitical and institutional interference. These features generate structural uncertainty that amplifies normative and mimetic pressures on strategic decision-making, exposing firms to strategic isomorphic bias and leading organizations to replicate legitimized sourcing templates rather than formulate strategies calibrated to their specific dependence structure. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Resource Dependence Theory, the study links key strategic levers (Supplier Substitutability, Discretion over the Resource, and Importance of the Resource) to underlying supply chain capabilities (resilience, agility, flexibility, sustainability, efficiency). A rank-ordered logit choice experiment with supply chain managers elicits preferred capability configurations in CRM supply scenarios, allowing the inference of the associated strategic levers while reducing strategic isomorphic bias in self-reported strategies. Findings Results show that Supplier Substitutability emerges as the dominant strategic lever for CRM-intensive supply chains. Resilience and sustainability are identified as the core capabilities underpinning this lever, supporting rapid reconfiguration of the supply base and the maintenance o…

title: Risk-taking orientation and entrepreneurial strategy as drivers of business performance: evidence from private childcare centres in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose Entrepreneurial orientation (EO) is a recognised driver of firm performance, yet findings remain inconsistent and the mechanisms linking entrepreneurial behaviour to performance are underexplored in socially sensitive service sectors. This study examines whether risk-taking orientation affects business performance in private childcare centres in Indonesia via entrepreneurial strategy as a mediator. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 338 owners and managers of registered private childcare centres was conducted via cluster sampling from a population of 2,775 centres. 315 valid responses (93.2%) were analysed using partial least squares–structural equation Modelling with 5,000-resample bootstrapping. Findings Risk-taking orientation is positively associated with business performance, although this direct effect is comparatively modest. Entrepreneurial strategy shows a substantially stronger association with performance and partially mediates the risk-taking–performance relationship, suggesting that formalised strategic action represents a crucial structural path through which risk-taking orientation is associated with performance gains. Together, the two constructs account for a large share of the variance in business performance, and the measurement model demonstrates adequate discriminant validity and predictive relevance. Originality/value This study e…

Improving Accuracy and Interpretability of Educational App Recommendations via Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Abstract— As the usage of mobile apps in digital education is growing, it has become more critical to provide accurate and personalised recommendation systems that can enhance user engagement and learning effectiveness. The difficulty of collaborative filtering techniques is caused by the sparseness, dynamism and time dependence of crowdsourcing educational information. As a means of solving these problems, a mobile app recommendation framework is created with the help of a crowdsourced educational feedback dataset from Kaggle. It was methodologically preprocessed using timestamp creation, discard of irrelevant attributes, label encoding, and feature engineering (pivoting) and 80/20 train-test split. A number of machine and deep learning models are used including SVD, SVD++, NMF, SlopeOne, variations of KNN, CoClustering, BaselineOnly, NormalPredictor, GRU, LSTM, Stacked Autoencoder, Gated Autoencoder and hybrid LSTM-GRU. Explainable variance, MAE and RMSE are used to assess the model performance. The experimental results show that the hybrid LSTM-GRU consistently gives the minimum mean RMSE value of 0.267332 and mean MAE value of 0.118370 with the largest individual performance at k = 16 (RMSE = 0.005066, MAE = 0.003821). LIME and SHAP enhance the explainability, and user interface with Flask enables practical applicability. This technique increases the accuracy, robustness an…

title: Perceived Student Workload in English-Medium Instruction: Evidence from a Large-Scale Study in Business Education
abstract: This study examines differences in perceived academic workload between students enrolled in English-Medium Instruction (EMI) and non-EMI programs, contributing to the broader discussion on student experience in higher education. Drawing on a large sample of 11,427 course evaluations from a Business Administration degree at a Spanish university (2016–2019), we compare self-reported workload scores across groups. Results indicate that EMI students report slightly higher workloads, particularly in the first year and in subject areas such as Economics and Quantitative Methods. However, these differences diminish in subsequent years, and effect sizes are generally small or negligible. The findings suggest that while EMI students initially invest more effort, likely due to adapting to instruction in a non-native language, this additional workload is temporary. These results reinforce the viability of EMI programs and highlight the value of targeted first-year support to optimize the student learning experience.

title: Machine learning driven analysis and development of LD sludge-polypropylene composites for industrial tribo-components
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effect of Linz–Donawitz (LD) sludge reinforcement on the microhardness and abrasive wear behavior of polypropylene (PP) composites, and to optimize and predict the specific wear rate (SWR) using Taguchi design and an artificial neural network (ANN) model for improved performance and sustainable utilization of industrial waste. Design/methodology/approach PP composites reinforced with 0–20 Wt.% LD sludge were fabricated by compression molding. Microhardness was measured using a micro-indentation test. Three-body abrasive wear tests were conducted according to ASTM standards and analyzed using Taguchi L25 design. An ANN model was developed to predict the SWR. Findings The incorporation of LD sludge significantly enhanced the microhardness and abrasive wear resistance of PP composites. Microhardness increased from 0.059 GPa for neat PP to 0.639 GPa at 20 Wt.% filler content. SWR decreased considerably with increasing LD sludge, indicating improved abrasion resistance. Taguchi analysis identified sliding velocity and filler content as the most influential parameters affecting wear behavior. The ANN model accurately predicted SWR with errors below 9%, confirming its effectiveness for reliable wear performance prediction. Originality/value This study demonstrates the effective utilization of industrial LD sludge as a reinforcement in PP comp…

title: TyG-CVAI for identifying hyperuricemia: geographical external validation, model updating, and explainable machine learning
abstract: Background TyG-CVAI can be calculated from routine metabolic and anthropometric measurements, but evidence for same-visit identification of prevalent hyperuricemia across regions, its incremental value beyond conventional variables, and its advantage over the constituent variables themselves remains limited. Objective To assess the geographical transportability of the triglyceride-glucose Chinese visceral adiposity index (TyG-CVAI) for identifying prevalent hyperuricemia and to determine whether model updating or more complex machine-learning methods materially improve externally validated performance. Methods We analyzed prospectively collected, single-visit health-examination and questionnaire data from 2,119 adults and performed a cross-sectional analysis. The Shandong center was used for model development (n=1,288) and the Jiangsu center for geographical external validation (n=831). Associations were estimated with multivariable logistic regression and robust Poisson regression, with restricted cubic splines for dose-response assessment. Single-index discrimination, transferred thresholds, calibration, decision-curve analysis, five prespecified logistic model formulations, recalibration, reverse validation, and dataset shift were evaluated. Machine-learning models were tuned by nested resampling in Shandong and evaluated once in Jiangsu; serum urate and all outcome-derived …

title: Visualizing use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
abstract: Purpose Higher education students are engaged with academic learning and research using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications. A major shift in pedagogical approach surfaces many challenges to academic integrity that urging to redefining assessment model and ethical literacy. This study aims to investigate impact of the GenAI apps among the students using survey of technical and non-technical disciplines. Survey is mainly focused on: use of GenAI apps, variations in observed effectiveness and student’s usage pattern, level of adoption and acceptance of GenAI apps. Reviews of existing literature on the implications of GenAI and emerging need for systemic changes are discussed with reference to result. Design/methodology/approach Survey was developed to assess the integration of GenAI apps in the higher education. It was conducted with undergraduate and postgraduate students so as to find the adoption and acceptance rate of GenAI apps among the students; it has been partitioned into two categories: non-technical disciplines and technical disciplines. Students from the social science and pure sciences are in the non-technical disciplines, while students from computer science and engineering students are in the technical discipline. The questionnaire included a mix of multiple-choice questions, scale items and open-ended responses. Findings This research is classi…

title: The no mesh breast reconstruction evaluation (No-BRA) study: protocol for a national prospective audit and shared learning study of pre-pectoral implant-based breast reconstruction with no mesh
abstract: Introduction: Implant-based breast reconstruction (IBBR) is the most common reconstructive modality for women undergoing mastectomy in the United Kingdom (UK). Practice has evolved from subpectoral to pre-pectoral implant placement, typically utilizing a mesh for implant support. A newer iteration of this technique, which omits the use of mesh entirely, is gaining popularity but lacks a robust evidence base regarding its safety, effectiveness, and optimal application. This study is positioned within phases 2a/2b of the Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment, Long-term study (IDEAL) framework to formally evaluate this surgical innovation. The No-BRA study aims to conduct a national audit to explore the safety and effectiveness of immediate pre-pectoral IBBR without mesh to inform the delivery of best care. Methods and analysis: This is a national, multicenter, prospective audit aiming to recruit 350 patients from 15 to 20 UK centers. The study employs a dual-component design. The first component is a quantitative audit of clinical and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) for women undergoing immediate pre-pectoral IBBR with no mesh. The primary outcome is implant loss at 3 months post-surgery. Secondary outcomes include other key complications (e.g., infection, unplanned re-operation, and readmission) and PROMs (preoperatively, at 1.5 and 5 years), which will be benchma…

title: Large Language Model Driven Reinforcement Learning based Intelligent Control Method for Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Controllers which can interpret and react to high-dimensional process state and perturbations without loss of stability are needed for industrial cyber-physical systems. In this paper, we propose a large language model driven reinforcement learning approach based on semantic state augmentation using the Llama-3-8B model and a Proximal Policy Optimization controller. Process numerical values are converted to structured operation descriptions and concatenated with normalized feature vectors from sensors to provide the policy with both dynamics of the process and relationships between its components. We create an environment for experiments using Siemens Process Simulate software and Python 3.11 with Tennessee Eastman Process data. As a result, we demonstrate that the proposed controller achieves the normalized control RMSE of 0.158 ± 0.014 versus 0.223 ± 0.018 for classical PPO and a settling time of 8.47 ± 0.71 s versus 11.36 ± 0.94 s. Under combined disturbances, the proposed controller achieves a recovery time of 12.8 ± 1.1 s and a cumulative reward of 846.7 ± 25.8, demonstrating improved control accuracy and disturbance adaptability while maintaining computational feasibility.

title: Application of a problem-based learning teaching method based on mini-CEX and DOPS assessments in the teaching of clinical molecular biology testing in higher vocational colleges
abstract: Objective To develop a problem-based learning (PBL) teaching method incorporating Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX) and Direct Observation of Procedural Skills (DOPS) assessments, and to investigate its application effect in the teaching of Clinical Molecular Biology Testing in higher vocational colleges. Methods This study adopted a quasi-experimental design involving two intact classes of students majoring in Medical Laboratory Technology at a higher vocational college. The two classes were assigned to the control group (traditional teaching method) and the experimental group (PBL combined with Mini-CEX/DOPS assessments), respectively. The experimental group adopted a teaching approach driven by authentic clinical cases, with Mini-CEX assessments incorporated into each round of PBL teaching to evaluate clinical reasoning ability and DOPS assessments to evaluate laboratory procedural skills, followed by immediate structured feedback. A total of five rounds were conducted. The control group received only traditional teaching. At the end of the course, the teaching outcomes of the two groups were compared using a theoretical knowledge examination, an independent Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), and a satisfaction questionnaire. Results After teaching, the total OSCE scores, clinical case analysis scores, core procedural skills assessment scores, and l…

title: Implementing lesson study as teacher professional development in English schools: exploring the role of the leader through an implementation science lens
abstract: Purpose Lesson study (LS) is a Japanese teacher professional development (PD) approach which has been adopted globally to emulate Japan's high student achievement. In Japan, three leadership roles ensure the high-quality implementation of LS: a school Research Steering Committee, in-school facilitators and external experts. Teachers can develop leadership expertise through their participation in LS. This study uses implementation science as a framework to investigate leadership functions that enabled and hindered LS implementation in English schools that voluntarily adopted LS, frequently without funding, policy guidance or systemic opportunities for LS leadership development. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a case study methodology, exploring data from six purposefully recruited schools that implemented and used LS for at least two years, four of which subsequently abandoned it. We analysed interview data from LS leaders and participants, alongside documents detailing LS policy and practice, to assess the extent to which leaders fulfilled the three Japanese leadership roles and to reveal the characteristics and behaviours of implementation leaders. Findings What distinguishes sustained from abandoned cases is the propensity of LS leaders to “champion” LS. These knowledgeable yet humble leaders led implementation with passion, solved problems, allocated funding and …

title: PENINGKATAN KETERAMPILAN MENULIS PUISI MELALUI MEDIA POP UP BOOK DIGITAL BERBASIS ASSEMBLR EDU
abstract: The low level of poetry writing skills among elementary school students remains a challenge in Indonesian language learning, particularly in generating ideas, selecting appropriate diction, developing imagery, and composing meaningful poems. This study aimed to improve students' poetry writing skills and describe teacher and student activities through the implementation of a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu. This study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 35 fifth-grade students of SDN 2 Tambakrigadung. Data were collected through observation, performance tests, and documentation, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed that teacher activity increased from 55% in Cycle I to 88% in Cycle II, while student activity increased from 53% to 88%. The average poetry writing score also improved from 67 to 79, with learning mastery increasing from 40% to 83%. These improvements indicate that three-dimensional visualizations provided through the learning media helped students generate inspiration, develop imagination, and select appropriate diction. Therefore, implementing a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu can serve as an alternative approach to improving elementary school students' poetry writing skills. ABSTRAK Rendahnya k…

title: Reimagining adolescent education with ephegogy: generative AI and active learning in practice
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces ephegogy, a theory addressing the gap between traditional educational models and adolescents' developmental needs in artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented societies. Blending constructivism, connectivism and generativism, it explores how integrating generative AI (GenAI) and active learning can scaffold motivation, autonomy, and relevance for adolescent learners. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods case study conducted in a single secondary-school geography course during 2024–2025. Quantitative data came from matched pre- and post-intervention surveys measuring motivation and self-efficacy (N = 17; N = 11 for the self-efficacy composite) and locus of control (N = 12), using instruments adapted for an under-14, predominantly English-as-an-additional-language cohort. A separate matched engagement survey (N = 24) and an end-of-course co-creation survey (N = 33) provided further data. Qualitative data comprised 74 individual student reflections analysed thematically using the cultural-historical activity theory (CHAT) framework, alongside open-text survey responses from 74 students. The study was designed using three frameworks (self-determination theory, ephegogy and CHAT). Findings Findings are associational and exploratory, specific to this pilot. title: A machine learning framework of ground-state properties of finite nuclei foraccelerated Bayesian exploration : NucleiML
abstract: Abstract The global behavior of the nuclear equation of state (EoS) is commonly studied using data from finite nuclei (FN), heavy-ion collisions, and astrophysical observations of neutron stars (NS). The constraints derived from FN such as binding energies and charge radii play the most crucial role in shaping the EoS up to saturation density. The computational cost associated with explicitly incorporating these constraints presents a significant challenge especially when the aim is to explore the model uncertainties rather than optimizing a single model. We address this by introducing NucleiML (NML), a machine learning framework trained on ground-state properties of a few finite nuclei generated by a relativistic mean-field model. NML allows us to integrate FN and NS properties within a Bayesian inference framework in an efficient manner. The results demonstrate reasonable accuracy and a speedup of $\sim 10^4$ times for calculation of FN properties for a single parameter set, yielding roughly $\sim 10^3 \times$ speed up in the Bayesian framework. The present study makes the case for extending the work to a larger set of nuclei, potentially enabling future studies of NS properties to incorporate the whole nuclear chart.

title: Intelligent Concealment of Healthcare Information: A Novel Machine Learning-Driven Multi-Layered Steganographic Approach for Enhanced Medical Data Privacy
abstract: Rapidly, the adoption of cloud computing, the “Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)”, telemedicine, and electronic medical records has made an increasing number of people concerned about the security of medical information being transmitted. This study suggests a novel multi-layered steganographic approach designed using an intelligent machine learning system for privacy preserving healthcare communication. The structure is based on the NIH Chest X-ray dataset of 112,120 X-rays from 30,805 patients. The basic steps of medical image preprocessing include resizing, image normalization, CLAHE enhancement, median filtering, and AES-256 encryption, ResNet-50 based deep feature extraction, adaptive region selection using XGBoost and DWT-LSB embedding. The medical images are preprocessed by resizing, image normalization, CLAHE enhancement, median filtering and AES-256 encryption followed by ResNet-50 deep feature extraction, XGBoost based adaptive region selection and DWT-LSB embedding. Experimental results give an impressive PSNR of 54.32 dB and SSIM of 0.978, embedding capacity of 0.175 bpp, and extraction accuracy of 99.21%. The proposed framework is also able to decrease the time of operation from 19.7% to 37.2% in terms of steganalysis detection ratio and 0.99 in terms of AUC, and reduce the encryption/decryption time to 1.72 s and 1.63 s, respectively. Based on these outcomes, the …

The effect of trade policy uncertainty, free cash flow, investment opportunity set, and liquidity on dividend policy of food and beverage sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, 2022–2025
abstract: Shifts in international trade policy may change how firms divide cash between shareholders and retention, yet evidence on this link for emerging-market firms remains scarce. This study examines whether trade policy uncertainty (TPU), free cash flow, the investment opportunity set (IOS), and liquidity are associated with the dividend payout ratio of food and beverage firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Drawing on agency, signaling, and pecking-order perspectives, we analyze a balanced panel of 27 regular dividend-paying firms over 2022–2025 (108 firm-year observations) using random-effects regression with standard errors clustered by firm, selected through Chow, Lagrange multiplier, and Hausman tests. IOS is the only variable significantly and positively associated with payout; the association is economically meaningful, equal to about one-third of the standard deviation of payout per standard-deviation increase in IOS, and it also holds in a fixed-effects specification. TPU, free cash flow, and liquidity show no statistically significant association, although the estimates are imprecise and do not rule out sizeable effects, and the model as a whole has low explanatory power. These results indicate that, among regular payers, payout is related more to the market’s valuation of growth prospects than to trade policy uncertainty. Because TPU varies only by year, the sampl…

Adaptive management under uncertainty: sustained participatory management of endemic species in Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Summary Given land-use change threatening both biodiversity and traditional extractive livelihoods since 2004, an action research process in Minas Gerais (Brazil) has focused on the management of two endemic species: the giant earthworm Rhinodrilus alatus and the pequi tree Caryocar brasiliense . Socio-ecological assessments, ecological field surveys and market analyses generated the evidence that extractivists and public institutions used to negotiate management agreements. Despite more than a decade of institutional uncertainty and the absence of formal regulation, local actors maintained voluntary harvesting restrictions, including a closed season during the reproductive period. Ecological evidence supported reassessing the conservation status of R. alatus , enabling discussions on regulated sustainable use. To address seasonal income losses, we developed a community-based pequi processing initiative that aligns livelihood activities with ecological cycles. Over two decades, sustained collaboration, co-produced knowledge and livelihood diversification reduced conflict, strengthened local organization and supported adaptive management under legal uncertainty. This demonstrates that long-term participatory processes can sustain conservation outcomes and reconcile biodiversity conservation with rural livelihoods in socially and biologically diverse landscapes.

SMED for optimization of changeover times in an electronics manufacturing workshop: a case study
abstract: Purpose In the electronic manufacturing services industry, frequent changeovers in high-mix, low-volume production significantly affect overall equipment effectiveness. Reducing these nonvalue-added activities is therefore essential for improving operational performance and competitiveness. This study aims to reduce changeover durations in a surface-mount technology (SMT) workshop through the structured application of the single minute exchange of die (SMED) methodology, combined with digital monitoring tools. Design/methodology/approach The proposed approach consists of three phases: an initial diagnostic based on time analysis and root-cause identification using Ishikawa diagrams, implementation of SMED through task separation, externalization, parallelization and standardization and performance monitoring using a real-time Power BI dashboard. Findings The results show reduction in average changeover time from 48 min to 18 min in week, corresponding to a 62.5% improvement. This reduction generates annual savings exceeding €600,000 while improving process reliability, traceability and working conditions. Originality/value Rather than proposing a new SMED technique or a new digital platform, this study contributes an integrated Digital SMED framework specifically adapted to high-mix SMT production. The framework links SMED task transformation with intelligent operator-support t…

title: HyEff-UNet: an attention-driven Efficientnet U-Net with hybrid loss optimization for UAV-based marine oil spill detection and segmentation
abstract: Introduction Monitoring oil spills in the port area is very difficult and can spread rapidly, resulting in considerable damage to the environment. This study proposes HyEff-UNet, a deep learning-based semantic segmentation model for the detection of oil spills using drone-captured RGB images of port environments. Methods HyEff-UNet employs a modified version of the U-Net model with an EfficientNet-B4 model as an encoder is used as the model architecture to classify the pixels of the input image as oil, water, or other surface regions. A combined categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss function is used to jointly optimize pixel-wise classification and region overlap. Results The results show that the complete architecture achieves the highest performance among the internally evaluated models, while the sequential ablation indicates that the largest performance improvement is observed after the hybrid categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss is introduced following the EfficientNet-B4 and attention-based architecture. Conclusion These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the complete architecture within the evaluated configurations. However, the sequential ablation study does not isolate the independent contribution of the hybrid loss. Furthermore, the measured inference latency indicates that further optimization and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-specific benchmarking are re…

Hybrid numerical-data-driven modeling and optimization of thermo fluid transport in magnetized Eyring–Powell fluid
abstract: Purpose Accurate prediction and optimization of nonlinear thermofluid transport are essential for the design of advanced thermal engineering systems. This study aims to develop a hybrid computational–optimization–data-driven framework for modeling coupled transport phenomena in magnetized Eyring–Powell fluids with variable thermophysical properties. The optimization analysis investigates coupled thermofluid transport in an unsteady magnetized Eyring–Powell fluid over a vertical surface with temperature-dependent viscosity and thermal conductivity. The primary objective is to analyze, optimize and predict convective heat transfer using response surface methodology (RSM) based on a central composite design. Design/methodology/approach The governing nonlinear partial differential equations are solved numerically using an explicit finite difference method to obtain the flow, thermal, concentration and entropy generation fields. The resulting numerical data are subsequently used to construct linear, quadratic and interaction regression models for the Nusselt number (Nu) as functions of the magnetic parameter (M), Eckert number (Ec), heat source/sink parameter (δ), Dufour number (Du) and the Eyring–Powell fluid parameter (K). DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, OPTIMIZATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF LINEZOLID MICRONEEDLE PATCH USING DESIGN EXPERT SOFTWARE FOR ACCELERATED WOUND HEALING PROCESS
abstract: Microneedles represent a promising advancement in wound healing treatment, combining precision drug delivery with minimally invasive techniques to enhance therapeutic outcomes. The study on the development of microneedle patches for the transdermal delivery of Linezolid aimed at improving localized drug therapy, especially for wound healing. The study's objective was to create and evaluate dissolving microneedle patches for the treatment of wound healing that are composed of polymers and Linezolid. Microneedle patches were developed by Solvent Casting and Micro molding technique. Linezolid was used as active constituent, and polymers like Hydroxyethyl Cellulose, Polyvinyl Alcohol and glycerol were used for the development of microneedle patches. Four formulations were created by altering the concentration of various polymers while maintaining a constant drug ratio. The optimization was performed by Design Expert software (DoE) using 22 full factorial design by taking 2 independent variable as factors and 2 dependent variables in-vitro Drug release(Y1) and Drug content(Y2). FTIR, as well as other metrics like drug content, moisture loss %, folding endurance, SEM analysis, in-vitro drug release, in-vitro release kinetics, and stability tests, were used to examine the produced Microneedle patches for the interaction study. Franz diffusion cell was used to conduct ex-vivo investiga…

title: Multi Objective Optimization of Distribution in Supply Chains using Green AI via an Enhanced Hippopotamus Algorithm
abstract: Modern supply chains require innovative, sustainable, and computationally efficient solutions for physical distribution. This paper proposes the Enhanced Hippo Optimization (EHO) algorithm, a novel, nature-inspired metaheuristic designed to solve the Multi-Objective Vehicle Routing Problem (MO-CVRP). The (EHO) algorithm mathematically models three key hippo herd behaviors: exploration (herd positioning), defensive coordination, and strategic withdrawal, to achieve a dynamic balance between global exploration and local exploitation. By integrating real-world geospatial data from the Google Maps Directions API and customer demand modeling via a Zipf distribution (α = 0.9), (EHO) simultaneously reduces total distance, delivery time, operating costs, and CO2 emissions. The algorithm was evaluated under twenty scenarios across a network of nineteen cities in Egypt, outperforming six advanced algorithms Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), RUN, Artemisinin Optimizer (AO), and Fata Morgana in eighteen cases. The framework achieved an average reduction of 26.9% in distance and emissions, with total computational runtime ranging from 12.77 to 25.1 seconds depending on the scenario. Visual analyses, including optimized route maps and radar performance charts, confirmed the robustness, scalability, and practical effectiveness of the EHO…

title: Amelioration of lipid production by Cunninghamella echinulata: statistical optimization and GC-MS characterization
abstract: Abstract Lipids have garnered attention for their importance in pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals. Famously, oleaginous filamentous fungi produce essential fatty acids. In this study, optimization using one factor at time (OFAT) and response surface methodology-Box-Behnken design (RSM-BBD) approaches, Cunninghamella echinulata showed the highest lipid content (61.23%) under optimized OFAT conditions (60 g/L, glucose; 2 g/L; ammonium tartrate; pH value, 7 at 30 °C, and shaking for seven days). Lipid content of 59.37% was achieved using the BBD. One-way ANOVA indicated temperature significantly affected lipid content, while two-way ANOVA revealed significant interactions between temperature and ammonium tartrate concentration, pH and incubation time, and inoculum size and glucose concentration. Various agro-wastes used as media for C. echinulata growth and production of lipid with peach yielding the best lipid content (49.30%). Comparative analysis of lipid extracts by GC-MS of the best yield conditions revealed nineteen different fatty acids, with oleic acid, linoleic acid, gamma-linolenic acid, and palmitic acid present in high percentages of 35.49%, 21.31%, 21.78%, and 13.44%, respectively. The extracted lipids demonstrated antibacterial potential towards Staphylococcus aureus , Escherichia coli , and Bacillus subtilis , as well as antifungal efficacy against Candida albicans…

title: Metal Additive Manufacturing of Engineering Alloys: Process–Material Interactions, Defect Formation, Property Optimization and a Decision-Making Framework
abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (MAM) has evolved into a strategic manufacturing route for producing, repairing, and remanufacturing high-value components; however, process selection and optimization remain challenging because manufacturing conditions, alloy behaviour, defect formation, microstructural evolution, and final properties are strongly interdependent. This review provides a critical and comparative assessment of four representative MAM technologies—Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF), Laser Metal Deposition (LMD), a laser-based variant of Directed Energy Deposition (DED), Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM), and Metal Binder Jetting (MBJ)—with particular emphasis on their interactions with titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys, steels, and aluminium alloys. Rather than comparing these technologies solely in terms of productivity, cost, or geometrical capability, the review examines the physical and metallurgical mechanisms governing thermal history, solidification or densification, phase evolution, defect formation, microstructure, and resulting component performance. Particular attention is given to porosity, lack of fusion, cracking, residual stresses, distortion, anisotropy, and surface integrity, together with process-specific mitigation and post-processing strategies. title: Exploring the capability–experience–satisfaction (CES) pathway in omnichannel retailing
abstract: Purpose This study proposes that fulfilment, fluency and flexibility represent the consequences of omnichannel capability and act as key drivers of journey satisfaction. The study also examines whether journey satisfaction affects broader retailer-level customer satisfaction over time. Design/methodology/approach This study utilised a multi-method design combining survey and experimental data. Structural equation modelling and PROCESS analyses were based on survey data from 420 customers with omnichannel shopping experience. To provide supplementary evidence for the proposed pathway, an additional experimental study was conducted with 80 participants, and the results were analysed using logistic regression. Findings Results showed that omnichannel capability had positive effects on fulfilment, fluency and flexibility, which, in turn, had positive effects on journey satisfaction. Longitudinal analysis showed that journey satisfaction at T0 had a positive effect on broader retailer-level customer satisfaction at T1 one year later. Originality/value This study emphasises the importance of omnichannel capability in understanding customer satisfaction over time. It develops and examines the capability–experience–satisfaction pathway. Findings suggest that omnichannel capability should be managed as an integrated organisational capability supporting journey experiences, satisfaction …

title: How scene features activate customer behaviour transformation in metaverse retailing
abstract: Purpose As a crucial nexus between technological innovation and customer experience within the metaverse, effectively designed scene features represent a vital source of competitive advantage in retail. However, current research focuses narrowly on either technology or consumer perceptions, overlooking the integration between the two and resulting in limited effectiveness in consumer retention. To bridge this gap, this study develops and tests an integrated model of metaverse retail scene features. Design/methodology/approach Grounding in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, the model integrates the Design-Ambient-Social-Trialability (DAST) dimensions, to specify the environmental Stimulus. It incorporates the customer inspiration mechanism (Organism) and the variable of immersive time to explicate the psychological process leading to behavioural Responses. The proposed relationships are examined through two experiments. Findings The results demonstrate that: (1) six scene features, i.e. Visual appeal, Navigability, Informativeness, Novelty, Embodied co-presence and Trialability, significantly enhance purchase intention, pleasure and loyalty; (2) the customer inspiration process, sequentially moving from inspired-by to inspired-to, fully mediates these effects; (3) the immersive time positively moderates the impact of Informativeness, Embodied Co-presence and Trial…

title: Rethinking retail patronage: beyond customer loyalty towards reciprocal customer–retailer relationships
abstract: Purpose This research clarifies retail patronage by combining consumer insights with bibliometric analysis to address conceptual fragmentation and support consistent measurement. Design/methodology/approach We combined qualitative interviews (n = 68) with a bibliometric analysis of 233 articles using Bibliometrix. Five experts provided an interpretive evaluation of the integrated findings. Findings Retail patronage emerges as a multidimensional relational construct integrating behavioural, intentional, and attitudinal components while remaining conceptually distinguishable from loyalty and love. The literature structures around antecedents and methodological foundations. Patronage occurs when repeated behaviour is relationally interpreted rather than situational. Practical implications Retailers should complement behavioural metrics with relational indicators to distinguish routine purchasing from genuine patronage and design relationship-focused loyalty programmes. Originality/value The study integrates consumer perspectives and intellectual foundations, positioning retail patronage as a reciprocal relational exchange construct to provide a basis for scale development. It explains why repetition can occur without loyalty and loyalty without patronage. The findings suggest that retail patronage extends beyond behavioural loyalty by reflecting reciprocal customer–retailer relati…

title: Temperature and returns: a climatic approach to global asset pricing
abstract: Purpose This study investigates whether a country's long-run temperature profile, both its level and its year-to-year variability, helps explain cross-country differences in stock market returns, volatility, and risk-adjusted performance, and whether the evidence is consistent with innovation serving as a potential channel linking climate to financial markets. Design/methodology/approach Using an annual panel of more than 60 countries from 2000 to 2019, this paper constructs country-level temperature measures from publicly available surface-temperature data and combines them with equity-market data from Bloomberg. It estimates country-fixed-effects panel regressions of returns, volatility, and a risk-adjusted return measure on the temperature variables, with macroeconomic controls and cluster-robust standard errors. Evidence consistent with a potential innovation channel is evaluated using the Global Innovation Index, and robustness is assessed with year fixed effects and a 500-replication bootstrap. Findings Countries with a higher long-run average temperature exhibit higher average equity returns and lower volatility, and correspondingly higher risk-adjusted performance. Both the level and the variability of temperature are positively associated with national innovation, and innovation, in turn, is positively associated with returns and negatively associated with volatility. …

title: Pricing Audits in Verifier-Guided Test-Time Scaling: Proxy Reliability and Budgeted Candidate Selection
abstract: In verifier-guided test-time scaling, a cheap proxy ranks candidates and an audit obtains the target score of the selected output. The best split of a budget between generation and audits depends on proxy reliability among still-competitive candidates. We study this reliability through decision-granularity correlation: the proxy–target association within a prompt's top-ranked shortlist. We connect classical range restriction to an audit-efficiency threshold for linear proxy-assisted estimation, then evaluate candidate selection under a shared generation-and-audit budget. PickScore–HPS correlation falls from 0.84 within full diffusion prompt pools to 0.32 in their top 10%, and an API judge agrees with the target on 53.4% of near-ties. On text, an approximate correlation diagnostic accepts GSM8K and abstains on ARC. Across five diffusion models, we separate ranking gains from allocation gains. On 80 new Stable Diffusion XL prompts, reallocating a random-audit policy improves the composite preference score by 0.01196, while screening retains only 0.00076 over tuned random auditing (95% interval includes zero); higher audit prices favor screening.

title: Transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation in end-stage paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension: lessons from a rescue decompression strategy
abstract: Abstract A 12-year-old girl with end-stage suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension and progressive right ventricular failure underwent transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation after deterioration despite targeted therapy and prior atrial septostomy. Right-to-left shunting was established, but haemodynamic improvement was limited; pulmonary pressures remained suprasystemic, persistent pericardial effusion developed, and the patient died despite intensive treatment, illustrating the complexity of rescue decompression in advanced disease.

title: Trojan Horse Strategy for Sustainable PET Plastics: A Comparative Evaluation of Techno-Economic and Lifecycle Impacts
abstract: Abstract Reactive comonomers known as Trojan Horse units can be built into the polyethylene terephthalate (PET) chain so that the polymer depolymerizes under milder conditions at the end of life without losing performance in use. We combined this strategy with bio-based terephthalic acid made from limonene and compared the resulting process with conventional alkaline hydrolysis of PET through a techno-economic analysis and a life cycle assessment. The base case incorporates 5% Trojan Horse units, 16.25% bio-based terephthalic acid, and 48.75% recycled terephthalic acid on a monomer basis. Its minimum selling price is $5.28/kg, compared with $1.32/kg for a plant that makes recycled terephthalic acid alone. Limonene and the nitrated comonomer account for three quarters of that price. The global warming potential is 1.80 kg of CO2-eq per kg of resin. That is 19% below that of virgin PET on the same cradle-to-gate basis but above the 0.91 kg CO2-eq per kg of mechanically recycled PET. Measured kinetics for the nitroterephthalate copolymer shorten the hydrolysis time at 100 °C from 12.5 to 7.6 h, which lowers the fixed capital investment by 20% relative to unmodified PET under the same conditions. title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses reveal developmental and metabolic differences between wild and cultivated Cordyceps chanhua
Toward sustainable mineral exploration: integrated EnMAP hyperspectral, Sentinel-1 SAR and aeromagnetic datasets for prospectivity mapping of the Gabal Hamadat area, central Eastern Desert, Egypt
abstract: Introduction Mineral exploration in Precambrian shield terrains requires the joint use of surface alteration, structural architecture, and subsurface geophysical evidence. This study builds a reproducible, quantitatively classified favourability map for structurally controlled magmatic-hydrothermal mineralization in the Gabal Hamadat area of the Central Eastern Desert of Egypt. Methods EnMAP Level-2A imaging spectroscopy, Sentinel-2 and Landsat-9 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 SAR, and airborne magnetic data were processed into ten evidence layers: six EnMAP band-ratio layers representing argillic, phyllic, propylitic, ferrous-mineral, ferrous-silicate, and ferruginous responses; two structural lineament-density layers derived from Sentinel-1 SAR and CET analysis of the RTP magnetic grid; and two aeromagnetic layers comprising CET porphyry-analysis circular sources and source-parameter-imaging (SPI) depth-to-magnetic-source response. Eight of these ten layers, the six alteration layers together with the CET-PA and SPI aeromagnetic layers, were implemented as red-channel digital-number values from color-rendered exports rather than as native spectral-index or depth values; the two structural lineament-density layers were computed directly from their respective datasets. title: Blue Light Reprograms Fatty Acid Metabolism in Scenedesmus sp. GSB9 Revealed by Integrated Transcriptomics and Metabolomics
abstract: Abstract Scenedesmus sp. GSB9, a freshly isolated fast-growing microalgal strain derived from wastewater, was cultivated under continuous white, blue, and sequential blue-to-red (9B3R) light regimes to investigate light-quality–mediated regulation of fatty acid biosynthesis. Integrated multi-omics analysis, combining de novo transcriptomics, LC–HRMS metabolomics, and GC–FID fatty acid profiling, revealed that blue light enhanced the metabolic landscape, including higher palmitic acid accumulation. Additionally, this response was complemented by enrichment of triglyceride biosynthetic pathways (GO:0019432) and upregulation of Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACCase), which encodes a key enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA for de novo fatty acid synthesis, and was supported by RT-qPCR validation of selected genes. In contrast, the 9B3R regime induced global transcriptional activation of stress-responsive metabolic pathways, including DNA repair (GO:0006281) and protein folding (GO:0006457), along with central carbon metabolism and reduced lipid accumulation. This divergence suggests a decoupling between transcriptional activity and metabolic output under dynamic light transitions, potentially mediated by post-transcriptional or post-translational regulation. Collectively, these findings indicated continuous blue light as a driver of lipid accumulation in Scen…

title: Competition between diffusive damping and instability growth in a rarefied Rayleigh–Taylor system
abstract: The mechanisms underlying the generation and evolution of Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) in rarefied gases are an important issue, particularly in many emerging problems where rarefaction effects become significant. Using a graphics processing unit parallelised direct simulation Monte Carlo approach, we simulate RTI across a wide range of Knudsen numbers ( upper K n K n $Kn$ ), and find that instability growth is progressively inhibited as upper K n K n $Kn$ increases, with complete suppression above a critical value upper K n almost equals 0.011 K n ≈ 0.011 $Kn \approx 0.011$ . Molecular-scale analysis reveals that rarefaction enhances super-diffusive transport of the molecules, extending the ballistic regime, and favouring the interfacial mixing. This microscale behaviour macroscopically manifests as a rapid decay of the density gradient and the effective Atwood number. To determine whether instability emerges in rarefied conditions, we introduce a stability criterion based on the competition between a diffusive time scale ( tau Subscript upper D τ D $\tau _D$ ) and an instability time scale ( tau Subscript upper I τ I $\tau _I$ ). title: User Engagement with Clinician-Developed Guided Meditations on a Global Digital Platform: A Multi-Method Study
abstract: Abstract Digital meditation applications are increasingly used to support stress management, emotional balance, and everyday coping among individuals seeking accessible mental health and wellness resources. At the same time, less is known about how people engage with and experience clinician-developed guided meditation content on large global wellness platforms outside of formal research settings. This multi-method study examined user engagement and user-reported experiences associated with a series of clinician-developed guided meditations delivered through a single clinician-developed Insight Timer account. Quantitative descriptive analyses were conducted using platform analytics, including total plays (N = 6,688 since February 2025), follower activity, and available geographic information for followers and commenters. In addition, 59 publicly available user comments were extracted; 29 comments met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Descriptive findings indicated ongoing listener interaction through plays, follows, and written commentary, while available geographic information for followers and commenters indicated engagement across multiple regions. Qualitative analysis identified four primary themes in commenters’ descriptions of their experiences with the recordings: emotional regulation and nervous system calming, perceived psychol…

Acute consumption of a multi-source peptide complex is associated with coordinated innate immune and hematopoietic stem cell responses: An exploratory pilot study
abstract: Background: Immune surveillance and regenerative responses depend on coordinated interactions among innate immune cells and hematopoietic progenitor populations. Food-derived peptides have been reported to influence immune function, but little is known about their acute effects across multiple interconnected immune and stem cell compartments. Objectives: This exploratory pilot study evaluated whether acute consumption of a multi-source peptide complex (MSPC) was associated with coordinated changes in circulating immune and stem cell populations. Methods: In a randomized, placebo-controlled pilot study, four healthy adults (N=4) consumed MSPC or placebo, and peripheral blood was collected before and after consumption. Flow cytometric analyses were performed to evaluate monocyte numbers and phenotype, γδ T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, and circulating stem/progenitor cell populations, including CD45dimCD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and CD45-CD31++CD34- endothelial progenitor cells. Results: MSPC consumption was associated with rapid and temporally organized changes across multiple cellular compartments. Within the monocyte compartment, coordinated increases in CD14 and CD16 expression occurred despite stable monocyte numbers, suggesting phenotypic remodeling rather than redistribution among classical, intermediate, and non-classical monocytes. title: Multi-tissue segmentation of knee MRI based on U-Net and conditional generative adversarial networks
abstract: Objective This study aimed to systematically compare the performance of U-Net and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) for multi-tissue segmentation of knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using the public SKI10 dataset, and to investigate the effects of loss functions, discriminator receptive fields, and normalization strategies on model performance through ablation experiments. Methods The segmentation targets included the femur, femoral cartilage, tibia, and tibial cartilage, with the background incorporated as an additional class to formulate a five-class segmentation task. All MRI images and labels were read from the original. mhd files and two-dimensional slices were extracted along the sagittal direction. Images were resized to 512 × 512 pixels and standardized using z-score normalization, whereas labels were resized with nearest-neighbor interpolation to preserve categorical encoding. Training and test sets were split at the MRI-volume level to prevent information leakage caused by adjacent slices from the same volume being assigned to different subsets. U-Net was used as the supervised baseline model, and a cGAN segmentation framework consisting of a U-Net-style generator and a discriminator was constructed. Evaluation metrics included the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Qualitative segmentation, erro…

title: Multi-scale dynamics and mesoscale drivers of the catastrophic September 2022 Marche (central Italy) flood
abstract: The catastrophic flood that hit the Marche region (central Italy) on 15 September 2022 has been analyzed using high-resolution Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model simulations. The convective rainfall event responsible for the flood was favored by the passage of warm, moist air masses that interacted with the central Apennines. The convective cells, triggered by the rough orography of the area, formed quasi-stationary bands that caused high rainfall accumulation in limited areas. The formation of these rainbands was sustained by the interaction between the low-level flow and the local topography, which generated a persistent low-level convergence line extending downwind from Mount Amiata northeastward towards the Apennines. The observed vertical profile upstream of the orography reveals that the instability was initially suppressed by an inversion layer and was released only when the humid air arrived at low levels and eroded the inhibition. Furthermore, the simulations suggest that gravity waves induced by the mountains may have helped to sustain the vertical motion of the impinging air, and highlight the role of upper-level dynamics (passage of a jet streak). The comparison with surface stations shows that the simulation underestimates peak accumulations (160–180 mm simulated vs. over 400 mm observed), delays the event by 1–2 h, and misses the final phase. However, ov…

title: The role of crowding and decision comfort during sales periods
abstract: Purpose Sales periods simultaneously attract consumers through price reductions and trigger avoidance behaviors: a paradox this study addresses by examining decision comfort as a potential mediator of the effects of human and spatial crowding on visit postponement and store-switching. Gender is also examined as a moderator of these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was adopted, with data collected from 378 consumers in France during official sales periods across several retail locations. The conceptual model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine relationships among perceived crowding, decision comfort, visit postponement, and store-switching. Multi-group analysis assessed gender differences. Findings Both human and spatial crowding were negatively associated with decision comfort. Lower decision comfort was associated with higher levels of visit postponement and, less robustly, with store-switching. The indirect effect of spatial crowding on visit postponement through decision comfort was supported; the indirect effects of human crowding on both avoidance behaviors were also supported but modest in magnitude, whereas the indirect effect of spatial crowding on store-switching was not supported. Gender differences were detected in the crowding–decision comfort relationships, whereas no gender differences were detected in t…

title: Ownership structure and the exploration–exploitation tradeoff: evidence from Chinese advanced manufacturing firms
abstract: Purpose Although the ambidexterity literature emphasizes the importance of balancing exploration and exploitation, less is known about whether the innovation–performance implications of relative exploration vary across corporate governance conditions. This study examines whether executive and institutional shareholding are associated with differences in the estimated exploration–exploitation turning point. Design/methodology/approach Using an unbalanced panel of 254 Chinese advanced manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2020, this study estimates two-way fixed-effects models of the relationship between relative exploration (RE) and innovation performance. The sample firms are identified from companies included in the SSE Made in China (2025) Index and the CSI Made in China (2025) Index during 2015–2020. We further examine whether executive shareholding and two types of institutional shareholding – pressure-sensitive and pressure-resistant – are associated with the location of the estimated conditional turning point. Findings RE is associated with innovation performance in an inverted U-shaped pattern. Higher executive shareholding is associated with a more exploration-oriented estimated conditional turning point, whereas higher pressure-resistant institutional shareholding is associated with a more exploitation-oriented turning point. By contrast, the interaction between RE and pres…

FINANCIAL LITERACY AND INVESTMENT DECISIONS AMONG RANK-AND-FILE BANK EMPLOYEES IN BORONGAN CITY, EASTERN SAMAR
abstract: Financial literacy is an important capability that helps individuals understand financial concepts, manage resources, evaluate financial products, and make informed investment decisions. This study examines the relationship between financial literacy and investment decisions among rank-and-file bank employees in Borongan City, Eastern Samar. It focuses on financial knowledge, financial behavior, and financial attitude as dimensions of financial literacy, and on employees’ investment decision practices. A quantitative, descriptive-correlational design is proposed. This study manuscript provides a framework for examining whether financial knowledge, behavior, and attitudes are associated with informed investment choices among bank employees.

title: When financial expertise shapes AI narratives in China: CEO financial background and symbolic AI disclosure
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether CEO financial background shapes corporate artificial intelligence (AI) overclaiming in an emerging-market context. Drawing on upper echelons theory (UET), we argue that financially experienced CEOs may frame AI as a market-oriented strategic narrative while underinvesting in the long-term technological capabilities needed to substantiate such claims. Design/methodology/approach Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we measure AI overclaiming as the gap between AI disclosure and invention-based AI capability. We estimate models with firm and year fixed effects and validate the findings through robustness tests, including AI investment- and residual-based measures, as well as endogeneity, placebo and channel analyses. Findings CEO financial background is positively associated with corporate AI overclaiming. Channel analyses suggest that financially experienced CEOs widen the disclosure–capability gap by increasing short-term financial asset allocation and reducing R&D investment. This effect is stronger when external verification is weak, market pressure is high and policy-driven AI narratives are more salient. Originality/value This study identifies CEO financial background as a managerial antecedent of AI overclaiming. It extends UET by showing how financial career imprints shape emerging-technology narratives and resource all…

title: Bankruptcy system reform and shadow banking activities of non-financial enterprises: evidence from China
abstract: Purpose Bankruptcy system reform is an effective measure to improve judicial efficiency in bankruptcy proceedings and protect the legitimate rights and interests of creditors. It plays an important role in promoting the development of credit markets. Design/methodology/approach Based on a quasi-natural experiment of establishing bankruptcy court in China, this paper examines the impact of the establishment of bankruptcy court on shadow banking activities of non-financial enterprises, using a multi-period difference-in-differences model with China's A-share listed enterprises as the research object from 2016 to 2022. Findings The findings show that the establishment of bankruptcy court increases the scale of shadow banking activities of non-financial enterprises. Furthermore, enhancing creditor protection and increasing management risk preference play important mechanism effect. Bankruptcy law enforcement efficiency demonstrates a strong moderating effect. Originality/value This study provides empirical evidence for evaluating the quality and effectiveness of bankruptcy system reform and offers instructive insights for activating informal finance, regulating shadow banking activities and maintaining financial market stability.

title: Islamic corporate social responsibility as a governance-embedded system: evidence from Islamic banks in Malaysia and Indonesia
abstract: Purpose Although there has been a rapid rate of expansion observed in the domain of Islamic banking, there remains an inconsistent degree of institutionalisation of Islamic corporate social responsibility (ICSR). The reason is that a higher priority level has been placed on contractual and financial compliance by existing CSR and Shariah governance models, rather than broader socio-economic aspects. The purpose of this study was to develop an ICSR framework to assess the capacity of existing Islamic banking institutions to institutionalise ICSR through relevant governance mechanisms and Islamic social finance instruments, while examining their relationships with socio-economic outcomes. Design/methodology/approach In this investigation, a qualitative multiple-case study design, which involved both Maybank Islamic (Malaysia) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (Indonesia), was employed. Specifically, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a total of 20 purposively selected senior informants, with 10 from each of the two institutions, who were directly involved in the process of ICSR governance and implementation. The interviews, which ranged between 60 and 120 min, were triangulated with corresponding institutional and sustainability documents. After collecting the data, a thematic content analysis was performed through the NVivo software, which incorporated iterative coding, int…

title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence into Financial Management Teaching: An Instructional Design for Finance Leasing
abstract: Financial Management courses often fall short in linking computational training with financing decision analysis. Taking finance leasing as a case, this paper explores how generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) can be brought into the classroom. The instructional design is built around a scenario in which a private hospital finances the purchase of medical equipment, and it connects rent calculation, comparison of financing alternatives, and scrutiny of decision conditions through a four-stage process: independent calculation, AI questioning, professional verification, and decision reconstruction. Students first carry out the calculations and form a preliminary financing judgment, then use generative AI to interrogate financing constraints and uncover the assumptions behind a plan, and finally verify the AI-generated content against financial principles to strengthen their argument. The design takes students' own judgments as the starting point of human-AI interaction and assigns AI the role of revealing and examining the conditions under which a financing plan holds, rather than making the decision for them. This approach offers a reference for bringing generative AI into accounting and finance courses.

title: Selecting the right path: a framework for lead-time reduction in consumer goods supply chains
abstract: Purpose Consumer goods firms often face severe shortages caused by forecast inaccuracy, where a few variants become unexpected bestsellers and trigger costly stockouts. This article positions the choice of lead-time reduction initiatives as a crucial decision for enhancing responsiveness and mitigating shortages and frames this decision as a performance-management prioritization problem under uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This work developed a pragmatic direction-selection framework grounded in a design science approach and applied in a case to guide managers in evaluating and prioritizing lead-time reduction initiatives. The framework integrates insights from the literature with feasibility-oriented evaluation criteria, applying the principles of multi-criteria decision analysis to assess initiatives in terms of expected return on investment (impact relative to effort) and implementation horizon. Findings The study offers a theory-based, empirically validated framework for identifying and planning lead time reduction initiatives in a context of hard-to-predict demand, making explicit a performance-management logic for prioritizing responsiveness initiatives. The case shows that initiatives with attractive expected impact–effort profiles are not necessarily robust priorities once implementation risk and sensitivity to assumptions are considered. Research limitations/…

title: Autologous pulmonary artery flap repair for aortopulmonary window with interrupted aortic arch and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
abstract: Abstract We describe a surgical technique using a pedicled autologous pulmonary artery wall flap for repair of aortopulmonary window in association with interrupted aortic arch and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery. A 29-day-old infant underwent definitive repair in which the pulmonary artery flap was used to close the defect and to achieve wide rerouting of the right coronary artery to the reconstructed ascending aorta. The pulmonary artery was reconstructed with a fresh autologous pericardial patch, and the aortic arch was repaired by direct anastomosis. Postoperative CT demonstrated patency of the right coronary artery and satisfactory aortic configuration. This anatomical repair using autologous tissue may reduce the risk of coronary distortion and provide a favourable coronary geometry in selected patients. However, further follow-up is required to evaluate coronary growth and the long-term durability of the reconstructed vessels.

title: The Effect of Financial and Non-Financial Incentives on Knowledge Sharing Through Elementary School Teachers' Work Motivation with Transformational Leadership as a Moderating Variable
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of financial and non-financial incentives on the knowledge-sharing behavior of elementary school teachers in Penajam Paser Utara (PPU) Regency, with work motivation as a mediating variable and transformational leadership as a moderating variable. This research is crucial considering PPU's strategic position as a buffer zone for the Nusantara Capital City (IKN), which demands continuous adaptation of teacher competencies. The research method used is quantitative with a causality approach. Data were collected through questionnaires from 88 elementary school teacher respondents in PPU Regency. Data analysis was performed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) based on Partial Least Squares (PLS) with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results of the study show that: (1) Financial incentives do not have a significant effect on teacher work motivation, as the teacher compensation system is strictly regulated by government policy, meaning small additional incentives are no longer a primary stimulant; (2) Non-financial incentives have a positive and significant effect on work motivation; (3) Work motivation has a positive and significant effect on knowledge sharing; (4) Work motivation successfully mediates the relationship between non-financial incentives and knowledge sharing, but fails to mediate the effect of financial incentives; (…

title: Rational Design of Novel Piperine Derivatives Bearing an N -Sulfonylpiperazine Moiety as Selectively Potent Of ChtII Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract OfChtII, an indispensable enzyme whose expression precedes other chitinases in the chitin metabolic system of Ostrinia furnacalis, becomes a promising target for green pest control. In this work, a series of novel piperine derivatives bearing an N-sulfonylpiperazine moiety were rationally designed and synthesized based on the binding cavity characteristics of OfChtII. Among them, compound I–H15 (Ki = 0.88 μM) exhibited superior inhibitory potency against OfChtII over piperine (Ki = 50.06 μM). In vivo bioassays demonstrated that I–H15 displayed high insecticidal efficacy and prominent growth-inhibitory effects on O. furnacalis at 500 μg/mL. Molecular mechanism demonstrated that I–H15 deeply occupies the previously unexploited subsite −2 of OfChtII and forms critical interactions through hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, and π–cation with key residues Trp1951 and Phe1889 in OfChtII, as shown by molecular simulations. This study validates a subsite-targeted optimization strategy by discovering novel piperine derivatives and offers a promising lead for developing eco-friendly Chitinase inhibitors against O. furnacalis.

Typological Differentiation and Industrial Fit in Local Enterprise-Related Enforcement Reform: A Comparative Study of Three Guangdong Cities and Implications for Shantou
abstract: Optimizing the business environment is a pivotal aspect of China’s governance modernization. Despite a unified top-level legal framework, local enterprise-related administrative enforcement exhibits significant typological divergence. Based on the theory of Responsive Regulation, this study constructs a three-dimensional analytical framework of “Deterrence—Flexibility—Efficiency” and examines enforcement practices in Jiangmen, Yunfu, and Shantou. Through structured coding of policy texts, the study identifies Jiangmen as deterrence-oriented (characterized by precise discretion), Yunfu as flexibility-oriented (relying on exemption lists), and Shantou as efficiency-oriented (focusing on cross-departmental coordination). The findings suggest that there is no universally optimal enforcement type; rather, each configuration is a conditional response to specific industrial risks and carries intrinsic tensions, such as compliance crowding-out and formalized coordination. Furthermore, targeting Shantou’s “Three New, Two Special, One Major” (3N2S1M) industries, this paper proposes a differentiated tool-combination scheme, arguing that local enforcement reform should shift from searching for “best practices” to diagnosing industrial risk structures, thus providing targeted institutional support for local high-quality development.

title: Statistical Methods for Measuring Financial Market Risk: A Literature Review
abstract: Financial market risk arises from adverse changes in asset values and is commonly assessed through volatility, Value at Risk (VaR), and tail risk. This literature review compares the variance–covariance method, Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) models, historical simulation, and Extreme Value Theory (EVT). Quantile regression is considered as a supplementary approach to dynamic VaR estimation. The methods are evaluated according to their statistical assumptions, predictive accuracy, tail-risk identification, data requirements, computational complexity, and practical suitability. The literature indicates that the variance–covariance method is efficient but vulnerable to distributional and linearity assumptions. GARCH models respond to time-varying volatility, although their performance depends on model specification and the innovation distribution. Historical simulation is transparent and accommodates portfolio revaluation, but relies on the relevance of past observations. EVT provides a direct framework for extreme losses but is sensitive to threshold selection and limited tail data. Backtesting remains necessary because theoretical flexibility does not ensure accurate forecasts. No method consistently dominates across all market conditions. Reliable measurement requires model selection to reflect return characteristics, portfolio structure, fore…
