The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
abstract: The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.

title: Harnessing genotype × environment interactions and multi-trait selection indices to identify nutritionally superior pearl millet accessions from global PMiGAP germplasm
abstract: Abstract Background Pearl millet is a climate-resilient and nutrient-dense cereal with immense potential to alleviate micronutrient malnutrition. However, the development of nutritionally superior and stable cultivars is challenged by the complex inheritance of nutritional traits and their strong genotype × environment interactions. Results In the present study, 218 pearl millet genotypes were evaluated across four environments for grain nutritional quality, anti-nutritional factors, and seed yield per plant. Multi-trait genotype selection was performed using the MTSI, followed by stability assessment using AMMI, ASV, GSI, WAASB, BLUP, and GGE biplot analysis. Factor analysis grouped the seven traits into five latent factors and predicted favourable selection gains for Fe (26.38%), Zn (9.81%), P (4.94%), and seed yield per plant (1.38%), while reducing the anti-nutritional traits, total tannin content (TTC; -16.36%) and phytic acid content (PAC; -0.78%). A modest negative response was observed for Mn (-6.89%), reflecting a trade-off under simultaneous multi-trait selection. Broad-sense heritability was high for all traits (0.83–0.99). Combined ANOVA revealed highly significant effects of genotype, environment, and G×E interaction for all traits. Based on MTSI values, 33 superior genotypes were shortlisted for detailed stability analysis. BLUP analysis identified G158 as the bes…

title: High-pyrolysis-temperature acidified straw biochar improves soil hydrological functioning and increases maize yield in saline soils
abstract: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. In this study, a four-year soil amendment experiment was conducted in moderately saline soils of the Hetao Irrigation District in China to evaluate the effects and underlying mechanisms of acidified biochar produced at three pyrolysis temperatures (C1: 300 °C, C2: 500 °C, and C3: 700 °C) and applied at two rates (T1: 10 Mg ha - ¹ and T2: 20 Mg ha - ¹) on soil hydrological properties. The results showed that: (1) application of acidified biochar significantly decreased soil salinity, pH, and bulk density, while increasing soil water content and organic matter. Moreover, it markedly enhanced crop yield and biomass; (2) acidified biochar markedly improved soil hydrological properties (0–40 cm), with the C3T1 treatment performing best, increasing soil saturated water-holding capacity, field capacity, soil water storage, and saturated hydraulic conductivity by 17.35%, 27.91%, 14.31%, and 26.92%, respectively; (3) Principal component analysis (PCA) and Mantel test results indicated tha…

title: Physiological responses of early-season rice to simulated root damage from mechanical transplanting
abstract: Yield loss from mechanical transplanting in early-season rice is often attributed to root damage, yet the physiological mechanism remains poorly understood. A two-year field experiment was conducted in early-season rice with two varieties (Lingliangyou 211, hybrid; Zhongzao 39, conventional inbred) under three root damage treatments: no damage (CK), mild (roots trimmed to 2 cm, T1), and severe (roots trimmed to 1 cm, T2). Root regeneration, leaf water status, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT), malondialdehyde (MDA), soluble protein, and PSII maximum quantum yield (Fv/Fm) were measured at 1, 3, 5, and 7 days after transplanting in 2022, whereas grain yield and yield components were evaluated in both 2021 and 2022. Results showed that T2 reduced grain yield by 8–9% across both years, whereas T1 had no significant effect. The two varieties exhibited consistent physiological responses to root damage. Both T1 and T2 stimulated compensatory new root proliferation, with significantly higher new root numbers at days 5–7 relative to CK. However, T2 induced sustained oxidative stress, as indicated by elevated MDA in roots throughout the recovery period and in leaves from day 5 onward. In contrast, T1 caused only a transient increase in root MDA. T2 reduced Fv/Fm by 23–26%, pre-heading biomass production by 13%, and highest tiller number by 10–21%. Conversely, T1 maintained al…

title: Disentangling environmental, irrigation, and clone effects on the cacao soil microbiome in a multi-location trial
abstract: Introduction Plant-associated microbiomes can shape host phenotypes, yet plant breeding programs rarely incorporate microbiome data into their selection criteria. For example, multi-location trials are central for studying genotype-by-environment interactions, yet the microbiome is a poorly characterized component of environmental variation. Methods This study sought to better understand effects of region, irrigation and nutrient management, and scion on variation in the cacao-associated soil microbiome within a multi-location breeding trial. Samples were sent for amplicon sequencing from four regions of Brazil and represented two cocoa scions and an irrigation trial comparing drip-irrigated and rainfed plots. Results Samples clustered by region for both prokaryotes and fungi, though the effects were not significant due to low statistical power and differences in multivariate dispersion. A conserved core microbiome was identified that included a complete prokaryotic nitrogen-cycling functional core as well as two omnipresent fungal ASVs belonging to the genus Fusarium . Irrigation and nutrient management explained 13% of fungal beta diversity and affected the relative abundance of 156 irrigation-responsive taxa across taxonomic levels. Depletion of irrigation-sensitive prokaryotes was linked to lower alpha diversity in drip-irrigated/fertigated plots relative to rainfed plots r…

title: Power Storage with Pumped-Hydro Storage Systems in the Island of Crete, Greece. A PESTEL Analysis
abstract: The deployment of pumped-hydro storage (PHS) systems in the island of Crete, Greece allows the higher integration of the abundant renewable energies of the island into the electric grid increasing its stability and quality. Pumped-hydro storage is broadly used worldwide for energy storage having many advantages compared with other energy storage technologies. The clean energy transition in Crete requires the higher use of solar and wind energy for power generation while power storage is necessary for integrating intermittent energy sources, like solar and wind energy, into the grid. A Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental and Legal (PESTEL) analysis regarding the development of PHS systems in Crete has been conducted. The external factors affecting their deployment have been analyzed. It has been indicated that the Greek and EU policies regarding the promotion of renewable energies and the mitigation of climate change affect their deployment in Crete. Additionally, the acceptance of PHS systems from local communities, the increase of local employment and the public concern about water availability as well as the maturity and reliability of PHS technology, the good morphological characteristics in Crete affect the deployment of PHS systems in the island. Finally, the impacts of PHS systems on natural ecosystems, landscapes, natural habitats, water resources a…

title: Assessing acceptability, feasibility, and utilization in a peer-to-peer tele-critical care model: a mixed-methods analysis to inform scalable remote ICU models
abstract: Abstract Introduction Critical care in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Pakistan, particularly in remote areas, is constrained by limited infrastructure and expertise. Telemedicine can bridge this gap by connecting frontline ICU physicians with remote critical care experts. While tele-ICU models have been evaluated in high-income settings, limited evidence exists from LMICs. This study evaluated the acceptability, feasibility, and utilization of a peer-to-peer tele-ICU consultation service launched by Aga Khan University in Pakistan. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods study using 145 survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews of physicians who had utilized a national Tele-ICU consultation service. Quantitative data were collected using a structured survey. Qualitative data were obtained through open-ended survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis by two independent reviewers to identify key themes related to service use, quality, and feasibility. Results Of 219 physicians, 145 (66.2%) responded. Consultations primarily occurred via voice (77.2%) and text (43.4%). Respondents reported high satisfaction across clinical (mean 4.50), process (3.82), and technical (4.18) domains. Key benefits included knowledge enhancement, support for complex …

title: Peer Assessment of Item Relevance in Mathematics Ability Test Instruments Designed by Mathematics Education Students: A Gregory Coefficient Approach
abstract: Designing test items that are relevant to their intended indicators is a core competency for prospective researchers and mathematics educators, yet empirical evidence from peer assessments of student-designed instruments remains limited. This study examined item–indicator relevance in mathematics ability test instruments developed by mathematics education students using peer assessment and the Gregory coefficient. A descriptive quantitative approach with a document-analysis design was employed, involving 15 constructed-response test instruments comprising 150 items assessed by two peers. Relevance ratings on a four-point scale were analyzed using the Gregory technique, descriptive statistics, and categorical agreement percentages in Microsoft Excel. The mean Gregory coefficient across instruments was 0.91; ten instruments achieved coefficients of 1.00, and twelve had coefficients ≥ 0.80. For the nine instruments with traceable item-level scores, the analysis covered 180 ratings, of which 77% were assigned the maximum score of 4. The mean rating was 3.76, and categorical agreement was 96.7%. For the remaining six instruments, coefficients were available only in student summary tables, with a mean of 0.83. The analysis also identified discrepancies between rating sheets and summaries, identical summaries, and misinterpretations of the coefficient. Although peer assessment provide…

title: The School-Bell Flywheel: peer reconvening and the delayed youth breakout of “Golden”
abstract: Purpose Diffusion models used in strategic marketing planning do not specify how calendar-driven transitions in peer-network density govern adoption timing among youth demographics, which may lead managers to withdraw support before conversion windows open. This study aims to introduce the School-Bell Flywheel, referred to as the BELL framework, which comprises four sequential processes: Build a Reservoir, Energize Rituals, Lift into Households, and Leverage Platforms. The framework aligns marketing resource allocation with network state transitions. Design/methodology/approach The study develops theory through integration of complex contagion theory, media richness theory and consumer socialization research, using an in-depth illustrative anchor case (Netflix’s KPop Demon Hunters and the delayed breakout of its song “Golden”) with a corroborating illustration from Disney’s Encanto. Findings The study proposes that summer visibility converts to mainstream adoption when reconvening peer networks enable crossing complex contagion thresholds. Under specified conditions, institutional device restrictions are proposed to amplify adoption by channeling influence into richer face-to-face interaction. The framework is formalized in six testable propositions. Practical implications The study provides a Sleeper-Hit Risk Map assessing delayed diffusion candidacy, a phase-by-phase resource…

title: BÜDCƏ SİYASƏTİN REALLAŞDIRILMASI NƏTİCƏSİNDƏ VERGİ POTENSİALININ FORMALAŞMASI
abstract: Məqalədə büdcə siyasətinin həyata keçirilməsi nəticəsində vergi potensialının formalaşması məsələləri araşdırılmışdır. Büdcə siyasətinin iqtisadi inkişafın təmin edilməsində, dövlət gəlirlərinin artırılmasında və vergi bazasının genişləndirilməsində rolu təhlil edilmişdir. Dövlətin fiskal siyasət vasitəsilə iqtisadi proseslərə təsir mexanizmləri, büdcə xərclərinin strukturunun vergi potensialına təsiri və Azərbaycanda həyata keçirilən büdcə islahatlarının nəticələri yerli alimlərin elmi yanaşmaları əsasında qiymətləndirilmişdir. Tədqiqat nəticəsində müəyyən edilmişdir ki, səmərəli büdcə siyasəti vergi potensialının artırılmasının əsas iqtisadi alətlərindən biridir. Açar sözlər: büdcə siyasəti, vergi potensialı, fiskal siyasət, dövlət maliyyəsi, büdcə gəlirləri.

title: MÜƏSSİSƏLƏRİN RƏQƏMSAL SİSTEMƏ İNTEQRASİYASI ŞƏRAİTİNDƏ İNNOVATİV İDARƏETMƏ MEXANİZMLƏRİNİN FORMALAŞMASI
abstract: Müasir dövrdə qloballaşma və sürətli texnoloji transformasiyalar biznes mühitini köklü şəkildə dəyişərək vahid rəqəmsal ekosistemin formalaşmasına zəmin yaratmışdır. Belə bir dinamik şəraitdə müəssisələrin rəqabət qabiliyyətinin qorunması və davamlı inkişafının təmin edilməsi, onların daxili biznes proseslərini innovativ idarəetmə mexanizmləri əsasında yenidən qurmasından asılıdır. Tədqiqatın əsas məqsədi müəssisələrin rəqəmsal ekosistemə inteqrasiyası prosesində qarşıya çıxan çağırışları təhlil etmək və effektiv idarəetmə modellərinin formalaşması yollarını müəyyənləşdirməkdir. Məqalədə ənənəvi iyerarxik idarəetmə strukturundan çevik (Agile) modellərə keçidin zərurəti əsaslandırılmış, verilənlərə əsaslanan (Data-driven) qərarvermə mexanizmlərinin əhəmiyyəti araşdırılmışdır. Eyni zamanda, açıq innovasiya strategiyalarının daxili korporativ mədəniyyətə inteqrasiyası mexanizmləri təhlil olunmuşdur. Aparılan tədqiqat nəticəsində müəyyən edilmişdir ki, rəqəmsal ekosistemdə uğurlu fəaliyyət sadəcə texnoloji infrastrukturun yenilənməsini deyil, həm də strateji idarəetmə metodologiyasının fundamental transformasiyasını tələb edir. Burada əsas hədəf rəqəmsal platformalar şəraitində müəssisələrin şəbəkələşmə prinsiplərinə əsaslanan inteqrasiya modelinin təklif edilməsidir. Açar sözlər: rəqəmsal ekosistem, innovativ idarəetmə, biznes proseslər, çevik idarəetmə (Agile), korporativ transfo…

title: İSTEHSAL HEYƏTİNİN İNKİŞAFINDA KARYERA İDARƏÇİLİYİNİN ROLU: MÜASİR YANAŞMALAR VƏ PERSPEKTİVLƏR
abstract: Məqalədə müasir istehsal müəssisələrində istehsal heyətinin inkişafında karyera idarəçiliyinin rolu araşdırılır. Texnoloji dəyişikliklərin sürətlənməsi, istehsal proseslərinin rəqəmsallaşması və əmək bazarında kompetensiyalara olan tələblərin dəyişməsi müəssisələrdə insan kapitalının davamlı inkişafını zəruri edir. Bu şəraitdə karyera idarəçiliyi işçilərin peşəkar potensialının müəyyənləşdirilməsi, kompetensiyalarının inkişaf etdirilməsi, daxili mobilliyinin təmin olunması və gələcək vəzifələrə hazırlanması vasitəsi kimi çıxış edir. Məqalədə karyera idarəçiliyinin nəzəri əsasları, ənənəvi və müasir yanaşmalar, istedadların idarə edilməsi, kompetensiya əsaslı inkişaf, fərdi inkişaf planları, mentorluq, varislik planlaşdırılması və rəqəmsal HR alətlərinin istehsal heyətinin inkişafına təsiri təhlil edilir. Eyni zamanda istehsal müəssisələrində karyera idarəçiliyinin təkmilləşdirilməsi istiqamətləri müəyyənləşdirilir. Tədqiqatın nəticələri göstərir ki, karyera idarəçiliyinin strateji insan resursları siyasəti ilə inteqrasiyası istehsal heyətinin peşəkar potensialının inkişafına, daxili kadr ehtiyatının formalaşmasına və müəssisənin dəyişən texnoloji tələblərə uyğunlaşmasına şərait yaradır. Açar sözlər: karyera idarəçiliyi, istehsal heyəti, insan kapitalı, karyera inkişafı, istedadların idarə edilməsi, daxili mobillik, varislik planlaşdırılması, rəqəmsal HR.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Muscle Energy Technique Combined with Ultrasonic Therapy versus Myofascial Release Combined with Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation in Sciatic Nerve Pain due to Prolapsed Intervertebral Disc: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Sciatic nerve pain due to Prolapsed Intervertebral Disc (PIVD) is a common cause of radiating low back pain, reduced mobility, neural tension, and functional disability. Muscle Energy Technique (MET), Myofascial Release (MFR), Ultrasonic Therapy (UST), and Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) are each individually supported by evidence, but comparative evidence on combined manual-therapyplus-electrotherapy protocols for PIVD-related sciatica remains limited. Objective: To compare the effectiveness of Muscle Energy Technique combined with Ultrasonic Therapy (Group A) against Myofascial Release combined with TENS (Group B) on pain intensity, functional disability, neural mobility, and lumbar range of motion in patients with sciatic nerve pain due to PIVD. Methods: In this randomized controlled trial, 60 participants aged 40–55 years with MRI-confirmed PIVD (4–8 mm disc protrusion) and clinical sciatica were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to Group A (MET + UST, n = 30) or Group B (MFR + TENS, n = 30). Both groups received treatment three sessions per week for 4 weeks. Outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), the Straight Leg Raise (SLR) Test, and lumbar Range of Motion (ROM) at baseline and after 4 weeks. Results: Both groups improved significantly on all outcome measures from baseline to post-t…
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: The Effects of Peer Correction in Flipped Essay-Writing Classrooms: A Study of Selected Universities in Vietnam
abstract: The study focused on a practical question in university writing classes: what changes when peer correction is built into a flipped lesson sequence, especially after students have produced a first draft. Over five months in the second semester of 2024–2025, 150 second-year English-major students from three universities in Ho Chi Minh City took part in a mixed-methods quasi-experiment. Seventy-five students experienced the flipped model with structured peer correction, and 75 followed the comparison condition. Nine English lecturers contributed written interview responses. The data included pre- and post-test essays, a student questionnaire, lecturer interviews, and the peer-correction checklists used during the intervention. Writing scores were examined statistically, while interview responses were coded for recurring themes. The experimental group moved from a mean of 5.18 on the pre-test to 6.45 on the post-test; the control group changed from 5.19 to 5.12. Students also described greater confidence in exchanging feedback and reported that the checklist helped with revision, organization, and time management. Lecturers mainly valued having more class time to discuss drafts and respond to individual problems. The results do not separate the effect of peer correction from the other elements of the flipped design, but they show that checklist-guided peer response can function eff…

title: GENERAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE SOURCES OF INVESTMENT IN THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR
abstract: The aim of the study is to identify the general characteristics of investment sources in the agrarian sector and to systematize their structure, their impact on the development of agricultural production, and the available financing options. The research employs methods such as a systems approach, comparative analysis, statistical generalization, and content analysis of existing scientific literature. The findings indicate that the financing of investment activities in the agricultural sector relies on a diversified structure of sources; this structure is characterized by enterprises' internal financial resources, state-funded financial support and subsidies, bank loans, foreign direct investment, financial resources from international financial institutions, as well as alternative and innovative financing mechanisms. The primary limitations in this field stem from the presentation of agrarian investment data across various sources using differing methodologies, the limited availability of certain indicators, and the difficulty of conducting comprehensive regional comparisons. The originality of the research lies in the comprehensive classification of investment sources for the agrarian sector, considered within the context of financial capabilities and the sustainable development of agriculture. Its scientific novelty stems from the systematization of the functional characteri…

title: Graduate Students’ Perspectives on Applying Mixed Research Fundamentals to Data Collection and Peer Feedback
abstract: This study explored graduate students' perspectives on applying the fundamentals of mixed methods research (MMR) during data collection and examined how peer feedback shaped these perspectives. We used archival data collected between 2020 and 2025 from an online doctoral research foundation class, and we analyzed participants' responses using thematic analysis. Three major themes emerged: comprehensive understanding through data integration, strengthening research evidence and methodological compatibility, and collaborative learning through peer feedback. Findings indicated that students view MMR as a valuable approach for integrating quantitative and qualitative data, deepening the depth and validity of research findings, and enabling richer interpretations of research problems. Peer feedback was identified as a critical factor in promoting collaborative learning, refining research designs, and increasing confidence in applying mixed methods principles. Future research could incorporate observational or performance-based assessments to complement self-reported perspectives and provide a more comprehensive view of how graduate students operationalize MMR principles in practice.

title: Effects of energy-group resolution on SpecKit-based neutron spectrum unfolding
abstract: Abstract Neutron spectrum unfolding based on neutron activation reactions is an inherently ill-posed inverse problem that is difficult to validate experimentally. This study extends the performance evaluation of the SpecKit software previously published in SoftwareX, with a focus on quantifying the effect of energy-group structure on unfolding accuracy. The ground-truth neutron spectrum was generated using MCNP simulations. The prior spectrum was modeled under the same geometric configuration; however, compared with the ground-truth spectrum, the cement layer in the 60-, 113- and 240-group cases was uniformly reduced by 3 cm to simulate scattering interference and geometric simplification commonly encountered in real-world applications. Comparative unfolding with SpecKit using 60-, 113- and 240-group structures shows that the mean activity error (ERRE) of calculated activities is significantly reduced from 0.165 to 0.050, while the integrated flux also approaches the ground-truth value more closely (ground-truth: 1.606 × 10 6 n/cm 2 /s; 60-group: 1.065 × 10 6 ; 240-group: 1.578 × 10 6 ). These empirical results demonstrate that, within the SpecKit framework, adopting a finer energy-group structure effectively mitigates the ill-posed nature of the problem, enhances numerical stability and reconstruction fidelity, and provides a reliable, reproducible software platform for nuclea…

title: MÜASİR TƏŞKİLATLARDA İSTEDAD MENECMENTİNİN STRATEJİ İNSAN RESURSLARI İDARƏETMƏSİNDƏ ROLU
abstract: Müasir qlobal iqtisadiyyat şəraitində insan kapitalı təşkilatların rəqabət qabiliyyətini müəyyən edən əsas strateji resurslardan birinə çevrilmişdir. Texnoloji inkişaf, rəqəmsal transformasiya və innovasiya proseslərinin sürətlənməsi müəssisələrdə yüksək potensiala malik əməkdaşların cəlb olunması, inkişaf etdirilməsi və saxlanılması məsələlərinin aktuallığını artırmışdır. Məqalədə istedad menecmentinin nəzəri əsasları, strateji insan resursları idarəetmə sistemində rolu və müasir təşkilatların inkişafında əhəmiyyəti araşdırılmışdır. Eyni zamanda istedad menecmentinin əsas funksiyaları, beynəlxalq təcrübədə tətbiq olunan modellər və təşkilatların rəqabət üstünlüyünün formalaşdırılmasına təsiri təhlil edilmişdir. Tədqiqat nəticəsində müəyyən edilmişdir ki, istedad menecmenti sisteminin strateji insan resursları idarəetməsinə inteqrasiyası təşkilatların innovasiya potensialının, əməliyyat səmərəliliyinin və uzunmüddətli dayanıqlı inkişafının təmin edilməsində mühüm rol oynayır. Açar sözlər: istedad menecmenti, insan resurslarının idarə edilməsi, insan kapitalı, strateji idarəetmə, təşkilati inkişaf, rəqabət üstünlüyü.

title: AZƏRBAYCANDA XARİCİ İNVESTİSİYALARIN CƏLB EDİLMƏSİNİN ARTIRILMASI İSTİQAMƏTLƏRİ
abstract: Məqalədə 2020–2025-ci illər dövründə Azərbaycanda xarici investisiyaların cəlb edilməsinin artırılması istiqamətləri kompleks şəkildə təhlil edilmişdir. Tədqiqatda birbaşa xarici investisiyaların dinamikası, sektorial strukturu və mənbə ölkələr üzrə bölgüsü rəsmi statistik məlumatlar əsasında araşdırılmışdır. Təhlil göstərir ki, 2020-ci ildən sonra ölkəyə cəlb olunan xarici investisiyaların həcmi mərhələli şəkildə artmış, xüsusilə 2022–2023-cü illərdə nəzərəçarpacaq yüksəliş müşahidə olunmuşdur. Ənənəvi olaraq neft-qaz sektoru investisiyalarda üstünlük təşkil etsə də, qeyri-neft sahələrinin, o cümlədən nəqliyyat-logistika, kənd təsərrüfatı, sənaye parkları və turizm sektorlarının payı artmaqdadır. Bundan əlavə məqalədə investisiya mühitinin yaxşılaşdırılması məqsədilə həyata keçirilən dövlət siyasəti, vergi və gömrük güzəştləri, azad iqtisadi zonaların yaradılması, rəqəmsal xidmətlərin genişləndirilməsi və institusional islahatların rolu xüsusi vurğulanmışdır. Həmçinin işğaldan azad edilmiş Qarabağ və Şərqi Zəngəzur regionlarında tətbiq olunan onillik vergi azadolmaları və investisiya təşviqlərinin regional inkişaf və kapital axını baxımından əhəmiyyəti əsaslandırılmışdır. Nəticə olaraq, aparılan islahatların və təşviq mexanizmlərinin xarici investisiyaların cəlb edilməsində mühüm rol oynadığı və ölkənin iqtisadi şaxələndirilməsinə töhfə verdiyi qənaətinə gəlinmişdir. title: Recent advances in spectrally selective structural designs for radiative cooling
abstract: Abstract Radiative cooling technology passively dissipates surface heat to outer space through the atmospheric window (8–13 μm), providing an innovative pathway for continuous cooling with zero energy consumption and zero carbon emissions. The core challenge for high-performance daytime radiative cooling lies in strict spectral selectivity: A solar reflectance exceeding 90% in the solar spectrum band (0.3–2.5 μm) is required to minimize solar heating, while an infrared emissivity higher than 90% must be maintained within the atmospheric window to maximize radiative heat dissipation. This review systematically provides the latest advances in radiative cooling materials and structures in recent years, centered on the core driving force of “spectral selective structural design”. According to the optical modulation hierarchy of structural design ranging from random to precise, existing research is categorized into two major technical pathways: (1) Random scattering structures based on intrinsic material properties, including polymer films and functional coatings. Their infrared emission relies on molecular bond vibrations or lattice phonon resonances, while micro/nano pores or fibrous structures enhance solar light reflection via multiple scattering. title: Combined experimental and simulation evaluation of interference-resilient and energy-efficient wireless sensor networks using ESP32, TSCH, and multi-criteria decision analysis
abstract: Introduction Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) used in industrial monitoring and Internet of Things (IoT) applications must simultaneously maintain reliable data transmission, low communication delay, and efficient energy consumption under resource and interference constraints. Methods This study combines an ESP32-based hardware-assisted interference-emulation platform with large-scale OMNeT++ network modeling and multi-criteria evaluation. A 300-node WSN comprising 240 end devices and 60 routers was evaluated using Star, Tree, conventional Mesh, and Mesh + Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) configurations. Performance was assessed using Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), mean transmission delay, energy consumption, and network-lifetime indicators. An additional reconstructed stochastic analysis used 20 independent runs per configuration, and scalability was evaluated for network populations from 50 to 1,000 nodes. Results In the archived scenario-level analysis, Mesh + TSCH increased PDR from 93% to 99%, reduced mean delay from 150 ms to 61 ms, reduced per-node energy consumption from 6.42 J to 2.14 J, and increased the reported LND from 30 to 120 days relative to conventional Mesh. In the reconstructed analysis, Mesh + TSCH maintained higher PDR (79.26 ± 0.83% vs. 51.46 ± 2.49%) and lower per-node energy consumption (59.02 ± 0.65 J vs. 125.96 ± 0.82 J), but showed higher mean end-to…

title: Analysis ANALISIS PENEMPATAN BARANG KONSUMSI DENGAN METODE FSN ANALYSIS DAN CLASS BASED STORAGE UNTUK MENINGKATKAN EFISIENSI PROSES PENGAMBILAN DI GUDANG PT. ARD
abstract: Penempatan barang yang belum mempertimbangkan tingkat pergerakan menyebabkan proses pengambilan barang di gudang menjadi kurang efisien dan dapat meningkatkan waktu operasional. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis penempatan barang konsumsi di gudang PT. ARD menggunakan metode Fast, Slow, Non-Moving (FSN) Analysis dan Class Based Storage (CBS) guna meningkatkan efisiensi penyimpanan dan proses pengambilan barang. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan memanfaatkan data persediaan periode Januari–Desember 2025 yang meliputi persediaan awal, barang masuk, barang keluar, persediaan akhir, ukuran produk, stok maksimum, serta waktu pengambilan barang. Klasifikasi FSN dilakukan berdasarkan nilai Turn Over Ratio (TOR), kemudian hasil klasifikasi digunakan sebagai dasar dalam menentukan kebutuhan area penyimpanan dan pembagian blok menggunakan metode CBS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa dari 64 jenis produk, terdapat 30 produk kategori fast moving, 20 produk kategori slow moving, dan 14 produk kategori non-moving. Total kebutuhan area penyimpanan sebesar 270,2696 m² atau sekitar 31,80% dari luas gudang sebesar 850 m². Total jarak perpindahan sebelum perbaikan tata letak sebesar 115.357,92 meter/tahun, kemudian menurun menjadi 68.593,00 meter/tahun setelah dilakukan penempatan barang berdasarkan tingkat pergerakan. title: Efficacy and safety of antifungal decontamination of preservation fluid under static cold storage conditions: an in vitro study
abstract: Objective To evaluate the antifungal efficacy and safety of amphotericin B (AmB), liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB), and voriconazole (VOR) against common fungal contaminants in preservation fluid (PF) under simulated static cold storage (SCS) conditions, providing in vitro evidence to future graft decontamination strategies. Methods Fungal suspensions of Candida albicans (C. albicans) , Aspergillus fumigatus (A. fumigatus) , and Mucor hiemalis ( M. hiemalis ) in PF were incubated at 0–4 °C for 3 h with AmB (5, 15, and 25 mg/L), L-AmB (50, 100, and 200 mg/L), or VOR (50, 100, and 200 mg/L). Colony-forming units and average inhibition rates (AIRs) were determined. Cytotoxicity was assessed in human renal proximal tubular epithelial (HK-2) cells exposed to the highest concentration of each agent at 0–4 °C for 3, 6, and 18 h. Results No viable colonies were detected for VOR against C. albicans at all concentrations. Against A. fumigatus , L-AmB achieved AIRs of 48.13%–86.14%, exceeding AmB (8.24%–23.22%; P = 0.033) and no statistically significant difference was observed between L-AmB and VOR (15.36%–62.55%; P = 0.267). Against M. hiemalis , medium- and high-dose L-AmB achieved AIRs of 64.93%–88.81%, exceeding AmB (25.37%–36.57%; P = 0.001) and VOR (0%–9.70%; P < 0.001). Investment and Revenue as Determinants of Profitability for Indonesian Banking Companies (2020–2024)
abstract: This study examines the effects of investment and income on the profitability of banking companies in Indonesia during 2020–2024. The research uses a quantitative explanatory design and secondary data from audited annual financial reports. From the banking population used in the thesis, 15 companies were selected through purposive sampling, producing 75 bank-year observations. Investment is measured as total investment relative to total assets, income is represented by the sum of interest and non-interest income, and profitability is proxied by return on assets. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26 after tests of normality, multicollinearity, autocorrelation, and heteroskedasticity. The results show that investment has a positive and statistically significant effect on profitability (B = 2.115, β = 0.249, t = 2.416, p = 0.018). Income also has a positive and statistically significant effect (B = 0.115, β = 0.413, t = 4.003, p < 0.001). Jointly, investment and income significantly explain variation in profitability (F = 11.072, p < 0.001). The model has R² = 0.235 and adjusted R² = 0.214, indicating that 23.5% of the observed variation in profitability is explained by the two predictors. These findings suggest that productive asset allocation and revenue generation are relevant to bank profitability, while substantial variation remains attributable …

Perceived environmental responsibility, green brand image, and green trust: asymmetric moderating roles of green self-concept consistency and green skepticism among electric-motorcycle users
abstract: Background Perceived Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) signals environmental priorities, but consumers may interpret this signal differently when judging brand image and trust. We examine how green skepticism and green self-concept consistency (GSCC) moderate these associations among electric-motorcycle users. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from 29/06/2026 to 28/07/2026, following the institutional ethical clearance issued on 25 June 2026, among 502 consenting adult electric-motorcycle owners or active users in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, recruited through purposive sampling. Six focal associations specified in the broader research framework were reported from SmartPLS 4 estimates using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples, two-tailed tests, and a 5% significance level. Separate composite-score analyses served as robustness checks. Results Perceived ECSR was positively associated with green brand image (β = 0.353, t = 9.363, p < 0.001) and green trust (β = 0.287, t = 7.030, p < 0.001); green brand image was associated with green trust (β = 0.319, t = 6.959, p < 0.001). Green skepticism weakened the ECSR–trust association (β = −0.125, p = 0.011). GSCC weakened the direct ECSR–trust association (β = −0.118, p = 0.002) but strengthened the ECSR–image association (β = 0.141, p < 0.001). The supplementary indirect ECSR → green brand image → green trust assoc…

title: MODELING A FORCED CARBODY TILTING SYSTEM FOR HIGH-SPEED ELECTRIC TRAINS
abstract: The paper examines the modelling of a carbody tilting system for Afrosiab-type high-speed electric trains. Particular attention is given to train operation on curved track, where the permissible running speed must be considered together with passenger ride comfort and the forces transmitted to the infrastructure. Numerical calculations of the adopted mechanical scheme were carried out in Mathcad 15.

title: Electric vehicle growth in Tamil Nadu: beyond major urban centers
abstract: Introduction The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) registrations requires a better understanding of how EV registrations vary across geographical areas. This study examines the geographical and temporal patterns of EV registrations across Regional Transport Office (RTO) regions in Tamil Nadu from 2022 to 2025. Methods Secondary data were obtained from the official Tamil Nadu EV Registration portal. Registrations of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and four-wheelers were analyzed using temporal trends, vehicle-category composition, RTO-level growth, registration concentration, and a separate analysis of Chennai RTO regions. Results Total EV registrations increased from 69,785 in 2022 to 165,818 in 2025, representing a 137.61% increase. Two-wheelers remained the dominant category, while four-wheelers recorded substantial growth. Tiruppur and Coimbatore emerged as important RTOs in 2025. The share of the top five and top ten RTOs decreased from 14.24% and 24.52% in 2022 to 11.28% and 19.90% in 2025, respectively. Chennai registrations increased from 11,663 to 17,499 during the study period. Discussion The findings show a clear increase in EV registrations across Tamil Nadu, along with changes in the contribution of different RTO areas and vehicle categories. IMPLEMENTASI MODEL PEMBELAJARAN MAKE A MATCH DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA KELAS II SD
abstract: Low learning outcomes in Pancasila Education among second-grade students at UPTD SD Negeri 076674 Orahili Tanoseo indicated the need for a more active and engaging learning process. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Make a Match learning model and the improvement of students’ learning outcomes on the topic “I Care for the Environment.” The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. The participants were 14 second-grade students, consisting of 6 boys and 8 girls. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning achievement tests, and field notes. The data were analyzed using qualitative and quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed an increase in teacher activity from 51% in the first meeting of Cycle I to 92% in the second meeting of Cycle II. Student activity increased from 58% to 95% across the same meetings. Learning outcomes also improved: the mean score in Cycle I was 67.7, with 36% mastery or 5 of 14 students, while Cycle II reached a mean score of 81.6, with 85% mastery or 12 students. The classical mastery therefore exceeded the predetermined success indicator of 75%. Thus, the Make a Match learning model can be used as an alternative approach to increase student engagement and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education at the eleme…

title: The scientific entrepreneur: an entrepreneurial strategy linking founder resilience to enhanced venture sustainability performance
abstract: Purpose Sustainability performance is increasingly becoming a core commercial requirement for new ventures rather than a peripheral societal responsibility initiative. However, we still lack a more systematic understanding of the role that entrepreneurial micro-foundations and strategies play in achieving superior venture sustainability outcomes. Drawing on the Resource-based View of the Firm and Stewardship Theory, we examine how founder resilience and an Entrepreneurs-as-Scientists (EaS) approach interact in shaping new venture sustainability performance. Design/methodology/approach We test our research hypotheses on a sample from the 2023 wave of the Global University Entrepreneurial Spirit Students' Survey, which includes over 13,000 active founders across 39 countries. Findings The findings demonstrate that founder resilience is positively associated with new venture sustainability performance. We find that the effect of resilience as a psychological resource improving sustainability performance is mediated through the adoption of an EaS approach. Moreover, we provide evidence that founder resilience moderates this relationship, helping founders leverage the EaS approach to strengthen sustainability performance. Originality/value Our study advances understanding of the micro foundations of sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship by identifying the EaS approach as a decisi…
venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behavior & Research

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PROJECT BASED LEARNING (PjBL) UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR IPAS SISWA KELAS III UPTD SDN 071030 AFIA
abstract: Learning outcomes are one of the indicators of the success of the learning process. However, the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia are still relatively low, necessitating a learning model that can improve student learning outcomes. This study aims to improve the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia through the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model. The research design used was Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of the planning, implementation, observation, and reflection stages. The research subjects were 20 third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia. Data collection techniques included tests, observations, and documentation. The data were analyzed both quantitatively and qualitatively. The results showed that students’ IPAS learning outcomes in the pre-cycle stage were 30%, then increased to 60% in Cycle I, and rose further to 85% in Cycle II. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model is effective in improving the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia.

title: Future of work in the era of AI: how technology strategy shapes daily job roles
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the impact of organizational technology strategies, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), on employees’ daily job activities. It also looks at the extent of the transformation and the role of leadership, supportive of innovation and cultural change, in reinforcing the transformation. Design/methodology/approach The researcher adopted a quantitative research design based on the survey data collected from employees in various industries in Pakistan. The researcher used structural equation modeling to analyze the relationships among technology strategies, organizational facilitators and the transformation of job roles. Findings The research shows that organizations that implement AI and automation alongside digitized processes and advanced data analysis capabilities will experience fundamental changes in their employees’ work functions, skills and job duties. The implementation of digital strategies enhances operational efficiency, but their impact extends beyond this benefit, as they completely transform how work is executed. The presence of an innovation-supportive culture together with strong leadership commitment creates an enhanced effect. The combination of encouragement of organizational experimentation and active leadership support for technological change results in more visible and positive changes in job responsi…

title: PENERAPAN MODEL KOOPERATIF TIPE NUMBERED HEAD TOGETHER DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA MURID KELAS IV
abstract: The learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at UPTD SD Negeri 074048 Luaha Bouso were still low because previous learning tended to be teacher-centered, resulting in limited student activity, collaboration, and participation. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Numbered Head Together (NHT) cooperative learning model and to determine the improvement of students' learning outcomes in Pancasila Education after its implementation. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection, with two meetings in each cycle. The subjects were 19 fourth-grade students in the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning outcome tests, documentation, and field notes, and were analyzed descriptively using qualitative and quantitative approaches. The NHT implementation involved heterogeneous group formation, assigning numbers to group members, presenting questions or tasks, group discussion, random number calling, presentation of answers, and reinforcement. The findings showed that teacher activity increased from 58% in Cycle I Meeting I to 90% in Cycle II Meeting II, while student activity increased from 57.69% to 94.23%. Learning outcomes also improved, as…

title: PENGARUH ENTREPRENEUR EDUCATION, FAMILY ENVIRONMENT, DAN ENTREPRENEURIAL PASSION TERHADAP ENTREPRENEUR INTENTION MELALUI SELF-EFFICACY PADA PESERTA PELATIHAN YAYASAN KARANG WIDYA (THE LEARNING FARM)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh pendidikan kewirausahaan, lingkungan keluarga, dan gairah kewirausahaan terhadap niat berwirausaha melalui efikasi diri sebagai variabel intervening pada peserta pelatihan Yayasan Karang Widya (The Learning Farm). Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan dalam penelitian ini dengan metode survei menggunakan kuesioner yang disebarkan kepada 100 responden, yang terdiri dari peserta dan alumni pelatihan kewirausahaan. Teknik analisis data menggunakan Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pendidikan kewirausahaan, lingkungan keluarga, dan gairah kewirausahaan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap efikasi diri dan niat berwirausaha. Selain itu, efikasi diri terbukti sebagai variabel mediasi yang memperkuat hubungan antara ketiga variabel independen dengan niat berwirausaha. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoritis bagi pengembangan literatur kewirausahaan dan implikasi praktis bagi lembaga pelatihan untuk meningkatkan efektivitas program kewirausahaan berbasis efikasi diri.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustne…

title: Hybrid one-shot and vertical federated learning framework for privacy-preserving brain tumor classification and segmentation using the BRISC2025 dataset
abstract: Introduction From MRI images, diagnosis of brain tumors may have limitations due to restriction over patient privacy and lack of annotated datasets so that models cannot be trained across multiple institutions. Methods HOS-VFL: A Hybrid One-Shot and Vertical Federated Learning framework with a two-round protocol that jointly enjoys the advantages of prototype-based one-shot aggregation and encrypted vertical feature space augmentation. Tested on BRISC2025 MRimages of glioma, meningioma, pituitary and non-tumor, with T1-weighted images, expert-annotated, at five simulated institutions, with simulated IID and Dirichlet setups. Results HOS-VFL obtained values of 98.73% on accuracy and 35–50 for conventional federated learning, with a 94.3% reduction compared to the best baseline valued. HOS-VFL performed 98.73% accuracy and 35–50 for the conventional federated learning with an improvement of 94.3% when compared with its best baseline accuracy. The mean Dice and IoU of Segmentation was 0.9147, 0.8423 respectively. Performance did not wane differently in terms of competitive levels and number of institutions, and was able to withstand gradient inference attacks. Discussion HOS-VFL philosophy is centralised performance with minimum communication with retention of raw data local. The method needs to be validated on larger real multi-center datasets before their clinical use.

title: Enhancing Cyber Security Through Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Approach to Intelligent Threat Detection and Prevention
abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies and interconnected systems has significantly increased cyber security risks worldwide. Traditional security mechanisms often struggle to detect sophisticated cyber threats due to the evolving nature of attacks. Machine Learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful solution for enhancing cyber security by enabling automated threat detection, anomaly identification, malware classification, and intrusion prevention. This paper examines the role of machine learning in strengthening cyber security frameworks, evaluates different ML algorithms used in cyber defense, and presents a comparative analysis of their effectiveness. The findings suggest that machine learning-based approaches significantly improve detection accuracy while reducing response times compared to conventional security methods.

Development of a Moodle LMS-Assisted Blended Learning Model in the Information Systems Study Program at Institut Hasan Sulur
abstract: Integrating face-to-face and online learning in higher education requires coherent instructional design and appropriate digital support. This study evaluated the feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness of a Moodle-assisted blended learning model in the Information Systems Study Program. A research and development (R&D) approach was employed, with data collected through expert validation, student responses, classroom activity observations, and pretest and posttest assessments. Evaluation scores were 90% for learning materials, 91% for media presentation, 90% for practicality, 88% for pedagogical aspects, 93% for instructional devices, and 89% for the user guidebook. Individual, small-group, and field trials yielded scores of 84.76%, 89%, and approximately 96%, respectively. The student learning activity assessment yielded 87%. Mean test scores increased from 31.53 before implementation to 45.93 afterward, out of a maximum of 54. These descriptive findings support the model’s feasibility and practicality, while the observed score increase provides preliminary evidence of potential learning benefits. The study contributes a technology-supported instructional model for systematically integrating face-to-face and online activities in higher education, with practical implications for lecturers and institutions implementing blended learning. title: Coarse-to-fine-grained insulator defect detection using two-stage deep learning framework
abstract: Introduction In power transmission and power distribution systems, insulators are the fundamental components which provide mechanical support and electrical isolation between conductors and supporting towers. However, these insulators are continuously exposed to extreme weather conditions, mechanical stress, pollution and dust, which can lead to surface damage and abnormal operation. Method Conventionally, manual on-site inspection is performed to identify faulty insulators. However, this method is labor intensive, risky, and reactive. With the advancement in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning method, automatic visual inspection has replaced the conventional methods. However, automatic visual inspection from UAV images is challenging task due to complex background and small size of the insulators. To address these challenges, we proposed a framework that consists of two stages. In the first stage, you only look once (YOLO)-based is used for extracting candidate region of insulator to get coarse class prediction. During the second stage, the candidate regions are then cropped from the image into image patches and fed to a lightweight patch-level classifier. In order to enhance inter-class separability, hard-pair contrastive classification loss is proposed by adding hard-pair contrastive term to the cross-entropy loss in the embedding space. Wearable sensor-based haptic feedback systems for motor learning and gait reshaping: a review
abstract: Purpose This review aims to examine wearable sensor-based haptic feedback systems for motor learning and gait reshaping, with emphasis on the closed-loop chain from sensing to behavioral change. Design/methodology/approach This structured narrative review used a transparent search boundary. Literature was identified from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar for work published from January 2000 to May 2026 using combined terms for wearable sensors, haptic or vibrotactile feedback, biofeedback, gait, motor learning, Parkinson disease, stroke, older adults and foot-progression retraining. Studies were included when they reported wearable sensing, closed-loop or cue-based feedback, gait or motor-learning outcomes, validation metrics or deployment constraints; papers were excluded when they were unrelated to gait, lacked wearable sensing/feedback relevance, provided no usable quantitative or architectural information or duplicated a more complete report. Because outcomes and populations were heterogeneous, findings were synthesized as a structured narrative with quantitative comparison tables rather than a pooled meta-analysis. title: Organizational trust in the workplace: explainable machine learning evidence from Ecuadorian workers
abstract: Organizational trust reflects employees' willingness to accept vulnerability on the basis of positive expectations about supervisors and the organization. This study examined whether organizational cynicism, organizational climate, job satisfaction, and worker characteristics contain reproducible information for distinguishing high organizational trust among workers in Ecuador. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was applied to 899 valid survey records obtained through non-probability availability sampling. The focal construct was the 12-item Organizational Trust Inventory, comprising trust in the immediate supervisor and trust in the organization. High trust was defined a priori as a mean score of at least 5.0, the first response anchor labeled “High,” yielding 555 high-trust and 344 non-high-trust cases. Ordinal confirmatory factor analysis supported the proposed measurement structures; composite reliability ranged from 0.833 to 0.965, and the four-construct measurement model showed good fit ( CFI = 0.991, TLI = 0.991, RMSEA = 0.036). Logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared through nested cross-validation, training-only hyperparameter tuning, a held-out test set, and bootstrap uncertainty intervals. Logistic regression achieved the highest nested cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.865), while CatBoost obtained the highest…

title: Multimodal machine learning approaches for accurate wave overtopping discharge predictions
abstract: Accurate prediction of wave overtopping discharge is essential for designing resilient coastal defences against increasing climate threats. This study demonstrates the superior performance of advanced machine learning models over traditional methods. Using an extensive dataset from EurOtop manual, authors developed and benchmarked models including convolutional and long short-term memory neural networks (CNNs and LSTMs), enhanced with attention mechanisms. Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation ensured robust performance. Predictive uncertainty was quantified via bootstrap resampling (100 ensembles). Results show LSTMs with attention achieved the highest predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.8704, RMSE = 0.0620), effectively capturing complex non-linear dependencies in wave-structure interactions. Coverage analysis revealed systematic under-coverage: 66.7% for the lowest predicted quartile rising to 89.2% for the highest, indicating overconfidence. Partial dependence plots are used to visualise the marginal effect of top input features of the best model, confirming physically expected trends. Permutation feature importance identified relative freeboard and roughness factor as the dominant predictors. The integration of attention mechanisms improved model interpretability by identifying most influential input features. This work provides a reliable, computationally efficient framework that …

title: GAMES BASED LEARNING DETECTIVE CONFLICT DALAM BIMBINGAN KELOMPOK UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN MENGELOLA KONFLIK SISWA SMP
abstract: Peer conflict represents a natural facet of adolescent social dynamics that can impair interpersonal relationships if left unmanaged. This study aimed to describe the implementation of group guidance utilizing a games-based learning approach through the Detective Conflict game and to identify differences in conflict management skill scores among seventh-grade students before and after the intervention. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with eight students of class VII C at SMP Negeri 11 Malang, selected via purposive sampling based on student needs assessment data. Data were gathered through a 40-item conflict management skill scale administered at pre-test and post-test sessions and analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed rank test. The results demonstrated a statistically significant increase in mean scores from 131.75 (SD = 7.03) to 138.88 (SD = 5.38) with Z = −2.457 and p = 0.014, indicating a significant difference in student scores following the intervention. In conclusion, active student participation in the Detective Conflict game exhibits viable potential as an alternative group guidance medium, although the limitations of a single-group pre-experimental design preclude definitive causal claims. title: Nurturing an Understanding of Trustworthiness in Cross-Cultural Doctoral Research: An Autoethnography Exploring Active Learning in Higher Education
abstract: <i>University leaders, researchers, students, and policymakers frequently call for increased active learning in higher education. Within this context, novice scholars grapple with how to meaningfully nurture an understanding of trustworthiness throughout the doctoral research process. This study addresses that gap by examining how an innovative reflexive binning system, grounded in the ICAP framework and informed by multilayered reflexivity, can help novice scholars develop an understanding of trustworthiness in cross-cultural doctoral research. Using autoethnography combined with visual vignettes, the study traces the author’s development as a doctoral student learning to engage with qualitative inquiry in reflexive and relational ways. The study examines how developing a reflexive binning system served as a methodological tool for building an understanding of trustworthiness and how engagement with the system reflected progression across the modes of the ICAP framework. The reflexive bins system organizes data across literature, artifacts, experiences, and interviews while integrating structured generative questions and interactive dialogue. Multilayered reflexivity provides the analytic lens for examining how self, interpersonal, and collective dimensions of reflexivity shaped meaning-making across the research process. Reducing Export Uncertainty: The Impact of the US-Colombia Free Trade Agreement
abstract: Abstract In an era of geopolitical instability and weakening multilateral trade regimes, the institutionalization of trade preferences influences the export behavior of firms. This paper examines the impact of the 2012 US-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on the export margins of Colombian companies. Prior to the FTA, most Colombian exports already enjoyed duty-free access under temporary preferential programs, but these could be extended and suspended without notice, leading to considerable trade policy uncertainty. Using detailed firm-product-destination export data from the Colombian National Export Registry, we perform a triple-difference estimation of the impact of the FTA on exports that exploits variation over time, product coverage, and destinations. A key contribution is a measure of policy uncertainty at the product level based on the difference between Most Favored Nation tariffs and past preferential tariffs. We find that the FTA has significantly increased exports of treated products to the US, primarily by reducing uncertainty. There is also evidence of modest indirect effects. The results underscore the importance of stable, credible trade policy frameworks for promoting export growth and investment at the firm level.

title: Heat treatment optimization and Chromium Nitride precipitation control in heavy-section Superduplex Stainless Steel forgings
abstract: The optimization of mechanical properties in superduplex stainless steel forgings requires precise control of phase balance and precipitation kinetics. This study investigates the effect of different heat treatment routes, including single- and double-step solution annealing and varying cooling rates, on Cr nitride precipitation and secondary austenite formation in S32760 superduplex stainless steel. Mechanical and corrosion properties were assessed through Charpy impact, tensile, Vickers hardness, and pitting corrosion tests, complemented by optical and SEM microstructural characterization. Unlike the heat treatment, the radial sampling position within the investigated forged component did not significantly affect the measured properties. While pitting corrosion resistance remained unaffected, impact toughness was highly sensitive to the thermal treatment. A single-step treatment at 1120 °C caused severe embrittlement due to extensive Cr nitride precipitation, whereas a second solution annealing step at 1060 °C was necessary to restore toughness. Its effectiveness, however, depended strongly on the cooling rate applied after the first step. title: STRATEGIC OPTIMIZATION OF PROVINCIAL-AUTHORITY IRRIGATION NETWORKS IN WEST JAVA: A MULTI- OBJECTIVE PROGRAMMING FRAMEWORK FOR PERFORMANCE-BASED BUDGETING
abstract: Provincial irrigation agencies in West Java must allocate limited operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation budgets across ageing networks in uneven condition. This study develops a Multi-Objective Programming (MOP) framework for the 99 provincial-authority irrigation areas that integrates the six-aspect Irrigation System Performance Index (IKSI) of Ministerial Regulation No. 12/PRT/M/2015 directly into the optimization model, and links it to physical-condition assessment, budget scenarios, a five-year simulation, and qualitative policy interpretation. The model minimizes public expenditure while maximizing IKSI-weighted performance and the share of crop-water requirements met, subject to water, hydraulic, regulatory, and fiscal constraints. Evidence comes from a field survey of 99 canal segments and planning and budget documents. Of the 99 surveyed segments, 38 (38.4%) were in good, 41 (41.4%) in moderate, and 20 (20.2%) in damaged condition. Under the realistic budget scenario, the good-condition share is projected to reach 45.4–48.4% by 2029, an increase of 7–10 percentage points; this is a scenario projection, not a Pareto-optimal solution. The framework reframes irrigation budgeting as a strategic portfolio-allocation problem.

Beyond Hemostasis: Integrated Anticoagulation Reversal, Hemodynamic Optimization, and Neurosurgical Decision-Making in Intracerebral Hemorrhage
abstract: Anticoagulant-associated intracerebral hemorrhage represents a life-threatening neurological emergency characterized by rapid hematoma expansion, secondary cerebral injury, and substantial risks of mortality and long-term functional disability. Its management requires coordinated therapeutic strategies addressing anticoagulant activity, systemic hemodynamics, and intracranial complications. This narrative review critically examines current international evidence regarding pharmacological reversal, blood pressure management, and neurosurgical intervention, incorporating perspectives relevant to Latin American healthcare systems. Twenty scientific publications, including randomized controlled trials, observational investigations, and clinical guidelines, were analyzed through a comparative qualitative approach. Evidence from the INCH trial demonstrated more rapid normalization of coagulation parameters with four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate than with fresh frozen plasma. ANNEXA-I reported greater hemostatic efficacy with andexanet alfa compared with usual care, although thrombotic complications were more frequent and functional benefits were not established. Findings from INTERACT2 and ATACH-II highlighted differences in clinical outcomes associated with intensive blood pressure reduction, whereas INTERACT3 demonstrated improved functional outcomes through coordinated m…

title: Formulation, Optimization and Evaluation of topical Niosomal Gel for Oxiconazole
abstract: Niosomes are novel vesicular drug-delivery systems that can improve drug entrapment, provide controlled drug release, and prolong drug residence at the site of application. Oxiconazole nitrate is a broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal agent used for the treatment of superficial fungal infections. However, conventional topical formulations may have limited residence time The objectives of the present study were to develop an ideal drugdelivery system for the effective treatment of fungal infections, maintain the therapeutic drug concentration for an appropriate period, enhance patient compliance, and improve the therapeutic effectiveness of the formulation. The study also aimed to reduce adverse effects and enhance the bioavailability of the drug. Furthermore, the study focused on formulating a novel drug-delivery system using an appropriate formulation technique and evaluating the developed formulation through SEM analysis, drug content, entrapment efficiency, and in-vitro drug-release studies. Finally, stability studies were performed to assess the physical and pharmaceutical stability of the optimized formulation. Oxiconazole-loaded niosomes were prepared by the ether injection method using Tween 80 and cholesterol. A Box–Behnken design was employed using cholesterol concentration, Tween 80 concentration, and stirring speed as independent variables. Particle size, zeta potenti…

title: A Stochastic Age-Structured SI Epidemics Model with Logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Process
abstract: In this paper, a new stochastic age-structured SI epidemic model with logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process is proposed. The study mainly focuses on the long-term behavior of solutions for the proposed stochastic system. For this, the existence and (global) asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the deterministic system without OU process are first discussed. Then the properties of extinction and asymptotic persistence of solutions for the stochastic system are investigated and the corresponding threshold conditions for them are obtained successfully. This research highlights the importance of considering randomness in the transmission of the epidemic, especially with complex disease mechanisms and random environmental factors. The findings here reveal that interestingly the reversion speed of the OU process impacts how quickly the system stabilizes, while the magnitude of random disturbances can alter the stability potentially and even cause a resurgence of an infectious disease which is expected to go extinct.
venue: East Asian Journal on Applied Mathematics

title: Stochastic nonlinear dynamics of the FitzHugh–Nagumo model: traveling waves, bifurcations and chaotic neuronal insight
abstract: Purpose This research investigates the nonlinear stochastic FitzHugh–Nagumo equation, with a focus on traveling wave solutions, bifurcation theory, chaotic behavior and emphasizing how noise, such as ion channel oscillations and conductivity changes, affects neuronal pulse behavior. Design/methodology/approach By utilizing the extended modified tanh expansion method, diverse analytical solutions, including hyperbolic, trigonometric and periodic forms, are achieved. The impacts of parameter changes on these solutions are visualized in 2D and 3D, and the effects of stochastic excitation are investigated for real-world neuroscience relevance. Findings The study explores the influence of noise on chaotic behavior and wave patterns, with visualizations revealing complex dynamics between parameters and their effects on neuronal activity. Research limitations/implications While the model provides valuable insights, it doesn't fully account for spatial heterogeneity or higher-dimensional systems, which could be explored in future research. Originality/value This work presents novel insights into the role of stochastic noise in neuronal dynamics, providing analytical solutions and deepening our understanding of nerve impulse communication in computational neuroscience.

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security. The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, mu…

title: Optimization of N, P, and K Fertilizer Rates for ‘IPB 13S’ Rice
abstract: Fertilizer recommendations for newly released rice varieties need to be optimized because nutrient requirements may vary among varieties and growing environments. ‘IPB 13S’ is a newly released rice variety developed by IPB University, and information regarding its optimal nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P2O5), and potassium (K2O) requirements is still limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the optimal rates of N, P2O5, and K2O fertilizers for ‘IPB 13S’ rice. The study was conducted from May to September 2024 at the Sawah Baru Experimental Farm, Dramaga, Bogor, Indonesia. Three fertilizer experiments (N, P2O5, and K2O) were arranged in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with five fertilizer levels (0%, 50%, 100%, 150%, and 200% of the regional recommended rate) and three replications. Growth parameters, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency were evaluated. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance, orthogonal polynomial analysis, and quadratic regression. The results showed that N, P2O5, and K2O applications significantly affected plant growth, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency. Quadratic regression analysis identified optimal fertilizer rates of 170 kg N/ha, 53 kg P2O5/ha, and 71 kg K2O/ha, resulting in the highest predicted grain yield. These findings indicate that variety-specific fertilizer recommendations are nee…

title: Integrated 3D-printed Raman spectrometers: rapid manufacturing and structural insights via CT-based analysis
abstract: Purpose Compact optical systems often face long fabrication and verification cycles that slow early-stage development. This study aims to shorten the development cycle of compact optical systems through rapid manufacturing and integrated validation. Design/methodology/approach An integrated design methodology combining optical simulation, additive manufacturing and nondestructive inspection is proposed. Mechanical structures for compact optical assemblies are fabricated using 3D printing. X-ray computed tomography (CT) is used to evaluate printing and assembly accuracy without disassembly. A Raman spectrometer is used as a demonstrator, in which both Czerny–Turner (C-T) and crossed C-T configurations are designed, printed, assembled and experimentally tested. Findings The experimental results show that clear Raman signals can be detected within an integration time of 0.5 s, demonstrating that the 3D-printed mechanical structures provide sufficient stability and alignment accuracy for functional optical performance. CT inspection successfully reveals manufacturing and assembly deviations, enabling rapid assessment and iteration of the system design. Originality/value This work presents a novel workflow that integrates simulation-driven design, rapid additive manufacturing and CT-based nondestructive inspection for compact optical systems. Cyclone-induced economic and non-economic loss and damage in coastal Bangladesh: A geospatial comparison of Kalapara and Dumki using an Integrated Loss and Damage Index
abstract: Tropical cyclones continue to cause extensive economic and non-economic losses across coastal Bangladesh. Empirical assessments often focus narrowly on monetary damage while ignoring spatial disparities and non-economic impacts. This study provides a comparative evaluation of cyclone-induced loss and damage (L&D) in two distinct upazilas of Patuakhali District: the highly exposed coastal zone of Kalapara and the inland Dumki. Using a quantitative–spatial framework, the research collected primary data from 400 households and integrated it with geospatial hazard modelling, socioeconomic vulnerability assessment, and spatial risk–hotspot analysis in QGIS 3.38. Three indices were developed: the total economic loss index (ELI), the non-economic loss index (NELI), and the integrated loss and damage index (ILDI). The ILDI was constructed as a composite index by assigning equal weights to the economic loss index (ELI) and the non-economic loss index (NELI). Mann–Whitney U tests showed that economic losses did not differ significantly between the two upazilas (p = 0.124), whereas non-economic losses were significantly higher in Kalapara (p < 0.001). This difference was reflected in the ILDI (p < 0.001), indicating that variation in non-economic dimensions, including psychological distress, displacement, educational disruption, environmental degradation, and decline in well-being, was mo…

Integrated multi-omics profiling identifies ECM-associated and systemic metabolic alterations associated with osteosarcoma metastasis
abstract: Introduction Osteosarcoma metastasis remains a major clinical challenge, and the molecular programs underlying metastatic progression across omics layers are still incompletely understood. Methods We established an orthotopic osteosarcoma metastasis model using fluorescence-labeled 143B cells and performed integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and serum metabolomic profiling. Multi-omics integration identified cross-layer RNA-protein-metabolite associations and prioritized hub molecules, including COL1A2, SPARC, ATP1A2, ACTA1, and MPZ. Public validation in TARGET-OS and GSE21257 supported a conserved hub/ECM co-expression module across independent cohorts. Functional assays evaluated the role of COL1A2 in osteosarcoma cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Results Histological examination confirmed lung metastatic lesions in 6/6 metastasis-bearing mice but not in non-metastatic controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling revealed concurrent ECM remodeling and metabolic pathway alterations. Multi-omics integration identified 32 consistently altered molecules across all three omics layers. COL1A2 was prioritized as a key hub molecule. COL1A2 knockdown promoted, whereas COL1A2 overexpression suppressed, osteosarcoma cell proliferation, migration, and Transwell invasion. Rescue experiments confirmed COL1A2-dependent regulation of these malignant phenotypes. Conclusion Th…
