title: BEYOND USABILITY: CRITICALLY EXAMINING USER-CENTERED WARDROBE DESIGN, INCLUSIVE ADAPTATION AND CONTEXTUAL OPTIMIZATION TRADE-OFFS
abstract: This systematic review comprehensively explores the multi-dimensional application mechanism, practical optimization effects and current research status of user-centered design (UCD) in residential wardrobe innovation. Guided by the PRISMA framework, this study adopts a rigorous systematic literature review methodology to ensure the standardization and transparency of the screening and synthesis process. Relevant literature covering wardrobe design, user-centered design, furniture usability and residential user experience was retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. Following strict screening based on unified inclusion and exclusion criteria, 48 peer-reviewed academic studies were finally selected for thematic coding and systematic synthesis. A standardized coding matrix was developed to extract core variables, including UCD dimensional characteristics, wardrobe functional and experiential performance, user adaptive effects and scenario-based boundary conditions. This review clarifies that UCD improves wardrobe comprehensive performance through three hierarchical pathways: physiological ergonomic adaptation, precise functional demand matching, and multi-scenario experience upgrading. The optimization effects of UCD exhibit prominent dual heterogeneity across user groups and residential usage scenarios. Design iteration, intelligent technology embedding and spatial…

title: The Effect of Income and Total Assets on Return on Assets with Total Asset Turnover as an Intervening Variable at PT Permodalan Nasional Madani Kabanjahe Branch
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of revenue and total assets on Return on Assets (ROA) through Total Asset Turnover (TATO) as an intervening variable at PT Permodalan Nasional Madani (PNM) Kabanjahe Branch. This study is motivated by the phenomenon of increasing revenue and total assets during the 2022–2025 period, which was not followed by an improvement in asset utilization efficiency and company profitability. Revenue increased from IDR 178.765 billion in 2022 to IDR 260.329 billion in 2025, while total assets increased from IDR 57.361 billion to IDR 412.354 billion. During the same period, TATO decreased from 3.12 times to 0.63 times, while ROA decreased from 133% to 29%. This condition indicates a gap between the growth of assets and revenue and the effectiveness of asset utilization and company profitability. This study employs a quantitative approach using causal or explanatory research. The data consist of secondary data obtained from the financial statements of PT PNM Kabanjahe Branch for the period from January 2022 to December 2025. The research sample consists of 48 monthly financial statement observations selected using a saturated sampling technique. Data analysis is conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics through descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, path analysis, hypothesis testing, and mediation analysis using the Sobel Test and Hayes Process Ma…

title: Regulatory Direction for Physical Protection Systems in the Standard Design Approval Stage of Light-Water Small Modular Reactors
abstract: As the deployment of small modular reactors (SMRs) and advanced reactors expands, physical protection system regulatory frameworks are shifting from prescriptive, compliance-driven approaches to risk-informed and performance-based methodologies. In Korea, the amendment to the Act on Physical Protection and Radiological Emergency, promulgated on March 31, 2026, establishes a legal basis for the institutionalization of Security by Design (SbD) by requiring physical protection regulations to be reviewed from the Standard Design Approval (SDA) stage onward. This study examines the applicable regulatory direction for the SDA stage of Light-Water SMRs based on an analysis of regulatory trends in major countries. It investigates alternative requirements reflecting SMR-specific characteristics and performance-based regulatory approaches and proposes a preliminary regulatory framework incorporating performance assessment feedback into design improvement. The findings serve as a technical foundation for developing review guidance at the SDA stage to advance SbD institutionalization in Korea.

title: Creative Tensions: Leveraging Cultural Diversity through Innovation to Drive Design Entrepreneurship
abstract: In today’s culturally diverse world, design entrepreneurs increasingly engage with people from various backgrounds but often struggle to leverage cultural differences for creative and business growth. While interest in inclusive innovation is rising, the role of cultural diversity in design entrepreneurship success remains unclear. This study explores how cultural diversity influences design entrepreneurship performance, emphasizing the mediating role of cross-cultural innovation. A narrative review of 22 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database, spanning entrepreneurship, design thinking, cultural studies, and innovation management was conducted. The findings informed a conceptual framework built on four key ideas: cultural diversity directly impacts both cross-cultural innovation and design entrepreneurship outcomes; cross-cultural innovation enhances entrepreneurial performance; and it also mediates the link between cultural diversity and business success. The analysis reveals that diverse perspectives create creative tension and generate richer, more culturally resonant solutions, particularly when innovation practices are inclusive. The study establishes new theoretical links among cultural intelligence, design thinking, and resource-based views. It also offers practical insights for entrepreneurs and educators on fostering culturally aware and innovative teams. Fur…

title: Design of an Adaptive English Vocabulary Learning System Based on Fuzzy Modeling of Second Language Vocabulary Features
abstract: Second language vocabulary acquisition is dynamic, individualized, and uncertain. Traditional vocabulary learning systems often use static difficulty grading or simple frequency statistics, which are difficult to accurately adapt to learners’ cognitive states and real-time needs. In response to this issue, this article designs and implements an adaptive English vocabulary learning system based on fuzzy modeling of second language vocabulary features, using the cognitive psychology knowledge acquisition theory (three stages of understanding consolidation application) as the teaching framework. The system focuses on personalized vocabulary resource recommendation as its core goal, aiming to improve learning efficiency and stimulate learning interest. The overall architecture includes five functional modules: pre-test diagnosis, vocabulary acquisition, consolidation and application, effectiveness testing, and learning feedback, forming a closed-loop iterative learning path. At the algorithmic level, the system introduces fuzzy logic as the main inference mechanism, breaking through the rigid discrimination of “right or wrong” in classical binary logic, and using multi value membership degrees to describe the continuous spectrum of learners’ abilities. In the fuzzification stage, four behavioral indicators are selected as input variables: daily online learning duration, daily vocab…

title: Hacia un consenso colombiano sobre el trastorno bipolar: protocolo y diseño de un Delphi modificado para la adaptación de la evidencia al contexto nacional
abstract: Introducción: El trastorno bipolar es una condición mental crónica y recurrente asociada con elevada carga de enfermedad, discapacidad funcional, mortalidad prematura y riesgo de suicidio. Aunque existen guías internacionales para su diagnóstico y tratamiento, su aplicabilidad puede verse limitada por diferencias entre sistemas de salud y contextos asistenciales. Objetivo: Describir el desarrollo metodológico del Consenso Colombiano sobre el Trastorno Bipolar, realizado mediante un Delphi modificado para contextualizar la evidencia científica al escenario nacional. Métodos: Se desarrolló un consenso de expertos basado en evidencia mediante un Delphi modificado. El proceso incluyó priorización de preguntas clínicas, estructuración PICO cuando fue aplicable, revisión estructurada y pragmática de la evidencia, formulación de enunciados y dos rondas Delphi virtuales. Los enunciados se valoraron en una escala de nueve puntos. Los criterios de consenso, establecidos a priori, fueron mediana ≥7, rango intercuartílico ≤2 y acuerdo ≥80%, sin objeciones cualitativas sustantivas. Los enunciados susceptibles de modificación fueron reformulados antes de la segunda ronda; aquellos que no alcanzaron los criterios tras esta fueron clasificados como sin consenso. Conclusiones: El proceso proporciona un marco estructurado y transparente para contextualizar la evidencia sobre el trastorno bipolar…

title: Identity-Telemetry Portfolio Design from MITRE ATT&CK Detection Analytics: Exact Frontiers and Single-Component Dependency Stress Tests
abstract: Security teams must prioritize telemetry collection, but technique-level coverage counts do not show whether the evidence declared by a detection analytic is available in a selected portfolio or how strongly that support depends on individual components. This study formulates identity-telemetry selection as an exact portfolio problem using MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Detection Strategies, Analytics, and Data Components. A prespecified name rule identified 18 active identity components. A strategy was conditionally supported (identity-side) when at least one associated Analytic had all its identity-component requirements in the portfolio, assuming that all nonidentity requirements are available. Exhaustive enumeration calculated nominal support and support under a single-component omission stress test across ATT&CK releases 18.0–19.2, together with a lower-bound measure that counts only Analytics declaring no nonidentity requirements. Each release contained 150 eligible strategies. In release 19.2, six components supported 129 strategies (86.0%), seven 135 (90.0%), ten 144 (96.0%), and fifteen all 150. Complete collection retained only 111 strategies (74.0%) after omission of the most damaging component; Logon Session Creation, User Account Authentication, and Logon Session Metadata accounted for losses of 39, 30, and 17 strategies. Only 123 of 326 eligible Analytics were identity-o…

title: Digital Technologies and Virtual Environments in Language Learning
abstract: Digital technologies can expand opportunities for language practice, feedback, and access to learning materials, but their educational value depends on how they are integrated into instruction. This conceptual article draws on a selective narrative review to examine automatic speech recognition, conversational agents, machine translation, and virtual environments in language learning. It distinguishes the functions of these technologies from the learning outcomes that teachers must evaluate. The discussion identifies opportunities for pronunciation practice, sustained interaction, reflective revision, and contextualized communication, alongside problems involving unreliable feedback, cognitive demands, unequal access, and personal data. Alpha School is considered briefly as an institutional illustration of adaptive learning and human guidance, rather than as evidence of foreign-language learning effectiveness. Four proposed classroom applications show how teachers can connect digital activity to observable language performance. The article argues that responsible integration requires clear learning objectives, appropriate scaffolding, human review of feedback, and opportunities to demonstrate learning beyond the original tool. Its contribution is a practical framework for evaluating instructional use; the proposed applications require subsequent classroom investigation.

title: Plant Dehydrin-Derived, Lysine-Rich Peptides Show Both Antifungal Activity and Blood–Brain Barrier Penetration
abstract: Abstract The plant-based, dehydrin-derived peptides represent an underexplored source of antifungal agents. In this study, we investigated the antifungal activity, cellular association, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability of a lysine-rich peptide (ERD-A) derived from the Arabidopsis thaliana dehydrin ERD14, as well as its rationally designed sequence variants. The amino acid substitutions were engineered to modulate charge, aromatic residue content, and conformational flexibility. Antifungal activity was assessed against clinically relevant yeasts, including Candida albicans, Candidozyma auris, and Cryptococcus neoformans. The parental ERD-A peptide exhibited moderate activity against C. albicans and C. neoformans, while most variants showed species-dependent changes in potency. Increased cationicity or introduction of tryptophan residues enhanced activity against C. neoformans, with several variants displaying 4-fold lower MIC values than the parental peptide. In contrast, C. auris showed limited susceptibility to all tested variants. Fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry demonstrated strong, time-dependent cell association of carboxyfluorescein-labeled ERD-A in C. albicans, reaching ∼98 to 99% positive cells after 16 h. title: Medicinal Plant Used in Management of Mouth Ulcer: A Review
abstract: Mouth ulcer is a common oral condition that may be associated with local trauma, aphthous stomatitis and other factors. Herbal medicines have been traditionally used for the management of oral disorders because many medicinal plants contain bioactive constituents with reported antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and wound-healing properties. This review summarizes medicinal plants reported for the management of mouth ulcer and discusses their traditional or experimental use in herbal formulations. Plants such as Aloe barbadensis, Psidium guajava, Glycyrrhiza glabra ,Curcuma longa, Punica granatum, Piper betle, Cordia dichotoma, Capsicum annuum and Morinda citrifolia have been reported in the literature. Herbal gels and other preparations containing these plants have also been investigated. The available literature provides a basis for further research and formulation development; however,evidence varies among individual plants and many reports are experimental rather than clinical. The two most causes are aphthous stomatitis, alsoknown as canker soreness, and local injury or trauma, such as rubbing agains t a tooth or dental filling's sharp edge. Aphthous stomatitis causes mouth ulcers to occur repeatedly, and its exact cause is often not known.

title: Deep generative virtual staining for breast cancer: from H&E histology to HER2 immunohistochemistry
abstract: Abstract Immunohistochemistry (IHC) remains the clinical gold standard for molecular profiling in breast cancer; however, traditional workflows are hindered by high costs, reagent dependency, and tissue exhaustion. Virtual staining has emerged as a computational alternative; however, prevailing virtual staining models often fail to preserve high-frequency structural details critical for perceptual and histological fidelity. We present a novel chemically-informed, two-stage conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) framework designed for high-fidelity H&E-to-IHC translation. Our approach uniquely decouples chemical stain extraction from high-resolution textural refinement through a specialized StainMapper (G₁) and a score-conditioned RefineGenerator (G₂). By integrating multi-scale hierarchical score conditioning with a hybrid loss function including adversarial, perceptual, Sobel edge, and stain-consistency terms, the framework enforces both global distributional realism and local morphological precision. Evaluated on the BCI and HER2match benchmarks, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 59.67 , PSNR of 22.50 dB , SSIM of 0.4773 , LPIPS of 0.5279 and KID of 0.0264 ± 0.0086 on BCI; PSNR of 20.66 dB , LPIPS of 0.4486 , FID of 20.42 , and KID of 0.0124 ± 0.0092 on HER2match, outperforming all baselines on distribut…

title: Voltage profile enhancement with efficient utilization of FACTs devices and reactive power reserve from solar power plants
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an innovative method for optimizing power grids with high renewable energy penetration by employing particle swarm optimization (PSO) to strategically allocate static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs). The approach, implemented through DIgSILENT’s programming language (DPL), aims to minimize voltage deviations and power losses while maximizing the reactive power reserve (RPR) from solar power plants to enhance grid stability and efficiency. The effectiveness of the method is tested under various system contingencies, including short-circuit faults and generation loss events. Results demonstrate that optimally placed STATCOMs significantly improve voltage profiles in the neighboring areas during disturbances. The study also evaluates different control modes for photovoltaic (PV) solar systems, with findings highlighting the importance of voltage control mode in preventing system collapse. Additionally, integrating RPR from solar power plants, particularly in combination with STATCOMs, is highly effective in maintaining a healthy voltage profile.

abstract: Abstract The CH₄ content of the LFG declines progressively while CO₂ increases, degrading combustion stability until engines can no longer sustain reliable operation below a CH₄ threshold of approximately 40 volume percent (vol.%). This paper investigates the combustion physics behind this degradation and evaluates hydrogen enrichment as a mitigation strategy that projects to extend plant operational life by more than a decade beyond the conventional shut-off point, under the assumptions and the empirically calibrated stability mapping. A custom numerical solver was developed in MATLAB and was validated against the canonical coflow diffusion flame benchmark experiments. Parametric simulations systematically varied the CO₂ fraction from 0 to 60 vol.% and the hydrogen (H₂) enrichment level from 0 to 40 vol.%, yielding quantitative maps of adiabatic flame temperature, equivalent flame speed, ignition delay, and radical pool concentrations. Increasing CO₂ from 0 to 60 vol.% reduces Da (Damköhler number) by 83%, doubles ignition delay to 3.16 ms, and depresses the OH radical pool by 49%; 30 vol.% H₂ enrichment fully restores stable operation (Da ≥ 5 in the laminar flame model), projecting, under the stated assumptions and pending engine-level validation, a 14-year plant-life extension and doubling CO₂-equivalent avoidance to 60,700 tonnes. title: Effects of DBC Copper Layer Thickness on the Electrical, Thermal, and Thermo-Mechanical Performance of Parallel SiC Chip Power Modules
abstract: Direct Bonded Copper (DBC) substrates simultaneously provide current conduction, heat spreading, and structural support in multi-chip power modules, making Cu thickness a key trade-off variable. This study investigates the effects of DBC Cu thickness on the electrical, thermal, and thermo-mechanical responses of a 300 A parallel SiC chip power module. Thermal-coupling analysis was performed to distinguish the temperature effects of chip spacing from those of top Cu thickness. Electro-thermal simulation showed that conduction loss and maximum chip temperature increased as the top Cu thickness decreased, with a pronounced change between 0.175 and 0.160 mm under the 300 A condition. Thermo-mechanical analysis showed that reducing the symmetric top/bottom Cu thickness from 0.30/0.30 to 0.15/0.15 mm decreases reflow warpage of the baseplate from 183.930 to 30.091 μm. Thermal-cycling analysis showed that the cycle increment in volume-averaged inelastic strain energy density in the evaluated solder region decreased by 17.2%. The results showed distinct thickness-dependent responses: reducing the top Cu thickness increased conduction loss and maximum chip temperature, whereas symmetrically reducing both the top and bottom Cu thicknesses decreased reflow warpage and solder inelastic strain energy density in simulation.

Secure Sharing Governance of User-Generated Content in Blockchain-enabled Virtual Communities
abstract: User Generated Content (UGC) is an important repository of knowledge in virtual communities but there are risks to it being widely available and replica. These risks include loss of privacy, unauthorized reuse, experience of misinformation, the infringements of rights, and maliciously distributed knowledge. Current governance on platforms concentrates on the ability to access the knowledge freely but also on reviewing and removing that data once the user generates it and subsequently posts it. Current governance structures cannot sufficiently balance the goals of knowledge sharing, user autonomy, accountability of the platform for the actions of the user, and the security of the user’s generated content. This paper presents a framework for governing UGC using a decentralized governance approach utilizing a blockchain. The technical approach to governance of blockchain was used in developing programmable trust infrastructure. This includes the use of decentralized identity, traceability of UGC content, a chain of evidence prohibiting modification of evidence, the use of smart contracts for providing consent, the ability to provide privacy for access, and providing both the incentive to share and accountability for why that incentive is used. title: ASSESSMENT OF SUSTAINABLE DESIGN STRATEGIES IN ENERGY-EFFICIENT HIGH-RISE MIXED-USE TOWERS IN TROPICAL CLIMATES
abstract: High-rise mixed-use towers in tropical climates, including Abuja's tropical savanna environment, face environmental conditions that can increase cooling demand, particularly high solar exposure, substantial diurnal temperature variation and the need for reliable environmental control. This study examines the extent to which sustainable design strategies are incorporated in selected mixed-use and high-rise precedents, with particular relevance to Abuja's Central Business District. A purposive case-study approach was employed to examine five precedents: World Trade Center Abuja, Pixel Building in Melbourne, The Edge in Amsterdam, PARKROYAL on Pickering in Singapore, and Oasia Hotel Downtown in Singapore. The cases were analysed thematically using architectural documentation, published project information, certification records and available performance literature. Recurring strategies included external solar shading, perforated and layered façades, controlled glazing, natural or mixed-mode ventilation, vertical functional zoning, atrium and void spaces, thermal buffering and integrated greenery. The analysis indicates that environmental performance in the selected precedents is generally approached through combinations of complementary architectural and building-system strategies rather than through a single intervention. The study contributes a precedent-based framework for tran…

title: Energy Efficiency and Thermal Performance Analysis of a Centrifugal Pump: Effect of Insulation Retrofit on Heat Loss Reduction
abstract: Centrifugal pumps are widely used in industry, agriculture, and the home. Their energy efficiency is determined by hydraulic losses, friction, and electrical losses in the drive system. This study experimentally examines the effect of external thermal insulation on the case heat transfer and the overall efficiency of a 0.5HP (0.373 kW) centrifugal pump. The suggested approach studies the case of an uninsulated pump at different insulation thicknesses – 5, 10, 15, 20 mm. The electric power, flow rate, head, surrounding temperature, fluid temperature, and case surface temperature are estimated to evaluate the hydraulic and thermal efficiency of the pump. The approximated heat loss from the case is observed to reduce from 31.5 W (uninsulated) to 16.8 W (with 20 mm insulation), suggesting a 46.7% reduction. The wire-to-water efficiency increases slightly from 12.25% to 12.28%. The findings suggest that insulating the external case might be successful in minimizing heat losses from the pump case. However, its effect on the overall efficiency of the pump seems to be small. The findings have to be considered within the framework of the measurement approach, experimental variability, and the necessity to ensure adequate cooling for the motor and other essential components.

title: Promoting Energy-Saving Behaviour in Households: The Integrated Technology Engagement Canvas (iTECH)
abstract: Home technology adoption in Sustainable Smart Cities (SSCs) is essential for reducing carbon emissions, yet household engagement remains limited and existing energy-saving strategies are often weakly grounded in behavioural theory. This study aims to systematically review household energy-saving intervention strategies and to develop a theory-informed framework to address this gap. A systematic review was conducted using Scopus, including peer-reviewed journal articles published from 2012 to 2024 that propose or evaluate household-level strategies for promoting energy-saving behaviour (ESB). Following screening and eligibility assessment, 24 studies were included in the review. The extracted strategies were analysed and synthesised using constructs from cognitive and technology adoption theories to develop the integrated Technology Engagement Canvas for Households (iTECH). The review shows that 38% of studies focus on knowledge enhancement strategies, primarily targeting perceived usefulness and social norms, while strategies addressing beliefs, personal norms, and awareness of consequences are rarely considered. By systematically linking existing intervention strategies with behavioural theory, this study moves beyond prior strategy-based approaches and proposes iTECH as a holistic, theory informed framework for evaluating and strengthening household energy-saving intervention…

title: Grid integration of renewable energy: A systematic review bridging techno-economic optimization and smart grid architectures
abstract: The escalating penetration of renewable energy (RE) sources necessitates addressing interconnected technical barriers across stability, power quality, and intelligent governance. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ScienceDirect databases (2018–2024) to synthesize critical challenges in large-scale RE integration. Diverging from existing reviews that isolate technical domains, this work adopts a holistic framework connecting frequency stability, power quality (PQ) disturbances, techno-economic optimization, and smart grid architectures. Key findings reveal that inverter-based resources (IBR) induce critical inertia deficits and harmonic distortions, requiring hybrid mitigation strategies combining Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Synchronous Condensers (SC). Moreover, prevalent simulation tools exhibit significant seasonal deviations (RMSE >30%), underscoring the absence of localized calibration protocols. The analysis identifies substantial research gaps in standardized PQ metrics for DC microgrids, real-time adaptive protection systems, and cybersecurity frameworks for prosumer ecosystems. This review contributes a comprehensive taxonomy of integration barriers and delineates future trajectories toward resilient, data-driven power systems.

abstract: Abstract Background Peer relationships are an important indicator of adolescents’ school-based mental health and social adjustment, but experimental evidence on whether cognitively engaging physical activity (CEPA) improves them remains limited. This trial tested the effect of a CEPA curriculum on peer relationships relative to a traditional physical education curriculum (TPEC), with exploratory pathways through executive function and cognitive reappraisal. Methods In this parallel two-arm cluster randomized controlled trial, 12 intact classes comprising 650 students in grades 10 and 11 from three urban public high schools in eastern China were randomly assigned within school-by-grade strata to 12 weeks of CEPA or TPEC (three 45-min sessions per week; six classes per arm). The primary outcome was the posttest total peer relationship score; secondary outcomes were executive function and cognitive reappraisal. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle, using linear mixed models with class random intercepts and multiple imputation; serial mediation was examined in exploratory analyses with Monte Carlo confidence intervals. Results 650 students entered baseline assessment (CEPA, 327; TPEC, 323) and 612 (94.2%) completed the posttest. This paper assesses the operational impact of rooftop PV and battery energy storage systems (BESS) on a real 22 kV urban feeder (outgoing feeder 480 of the 110 kV ADO substation) in Da Nang City, Vietnam. A network model with 17 medium-voltage nodes and 49 monitored 0.4 kV busbars was built in DIgSILENT PowerFactory from utility network data and measured PV and load profiles. These beverages combine caffeine with taurine, sugars, B-group vitamins, and other stimulant compounds that, at the doses commonly consumed, can produce electrophysiological changes capable of predisposing susceptible young individuals to cardiac rhythm disturbances (Ciliberti et al., 2024). title: Biophysical factors associated with radiation use efficiency and productivity of Mimosa scabrella plantations for energy
abstract: Abstract Forest plantations managed for biomass production play an important role in the transition toward renewable energy systems. However, the biophysical factors underlying biomass production and radiation use efficiency (RUE) in native tree species remain poorly understood. This study evaluated radiation use efficiency, biomass accumulation, radiation interception, and potential energy yield of Mimosa scabrella Benth. plantations established under different planting spacings in southern Brazil. A nine-year field experiment was conducted in a randomized complete block design with three replications and four planting spacings (2.0 × 1.0, 2.0 × 1.5, 3.0 × 1.0, and 3.0 × 1.5 m). Measurements were performed at 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 years to evaluate leaf area index (LAI), photosynthetically active radiation interception, biomass accumulation and partitioning, and RUE. The relationships among these variables were further investigated using principal component analysis based on treatment means for each spacing × age combination. Planting spacing affected stand development, radiation interception, biomass production, and energy yield. The densest spacing (2.0 × 1.0 m) exhibited the highest RUE (0.0021 kg MJ −1 ), aboveground biomass production (264 Mg ha −1 ), and potential energy yield (1,276.9 MWh ha −1 ), indicating greater biomass production per unit of intercepted radiation. title: Palm-Oil-Derived Phase-Change Materials for Thermal Energy Storage: Molecular Design, Encapsulation, Heat-Transfer Enhancement, and Engineering Applications A Critical Review
abstract: Phase-change materials (PCMs) can decouple thermal-energy supply from demand by absorbing and releasing latent heat across a narrow temperature interval. Bio-based PCMs have consequently attracted attention as renewable alternatives to petroleum-derived paraffins, yet most reviews treat plant oils as a single broad category and rarely examine the palm-oil platform as an engineerable family of thermalstorage molecules. This critical qualitative literature review evaluates palm oil, palm fractions, palm-derived fatty acids, esters, and related lipids as tunable PCMs rather than as a single biological material. It synthesizes recent evidence on molecular structure–transition relationships, eutectic design, hydrogenation and fractionation; low thermal conductivity and heat-transfer enhancement; encapsulation, form stabilization and leakage control; thermal cycling, corrosion and chemical stability; and emerging applications in buildings, cold chains, photovoltaic systems, battery thermal management, solar-thermal storage and low-grade industrial heat recovery. The analysis shows that palm-derived PCMs are technically credible where phase-transition temperature, latent-heat density and source sustainability are matched deliberately to the application. However, conductivity enhancement creates a recurring latent-heat dilution penalty, while encapsulation improves handling but introdu…

title: ADVANCED NON-DESTRUCTIVE INSPECTION AND INTEGRITY ASSURANCE OF OFFSHORE AND MARINE PIPELINES FOR CRITICAL ENERGY AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE IN SAUDI ARABIA
abstract: Offshore pipelines connect hydrocarbon production, coastal industrial operations and seawater-dependent water systems, yet their integrity cannot be inferred from occasional inspection results alone. Saudi Arabia presents a demanding case because high-consequence energy assets coexist with seawater intakes, desalination facilities and transmission networks serving arid regions. This critical review evaluates non-destructive inspection technologies reported between 2020 and 2025 and develops an assurance framework that links defect detection,sizing uncertainty,deterioration mechanisms and maintenance decisions. Evidence from ultrasonic testing, guided waves, magnetic flux leakage, acoustic monitoring, distributed fibre sensing, robotic inspection and digital modelling is compared against practical access and validation constraints. The review distinguishes metal loss from cracks, active leakage from latent deterioration, and continuous surveillance from periodic verification. It argues that reliable assurance requires an evidence chain extending from sensor qualification to fitness-for-service assessment, rather than substituting algorithmic predictions for measurements. Two synthesis tables map inspection capabilities to threats and identify the most consequential implementation gaps. A staged Saudi deployment pathway is proposed, prioritizing repeatable baselines, representati…

abstract: Abstract The limited distribution of suitable salt caverns has stimulated interest in depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs as alternative geological media for large-scale underground compressed air energy storage (CAES). Depleted shale gas reservoirs may offer connected fracture networks for rapid air injection and withdrawal and adjacent matrix pores for additional storage, while their relatively limited mobile water may reduce the gas–water displacement losses encountered in conventional water-driven reservoirs. However, black shale contains organic matter and reduced minerals that can react with injected O2 and deplete oxygen from stored air. This process is particularly important for fuel-assisted CAES because the recovered air serves as both the expansion working fluid and the oxidant for fuel combustion. Oxygen–shale interactions in Longmaxi Formation shale were investigated using scanning electron microscopy, repeated electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) mapping, and high-pressure batch experiments under different temperatures, moisture conditions, and successive air-exposure cycles. Organic matter and Fe(II)-bearing minerals, including framboidal pyrite and ferroan dolomite, were identified as widely dispersed, potentially oxygen-reactive constituents. title: BEYOND MICROCREDIT: SELF-HELP GROUPS, SOCIAL PARTICIPATION AND PUBLIC VOICE AMONG WOMEN IN RURAL INDIA
abstract: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are widely recognised as mechanisms for financial inclusion and livelihood support; however, their contribution to women’s social participation and public voice remains equally important. This study examines the association between SHG membership and changes in community interaction, participation in local governance and public-speaking confidence among women in Ananthapuramu district, Andhra Pradesh. A multi-stage random sampling design was used to select 320 SHG members, comprising 160 Muslim minority and 160 non-minority women across five revenue divisions. Primary data were collected through a structured interview schedule, and changes associated with SHG membership were analysed using frequencies, percentages and chi-square tests. The findings indicate substantial improvement in women’s social engagement following SHG membership. Frequent community interaction increased markedly, while non-participation in Gram Sabha and Panchayat meetings declined in both groups and active participation increased. Public expression also strengthened, with 79.06% of respondents reporting moderate or significant improvement in public-speaking confidence. Overall, the findings suggest that SHGs extend beyond their conventional microcredit function by providing collective spaces that facilitate social interaction, civic participation and confidence in public expression…

title: Perceived Barriers and Opportunities for Rural Women’s Participation in Agricultural Extension Activities in Afgoi District, Somalia
abstract: Agricultural extension services can improve farming knowledge and rural livelihoods, but access may be constrained by financial, institutional, and information barriers. This descriptive quantitative study summarizes the perceptions of 80 agricultural stakeholders in Afgoi District, Somalia. Responses were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and five-point Likert mean scores. Limited access to agricultural information (M = 4.05), training (M = 4.03), and modern farming techniques (M = 3.94) were rated as challenges. Lack of financial support (M = 4.19) and limited access to inputs (M = 4.18) were perceived as major economic constraints. Program availability (M = 3.44) and government support (M = 3.38) received comparatively lower ratings. Proposed improvements included agricultural credit (M = 4.35), technologies and inputs (M = 4.33), extension services (M = 4.30), and training (M = 4.28). The results reflect the views of a mixed-gender stakeholder sample rather than measurements of women’s actual participation or effects of interventions. Documented reliability testing of the questionnaire was not available, and the findings are descriptive and limited to Afgoi District.

FOAM STABILITY AS A QUALITY PARAMETER FOR HERBAL SURFACE CLEANERS: CORRELATION WITH CONCENTRATION AND STORAGE CONDITIONS
abstract: Foam stability-an essential quality indicator of liquid cleaning products not just in terms of a consumer feel for performance, but as an indicator of cleaning efficacy. This study focused on investigating the foam stability of neem- Azadirachta indica and lemon- Citrus limon based herbal surface cleaners at concentrations of 3%, 4%, 5%, 6% and 7% and storage temperatures 25C, 30C and 45C for 4 weeks duration with effect on foam stability monitored and evaluated weekly by test tube dilution method. All of the formulations that tested positively (stable foam above liquid level) yielded positive initial foam test-signifying the presence of triterpenic glycosides (saponins). As the duration of storage extended the rate of foam stability reduced for all of the formulations and more than anything the effect of temperature showed a significantly high influence on degradation (p<0.001) The most sensitive test was the one at 45C where foam test became negative (full collapse of foam) with 3% at week 4, whereas the most concentrated product of 7% was most resistant to complete foam collapse.

abstract: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the impact of community participation on solid waste management in Rwanda, a case of AGRUNI Company in Rwamagana District (2021-2025)”. Research design to be used was descriptive and explanatory research design. The study used the population of 12,008 people and the sample size of 388 clients of AGRUNI Company. Questionnaire, interview were used to collect primary data and documentary review was used to collect secondary data. Descriptive statistics and inferential statistics were used to analyse data with a help of SPSS version 26. The study found that community participation significantly influences solid waste management practices in Rwamagana District, with decision-making and monitoring being the strongest predictor (B = 0.659, p = 0.000), followed by clean-up activities (B = 0.100, p = 0.000) and communication (B = 0.081, p = 0.000), while awareness and environmental education was not significant (B = 0.020, p = 0.203). Secondary data show high waste generation of 36 MT per month, only one dumping site, 324 waste bins, and low collection coverage of 40%. Transportation challenges and poor rural recycling systems further reduce efficiency, despite 80% biodegradable waste and 20% recycled materials. Regression results clearly indicate a significant positive relationship between community participation and waste management performance.…

title: Performance Evaluation Procedures for Fire Extinguishing Agents and Devices in Small-Scale Lithium-Ion Battery Fires
abstract: Small-scale lithium-ion battery fires involve thermal runaway, propagation to adjacent cells, and possible re-ignition; therefore, flame suppression alone does not adequately reflect the extinguishing performance. This study reviewed the major test elements of KFI 630 and NTA 8133 and proposed an improved procedure based on fire and extinguishing tests using small-scale pouch-type lithium-ion batteries. In the free-burn tests, thermal runaway propagated through the five-cell test specimen within approximately 60-120 s, whereas the suppression tests showed different cell temperature histories and subsequent thermal runaway propagation behaviors depending on the extinguishing agent. The proposed revision maintains the KFI test configuration, heating method, and one-hour reignition observation period, while additionally recording the cell-by-cell thermal runaway timing, flame extinguishment time, and actual agent consumption. Additionally, a supplementary procedure is also proposed to evaluate the thermal stabilization and thermal runaway propagation delay using cell-temperature histories, cooling performance, propagation time, and the total number of cells undergoing thermal runaway. Further replication is required to establish the reproducibility and quantitative acceptance criteria for these proposed indicators.

title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
abstract: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.

title: DATA AS A FINANCIAL ASSET: HOW FINTECH COMPANIES USE CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR DATA FOR PERSONALISATION, RETENTION, AND REVENUE GROWTH
abstract: This study examines how FinTech companies transform consumer behaviour data into financial value through artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and hyper - personalisation. It explores how transactional, behavioural, and demographic data are collected, analysed,and converted into personalised financial products, recommendations, interfaces, and communication strategies. The study further evaluates how these practices influence customer retention, customer lifetime value, return on investment, average revenue per user, customer acquisition cost, and churn. Particular attention is given to machine learning, customer segmentation, recommendation systems, and predictive models used to anticipate consumer needs and improve engagement. The paper also considers the strategic role of data in product development, cross-selling, and marketing optimization. Alongside these benefits, it critically examines privacy, consent, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance. The study concludes that AI-driven personalisation can create substantial commercial value in FinTech, but sustainable growth depends on transparent, secure, fair, and responsible use of consumer data over the long term.

title: Simulation of a PV-Integrated Dual Active Bridge Converter for EV Charging
abstract: The increasing use of renewable energy and electric vehicles (EVs) has created a growing need for efficient powerelectronic interfaces that can integrate solar energy with high-voltage battery-charging systems. This work presents the design and MATLAB/Simulink analysis of an approximately 11.56 kW photovoltaic (PV)-fed Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter for isolated and controllable power transfer in EV battery-charging applications. The PV array consists of 33 modules rated at approximately 350 W each, configured as 11 series-connected modules per string and three parallel strings, providing approximately 423.5 V and 27.3 A at the maximum power point. The DAB converter employs two active full bridges coupled through an 11 kVA, 50 kHz high-frequency transformer with 419/409 V windings and a 29 µH series transfer inductor. A 220 µF DC-link capacitor is connected at the output. Power transfer is controlled using single-phase-shift (SPS) modulation, where both bridges operate at approximately 50% duty cycle and the relative phase angle between their switching signals determines the transferred power. For closed-loop control, the measured DC output voltage is compared with a predefined reference, and the resulting error is processed by a PI controller to generate the required phase-shift command. title: Tuning Moving Vehicle Suspensions for Vibration Mitigation of Damped Bridges
abstract: It has been widely recognized that traversing vehicles can dampen bridge vibrations. This work clarifies the efficacy of different vehicle suspension tuning approaches for bridge vibration mitigation using an equivalent tuned mass damper (TMD) model and presents a parametric analysis of the key physical factors governing vehicle-bridge interaction. The vehicle-bridge system is modelled as a TMD traveling on an elastically supported beam. A finite element model is developed to numerically validate the analytical model. Transmissibility functions, obtained using the time-freezing technique, and complex eigenvalue loci are employed in the tuning process. For an undamped bridge, the optimal stiffness and damping ratio of the vehicle suspension are obtained from an extended fixed-point principle, under which the analytical model is equivalent to a smooth bridge coupled to a TMD and subjected to a harmonic transverse excitation at the contact point. For a damped bridge, the optimal vehicle suspension parameters are determined from the intersection of the eigenvalue loci of the system. Vehicle damping can induce curve veering of the instantaneous coupled eigenvalues during the vehicle passage, and this phenomenon is further examined through a perturbation analysis. title: OPTIMIZATION OF MIXED VEHICLE-DRONE ROUTING WITH TIME WINDOWS FOR LAST-MILE DELIVERY
abstract: The growth of e-commerce and the demand for ever shorter delivery lead times put considerable pressure on last-mile logistics operators. This article proposes a unified mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for mixed vehicle-drone routing with time windows (VRPTW-D). A conventional vehicle may, at each of its stops, launch a drone that serves a customer on its own and is then recovered by the vehicle, either at the same stop or at a later stop. The compact formulation relies on ternary flight variables, continuous time variables and an exact linearization of the vehicle-drone synchronization; it embeds valid inequalities (Dantzig - Fulkerson - Johnson subtour elimination and use - flow linking) that strengthen the continuous relaxation. For larger instances, we develop an ALNS (Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search) heuristic calibrated against the exact solutions. The exact model proves optimality on small instances (n - 10) and, beyond, provides feasible solutions together with bounds; the ALNS is the practical solution method for large instances. A reproducible instance set, generated in the style of Solomon (classes C1, R1 and RC1) with an extension of the time windows to drones, allows us to measure precisely the contribution of the drones, the value of the relaxation and the comparative performance of the exact model and the ALNS, complemented by a sensitivity analys…

title: Edge AI-Based Vehicle Surveillance System
abstract: Urban vehicle numbers have grown far faster than the capacity of traffic police to watch every intersection and parking lane, and the result is a steady stream of hit-and-run incidents, wrong-parking, and double-parking cases that pass unrecorded under conventional patrol- and CCTV-based enforcement. This paper describes an Edge AI vehicle-surveillance pipeline built to close that gap while running entirely on low-cost, offline-capable hardware — a laptop or a Raspberry Pi — with no cloud backend and no purpose-built sensors. Vehicles are localised and classified frame by frame with YOLOv8, and a DeepSORT tracker then follows each detected vehicle through the sequence so that its position can be monitored continuously. A collision is inferred when two tracked bounding boxes overlap sharply, measured through Intersection over Union, together with an abrupt motion change captured by Lucas–Kanade optical flow; if the vehicle involved does not remain at the scene within a five-second grace period, the event is recorded as a hit-and-run. Separately, restricted-zone polygons combined with a configurable stay-duration check are used to catch vehicles parked illegally or blocking a live lane. title: A TWO-PHASE DECOMPOSITION HEURISTIC VERSUS A HYBRID GENETIC ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING A MULTI-PRODUCT, MULTI-COMPARTMENT VEHICLE ROUTING PROBLEM WITH SIMULTANEOUS PICKUP AND DELIVERY AND TIME WINDOWS FOR THE TRANSPORT OF PERISHABLE PRODUCTS
abstract: We compare two approximate methods for solving the MPMC-VRPSPDTW, a vehicle routing problem for the transport of perishable products. The problem combines the following features: multiple products, multiple compartments, simultaneous pickup and delivery, time windows and a product degradation that depends on the road category. A single objective function minimizes the transport cost and the opportunity cost due to the loss of economic value of the products. The first solution method is a two-phase decomposition heuristic (TPDH) that works as follows: nearest-neighbour clustering of customers, then inter-route local search. The second is a hybrid genetic algorithm (GA) whose initial population is built from a feasible solution provided by an insertion heuristic inspired by Solomons I1. On 45 configurations derived from Solomons instances C101, R104 and RC107, the hybrid GA obtains a lower cost in 34 configurations and reduces the mean cost by 5.1% and the mean number of vehicles by 25.8%. Its mean run time is 1.5 times that of the TPDH (497 s vs 339 s).

abstract: Formula 1 publishes one of the richest open telemetry streams in professional sport, yet most public tools built on it are descriptive: they show what happened and stop there. This paper presents OpenTyreF1, a full-stack system that turns that data into decision support on a mobile phone. The system integrates three public sources (Jolpica-F1/Ergast, OpenF1 and FastF1) into one normalised 15-table relational corpus of 237,308 records covering 492 races from 2002 to 2026. On top of this corpusit builds a shared clean-lap filter, a gradient-boosted (XGBoost) lap-time model, a counterfactual stint-strategy simulator, a 1,500-run Monte Carlo outcome estimator, seven pit-wall decision modules and a grounded question-answering assistant, all served by a FastAPI backend to an Expo/React Native app. Evaluated on 12 completely unseen races, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.893 s, RMSE of 1.205 s and R 2 of 0.978, beating the strongest naive baseline by 0.270 s. An ablation shows that predicting a lap’s offset from its race median, rather than the absolute lap time, cuts error four-fold, a far larger effect than adding features. The results show that, for motorsport data of this size, careful lap admission, target design and leakage-free evaluation matter more than the choice of learner.

title: Effectiveness of Cognitive Conflict Strategy in Improving Conceptual Understanding of Evolution among Senior Secondary School Students in Zamfara State, Nigeria
abstract: Misconceptions about evolution can impede students’ understanding of natural selection, adaptation, genetic variation and evolutionary relationships. This study compared students’ conceptual understanding of evolution after instruction using the Cognitive Conflict Strategy (CCS) and conventional method. It also examined gender differences among students exposed to CCS. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design involved 283 SS II Biology students from public secondary schools in Zamfara State, Nigeria. Data were collected using an adapted 30-item, two-tier Evolutionary Misconception Test (KR-20 = 0.84) and analysed using descriptive statistics and ANCOVA at the 0.05 significance level. The study revealed that students taught using CCS recorded a higher mean gain (12.86) than those taught using the conventional method (6.71). ANCOVA showed a statistically significant difference between the two groups, F(1, 280) = 71.47, p < .001, partial η² = .203. However, no statistically significant gender difference was found among students taught using CCS, F(1, 143) = 0.48, p = .490, partial η² = .003. The study concluded that CCS improve students’ conceptual understanding of evolution. It is recommended that Biology teachers incorporate CCS into evolution lessons to help students identify, examine and correct misconceptions.

title: Artificial Intelligence’s Transformative Impact on Management, Strategy, and Workplace Dynamics: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizations is reshaping management practice, competitive strategy, and the experience of work, yet scholarship remains fragmented across disciplines and is predominantly Western-centric. This systematic literature review synthesizes interdisciplinary evidence on how AI transforms leadership and management functions, drives business model innovation, and alters workplace dynamics, with particular attention to Southeast Asian and Philippine contexts. Peer-reviewed, English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 addressing the organizational, strategic, or workforce implications of AI were included; purely technical studies and non-peer-reviewed materials were excluded from the corpus, with institutional reports used only for contextualization. Scopus, Web of Science, ABI/INFORM, Business Source Complete, and the ACM Digital Library were searched. Screening followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines: 1,245 records were identified, and 128 studies met all inclusion criteria and were synthesized thematically. First, AI integration facilitates an augmented leadership model in which effective managers combine human judgment with algorithmic capability. Second, AI operates as a strategic capability that enables adaptive, data-centric business models. Third, workplace dynamics exhibit a bifurcation effect whereby AI aug…

title: Green Tourism Governance: Strategy for Implementing Ecosystem-Based Sustainable Tourism Policies in Tojo Una-Una Regency
abstract: Implementation of Green Tourism Governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency: Policy, Governance, and Ecosystem Sustainability Analysis The purpose of this study is to analyze the implementation of green tourism governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency, identify the factors that influence the application of green governance in sustainable tourism, and formulate optimal development strategies based on SWOT analysis and the internal and external conditions of the region. This study uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive-analytical design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 24 informants from various stakeholders (government, local communities, business actors, academics/NGOs), participatory observation, and Focus Group Discussions (FGD). Data analysis was conducted using the Miles and Huberman interactive model, complemented by SWOT analysis, the Internal Factor Analysis Summary (IFAS), and the External Factor Analysis Summary (EFAS). This research was carried out in Tojo Una-Una Regency, specifically in the Togean Islands, during January-June 2024.The findings show that the implementation of green tourism governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency has made significant progress with Regional Regulation No. 7/2013 regarding RIPPARDA, which regulates sustainable tourism. title: Digital Transformation Strategy in Improving Public Service Efficiency: A Study on the Implementation of Smart Governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to analyze digital transformation strategies in improving public service efficiency through the implementation of smart governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency, as well as to determine the strategic position and recommend strategies that can be implemented to address the geographical challenges of an archipelagic region in government digitalization. The research uses a descriptive analytical qualitative approach with purposive sampling of 25 informants, including local government officials, civil servants, academics, community members, and the private sector. Data was collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, document studies, and focus group discussions during the 2024-2025 period. Data analysis was conducted using the Miles-Huberman-Saldana model with eight research dimensions, reinforced by quantitative SWOT analysis through IFAS and EFAS to determine the organization's strategic position. Research results show that digital transformation in Tojo Una-Una has made significant progress with the SPBE score increasing from 2.13 to 3.06, the construction of 84 BTS towers, and the implementation of various digital innovations such as AKSI-BPKAD. However, there are still challenges with uneven infrastructure, human resource competency gaps, and organizational culture resistance. title: Impact of NCS-Based Retail Training in Beauty Retail Companies on Sales Employees’ Job Satisfaction and Sales Performance
abstract: With the rapid growth of K-beauty, the number of sales employees in domestic and international beauty retail companies in Korea has expanded accordingly. However, compared to the quantitative expansion of companies, field-oriented job training for sales employees remains insufficient. This study aimed to design and validate an educational program for beauty retail companies based on the National Competency Standards(NCS). An online survey was conducted over one month, from July to August, with 248 sales employees of a beauty retail company. Using SPSS 21.0, EFA was performed, and CFA with AMOS 21.0 was conducted to assess reliability and validity. Hypotheses were tested through regression analysis, and mediating effects were examined using bootstrap and multiple regression. The empirical results confirmed three findings: First, NCS-based beauty retail training positively influenced job satisfaction; second, job satisfaction significantly affected sales performance; and lastly, job satisfaction played a partial mediating role. Moreover, NCS-based beauty retail training impacted sales performance both directly and indirectly, with sales-oriented training showing the strongest effect. This study highlights that strengthening field-based competencies is a key factor in enhancing training effectiveness and suggests that practical competency development directly linked to sales activ…

title: The Influence of Membership Programs and Application Ease of Use on Consumer Purchasing Decisions in Modern Retail
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of membership programs and application ease of use on consumer purchasing decisions in modern retail. The subjects of this study were consumers using the membership application at Indomaret in Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling with 100 respondents. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares (PLS) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The results indicate that, partially, the membership program does not have a significant effect on consumer purchasing decisions, while application ease of use has a positive and significant effect. These findings indicate that although membership provides various benefits, consumers may consider other factors such as price, needs, store location, product quality, and direct promotions when making purchases. Meanwhile, an application that is easy to learn, understand, operate, flexible, and practical can facilitate the purchasing process and support consumer purchasing decisions.

title: RETAIL INVESTOR PARTICIPATION AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION IN INDIA
abstract: Indias retail investor base has grown nearly sixfold since March 2020, but participation remains narrow when measured against the country's near-universal bank account ownership. Total demat accounts rose from 4.09 crore in March 2020 to about 23.4 crore by July 2026, and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) crossed 13 crore unique registered investors in April 2026. Monthly SIP contributions to mutual funds reached a record â‚¹32,490 crore in September 2026. Over the same period the RBI's Financial Inclusion Index rose from 53.9 (March 2021) to 70.0 (March 2026), and Jan Dhan accounts crossed 59 crore.Yet SEBI's Investor Survey 2025 finds that only 9.5% of Indian households invest in any securities product, even though 63% are aware of one. Participation is also uneven: it is concentrated in a few states, only about one in four NSE investors is a woman, and a large share of young new entrants has moved into equity derivatives, where SEBI found that 87.7% of individual traders made net losses in FY26.Using secondary data from SEBI, NSE, the depositories (NSDL and CDSL), AMFI, the RBI, NPCI, the Ministry of Finance and the World Bank, this paper argues that India has largely solved the problem of access to the financial system and is now facing the harder problem of quality of participation. It concludes with recommendations on financial literacy, product design, investor protectio…

abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive impairment (CI) is a common and disabling feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is increasingly recognized as a manifestation of progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA). Recent studies have characterized cognitive PIRA as gradual, relapse-independent cognitive decline identified through longitudinal neuropsychological assessment, most commonly affecting information processing speed. However, distinguishing MS-related cognitive PIRA from comorbid neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging, particularly in younger patients, in whom diagnostic overshadowing may delay appropriate diagnosis and management. Herein, we report a case of MS with rapidly progressive, memory-predominant CI mimicking cognitive PIRA. Case presentation A 46-year-old man with a 10-year history of MS presented with rapidly progressive, memory-predominant CI developing over the preceding 5 years, mimicking cognitive PIRA. Despite the absence of clinical relapses and limited magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) activity, cognitive decline progressed and was disproportionate to physical disability. Neuropsychological assessment revealed an early amnestic-dominant profile rather than the processing speed-predominant pattern observed in MS-related CI. Despite escalation from interferon-β1a to high-efficacy anti-CD20 therapy (ofatumumab), cognitive deterioration persisted, …

title: When Algorithms Set Prices: Emerging Consumer Fairness Challenges in AI-Driven Dynamic Pricing
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.

abstract: El presente artículo analiza la orientación familiar como estrategia parafortalecer la aceptación parental de Necesidades Educativas Específicas (NEE) en elcantón Otavalo. Con un enfoque mixto, se investigó la percepción de docentes, padres ypsicólogos. Se defiende que la aceptación parental no es espontánea, sino un procesomediado por la intervención profesional que reduce el duelo y la negación. Losresultados indican una brecha entre la importancia de la orientación y suimplementación real. Se propone una guía metodológica y talleres para facilitar lainclusión educativa efectiva y humana.

title: DATA PRODUCT STRATEGY FOR SCALABLE MICROSERVICE ARCHITECTURES
abstract: Applications are becoming increasingly distributed and data-centric and require scalable data management in microservice architectures. Traditional solutions tend to create complexity and bottlenecks, including managing data consistency, schema changes, cross-domain coordination, and more. While maintaining domain modularity and interoperability, a data-product-based architectural model can enhance discovery and ownership. This paper proposes a conceptual design and provides a reference architecture that includes domain-oriented design, metadata-driven governance and a self-service data platform. The results indicate that the proposed architecture provides greater throughput, lower latency, and better utilization of resources than baseline architecture. The paper also discusses key architectural components and future directions related to automated governance, interoperability of semantic data, and adaptive services of data platforms.

title: Research on Scheduling Strategy of Wind-Solar-Thermal-Storage System Based on MNSGA-II
abstract: This paper proposes an improved NSGA-II algorithm (MNSGA-II) to address the issues of local optima and insufficient population diversity in the process of solving economic dispatch strategies for power systems. The algorithm first uses Faure sequences to initialize the population, improving the quality and distribution uniformity of the initial solution; Secondly, design a dual archive maintenance strategy that updates the convergence archive through PBI values, updates the diversity archive through Manhattan distance, and combines truncation mechanism to prevent archive overflow, enhancing the algorithm’s global search capability. In the process of evolution, combining two archive information for environmental selection balances convergence and diversity. The application of MNSGA-II to the power scheduling problem of four generator units shows that compared with traditional NSGA-II and its variants, the algorithm proposed in this paper performs better in terms of optimization accuracy and stability, providing an effective solution for multi-objective optimization of power systems under complex constraints.

title: DECOUPLING OF ASSET PRICING FROM INCOME FUNDAMENTALS: A CROSS-CONTINENTAL ANALYSIS OF RENTAL YIELD COMPRESSION, SPECULATION, AND STRUCTURAL HOUSING INEQUITY
abstract: Standard financial models suggest that property values should align with rental income, yet global residential real estate consistently exhibits gross rental yields falling well below mortgage financing costs. This paper investigates why gross rental yields vary dramatically across global markets and examines the structural mechanisms distributing housing risk and return across income groups. Utilizing cross-national data from Numbeo across a 57-country national income dataset and a 339 - city continental dataset (spanning Asia, Europe, and North America), we evaluate rental yield spreads alongside key affordability and inequality indicators-including Price-to-Income Ratio (PTI), Price-to-Rent Ratio (PTR), Mortgage-as-a-Percentage-of-Income (MAPI), and Loan Affordability Index (LAI). The empirical analysis reveals four primary findings. First, gross rental yields do not vary significantly by national income classification, remaining between 5% and 6.7% globally; rather, outcomes are governed by underlying market structures and speculative orientations. Second, North American urban markets demonstrate rent-calibrated dynamics with high average yields (9.52%) where asset prices tightly track carrying costs. Third, European cities reflect policydriven yield compression (4.38%) enforced via strong tenant protections and rent controls.

title: Talent management practices for bridging the staffing strategy gap in a Gauteng-located higher education institution, South Africa
abstract: Talent management (TM) has emerged as a strategic imperative for universities globally as institutions compete for scarce academic and professional talent. Despite increasing attention to TM practices, many universities continue to experience staffing inefficiencies, weak recruitment systems, and limited workforce planning strategies. This study examines staffing practices as a core component of TM at a university in the Gauteng province of South Africa. Using a quantitative survey approach with a convenience sample of n=400 employees, data were collected from university employees who rated both the status and the importance of staffing practices on a five-point Likert scale. The findings revealed significant discrepancies between the perceived importance and current implementation of staffing practices. While respondents consider strategic staffing practices highly important for institutional performance, their implementation is rated only moderate to low. These findings highlight the need for universities to adopt integrated staffing strategies that align recruitment, workforce planning, and TM with institutional objectives. The study contributes to the literature on higher education human resource management by providing empirical evidence on staffing gaps and proposing a strategic staffing framework suitable for universities in developing contexts.

title: A Multi-Strategy Optimized Dung Beetle Algorithm
abstract: To address the shortcomings of the Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO) in solving complex optimization problems—namely insufficient global exploration capability, relatively slow convergence, and a tendency to become trapped in local optima—this paper proposes a multi-strategy improved DBO, termed CWSADBO, and applies it to the economic dispatch problem of microgrids. The proposed algorithm integrates Cubic chaotic initialization, a black widow behavior mechanism, a sparrow-inspired perturbation strategy, and a Cauchy–Gaussian hybrid mutation mechanism to enhance both search efficiency and solution accuracy. Specifically, the Cubic chaotic map is employed to increase the diversity of the initial population; the black widow behavior mechanism strengthens global exploration during the search process; the sparrow-inspired perturbation strategy helps the algorithm escape local optima; and the Cauchy–Gaussian hybrid mutation mechanism achieves a dynamic balance between global exploratory jumps and local fine-grained exploitation. To evaluate its performance, 16 standard benchmark functions are tested, and comparative experiments are conducted against DBO, IDBO, SSA, and SABO. The results demonstrate that CWSADBO achieves faster convergence and higher optimization accuracy on most benchmark functions, with particularly notable advantages in unimodal, multimodal, and complex multimodal cases.…

title: The Impact of Gamified Learning on Student Achievement: A Narrative Literature Review
abstract: This narrative literature review explores the statistically significant relationship between gamified learning, student engagement, and academic achievement. Drawing from quasi-experimental studies, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews, the paper highlights how game-based elements—such as points, badges, leaderboards, and immediate feedback—enhance motivation and foster higher-order thinking skills. The review also examines the differential impact of gamification across achievement levels and the moderating role of socio-demographic variables such as age, sex, parental education, and school type. Findings suggest that while gamification is broadly effective, its success depends on thoughtful design and contextual alignment with learner needs.

When GPUs Fail Quietly: Separating GPU Hardware Degradation from Monitoring Failure under Degraded Observability
abstract: A missing GPU measurement in a production supercomputer is ambiguous: either the device has failed, or the pipeline that reports on it has. The two call for different responses – an engineer sent to the hardware, or a ticket raised against the collector – so the ambiguity has to be resolved before either one is right. We ask which half of that decision needs a model. Whether the monitoring path has degraded is close to directly readable: one lightweight statistic that is never fitted, the gap between the data-delivery rates on the out-of-band hardware-sensor path and the in-band host path, ranks monitoring incidents at AUPRC 0.237 where they are only 5.2 % of the units ranked, and no learned component we trained improves on it. Deciding whether already-degraded evidence has a physical cause is harder, and needs both workload-aware residuals on the hardware sensors and an explicit model of the observation process. PARALLAX supplies these, tracking device health and monitoring health as separate latent states over out-of-band IPMI measurements, in-band telemetry, workload context, and structured missingness; the configuration we recommend is the hybrid that takes its physical risk from PARALLAX and its monitoring risk from the lightweight statistic. title: TRUSTWORTHY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF ROBUST DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUES FOR CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT
abstract: Medical image analysis has been revolutionized by the advent of artificial intelligence, which has made automated disease detection, segmentation and diagnosis possible across a range of imaging modalities, thus supporting clinical decisions. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has raised concerns regarding their reliability, interpretability, fairness, privacy, and regulatory compliance, highlighting the need for trustworthy AI in healthcare. The review focuses on recent breakthroughs in deep learning models for medical image analysis, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), segmentation networks based on U-net, Vision Transformers, and foundation models, and explores their use in clinical decision support. It also examines the fundamental principles of trustworthy AI, including explainability, robustness, fairness, privacy preservation, reliability, transparency and regulatory governance. The review summarizes the current state of the art for the strengths and limitations of current AI models and highlights some of the challenges that hamper the use of these models in the clinical workflow, such as limited data availability, domain shifts, algorithmic bias, computational complexity, and integration into the clinical workflow. New concepts like multimodal foundation models, federated learning and privacy-preserving AI are also explored as potential…

title: A Multisensor Baseline and Abstention Architecture for Low Voltage Rotating Machine Condition Assessment
abstract: Condition assessment of small rotating machines is often demonstrated with a single sensor and a fixed threshold, although operating point, mounting and environment can alter measured signals. This paper presents NEXUS PRIME V1 as a documented design for a low voltage, ESP32 based bench instrument using device specific baselines, validity checks and corroborating channels. Its proposed rule set reports NORMAL when required measurements agree with calibrated healthy bands, ABNORMAL only for a coherent pattern in at least two independent condition channels, and INCONCLUSIVE when evidence is missing or contradictory. The design specifies vibration, current, voltage, temperature and RPM sensing, with distance serving primarily as a setup validity check; it also specifies local indication and a web dashboard. The supplied 71 page blueprint reports a design audit, including 18 distinct GPIO assignments and an estimated INR 1,894 parts budget. Hardware, firmware, diagnostic accuracy and reliability have not yet been measured. The contribution is an inspectable architecture and a preregisterable validation protocol, not an experimentally demonstrated diagnostic improvement

title: Hybrid Machine Learning and XAI Approach for Real-Time Intrusion Detection
abstract: The growth of communication technologies and advancement in cloud computing have led to an increase in the possibility of cybercrime and attacks. Traditional IDSs (Intrusion Detection Systems) are ineffective in detecting sophisticated attacks that evolve rapidly and target information systems and therefore do not provide sufficient protection. Moreover, traditional systems are slow to adapt to the appearance of new threats and produce a high number of false alarms which are often considered a nuisance. The proposed study offers an intrusion detection system framework that incorporates the hybrid techniques of machine learning to enhance the security of networks and detect cyber threats. The key aspects of the system are the following: the model uses various machine learning algorithms as well as anomaly detection methods in order to detect intrusions effectively. The effectiveness of the framework in terms of its accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and false positive index calculation is measured through conducting empirical testing applying public datasets as references for verification of the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results of the study show that the hybrid intrusion detection system manages to achieve better performance in comparison with conventional solitary models due to its adaptability, low computational complexity and ability to provide security in…
