From Prompt to Polygon: Evaluating End-to-End Human–AI Workflows for Web-Based Generative 3D Authoring
abstract: Prompt- and image-driven 3D generation can lower the interaction barrier to digital asset creation, yet model-level advances do not establish whether non-specialists can operate a complete authoring workflow. This study designed and evaluated a web-based human–AI prototype integrating a React interface, FastAPI services, ComfyUI workflow orchestration, asynchronous job processing, persistent asset storage, and browser-based 3D visualization. We implemented four modes: Text-to-3D, Text-to-3D with ControlNet, Single Image-to-3D, and Multi Image-to-3D. Evaluation combined 14 requirement-derived black-box scenarios, cross-viewer GLB compatibility checks in three viewing environments, 35 completed generation jobs, task-based observation with seven participants completing 84 task executions, System Usability Scale (SUS) responses from a separate group of 12 students, and one expert assessment of implementation and output quality. All 14 functional scenarios produced the expected outcomes, and the tested GLB outputs opened in the integrated viewer, Blender, and 3dviewer.net. Mean server-side turnaround was 66.15 s; an exploratory Kruskal–Wallis test indicated differences among the observed workload distributions (H(3) = 10.52, p = .015, ε² = .243), but did not support causal or pairwise speed claims. title: Adaptive Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Systematic Review of Concept Drift Detection and Mitigation in Data Streams
abstract: The proliferation of high-velocity data streams in domains such as IoT, cybersecurity, and financial technology has exposed the limitations of static machine learning models. When the underlying data distribution changes over time, a phenomenon known as concept drift occurs, leading to severe model degradation `[1]`. This paper presents a systematic review of 29 foundational and contemporary studies on concept drift detection and adaptation. We categorize detection mechanisms into statistical, window-based, and model-based approaches, while evaluating adaptation strategies ranging from dynamic ensembles to lightweight incremental learning `[16]`. Furthermore, we address compounding challenges, including class imbalance and the emergence of novel classes `[2]`, `[30]`. By synthesizing recent advancements, this review provides a comprehensive roadmap for developing robust, real-time, and resource-efficient streaming machine learning systems `[27]`

title: Deep learning investigation of discrete fractional order Shingles disease model with neural networking
abstract: This study investigates the discrete fractional-order Shingles disease (DFOS) mathematical model. The considered model is framed with five compartments over time. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are determined via fixed point theory, confirming well-defined solutions. Three scenarios, each with various fractional orders, were used to study the effects of memory and fractional dynamics on disease propagation. To solve the model, we operate a discrete numerical iterative method (DNIM) linked to neural networks, specifically employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, denoted DNIM-LM. This hybrid technique increases the accuracy of numerical results from neural networks. The data sets are distributed into 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing, confirming a balanced calculation. The performance of the discrete fractional mathematical modeling is evaluated through artificial intelligence (AI), which involves training progress, error distribution, regression metrics, and overall model fit. The outcomes are thoroughly visualized via graphical illustrations, providing insights into the dynamics of each part and the impact of various fractional orders on the spread of shingles. This research addresses a novel approach to demonstrate infectious diseases with fractional dynamics and enhanced computational methods, improving our understanding of shingle …

title: Deep brain stimulation surgery under general anesthesia in patients with Parkinson’s disease: a retrospective study in Korea
abstract: Objective: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the subthalamic nucleus (STN) is conventionally performed under local anesthesia to preserve intraoperative microelectrode recording (MER) quality. However, awake surgery poses challenges for Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients with severe anxiety, respiratory compromise, or debilitating “off-medication” dystonia. This study evaluated the clinical efficacy and surgical feasibility of bilateral STN-DBS under general anesthesia.Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 29 advanced PD patients who underwent bilateral STN-DBS under general anesthesia. Thirteen patients underwent a two-stage operation (Activa implantable pulse generator [IPG]), and 16 underwent a one-stage procedure (directional leads, Percept PC IPG). Target localization relied on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography (CT). Intraoperative MER was performed under inhalational anesthesia with sevoflurane (n=27) or desflurane (n=2). Outcomes were assessed after ≥6 months using the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) parts III and IV and the levodopa-equivalent daily dose (LEDD).Results: Intraoperative MER successfully identified STN and substantia nigra pars reticulata boundaries in all 29 patients. UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION AND CARRIER-COLLECTION ROBUSTNESS UNDER PHYSICAL TOLERANCES IN A SERIES VERTICAL-JUNCTION SILICON SOLAR CELL
abstract: This work investigates the propagation of uncertainties in physical parameters to carrier collection in a series vertical-junction silicon solar cell. Starting from an exact dimensionless collection law, uncertainties are introduced in the base thickness H, diffusion coefficient D, carrier lifetime τ, and interface recombination velocities Sf and Sb. For each realization, the diffusion length and the reduced parameters h, f, and b are recalculated, thereby preserving the dependencies induced by the physical transformation. Twenty-seven nominal regimes and four controlled uncertainty amplitudes, from ±5% to ±30%, are investigated using a Monte Carlo campaign of 120,000 realizations per scenario. Robustness is characterized by the coefficient of variation of collection and by R90 = P(C ≥ 0.9 C0). The median coefficient of variation increases from approximately 3.13% at ±5% to 18.94% at ±30%, while the maximum value reaches 37.14%. Over the same range, the median R90 decreases from 100% to approximately 68.12%. At ±30%, some regimes retain R90 close to unity, whereas the least robust regime in the grid reaches approximately 60.17%. The regime of maximum statistical dispersion does not exactly coincide with that of minimum R90. These results show that nominal performance, statistical dispersion, and probabilistic robustness are distinct properties and establish a regime-dependent m…

title: DeepFake Shield: A Multi-Modal Generative AI Fraud Detection Pipeline with Explicit Uncertainty Handling
abstract: Synthetic media is now cheap to make and hard to judge by eye. A cloned voice can approve a payment, a generated face can get past a casual identity check, and a fluent paragraph written by a language model can pass for a statement from a real person. Most detectors cover only one of these cases, and almost all return a confident verdict even for input far outside their training data. This paper presents DeepFake Shield, a Flask-based web application that screens images, text, audio and video through one interface. Each modality is served by a pre-trained deep learning classifier, and a threshold layer turns the raw model score into one of three outcomes: authentic, synthetic or inconclusive. For video, the visual and audio streams are analysed separately and any disagreement between them is reported as a conflict. The paper gives a detailed justification for the topic, describes the architecture and decision logic, and sets out an evaluation protocol based on precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and Brier score with thresholds tuned on validation data only. We report the engineering checks completed so far and state clearly that they are not accuracy measurements

CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
abstract: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Other limitations include insufficient semantic interoperability, inadequate model fidelity, inconsistent latency assessment, deployment evidence, and consideration of cybersecurity and human intervention. title: Artificial Intelligence in Production and Optimization
abstract: This review is a systematic literature review-cum-bibliometric analysis of the field of Artificial Intelligence in Production and Optimization with a view to mapping the field in holistic manner. In this review the authors have attempted to identify the predominant strands in the field and identify where learning approaches have been linked to decision making frameworks and where learning approaches end at prediction. Data for the review are sourced from Elsevier's Scopus database, and are limited to English language journal articles and reviews published between 2014 and 2027 using key words. This review is based on 3,727 records in the final database. The number of documents published has increased from 38 in 2014 to 1,161 in 2026 and the top producers are China, India, and the United States. The most prevalent themes were identified as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Optimization. The formal decision model seems to be mainly in the field of scheduling, while in bioprocess and additive manufacturing, and food systems, it is not often that the decision is made to end at prediction.

title: Privacy and Data Protection Governance for Implementing Indonesia’s Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27/2022): A Structured Literature Review
abstract: Indonesia’s Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection (PDP Law) imposes extensive duties on controllers and processors, yet organizational governance for implementation remains unevenly documented. This structured literature review, informed by PRISMA reporting principles, synthesizes 23 governance-focused peer-reviewed publications (2022–2026) identified through a transparent purposive corpus strategy. No multi-database search was conducted in this study. Implementation is influenced by legal certainty, institutional accountability (including supervisory officer models), sector capacity, third-party ecosystem risk, rights interoperability, measurable compliance tools, and automated decision-making challenges. Privacy governance (74%), audit and compliance assessment (48%), and integrated data governance (39%) are the most frequent components; data protection impact assessment is rarely explicit. Governance structures are portrayed as prerequisites for compliance where accountability, assessment instruments, and platform intermediaries align. A seven-layer implementation framework for the PDP Law is proposed. Limitations include the purposive corpus, limited Indonesian empirical evidence, and the absence of exhaustive database screening.

Closed but Not Recovered: Size, Time, and the Limits of Audit Follow-Up in Indonesia
abstract: Follow-up of audit recommendations is usually measured by how many recommendations are closed. That measure ignores whether the money at stake is actually recovered. This study separates the two. Data come from the Supreme Audit Board's recommendation follow-up monitoring appendix for local governments, status as of Semester I 2024, covering 518 entities that reconcile on both counts and values. Across the 2018 to 2022 cohorts, local governments closed 72.13 percent of recommendations on average but recovered only 53.1 percent of the 11.34 trillion rupiah at stake. Recovery falls monotonically with the size of the recommendation, from 99.06 percent in the smallest decile to 55.71 percent in the largest, and to 39.65 percent on an aggregate basis. Closure falls by only 9.0 points across the same deciles. With cohort and entity fixed effects, a tenfold larger recommendation portfolio is associated with recovery lower by 18.7 percentage points. Resolution also stalls: closure rises by 5.12 points a year up to age eight and by 0.09 points a year thereafter, leaving 49,639 recommendations issued between 2005 and 2017 still open. The follow-up system settles small and recent matters and leaves large and old ones unresolved.

title: Future directions on integrated wildlife monitoring based on non-invasive approaches in Europe
abstract: Abstract The growing trend of emerging diseases at the wildlife-livestock-human interface underscores the need to establish integrated surveillance strategies within a One Health framework. In Europe, Integrated Wildlife Monitoring (IWM) tends to focus on specific pathogens, often with limited spatial and temporal scope. In this perspectives article, we address some of the most recent technological advances that could strengthen future IWM programs, with special emphasis on non-invasive approaches for monitoring wildlife populations and pathogen communities. We analyse the potential complementarity of different monitoring tools, such as camera traps, unmanned aerial vehicles, acoustic recording, and especially the detection of environmental nucleic acids (ENAD) using next-generation sequencing techniques, for the simultaneous characterization of pathogen and host communities. Despite the potential of molecular tools for large-scale monitoring, the lack of methodological standardization, the limited capacity to obtain quantitative information (e.g. population abundance or pathogen prevalence), and the difficulty of inferring the epidemiological significance of findings (e.g. whether molecular detection indicates viable pathogen) remain key challenges that limit their application. Finally, we argue that integrating these technologies with artificial intelligence (AI) represents a…

title: A Dempster-Shafer-Based Expert System for Personalized Higher Education Major Recommendation
abstract: Selecting a study program at a State University (Perguruan Tinggi Negeri/PTN) is a decision that many senior high school students approach without a systematic review of their interest, aptitude, achievement, and career goals, a gap made more pressing by the limited counseling capacity available at most schools. Earlier expert systems for major recommendation have relied on Forward Chaining or Certainty Factor, methods that combine evidence into a single rule outcome or scalar confidence without explicitly representing the uncertainty left by incomplete evidence. This study developed and implemented a web-based expert system, Peta Kampus, that applies Dempster-Shafer evidence theory to generate a personalized major recommendation from a student's answers to a structured questionnaire. The knowledge base was constructed with school counselors and an education practitioner into 275 evidence-linked questions covering 55 majors across 21 faculties, each carrying an expert-assigned belief value. The system was built on a native PHP Model-View-Controller architecture with MySQL as the data store, and its inference engine combines successive evidence using Dempster's rule of combination while tracking residual uncertainty and evidentiary conflict. The system was verified through Black Box Testing of its functional modules, with all 15 tested scenarios passing, and evaluated through an…

StreamHub - Multi - Agent Framework for Movie Recommendation System Using Langchain
abstract: The rapid growth of digital entertainment platforms has made it difficult for users to discover suitable movies and music from a large collection of content. Conventional platforms commonly depend on separate search interfaces and recommendation features, which may not provide a unified or context-aware experience. This paper presents StreamHub, an OTT and Music Multi-Agent Recommendation System that combines movie discovery, music discovery, personalized recommendations, user interaction, and premium-content access in a single web application. A Supervisor Agent coordinates user requests and directs them to specialized agent functions. The Movie/Content Agent integrates the TMDB API to retrieve available movie and television information, while the Music Agent connects to an external royalty-free music API to obtain available tracks and related metadata. User preferences, watch history, ratings, and watchlists can be maintained through a MySQL database to support more relevant content suggestions. The system uses React.js for the frontend and FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic for backend services. JWT-based authentication supports protected access, while the modular multiagent design separates responsibilities and supports future extension. The platform demonstrates how Al-assisted interaction, external APIs, persistent user information, and coordinated agents can simplify ente…

title: INVESTIGATING CHALLENGES IN TOEFL IBT INTEGRATED SPEAKING: EVIDENCE FROM HIGH-QUALITY PROGRAM STUDENTS AT PTIT, VIETNAM
abstract: Integrated Speaking in the TOEFL iBT exam presents significant cognitive and linguistic demands as it requires test-takers to synthesize information from multiple input modalities (reading and listening) before producing an oral response. This study investigates the primary subjective and objective challenges faced by non-English major students enrolled in the High-Quality (HQ) program at the Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology (PTIT), Vietnam, where the English curriculum is benchmarked against the TOEFL iBT standard. Data were gathered through a mixed-methods approach involving a quantitative survey ($N = 120$) and semi-structured interviews ($n = 12$) with students working at the B1 CEFR proficiency level. Findings reveal three dominant categories of difficulty: linguistic limitations (insufficient vocabulary and limited listening synthesis), lack of systematic instruction in speaking strategies, and affective barriers (low self-efficacy and anxiety). Based on these empirical insights, targeted pedagogical solutions are proposed, including structured note-taking frameworks, integrated skills scaffolding, and strategy-based instruction to enhance student performance.

title: Comparative Study on the Perceptions of Residents and Inspectors Regarding the In-Unit Fire Safety Inspection System in Multi-family Housing
abstract: In this study, a survey was conducted with residents and inspectors in multifamily housing to identify ways to improve the effectiveness of the in-unit fire safety inspection system. Their perceptions, satisfaction levels, perceived problems, and support system requirements were comparatively analyzed. Residents recognized the necessity of in-unit inspections but lacked understanding of the system and inspection methods, whereas inspectors showed a high level of institutional understanding but lower recognition of the need for in-unit inspections, confirming a perception gap. Satisfaction was significantly lower among the inspectors. Both groups identified inspectors' awareness as the primary problem, whereas inspectors additionally pointed to the result collection method and residents’ inspection frequency. Both groups agreed on the need for a support system, with residents prioritizing information provision and inspectors administrative support. The findings empirically identify the stakeholder perception gap and provide baseline data for institutional improvements and support system design.

Tenant-Aware HR Master Data Harmonization: A Logical Bronze-Silver-MDM-Gold Workflow for Multi-Tenant HCM Data
abstract: Enterprise human resources (HR) systems often apply inconsistent labels to shared employee master-data attributes. This study evaluates an ordered, tenant-aware harmonization workflow represented by Bronze, Silver, master data management (MDM), and Gold logical layers; it does not claim an implemented transactional lakehouse platform. Four synthetic HR datasets contribute 3,000 core employee records. A fixed-seed simulation creates four tenants and introduces controlled categorical corruption, missingness, and duplicate identifiers while retaining independent canonical labels. Exact, normalized, synonym, and bounded fuzzy matching run in sequence, and unresolved nonmissing values are referred for manual review. At a fuzzy cutoff of 0.82, the study records 8,842 nonmissing field values, 8,731 canonical assignments, and 8,480 correct assignments, giving 98.74% assignment coverage, 95.91% recall under the study definition, and an F1 of 0.9651. Field-level denominators reconstructed from the method-by-field matrix allow independent arithmetic checking and identify 251 erroneous assignments across all four matching tiers. In the deduplicated employee classification population, department and job-title vocabularies shrink from 228 raw labels to 37 mastered labels. title: HOUSEHOLD SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT IN THE URBAN COMMUNE OF DIFFA, NIGER: PRACTICES, PERCEPTIONS AND GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES
abstract: Rapid population growth, urbanization and changing consumption patterns are increasing the quantity and complexity of household solid waste generated in low- and middle-income cities. In Niger, solid waste management remains constrained by limited infrastructure, weak institutional coordination, predominantly informal collection practices and very limited source separation. In the urban commune of Diffa, these constraints are particularly important because household waste is largely managed individually and disposed of at nearby uncontrolled dumpsites. This study assessed household solid waste-management practices, knowledge and perceptions, as well as selected governance and willingness-to-pay dimensions in the urban commune of Diffa, Niger. A cross-sectional household survey was conducted from August to September 2026 using a structured questionnaire administered through Kobo Collect. Simple random sampling was used to select 152 households distributed across 13 neighbourhoods. Data were exported to Excel for organization and graphical presentation, while descriptive statistical analyses and willingness-to-pay calculations were performed using Minitab 18. Kitchen waste was reported by 89.47% of households and packaging waste by 60.53%. A majority of households (58.55%) had no waste container, while 41.45% used a container. title: A Review on Pharmaceutical Marketing and Management
abstract: Pharmaceutical marketing and management occupy a distinct position among commercial disciplines because they operate at the intersection of profit-driven business objectives and public health responsibility. Thisreview examinesthe strategic, operational, and ethical dimensions of pharma marketing and management, drawing on recent literature covering promotional practices, digital transformation, supply chain operations, and regulatory oversight. The review finds that traditional promotional tools such as medical representative (MR) visits, free drug samples, and continuing medical education (CME) sponsorships remain influential in shaping physician prescribing behaviour, even as digital channels, artificial intelligence (AI), and data analytics increasingly reshape how companies engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and patients. On the management side, the Indian pharmaceutical supply chain continues to face structural challenges including fragmentation, import dependence on active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), cold chain limitations, and counterfeit products, even as digital tools and regulatory reforms attempt to close these gaps. Ethical concerns persist around inducements, exaggerated promotional claims, and inconsistent enforcement of codes such as the Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP), which became legally binding in 2024. title: Leveraging Industry 4.0 to overcome supply chain challenges in Gauteng manufacturing small- and medium-sized enterprises: A Supply Chain Operations Reference model perspective
abstract: Background: Manufacturing small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Gauteng, South Africa, face persistent supply chain challenges that hinder performance and sustainability. Although Industry 4.0 technologies offered opportunities to improve supply chain performance, limited research had linked these technologies to specific challenges across the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model. Objectives: This study aimed to identify and validate supply chain challenges affecting manufacturing SMEs and recommend Industry 4.0 technologies to address them across SCOR processes. Method: The study was conducted among supply chain professionals employed in manufacturing SMEs in Gauteng, South Africa. This quantitative study, grounded in the positivist paradigm, included 252 supply chain professionals. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and snowball sampling. IBM SPSS Statistics and SmartPLS 4 were used for descriptive analysis and measurement model evaluation. Results: Significant challenges were identified across all SCOR processes, including forecasting inaccuracies, supplier unreliability, inadequate visibility and traceability, inventory inaccuracies, poor returns monitoring, and miscommunication. The measurement model demonstrated strong reliability and validity, with Cronbach’s alphas above 0.86 and composite reliabilities exceeding 0.89. A SCOR Technolo…

title: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy and surgical innovation reshape multimodal management of esophageal cancer
abstract: Abstract Esophageal cancer requires multimodal management that accounts for histology, resectability and operative fitness. This narrative review examines selected literature published through December 2025 on neoadjuvant systemic therapy, minimally invasive esophagectomy and perioperative decision-making. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy have established roles, but their relative benefits depend on the population and regimen. CROSS demonstrated a survival benefit over surgery alone, whereas ESOPEC favored perioperative FLOT over CROSS chemoradiotherapy in resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma. For esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, randomized phase III trials have demonstrated higher pathological complete response rates with selected chemoimmunotherapy regimens than with chemotherapy alone. However, pathological response should not be equated with an established survival benefit, and mature comparisons against chemoradiotherapy remain important. Evidence from gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma also requires careful interpretation before extrapolation to esophageal primary tumors. The TIME, MIRO and ROBOT randomized trials support reductions in postoperative pulmonary morbidity with the minimally invasive approaches evaluated compared with open esophagectomy. title: Public Financial Management and Rural Development in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: Evidence from 2008–2017
abstract: Public financial management is widely regarded as a key determinant of development outcomes in resource-dependent economies, yet the extent to which it translates into tangible rural development remains under-examined at the subnational level in Nigeria. This study investigates the relationship between public financial management and rural development in Akwa Ibom State between 2008 and 2017, focusing on whether the pace of rural development kept pace with the state's rising public budgets and expenditures. Anchored in John Rawls's Theory of Justice, the study adopted a historical/descriptive survey design, drawing a sample of 182 respondents from five public establishments in the state using proportional stratified random sampling. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using percentage tables and chi-square statistics. Findings show that the calculated chi-square value (9.75) was less than the critical value (21.03) at the 0.05 significance level, leading to the acceptance of the null hypothesis: the level of rural development recorded in Akwa Ibom State was not commensurate with the state's rising public expenditure over the period. title: The Effect of Digital Payments, Financial Literacy, Financial Access, and Mental Accounting on Microenterprise Performance
abstract: Introduction/ Main Objectives: This study investigates the effects of digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting on the performance of microenterprises in Kuningan Regency, Indonesia. Using the Resource-Based View (RBV) framework, these four factors are conceptualized as technological, financial, and cognitive capabilities that may enhance business outcomes. Novelty: This study lies in integrating digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting into a single empirical model and testing their simultaneous effects on microenterprise performance within the specific context of Kuningan Regency using SEM-PLS. Research Methods: The research employed a quantitative survey method with 277 respondents selected from a population of 901 registered microenterprises, determined using the Slovin formula. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. Finding/Results: The results show that the research model has adequate explanatory and predictive capabilities. Digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting have positive and significant effects on microenterprise performance. abstract: В умовах тривалих економічних, безпекових та інституційних викликів особливого значення набуває здатність системи державного фінансового контролю гарантувати безперервність контрольних функцій, своєчасно реагувати на бюджетні ризики та сприяти збереженню й ефективному використанню публічних ресурсів. Метою дослідження є теоретичне обґрунтування та емпірична оцінка резильєнтності системи державного фінансового контролю як детермінанти ефективності використання бюджетних ресурсів і чинника забезпечення національної безпеки України. У статті запропоноване визначення стабільності державної системи фінансового контролю та систематизовані її основні компоненти: інституційний, операційний, цифровий та адаптивний. На основі цього розроблено концептуальну модель взаємозв'язку між державним фінансовим контролем, бюджетною ефективністю та національною безпекою, що відображає взаємодію інституційного, регіонального та макрофінансового рівнів. title: PENGENALAN PENCATATAN KEUANGAN DIGITAL UNTUK PENGUATAN LITERASI KEUANGAN RUMAH TANGGA
abstract: Pencatatan keuangan keluarga membantu penyusunan anggaran dan evaluasi pengeluaran. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini memperkenalkan penganggaran, pencatatan sederhana, dan media pencatatan digital kepada warga di wilayah Cidahu, Kabupaten Sukabumi, Jawa Barat. Sesi literasi keuangan dilaksanakan pada 20 Agustus 2026 pukul 13.00–15.00 WIB, sesuai waktu yang tercantum dalam abstrak. Metode meliputi edukasi, diskusi, latihan kasus terbimbing, dan pengenalan aplikasi Money Lover. Hasil pembelajaran dianalisis secara deskriptif menggunakan nilai pre-test dan post-test berpasangan dari 15 responden. Rata-rata nilai meningkat dari 52,00 menjadi 83,33, dengan kenaikan rata-rata 31,33 poin. Seluruh responden mengalami kenaikan 25–35 poin. Luaran lain meliputi materi edukasi, contoh pencatatan keuangan keluarga, dan dokumentasi. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan capaian pada tes yang diberikan setelah kegiatan. Dokumen yang tersedia belum menjelaskan butir soal, pedoman penskoran, validitas dan reliabilitas instrumen, hasil praktik individual, atau penggunaan aplikasi secara mandiri. Ketiadaan kelompok pembanding dan evaluasi lanjutan membatasi kesimpulan tentang dampak kausal dan perubahan kebiasaan yang berkelanjutan.

title: MECHANISMS FOR INCREASING THE EFFICIENCY OF TAX CONTROL AS A FACTOR IN ENSURING THE TAX SECURITY OF THE NATIONAL ECONOMY
abstract: Taxes are the main source of state revenue generation, so mechanisms for ensuring tax security are of critical importance for the stability of the national financial system. The aim of the study is to empirically measure the relationships between administrative costs, technological development of tax authorities, institutional characteristics, and tax administration results. The work employs the following methods: structural analysis — for logical organization of available data and creation of a holistic research model; regression analysis — for assessing the joint impact of several independent variables on the dependent one; ANOVA — to check the quality of the obtained models. The study found that operating costs and expenses for information and communication technologies (ICT) have a direct and statistically significant relationship with the growth of tax losses. An increase in operating costs per unit is accompanied by an increase in tax losses by 0.0031, and ICT expenses — by 0.0121. The technological mechanisms model revealed an inverse effect of artificial intelligence (AI) and mandatory electronic invoicing on the tax competitiveness indicator. The introduction of AI reduces the indicator by 15.7 points, and the introduction of E-Invoicing — by 10.1 points. title: Role of Financial Advisors and Media in Mutual Fund Investments Behaviour: Preliminary Evidence from Punjab
abstract: The relevance of financial advisors and media is being expanded in decision processes of investors. It is mainly due to increasing range of mutual fund products and financial-information channels. This pilot study investigates the role of Financial Advisor (FA) and Media Influence (MI) in investors’ behaviour towards mutual funds by emphasizing on Decision to Invest (DI) and Fund Preference (FP). A quantitative, cross sectional and exploratory design was employed using 43 complete responses from existing mutual fund investors in Punjab, India. Some statistical tools were used like descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) and Bartlett’s tests, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), composite reliability (CR), average variance extracted (AVE), Pearson correlation, multiple regression and regression diagnostics. In total, 19 Liker-scale items were evaluated. The scales confirmed satisfactory internal consistency (Alpha = .805-.948). The overall KMO was .689 and Bartlett’s test was significant, while the four-factor Principal Axis Factoring solution explained 68.13% of the variance. FA and MI did not significantly predict DI or the supplementary aggregate measure of investment behaviour. title: GIANT RIGHT PARADUODENAL HERNIA WITH INCARCERATION OF THE ENTIRE SMALL BOWEL: A RARE CAUSE OF SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION IN A VIRGIN ABDOMEN. A CASE REPORT
abstract: Introduction: Internal hernias are protrusions of abdominal viscera through a peritoneal or mesenteric aperture within the abdominal cavity. They account for 0.5–5.8% of intestinal obstructions. Paraduodenal hernias are the classic congenital type, and incarceration of the entire small bowel within the hernia sac is exceptional. Case presentation: We report the case of a 40-year-old man with no past medical or surgical history who presented with a three-month history of postprandial vomiting and early satiety, progressing to intractable vomiting with cessation of stool and flatus. Examination revealed mild abdominal distension and an empty rectum; laboratory tests were unremarkable. The plain abdominal radiograph showed multiple air-fluid levels, and computed tomography showed small bowel dilatation up to 4 cm, initially attributed to a congenital band. As the patient did not improve after 24 hours of conservative management, a midline laparotomy was performed. Exploration revealed a giant right paraduodenal hernia whose sac contained the entire small bowel. The loops were released by meticulous dissection and were found viable, so no resection was needed; the sac was excised. The postoperative course was uneventful and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 4. At two months, he remained free of vomiting. Conclusion: Paraduodenal hernia should be considered in any smal…

title: HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE AND FINANCIAL PROTECTION AMONG LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS IN NIGERIA: EVIDENCE FROM THE NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE AUTHORITY (NHIA)
abstract: The health financing system in Nigeria is highly dependent on out-of-pocket (OOP) payments, which exposes households to catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) and impoverishment. Although the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) Act 2022 provides for coverage for all Nigerians, insurance penetration is extremely low, especially among low-income earners. This study investigated the relationship between health insurance coverage and financial protection among low-income households in Nigeria, testing whether coverage is negatively associated with OOP expenditure, CHE and delayed or forgone care. A quantitative explanatory design was applied to secondary data from the Nigeria General Household Survey (NGHS) 2023/2024, restricted to households in the lowest two consumption expenditure quintiles. Current enrolment status indicated coverage; OOP expenditure, CHE incidence at the 10% and 40% thresholds, delayed or forgone care, and coping strategies indicated financial protection. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for the complex survey design. Only 2.2% of households were insured, and CHE incidence was 45.5% nationally, rising to 52.7% among rural poor households. Among the insured, coverage was associated with a 42% reduction in OOP expenditure during health shocks and significantly lower odds of CH…

title: FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH TUBERCULOSIS TRANSMISSION AMONG HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS OF BACTERIOLOGICALLY CONFIRMED PULMONARY TUBERCULOSIS PATIENTS NAKURU COUNTY: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
abstract: Introduction: Tuberculosis (TB) remains an important communicable disease and people living in the same household with a person with bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB are at increased risk of TB infection. The World Health Organization recommends systematic screening of household and close contacts and TB preventive treatment for eligible contacts. In 2024, an estimated 14 million household contacts of people who were diagnosed with bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB, were reported globally but only a proportion were evaluated and provided with preventive treatment. Objective: To determine factors associated with tuberculosis transmission among household contact of bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Nakuru County. Methods: The proposal will use a quantitative cross-sectional approach among household contacts of bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB patients identified in Nakuru County. Eligible contacts will be identified, consented and interviewed using structured questionnaires. TB status and screening information will be obtained from participant assessment and relevant clinical records where available. Data will be coded, entered into Microsoft Excel and analyzed using descriptive analysis. Results: The findings will provide local evidence that can support targeted household contact screening, health education, infection preventio…

title: Optimal control strategies for dengue transmission under varying adult prevalence of Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes: a deterministic mathematical modeling study
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to develop prevalence-informed post-release dengue control strategies for settings in which Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes have become established through population replacement and to quantify how optimal supplementary intervention intensity and duration vary with adult Wolbachia prevalence, pW. Methods: A deterministic human–mosquito model was formulated that included Wolbachia-free and Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes and incorporated cytoplasmic incompatibility, maternal transmission, and reduced vector competence. Two bounded supplementary controls were optimized over a 3-year horizon: reduction of effective human–mosquito contact and conventional adult mosquito suppression, represented by increased adult mortality. A quadratic-cost optimal-control problem was solved numerically using the Pontryagin maximum principle and a forward/backward sweep algorithm. Outcomes were compared across representative pW scenarios and prevalence scans. Results: The optimal policies applied high-intensity supplementary control early in the planning horizon and then relaxed control as infection pressure declined. Higher pW reduced the uncontrolled infection burden, decreased the incremental benefit of additional intervention, and shortened the duration of maximum control. title: The Impact of Asymmetry in Industrial Site Heat Index Information on the Right to Stop Work
abstract: Workers face “information asymmetry” because heat-related illness prevention guidelines in industrial settings lack enforceability—remaining merely “recommendations”—and the complex method for calculating apparent temperature can limit workers' access to workplace heat-risk information. In Korean industrial settings without access to objective risk data, workers cannot effectively exercise the right to stop work under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. effectively. To bridge this gap, this study proposes a worker-centric overhaul of the Ministry of Employment and Labor’s heat-related illness guidelines that would enable on-site workers to recognize immediately risks and exercise their rights. Furthermore, to prevent these rights from becoming ineffective due to fear of reprisal, this study suggests institutional safeguards, such as codifying guidelines for exercising the right to stop work based on objective indicators and establishing provisions that exempt subcontractors from liability to prime contractors for delays caused by legitimate work stoppages. Ultimately, this study presents a concrete roadmap that directly links prevention policies—previously limited to mere recommendations—to workers’ right to know. The proposed framework aims to support the effective exercise of the right to stop work by improving access to risk information and strengthening institutional sa…

title: Early Detection of Fraud Indications in Ultra-Micro Financial Institutions Using Machine-Learning-based Financial Journal Data Analysis
abstract: Ultra Micro Financial Institutions (UMFI) play an important role in expanding financial inclusion, but their high transaction volume, relatively small transaction values, direct cash handling, and limited internal control capacity may create fraud risks that are difficult to detect from aggregated financial statements. This study develops an early fraud-indication detection framework using transaction-level accounting journal data from PT Permodalan Nasional Madani (PNM), Magelang Branch. The study adopts a quantitative predictive case-study and proof-of-concept design. The available dataset covers 1 January to 31 March 2026 and contains 305,343 transactions from five units, 104 unique general-ledger codes, and balanced debit and credit totals of IDR 160,274,807,743. The novelty lies in translating the Fraud Triangle—pressure, opportunity, and rationalization—into operational transaction features, including end-period activity, transaction spikes, outliers, duplication, unusual account combinations, reversals, and correction-related descriptions. Rule-based screening is used only to identify risky candidates, while final fraud and non-fraud labels must be validated by internal audit. The analytical pipeline includes anonymization, leakage-aware preprocessing, feature engineering, train-validation-test splitting, SMOTE only within training data, Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validatio…

У дослідженні проаналізовано сучасні тенденції розвитку міжнародної торгівлі, визначено роль макроекономічних, логістичних і геополітичних чинників у формуванні глобальних торговельних потоків. Для кількісної оцінки взаємозв’язку між міжнародною торгівлею та ключовими факторами використано метод множинної лінійної регресії. Як результативний показник обрано світовий обсяг міжнародної торгівлі товарами та послугами (TRADE), а факторними ознаками визначено світовий ВВП (GDP), індекс тиску на глобальні ланцюги постачання (GSCPI), індекс геополітичного ризику (GPR) та потоки прямих іноземних інвестицій (FDI). A TIERED LIFECYCLE GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK FOR AGENTIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FINANCIAL SERVICES
abstract: The rapid emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) presents significant governance challenges for financial services, where autonomous systems increasingly support high-impact financial activities. Existing regulatory approaches remain fragmented and continue to rely primarily on non-binding supervisory guidance, leaving important gaps in lifecycle oversight, accountability, and systemic risk management. This paper proposes the Tiered Lifecycle Governance (TLG) Framework, a strategic governance model that integrates lifecycle-based AI oversight with responsive, risk-based regulation. The framework combines three transaction-risk tiers with four AI lifecycle stages to establish proportionate oversight obligations that balance innovation, regulatory accountability, and financial stability. Drawing on technological, economic, legal, and institutional perspectives, the framework is applied to the 2026 U.S. interagency review of model risk management guidance (SR 26-2) to demonstrate how lifecycle governance can strengthen oversight of agentic AI in financial services. The analysis shows that the TLG Framework provides a structured alternative to the existing guidance-versus-rulemaking approach by aligning regulatory obligations with transaction risk rather than institutional size or technology labels. The paper concludes that binding, lifecycle-based oversight offers a pra…

title: Subsidised Micro-Takaful and the Financial Well-Being of Low-Income Households in Malaysia: Evidence from the Perlindungan Tenang Voucher
abstract: This paper evaluates the Perlindungan Tenang Voucher (PTV), a Malaysian government subsidy that enabled low-income households to buy micro-takaful and micro-insurance cover. Using a survey of 599 heads of household who reported on the periods before and after the intervention, a difference-in-differences model compares the change in health expenditure of PTV beneficiaries with that of non-beneficiaries, and the same comparison is made for households holding other takaful or insurance policies. Kaplan–Meier estimates and a Cox proportional hazards model describe the risk of a hospital visit, and a logit model identifies which households hold unsubsidised cover. Health expenditure fell for all households after the intervention, but by less among PTV beneficiaries than among non-beneficiaries, so the voucher did not by itself produce a measurable reduction in out-of-pocket spending; this is consistent with the very small number of claims made under the programme. Households with other takaful or insurance policies, by contrast, recorded a large relative fall. The risk of a hospital visit rises with household spending and chronic illness, and unsubsidised cover is more common among households with higher income, more education and more assets. Because pre-intervention values were recalled and households chose whether to use the voucher, the estimates are best read as associations. …

title: SECURE AND SCALABLE MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION FOR ENTERPRISE FINANCIAL DOCUMENT PROCESSING
abstract: Banking document reviews depend on whether information agrees across a case file. Reading each document correctly is only part of the job. In loan processing, KYC onboarding and trade finance, staff must also reconcile names, amounts, dates and conditions before a case moves forward. OCR and fixed rules work reasonably well on predictable documents, but exceptions and free-text entries still require judgment. This paper describes a multi-agent document-processing architecture that keeps that judgment separate from operational authority. Specialized agents identify documents, extract fields and flag inconsistencies. A rule-driven orchestrator controls case status, permitted tool calls and release to downstream banking systems. Extracted values retain references to their source pages and text locations, while policy rules determine when human review is required. The paper sets out a test plan covering cross-document accuracy, matched-compute baselines, audit evidence, prompt injection and throughput. The architecture is proposed rather than deployed; no measured performance results are claimed.

title: THE MEDIATING FUNCTION OF PERCEIVED CREDIBILITY IN THE IMPACT OF SUSTAINABILITY REPORT QUALITY ON INVESTOR TRUST
abstract: This study examines the relationship between investor trust and perceived sustainability reporting quality, paying special attention to the mediating function of perceived credibility. The study creates an integrated framework based on signaling theory and information asymmetry theory to explain how investors understand sustainability disclosures and convert their evaluations into trust in reporting firms. In particular, the study looks at the direct connections between investor trust, perceived sustainability reporting quality, and perceived credibility. It also evaluates whether credibility may explain the relationship between investor confidence and reporting quality. Individual investors and representatives of institutional investors in Vietnam provided survey data. With investor type included as a control variable and bootstrapping used to assess the mediating link, covariance-based structural equation modeling was used to analyze the suggested correlations. The results show that investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated with higher perceived sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated, and the relationship between reporting quality and trust is partially mediated by perceived credibility. Методологія дослідження побудована на застосуванні описової статистики та економетричного моделювання з розробленням однофакторних і багатофакторної лінійних регресійних моделей. Емпіричний аналіз включає показники обсягу торгів на ринку капіталу, як показники інвестиційної активності, та кількості електронних операцій і кількості активних рахунків у цінних паперах, як показників цифровізації.Результати дослідження підтверджують позитивний статистичний взаємозв’язок між кількістю електронних опера-цій та обсягом торгів. Розроблена багатофакторна модель має вищу пояснювальну здатність (R² = 0,815). Коефіцієнт при кількості електронних операцій є позитивним і статистично значущим. title: ECONOMIC RESILIENCE IN EUROPE AMID INVESTMENT RISKS
abstract: Amid global economic volatility and growing geopolitical uncertainty, understanding how investment risks and economic resilience differ across regions of Europe has become increasingly important for shaping effective investment and regional development policy. This study assesses differences in investment risks and economic resilience between the regions of Europe and determines their relationship with actual volumes of foreign direct investment (FDI). Using the Global Investment Risk and Resilience Index (GIRRI) and United Nations FDI statistics for 38 European countries grouped into four regions (Western, Northern, Southern, and Eastern Europe), the study uses comparative, statistical, and graphical analysis to assess the homogeneity and regional distribution of risk and resilience indicators. The results show that Western and Northern Europe have the lowest investment risk and the highest resilience, while Southern and Eastern Europe display greater risk, particularly in inflation, political stability, legal-regulatory, and physical climate dimensions, as well as lower resilience in external accounts, innovation, and quality of governance. The analysis indicates that the relationship between investment resilience and actual FDI inflows is not linear. title: SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND UNIVERSAL DESIGN: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THREE GREEK CITIES
abstract: Universal Design has emerged as an increasingly important approach to the development of inclusive, accessible, and sustainable environments. Its significance extends beyond the provision of technical accessibility measures, as it addresses the ability of people with different physical, sensory, cognitive, and social characteristics to participate independently and equitably in everyday life. In the urban environment, this perspective is particularly important because streets, pavements, public transportation, squares, cultural sites, and public buildings form interconnected systems through which people move and interact. This study investigates the relationship between Universal Design and sustainable urban development through a comparative analysis of three Greek cities: Larissa, Trikala, and Athens, within the framework of a study conducted based on questionnaires and interviews with responsible municipal officials. The research adopts a qualitative multiple-case-study methodology combining an extensive literature review, analysis of planning and municipal documentation, examination of urban interventions, and qualitative primary research based on semi-structured interviews with relevant municipal authorities. The three cities were selected because they demonstrate different approaches to accessibility, sustainable mobility, public-space transformation, and urban innovation.…

title: Trends in Rehabilitation-Based Narcotics Law Reform and Role-Based Evidence: The Integrated Rehabilitation–Role Evidence (IRRE) Model for Justice for Drug Users and Disrupting Trafficking Networks in North Sumatra
abstract: Drug abuse is not merely a criminal problem but also a matter of health and recovery. Law No. 35 of 2009 requires addicts and victims of drug abuse to undergo medical and social rehabilitation, yet in practice a person found carrying narcotics may hold very different roles, from user and addict to courier, recipient, or part of a larger trafficking network. This article examines whether law enforcement can adequately distinguish people who need treatment from those who control illicit circulation, in the context of North Sumatra, where the provincial police reported 6,078 cases and 7,634 suspects in 2025. Using a normative juridical and conceptual method, the article develops the Integrated Rehabilitation–Role Evidence Model (IRRE), which integrates rehabilitation assessment of drug users with role-based evidence mapping across the narcotics network and a digital dashboard linking arrest data to final and binding judgments. IRRE has five components: a Rehabilitation Gate, a 0.1 Gram Research Threshold, a Role Evidence Matrix, an Arrest-to-Final-Judgment Dashboard, and an Online Rehabilitation Legal Gateway. The 0.1 gram figure is proposed only as a hypothesis to be tested legally, medically, and empirically, not as a legal limit. title: The Evolution of Electricity Spot Markets, Strategy, Behavior, and Settlement: A Comparative Review
abstract: This review paper synthesizes recent research on the evolution of electricity spot markets, focusing on the transition from national power exchanges to local peer-to-peer (P2P) trading systems(Ahmad 2019; Poplavskaya 2020) . By analyzing market designs in India, Europe, China, and Switzerland, the paper evaluates the effectiveness of various pricing mechanisms, including Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP), zonal pricing, and Marginal Pricing versus Pay-as-Bid (Ableitner 2020; Wang 2022) . Using advanced multi-agent-based simulations (MABS) and reinforcement learning (RL), the review demonstrates that while granular pricing mechanisms like LMP provide superior location signals, they often require hybrid settlement methods—such as System Average Pricing (SAP)—to ensure consumer fairness and acceptance(Ableitner 2020; Wang 2022) . Furthermore, the review explores the behavioral aspects of market participation, identifying a heterogeneous user base in local markets that values a balance between active price-setting agency and automated convenience(Poplavskaya 2020) . title: Dual-layer coordinated economic dispatch for transmission-distribution system considering interregional peer-to-peer energy trading in DNs
A just energy transition approach for the Global South: insights from Brazil for South Africa and beyond
abstract: This article examines the institutional conditions shaping energy transitions in resource-dependent economies, drawing on Brazil’s experience to derive policy insights for South Africa and comparable African contexts. Transitions are often framed as processes of technological substitution. This article argues instead that outcomes are determined primarily by institutional configurations that structure incentives, allocate risk and manage distributional conflict. Grounded in institutional political economy and the literature on directed technical change, the analysis focuses on four dimensions: fossil fuel rent structures; industrial policy sequencing; electricity market design; and development finance architecture. Brazil’s trajectory reflects institutional layering, with renewable electricity expansion occurring alongside hydrocarbon production. Comparison with South Africa highlights the limits of policy transfer in a more carbon-intensive and regionally concentrated political economy. Programmes such as the Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme and the Just Energy Transition Partnership illustrate both the potential and constraints of procurement design and concessional finance.

title: Optimizing Classification-Based Machine Learning Models for Bacterial Spot Disease Detection in Tomato Plants
abstract: Plant pests and diseases destroy up to 40% of global crop production each year, causing more than US$220 billion in losses [4]. Tomatoes are among the most widely consumed crops, with approximately 160 million tons consumed each year [13]. In Florida, bacterial spot, caused mainly by Xanthomonas perforans [9, 11] and favored by hot, humid, rainy weather, cost tomato growers almost $900,000 in the 2007–2008 season [2]. We hypothesized that infected tomato leaves differ measurably from healthy leaves in color and texture, and tested whether machine learning could detect these differences. Using 3,769 PlantVillage leaf images, we compared Logistic Regression, Ridge Classifier, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Classifier (SVC) models with a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN). The tuned SVC performed best among the classical models (99.34% accuracy, 99.44% F1, ROC-AUC 1.00) and matched the CNN (McNemar’s test, p = 1.00). However, its accuracy fell sharply on rotated or brightened images, so field performance is likely lower. Machine learning shows promise for early detection of bacterial spot, but it must be validated on field images before practical use.

title: A review of the governance challenges in the regional integration of the ASEAN Single Aviation Market
abstract: Purpose This article aims to critically examine the governance challenges in the ASEAN Single Aviation Market (ASAM) at policy and operational levels. Design/methodology/approach An integrative review framework was adopted to synthesise diverse sources, including academic literature and policy documents. The data were examined through qualitative document analysis with content analysis and thematic coding to identify obstacles in implementing ASAM. Findings While ASAM has advanced aviation connectivity and liberalisation in ASEAN, the findings reveal that governance limitations, particularly the absence of a supranational authority, have created uneven outcomes in the region. At the policy level, ASAM is impacted by the protection of national carriers, foreign investment control, and divergent competition policies; while at the operational level, key challenges include gaps in operational and safety oversight as well as in slot coordination, which collectively limit the extent to which ASAM is effectively leveraged. Originality/value This study provides a holistic synthesis of the institutional and regulatory challenges shaping ASEAN’s aviation integration, contributing to academic literature by identifying the impact of governance structure on ASAM’s implementation and offering practical considerations for industry players to realise its full potential.

title: Top management attributes and market valuation across economic regimes: an ESG accountability signalling perspective from an emerging EU capital market
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether the market-valuation associations attached to female and foreign executive representation, managerial interlocks and managerial ownership differ between stable and crisis periods, and whether the observed patterns are compatible with an Environmental, Social, and Corporate Governance (ESG) accountability-signalling perspective alongside competing governance interpretations. Design/methodology/approach The study uses Orbis data for non-financial Warsaw Stock Exchange firms over 2017–2023. Baseline difference and system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimates are supplemented by CRE/Mundlak and firm fixed-effects specifications. The governance variables are based on the available 2023 records, and treated as structurally persistent; main coefficients therefore rely primarily on cross-sectional differences between firms, while COVID interactions capture regime-contingent valuation differences. Findings In the baseline system GMM, female and foreign executive representation and managerial interlocks are positively associated with firm valuation during stable periods. Their COVID-period interactions are negative; combined COVID-period associations remain positive. Segmenting QRIS Readiness Among Traditional Market Traders Using Technology Readiness Index 2.0 and K-Means Clustering
abstract: Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) is widely available in Indonesian traditional markets, but availability alone does not show whether traders are ready to use it, suggesting that technology readiness may be an important factor beyond physical access to payment infrastructure. This study profiles and segments the technology readiness of 60 smartphone-owning traders at Pasar Beriman Tomohon, North Sulawesi, using the four dimensions of the Technology Readiness Index 2.0 (TRI 2.0): Optimism, Innovativeness, Discomfort, and Insecurity. K-means clustering on standardised dimension scores produced five segments that follow the TRI 2.0 archetypes. The five-cluster solution was chosen on theoretical grounds, because the silhouette check slightly favoured three clusters; the segments are weakly separated and only moderately stable. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha (Innovativeness and Discomfort fell below the 0.60 criterion), and group differences were examined through non-parametric tests. Paranoids formed the largest segment (25.0%) and Pioneers the smallest (11.7%). Insecurity had the higher mean score of the two inhibitor dimensions, exceeding Discomfort. Age showed a stronger demographic association with readiness than merchandise type, and the observed association was concentrated in Innovativeness and Discomfort rather than Insecurity. These f…

title: Sun'iy intellekt ta'sirida mehnat bozori: texnologik ishsizlik, kasblar qayta taqsimlanishi va inson kapitaliga yangi talablar
abstract: Ushbu maqolada sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarining global va milliy mehnat bozoriga ta'siri makroiqtisodiy nuqtai nazardan tadqiq etilgan. Tadqiqotda avtomatlashtirishning vazifalarga asoslangan nazariy yondashuvi asosida sun'iy intellektning mehnat jarayonlariga ta'siri, xususan, ayrim vazifalarning inson mehnatidan siqib chiqarilishi hamda yangi faoliyat yo'nalishlarining shakllanishiga olib keluvchi qayta tiklash effektlari tahlil qilingan. Jahon Iqtisodiy Forumi, Xalqaro Valyuta Fondi va Xalqaro Mehnat Tashkilotining zamonaviy statistik ma'lumotlari asosida ish o'rinlarining qisqarishi va yangi ish o'rinlarining yaratilishi jarayonlari, kasblar tarkibidagi o'zgarishlar hamda inson kapitaliga bo'lgan talabning yangilanishi baholangan. O'zbekiston misolida rivojlanayotgan iqtisodiyotlar sharoitida sun'iy intellektdan samarali foydalanish va mehnat bozoridagi o'zgarishlarga moslashish bo'yicha amaliy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan. Tadqiqot natijalari sun'iy intellektning mehnat bozoriga ta'siri mamlakatlar, iqtisodiyot tarmoqlari va turli ijtimoiy guruhlar kesimida bir xil namoyon bo'lmasligini ko'rsatadi. Mazkur jarayonlarni samarali boshqarishda ta'lim tizimini rivojlantirish, inson kapitali sifatini oshirish va davlat siyosatini takomillashtirish muhim ahamiyat kasb etadi.

title: Gold Price Forecasting and Market Analysis Using LSTM and Visibility Graph
abstract: Much research has focused on financial market time series. This thesis presents a comprehensive analysis of gold price prediction and market structure using a visibility graph network. With a specific focus on the years 2008 and 2024, we discuss the price dynamics of gold in two currencies: Bangladeshi Taka (BDT) and US Dollars (USD), using two complementary methods: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) forecasting and Visibility Graph (VG) analysis, which revealed the structural complexity of the market. The LSTM model captures the non-linear movements of highly volatile gold prices, giving it strong predictive capability and providing useful insights for investors and policymakers in Bangladesh. Golds popularity as a safe-haven investment during economic uncertainty underscores the importance of forecasting, and our results show that LSTM can generate effective long-term projections. At the same time, by constructing gold price time series as complex networks using the VG algorithm, we study structural characteristics every year. Important network measurements-Average Clustering Coefficient, Mean Degree, Modularity, Average Shortest Path Length, Structural Entropy and Global Reaching Centrality are calculated to find underlying structures and market dynamics. Comparative analysis between BDT and USD markets reveals that the Bangladeshi gold market exhibits higher modularity and entr…

From Home-Market Foundations to Transnational Reach: A Contextual Model of African Service-Firm Internationalisation
abstract: This study examines how established African service-sector firms progress from strong domestic positions to regional and wider transnational reach. Using longitudinal multiple-case evidence from MTN, FirstBank and Shoprite, it traces how firms deploy, test, and reconfigure capabilities built in the home market across diverse institutional environments. The findings show that domestic scale, managerial experience, organisational routines, financial capacity, technology and market knowledge formed important foundations for later expansion. Regionalisation served as both a scaling and learning process, while entry into more distant or institutionally complex markets required reconfiguration of capabilities. Retrenchment in MTN and Shoprite further shows that internationalisation is neither linear nor irreversible. The study develops a contextual pathway linking home-market foundations, capability accumulation, regional scaling and learning, capability reconfiguration and transnational reach, moderated by strategic intent, host-country institutions, digital capability and service characteristics.

title: Micro-batch clearing: Uniform pricing as a pricing-rule reform for latency rents
abstract: In this paper, we propose Micro-Batch Clearing, a matching mechanism that eliminates latency rents through a change to an exchange’s pricing rule rather than a redesign of its architecture. The change is to matching-engine logic only — uniform within-batch clearing, pro-rata allocation, and sealed-interval handling — with no change to network topology, order routing, co-location, or the persistent order book. Within each short sealed batch interval, all crossing orders execute at one uniform clearing price, removing the within-event mapping from speed to execution price that a continuous limit order book (CLOB) creates. Unmatched orders persist in the resting book and roll into the next batch, so the mechanism retains CLOB’s order-book persistence while altering only the price at which the matching engine clears, leaving order submission, routing, and co-location unchanged. This distinguishes it from Frequent Batch Auctions (FBA), which deliver the same speed-rent elimination but require the exchange to operate as a discrete-time auction and discard unmatched orders. title: Analysis of the Influence of Service Quality on Patient Satisfaction at the Bumidaya Inpatient Health Center, South Lampung Regency
abstract: The quality of healthcare services is an important factor in improving patient satisfaction, as patient experience is shaped by the comparison between the service received and their expectations. This study aims to analyze the relationship between five dimensions of service quality tangible evidence, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy with patient satisfaction and to identify the most influential dimensions at the Bumidaya Inpatient Community Health Center (UPTD) in South Lampung Regency. This study employed an analytical survey design with a cross-sectional approach. Respondents consisted of 100 outpatients selected using an accidental sampling method. Data were obtained through a Likert-scale questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability, then analyzed using multiple linear regression and Spearman correlation. The results showed that tangible evidence was positively and significantly associated with patient satisfaction (r=0.370; p<0.001), as well as empathy (r=0.317; p=0.001). Meanwhile, reliability (r=-0.060; p=0.556), responsiveness (r=0.189; p=0.060), and assurance (r=0.125; p=0.214) did not show any significant relationship in the bivariate analysis. In the multivariate analysis, physical evidence (β=0.444), responsiveness (β=0.232), and empathy (β=0.252) had a significant relationship with patient satisfaction, with the model explainin…

title: The Influence of Human Resource Competencies, Internal Control Systems, and Service Innovation on Financial Performance
abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of human resource (HR) competence, internal control systems, and service innovation on the financial performance of PT Pelindo Jasa Maritim Region 4. The research employed a quantitative approach by distributing questionnaires to 53 respondents consisting of management, finance, and operational staff across five operational areas of PT Pelindo Region 4. The data were analysed using multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that HR competence has a positive effect on financial performance, particularly in the understanding of accounting standards and the preparation of transparent financial reports, although the aspect of providing strategic financial recommendations still requires improvement. Internal control systems significantly affect financial performance, with strengths in task distribution, written policies, and financial supervision, while routine evaluations and error detection remain weak. Service innovation positively affects financial performance through the utilization of digital technology, although consistency in following up on customer feedback needs to be strengthened. Overall, the company’s financial performance is categorized as good to very good, with its main strength in asset optimization, while budget efficiency remains a challenge.

title: Ceiling Effects and Item Discrimination in Satisfaction-Based Instructional Facilitation Measures Among Indonesian Pre-Service Science Teachers
abstract: Background Satisfaction-based surveys are widely used in educational quality assurance, yet their ability to distinguish among respondents may be limited when responses are concentrated at the upper end of the scale. This study examined ceiling concentration and item discrimination in instructional facilitation measures among Indonesian pre-service science teachers, together with their observed associations with learning motivation. Methods A cross-sectional measurement diagnostic analysis was conducted using responses from 348 pre-service science teachers from 29 higher education institutions in Indonesia. The analysis included 22 instructional facilitation items covering Lecture Implementation, Teaching Material Use, and Science Practicum, together with six Learning Motivation items. Ceiling concentration was assessed using a 15% maximum-response benchmark, while corrected item-total correlations were examined as indicators of item discrimination. Facilitation-Motivation associations were evaluated using 132 Pearson correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Instructional facilitation scores were also compared across study programme, semester, gender, age, and academic achievement groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests with epsilon-squared effect sizes. Results All 22 instructional facilitation items exceeded the 15% ceiling benchmark, with approximately…

Realita di lapangan menunjukkan bahwa pelaksanaan alur pengelolaan limbah medis masih menghadapi berbagai kendala, terutama terkait kepatuhan petugas terhadap prosedur yang telah ditetapkan (Saputra & Wijaya, 2022). abstract: Maqolada Buxoro viloyatida elektron xizmatlarni rivojlantirishning hududiy iqtisodiy o'sishga ta'siri Buxoro viloyati statistika boshqarmasining (buxstat.uz) rasmiy ma'lumotlari asosida tahlil qilingan. 2016-2024-yillar davomida "axborot va aloqa xizmatlari" (elektron xizmatlarga eng yaqin rasmiy statistik toifa) hajmi va uning umumiy xizmatlar hajmi o'sish sur'ati bilan bog'liqligi Pirson korrelyatsiya koeffitsienti yordamida hisoblangan. title: Analyzing the Relationship Between Online Patient Registration System Implementation, Service Effectiveness, and Patient Satisfaction at Drs. H. Amri Tambunan Regional General Hospital
abstract: Hospital administrative services that are not yet optimal, such as long waiting times, disorganized queues, and limited access to information, may affect service effectiveness and patient satisfaction. The implementation of an online patient registration system is one of the strategies to improve service efficiency and provide easier access for patients. The effectiveness of its implementation and its relationship with patient satisfaction still need to be empirically examined. This study aims to analyze the relationship between the implementation of an online patient registration system and service effectiveness as well as patient satisfaction at RSUD Drs. H. Amri Tambunan. This research employed a quantitative design with a correlational approach. The sample consisted of 95 outpatients who used the online registration system through WhatsApp and the Mobile JKN application, selected using accidental sampling. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using univariate analysis, Shapiro–Wilk normality test, and Spearman Rank correlation test. The results showed that the level of implementation of the online registration system was categorized as high (63.2%) with a mean score of 82.46. Service effectiveness was also categorized as high (65.3%) with a mean score of 83.12, and patient satisfaction was categorized as high (67.4%) with a mean score of 84.25…

title: Income-related disparities in dental outpatient service utilization among Korean adults: a study using the 2019–2023 Korea Health Panel
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to investigate disparities in dental outpatient service utilization according to income level among adults using the 2019–2023 Korea Health Panel data. Methods: This study included 54,446 adults aged 20 years or older who participated in the Korea Health Panel from 2019 to 2023. Income level was classified into five income quintiles (Q1–Q5). Complex samples logistic regression analysis was performed to examine the association between income level and dental outpatient service utilization. Results: After adjusting for sex, age, marital status, education level, health insurance type, and chronic disease status, Q5 showed significantly higher odds of dental outpatient service utilization than Q1 in every year from 2019 to 2023. The adjusted odds ratios for Q5 versus Q1 were 1.81 in 2019, 1.75 in 2020, 1.50 in 2021, 1.47 in 2022, and 1.39 in 2023 (all p<0.05). Adults in Q3 also had significantly higher odds of dental outpatient service utilization than those in Q1 in most years after 2020. Conclusions: Disparities in dental outpatient service utilization according to income level persisted among adults throughout 2019–2023. These findings suggest that socioeconomic inequalities in dental care utilization remain and highlight the need for policy support to improve equity in dental care utilization and enhance access to dental care for low-income populati…
